IN.title: Trump-backed candidate calls for recount in state Senate District 23 race
IN.summary: Paula Copenhaver, the Trump-endorsed challenger who lost Indiana Senate District 23 by three votes, filed a recount petition alleging illegal voting by unqualified voters, claiming her campaign identified 14 people who disclosed they voted Republican despite being registered Democrats.

IN.title: Trump-backed candidate seeks recount in Indiana Senate race with 3-vote margin
IN.summary: Copenhaver's legal team filed a verified recount petition against incumbent Sen. Spencer Deery's three-vote primary victory in Senate District 23, with the Indiana Recount Commission indicating the manual recount spanning six counties could extend into July.

KY.title: Kentucky primaries 2026: Poll times, key races and what to watch
KY.summary: Al Jazeera previewed Kentucky's May 19 closed primary, highlighting the open U.S. Senate race to succeed retiring Mitch McConnell and the nationally watched 4th Congressional District primary between incumbent Rep. Thomas Massie and Trump-backed challenger Ed Gallrein.

KY.title: Here are the state and federal primary races to watch in Kentucky
KY.summary: Louisville Public Media outlined the key contests on the May 19 Kentucky primary ballot, including the Republican U.S. Senate primary for McConnell's seat and competitive congressional primaries, with voting information including poll hours.

KY.title: Here are Kentucky's 2026 primary election results
KY.summary: VPM/NPR reported results from Kentucky's May 19 primary, covering the Republican and Democratic Senate nominations and the outcome of the high-profile 4th Congressional District race between Rep. Thomas Massie and Trump-endorsed challenger Ed Gallrein.

LA.title: Cassidy falls short as Louisiana Senate race heads to runoff
LA.summary: Sen. Bill Cassidy lost renomination in the May 16 primary—the first incumbent senator to do so in 14 years—as Rep. Julia Letlow (45%) and state Treasurer John Fleming (28%) advanced to a June 27 runoff; Louisiana voters also rejected all five constitutional amendments on the ballot.

LA.title: Political analyst gives early look at Louisiana's U.S. Senate GOP runoff
LA.summary: A political analyst previewed the June 27 Republican Senate runoff between Julia Letlow and John Fleming, analyzing the electorate dynamics and what each candidate needs to secure the nomination following the primary that ousted incumbent Bill Cassidy.

LA.title: Fewer than 300 votes decide Democratic runoff in Louisiana Senate primary, recount still possible
LA.summary: Fewer than 300 votes separated the second- and third-place finishers in the Democratic Senate primary, raising the prospect of a recount that could affect which candidate advances to face the Republican nominee in the general election.

LA.title: U.S. House primaries officially rescheduled to fall, Louisiana officials say
LA.summary: Louisiana's Secretary of State confirmed all six U.S. House races—previously suspended after the Supreme Court struck down the congressional map—are officially moved to a November 3 open primary with a December 12 runoff, with new candidate qualifying scheduled for August 5-7.

MD.title: Trump calls for DOJ investigation after mail ballot error in Maryland
MD.summary: Trump called for a DOJ investigation into Maryland's mail-in ballot printing error, in which a vendor sent some voters the wrong party's gubernatorial primary ballot; Maryland's Board of Elections said safeguards prevent duplicate voting and only replacement ballots will be counted.

MD.title: Maryland Board of Elections pushes back on Trump's claim of 500,000 fake mail-in ballots
MD.summary: Maryland election director Jared DeMarinis refuted Trump's claim that 500,000 'fake' mail-in ballots had been sent, affirming the error involved incorrect party ballots from a vendor and that only replacement ballots mailed the week of May 18 would be counted.

MD.title: Maryland is resending thousands of mail-in primary ballots after a vendor mix-up
MD.summary: Maryland election officials announced they would resend mail-in ballots to all potentially affected voters after a printing vendor error caused some voters to receive the wrong party's gubernatorial primary ballot, with replacement ballots mailed starting the week of May 18 and original ballots voided.

MI.title: Antrim County Clerk has changed at least 6 voters' statuses to 'cancel'
MI.summary: Records show Antrim County Clerk Victoria Bishop altered at least 6 voters' statuses to 'canceled' and changed registrations for at least 8 additional voters in defiance of a Michigan Bureau of Elections order to stop unauthorized voter roll maintenance.

MN.title: MN Legislature closes out session marked by partisan division, election year politics
MN.summary: The Minnesota Legislature adjourned its 2026 session on May 18; the 67-67 split House had passed an elections administration bill (HF4240) streamlining absentee voting procedures, standardizing the statewide voter registration system, and clarifying early voting recordkeeping.

MN.title: 2026 Minnesota Legislative Session Adjourns
MN.summary: The Minnesota Legislature officially adjourned the 2026 session on May 18, concluding a session shaped by divided government and election-year politics that included passage of election administration reforms alongside major infrastructure spending.

NC.title: NC committee votes to put 'right to work,' 'right to farm' amendments on 2026 ballot
NC.summary: A North Carolina Senate committee advanced two proposed constitutional amendments—enshrining the right to engage in farming and forestry and guaranteeing a right to work free from union mandates—that would appear on the November 2026 ballot if approved by the full legislature.

NC.title: NC Senate committee advances amendment on income tax cap for 2026 ballot
NC.summary: A North Carolina Senate committee approved a proposed constitutional amendment to cap the state income tax rate, adding to a growing list of measures Republican lawmakers are seeking to place before voters on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot.

NC.title: Republican lawmakers revive effort to elect NC State Board of Education members
NC.summary: North Carolina Republican legislators advanced a proposed constitutional amendment that would allow voters to select members of the State Board of Education—rather than the governor—as part of a broader push to add conservative-leaning measures to the November 2026 ballot.

NC.title: NC's right to work, right to farm constitutional amendments start to move in State Senate
NC.summary: North Carolina's Senate committee moved forward two constitutional amendments—establishing right-to-work and right-to-farm protections—that would require voter ratification on the November 2026 ballot, which could feature as many as six total constitutional amendments.

NM.title: As expanded early voting opens, most New Mexico independents choose Democratic ballot
NM.summary: On the first weekend of expanded early voting under New Mexico's new semi-open primary system—the first time independent voters could cast primary ballots—roughly three-quarters of the 2,461 independents who voted chose the Democratic primary ballot.

NV.title: Backed by pro-film subsidy groups, carpenter challenges progressive Assembly Democratic incumbent
NV.summary: Union carpenter Douglas Candido, heavily funded by labor groups backing film tax credits, is mounting a primary challenge against Democratic incumbent Assemblymember Javon Jackson in Assembly District 6 ahead of Nevada's June 9 primary election.

NV.title: Three Republicans vie for chance to beat Horsford in CD4
NV.summary: Three Republican candidates are competing in Nevada's June 9 primary for the chance to challenge incumbent Democratic Rep. Steven Horsford in a district where Democrats outnumber Republicans by over 20,000 registered voters.

OK.title: Oklahoma Voice launches voter guide ahead of June 16 primary election
OK.summary: Oklahoma Voice published a comprehensive voter guide for the June 16 partisan primary election, covering all statewide and federal candidates, contested legislative primaries, and the nonpartisan State Question 832 minimum-wage ballot measure, with the voter registration deadline set for May 22.

OR.title: Primary election 2026: Oregonians head to the ballot box
OR.summary: Oregon held its May 19 primary with Gov. Tina Kotek seeking renomination against nine Democratic challengers, a 14-candidate Republican field, and Referendum Measure 120—a gas tax hike widely expected to fail—on the ballot; nearly 513,000 ballots had already been cast by mail by election day.

OR.title: Here are Oregon's 2026 primary election results
OR.summary: NPR affiliate coverage of Oregon's May 19 primary results, covering the gubernatorial race, U.S. Senate and House primaries, and the fate of the fuel tax referendum on the ballot.

PA.title: 4 US House races to watch in Pennsylvania on Election Day
PA.summary: Spotlight PA previewed four Pennsylvania congressional Democratic primaries on May 19 where voters chose nominees to challenge vulnerable Republican incumbents in seats key to retaking the U.S. House, including districts in Bucks County, Lehigh Valley, the Scranton area, and the open Philadelphia 3rd District seat.

PA.title: 2026 PA primary: Your election day voting FAQs answered
PA.summary: Spotlight PA answered voter questions for Pennsylvania's May 19 primary, covering poll hours (7 a.m.–8 p.m.), mail ballot status (approximately 74% of 850,000+ requested ballots returned by election morning), registration lookup, and how voters still in line at 8 p.m. are entitled to vote.

PA.title: Pennsylvania 2026 primary election results
PA.summary: WHYY provided live results from Pennsylvania's May 19 primary, where voters selected nominees for governor, all 17 congressional seats, all 203 state House seats, and half of the state Senate seats.

PA.title: Here are Pennsylvania's 2026 primary election results
PA.summary: NPR summarized May 19 Pennsylvania primary outcomes, covering the governor's race, competitive U.S. House primaries including the open Philadelphia 3rd District, and the state's significance for determining House control in November.

SC.title: Early voting begins in one week. What to know before you head to the polls
SC.summary: South Carolina Public Radio reported that early voting for the June 9 primary begins May 26, explaining photo ID requirements and polling hours, while noting congressional primaries could be delayed if the state moves forward with mid-cycle redistricting targeting Rep. James Clyburn's majority-Black district.

SC.title: SC House weighs redrawing congressional maps in mid-decade redistricting push
SC.summary: South Carolina's House debated a Republican-drawn congressional map in a special session, aiming to eliminate the state's only majority-Black district held by Rep. Jim Clyburn and potentially delay congressional primaries to August 18, with a self-imposed deadline of May 26—the start of early voting.

SD.title: SD Senate primaries see rematches as SB 201, governor race loom
SD.summary: Several South Dakota state Senate Republican primaries ahead of the June 2 election are rematches of 2024 contests, including challenges to Senate President Pro Tempore Chris Karr and Senate Majority Leader Jim Mehlhaff, reflecting continued intra-party tension.

SD.title: Deadline to register to vote for primary election is Monday, May 18
SD.summary: South Dakota Secretary of State Monae L. Johnson reminded voters that May 18 at 5 p.m. is the last day to register to participate in the June 2 primary election, which includes Republican primaries for governor, U.S. Senate, and U.S. House under new citizenship proof-of-registration laws.

TN.title: Three Federal Challenges to Tennessee Redistricting Consolidated Into One Case
TN.summary: A federal judge consolidated three separate lawsuits—filed by the ACLU, the NAACP/League of Women Voters, and Democratic candidates—challenging Tennessee's redrawn congressional map that splits Memphis's majority-Black district across three seats, with a hearing on a temporary injunction scheduled for May 20.

TX.title: Trump endorses Ken Paxton in Senate GOP runoff
TX.summary: President Trump endorsed Attorney General Ken Paxton over incumbent Sen. John Cornyn in the Texas Republican U.S. Senate primary runoff, with early voting already underway for the May 26 election, potentially deciding a race that polling showed in a dead heat.

TX.title: Trump delivers 11th-hour endorsement to Paxton in Texas Senate runoff
TX.summary: Axios confirmed Trump's May 19 endorsement of Ken Paxton over John Cornyn in the Texas GOP Senate primary runoff, with early voting in progress for the May 26 runoff election.

TX.title: Trump picks Paxton over Cornyn in Texas' GOP Senate primary runoff as early voting is underway
TX.summary: Austin's NPR station reported Trump endorsed Paxton on the second day of early voting for the May 26 runoff, with 38 total races on the runoff ballot and the Cornyn-Paxton Senate contest drawing the most national attention.

TX.title: When are the 2026 Texas primary runoff elections? Dates and times to know to cast your vote
TX.summary: CBS Texas published a voter guide explaining that early voting runs May 18-22 for the May 26 primary runoff, covering key races including the Cornyn-Paxton Senate runoff, the Republican and Democratic attorney general runoffs, and the Democratic lieutenant governor runoff.

UT.title: Why is Phil Lyman running for Utah's 3rd Congressional District?
UT.summary: Former gubernatorial candidate Phil Lyman explained his challenge to incumbent Rep. Celeste Maloy in Utah's redrawn 3rd Congressional District primary, with the race shaped by a new court-ordered district map and election-integrity concerns, ahead of the June 23 primary.

WA.title: Federal judge rebuffs bid to toss WA legislative maps
WA.summary: U.S. District Judge Robert Lasnik denied a motion to undo court-ordered Washington state legislative district maps drawn to enhance Latino voter representation in the Yakima Valley, ruling that altering the maps on the eve of the August 4 primary would cause significant voter confusion; challengers immediately petitioned the U.S. Supreme Court.

WV.title: Canvass confirms narrow win in Cabell County House of Delegates District 22 race
WV.summary: The Cabell County Board of Canvassers certified Aaron Holley's 650-647 victory over incumbent Delegate Daniel Linville in West Virginia House District 22 after reviewing provisional ballots, as all 55 counties began their official canvassing of the May 12 primary.

WV.title: WV Secretary of State Kris Warner announces canvassing will commence on Monday, May 18, in West Virginia
WV.summary: Secretary of State Kris Warner announced all 55 West Virginia counties would begin canvassing May 12 primary results on May 18, noting three legislative races were decided by five or fewer votes and explaining the hand-count audit process that could trigger full county recounts.

WV.title: Election Canvass Kicks Off Monday
WV.summary: West Virginia Public Broadcasting reported on the statewide primary canvass beginning May 18, covering close races where incumbents lost by two to four votes and explaining that candidates have 48 hours following declared canvass results to request a funded recount.

GA.title: Georgia Republicans Head to Runoffs for Senate and Governor Races
GA.summary: Georgia's May 19 primary sent both the governor and Senate Republican nominations to a June 16 runoff; Lt. Gov. Burt Jones faces billionaire Rick Jackson for the governor's race while Collins faces Dooley for the Senate nod, as Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms won the governor nomination outright.

KY.title: Takeaways from primaries in Georgia, Kentucky, Pennsylvania, Alabama and more
KY.summary: Trump-backed Ed Gallrein defeated Rep. Thomas Massie in the most expensive House primary in history ($33M), while Andy Barr won the Republican Senate primary to succeed retiring Sen. Mitch McConnell in a key seat.

PA.title: 4 takeaways from Tuesday's primary night in half a dozen states
PA.summary: Gov. Josh Shapiro and Treasurer Stacy Garrity both won uncontested primaries, setting up the fall Pennsylvania governor race with Shapiro entering as a heavy favorite in this critical battleground state.

OR.title: 4 takeaways from Tuesday's primary night in half a dozen states
OR.summary: Christine Drazan won Oregon's Republican gubernatorial primary, setting up a fall rematch with incumbent Gov. Tina Kotek; Drazan narrowly lost to Kotek in 2022 and Kotek is rated a favorite to win again.

ID.title: Key races called in Idaho primary elections
ID.summary: Gov. Brad Little secured the Republican gubernatorial primary with 60% and Sen. Jim Risch won his fourth-term bid; Little will face Democrat Terri Pickens in November in a state with a strong GOP lean.

AL.title: Takeaways from primaries in Georgia, Kentucky, Pennsylvania, Alabama and more
AL.summary: Alabama held regular May 19 primaries for most races while candidate qualifying for the separate August 11 special primaries in four redistricted House districts opened May 20, following SCOTUS approval of the state's 2023 congressional maps.

TX.title: Donald Trump's endorsement of Ken Paxton over John Cornyn roils Texas Senate race
TX.summary: Trump's endorsement of AG Ken Paxton over incumbent Sen. Cornyn in the May 26 GOP Senate runoff — announced on the second day of early voting — is expected to dramatically shift the closely contested race.

SC.title: S.C. redistricting proposal passes House, heads to state Senate
SC.summary: After an overnight session, the Republican-led House passed a redistricting bill 74-37 at 12:39 a.m. that would redraw Rep. Jim Clyburn's majority-Black congressional district; the measure now moves to the more skeptical state Senate.

CT.title: Governor Lamont Signs Legislation Making Absentee Ballots an Option for All Voters in Connecticut Elections
CT.summary: Gov. Lamont signed legislation removing the excuse requirement for absentee voting, fulfilling the 2024 constitutional amendment approved 58%-42%; the law takes effect immediately and allows all Connecticut voters to request mail ballots.

NC.title: Whatley, Cooper win North Carolina primaries, CBS News projects, teeing up key Senate contest
NC.summary: Former Democratic Gov. Roy Cooper and former RNC Chair Michael Whatley won their party primaries in North Carolina's open Senate race, setting up a competitive fall contest to replace retiring Republican Sen. Thom Tillis.

ND.title: US Supreme Court sends North Dakota tribal redistricting case back for review
ND.summary: The Supreme Court vacated the 8th Circuit ruling in Turtle Mountain Band v. Howe and remanded it for reconsideration under the Callais VRA decision, potentially eliminating court-ordered Native American voting district protections.

MS.title: 'We're going backwards.' Mississippians share experiences of voter suppression, dread of redistricting battle
MS.summary: Mississippi voters and civil rights advocates express alarm following the Supreme Court vacating of court-ordered legislative redistricting maps meant to protect minority voting rights, with Gov. Reeves delaying broader redistricting to 2027.

MD.title: Trump calls for DOJ investigation after mail ballot error in Maryland
MD.summary: Trump called for a DOJ investigation after a vendor error sent wrong-party primary ballots to roughly 500,000 Maryland voters; state officials said new ballots are being mailed and safeguards prevent duplicate voting.

NY.title: Voting early and by mail: What you need to know
NY.summary: NYC voters can request mail ballots for the June 23 primary through June 13 or vote early June 13-21; voter registration and party enrollment changes must be received by June 13 to be eligible for primary races.

HI.title: Hawaii Gov. Joshua Green signs bill restricting corporate political activity
HI.summary: Gov. Green signed SB 2471 making Hawaii the first state to comprehensively prohibit corporations from spending on elections and ballot measures, directly challenging the Citizens United ruling; the law takes effect July 1, 2027.

AK.title: Lawmakers look to enact campaign contribution limits, preempting Alaska ballot initiative
AK.summary: On the final day of the legislative session, Alaska lawmakers passed HB 16 imposing a $2,000 per-candidate contribution limit; because the bill is substantially similar to a scheduled ballot initiative, it could cancel the initiative from appearing on the general election ballot.

AK.title: Alaska Legislature's last-day action could cancel campaign-finance ballot measure
AK.summary: The Alaska Legislature passed a campaign finance contribution limits bill on its final day that could preempt a voter-initiative on the same subject scheduled for the August primary ballot, removing that direct-democracy question from voters.

IA.title: Supreme Court voting rights ruling could play a big role at the local level
IA.summary: The Supreme Court's Louisiana v. Callais ruling weakening the Voting Rights Act now threatens at least 17 state and local redistricting maps nationwide, shifting the legal standard for Section 2 challenges from results-based to intentional discrimination — a much harder bar to meet.

IL.title: Illinois county clerks are preparing for mail voting amid continued attacks, changes
IL.summary: Illinois county election clerks are preparing for the 2026 midterms as multiple threats to mail voting converge, including Trump's executive order, the SAVE Act, USPS postmark rule changes, and a Supreme Court ruling on ballot receipt deadlines; Illinois is among 23 states challenging the executive order in court.

IN.title: Indiana recount fight takes 'unprecedented' step to subpoena voters
IN.summary: Indiana's recount commission is being asked to subpoena and depose individual voters accused of illegally crossing party lines in the Republican primary based on their social media posts; legal experts call this use of the recount process to challenge legal voters without precedent in the state.

KS.title: Kansas Democrats in governor's race claw for traction with anti-Brownback attacks on GOP foes
KS.summary: Kansas Democratic candidates for governor are running ahead of an August 4 primary in a state where new election laws — including elimination of the mail ballot grace period and the SAVE database voter-roll verification requirement — have recently taken effect.

KS.title: Democrat hopes to pull off upset for U.S. House seat with military experience, disapproval of Trump
KS.summary: A Democratic challenger is mounting a U.S. House campaign in Kansas's 4th District, in a state where recent changes to voting laws — including the elimination of the three-day mail ballot grace period — have reshaped the electoral landscape for both parties.

MD.title: Maryland lawmakers enact state-level voting rights act, 21 other election bills in 2026
MD.summary: Maryland enacted 22 election-related bills in its 2026 legislative session; the centerpiece is SB 255, the Maryland Voting Rights Act, which prohibits discriminatory election methods at the local level.

ME.title: New poll shows Platner leading Collins in general election match-up
ME.summary: A Pan Atlantic Research survey shows Democratic Senate candidate Graham Platner leading Republican incumbent Susan Collins 48% to 41% among likely voters; the race will be decided in November under Maine's ranked-choice voting system for Senate.

ME.title: Platner holds 7 point lead over Collins in new Maine Senate poll
ME.summary: A new Maine Senate poll shows Democrat Graham Platner with a seven-point lead over Sen. Susan Collins ahead of the November general election, to be determined after Maine's June 9 primary under ranked-choice rules.

ME.title: Platner leads Collins in new poll of Maine Senate race
ME.summary: A new Maine survey finds Democratic Senate hopeful Graham Platner ahead of Republican incumbent Susan Collins by seven points, with Collins trailing in the 1st Congressional District by 20 points while holding a narrow lead in the 2nd District.

MI.title: Senate Dems want to create Michigan Voting Rights Act to counter Supreme Court ruling
MI.summary: A Senate committee advanced legislation to establish a Michigan Voting Rights Act in response to the Supreme Court decision stripping key federal voting protections; the bills face an uncertain path through the Republican-controlled House.

MN.title: Candidate filings for 2026 election open May 19 in Minnesota
MN.summary: The candidate filing period for all federal, state, and county offices in Minnesota opened May 19 and runs through June 2, a key procedural milestone ahead of the August 11 primary and November general election.

MO.title: Missouri legislature ends 2026 session marked by GOP wins, fewer meltdowns
MO.summary: The Missouri Legislature adjourned its 2026 session after passing voting rights restoration for certain parolees, election administration changes, and sending multiple ballot measures to voters in November.

MT.title: Montana U.S. Senate candidates largely unknown to voters, poll finds
MT.summary: A new poll shows that most Montana voters heading into the June primary are unfamiliar with the major U.S. Senate candidates, raising concerns about informed voter participation in the upcoming election.

ND.title: Dems, secretary of state disagree on process to replace candidate after lawmaker's death
ND.summary: Following the April plane-crash death of Rep. Liz Conmy (D-Fargo), North Dakota Democrats and the Secretary of State's office disagree over ballot procedures: state officials say it is too late to add a replacement to the primary ballot, while Democrats argue they can name a replacement for the November general election.

NJ.title: New Jersey primary election 2026: What to know before you vote
NJ.summary: Voter guide covering New Jersey's June 2 primary, including early voting dates (May 26–31), mail ballot application deadlines, and how unaffiliated voters can participate in the state's closed primary by declaring a party at the polls.

NJ.title: State Voting Laws Roundup: May 2026
NJ.summary: National roundup noting New Jersey enacted three expansive voting access laws in 2026, including allowing voters to cure mail ballot technical defects and expanding automatic voter registration to additional state agencies.

NV.title: 2026 Primary Election: Nevada Secretary of State – Republicans
NV.summary: Coverage of the Republican candidates vying for Nevada Secretary of State in the June 9 primary, a key race overseeing election administration as Nevada implements its new open-primary and ranked-choice voting system for the first time.

OH.title: Ohio already requires voter photo ID. Some Republicans want statewide vote on it this fall
OH.summary: Ohio Republican legislators introduced joint resolutions to place a constitutional amendment enshrining the state's existing photo ID voting requirements on the November 2026 ballot, drawing Democratic concern that it could later be used to restrict mail-in or early voting.

OH.title: Photo ID amendment likely to make ballot with Ohio GOP leaders behind it
OH.summary: Ohio House and Senate Republican leaders are backing House Joint Resolution 9 and Senate Joint Resolution 10, which need 60% approval in each chamber to send a voter photo ID constitutional amendment to voters; a floor vote could come as early as June 10.

OH.title: Lawmakers propose changes to reduce standing time for some Ohio voters
OH.summary: House Bill 893 would require Ohio county boards of elections to create accommodation plans for voters who have difficulty standing for prolonged periods while waiting to sign pollbooks or cast ballots.

WI.title: Judge Rules 23 Madison Absentee Ballots Must Be Counted
WI.summary: Urban Milwaukee reported on the Dane County ruling requiring Wisconsin to count 23 late-arriving Madison absentee ballots from the April 7 Supreme Court election, with implications for how election errors are treated under Wisconsin ballot-counting laws.

WY.title: 100 candidates now running for office in Wyoming
WY.summary: More than 100 candidates filed for Wyoming office within the first two days of the candidate filing period opening May 14, with races for governor, secretary of state, two congressional seats, and all 62 House legislative seats ahead of the August 18 primary.

WY.title: 100 candidates now running for office in Wyoming
WY.summary: Wyoming's 2026 candidate filing period opened under new election rules including closed primaries and proof-of-citizenship requirements; Rep. Harriet Hageman is among those who filed for the open U.S. Senate seat, with filing closing May 29.

WY.title: 100 candidates now running for office in Wyoming
WY.summary: After Wyoming's May 13 party affiliation deadline passed and candidate filing opened, more than 100 candidates entered races for the state's most wide-open election cycle in years, with multiple statewide offices and congressional seats without incumbents.

AZ.title: Maricopa County Recorder Justin Heap threatens felony charges over 'unauthorized' drop boxes
AZ.summary: Maricopa County Recorder Justin Heap warned that election workers setting up drop boxes approved by the Board of Supervisors without his sign-off could face class 5 felony charges, reigniting a legal and political battle over who controls election administration in Arizona's most populous county ahead of the 2026 primary.

AZ.title: Maricopa County, Arizona, recorder threatens felony charges over 'unauthorized' drop boxes ahead of primary election
AZ.summary: A dispute over who controls ballot drop box placement in Maricopa County escalated when Recorder Justin Heap's attorney threatened felony charges against election workers handling 'unauthorized' drop boxes, while the Board of Supervisors voted 5-0 to proceed with approving drop box locations over the recorder's objection.

AZ.title: Half of Benson's city council ousted in recall election
AZ.summary: Three of Benson's six city council members were recalled by voters in a southern Arizona election, with the recall effort driven by community backlash over an aluminum plant under construction in the small Cochise County city.

AZ.title: Arizona regulators defend decision to let utilities seek annual rate increases
AZ.summary: Arizona Corporation Commission incumbents Kevin Thompson and Nick Myers — both seeking reelection in the July 21 primary — defended their vote to allow electric, water and gas utilities to seek annual rate adjustments rather than the current system of larger periodic rate cases.

AZ.title: PRIMARY DEBATE: Arizona Corporation Commission (R)
AZ.summary: Republican Corporation Commission incumbents Kevin Thompson and Nick Myers debated ahead of the July 21 primary, agreeing that data center costs should fall on data center owners rather than residential ratepayers, while challenger Ralph Heap declined to participate.

CA.title: LA County to open 122 early vote centers on Saturday for 2026 statewide primary election
CA.summary: Los Angeles County will open 122 vote centers on Saturday May 23, operating 10 a.m. to 7 p.m. daily through June 2 primary election day, offering in-person voting, same-day voter registration, and mail ballot drop-off ahead of the June 2 statewide primary.

CA.title: Hilton, Becerra Lead Democrats' Final Poll for California Governor
CA.summary: The California Democratic Party's final pre-primary poll shows Republican Steve Hilton leading the crowded governor's field at 22%, with Democrat Xavier Becerra at 21%, setting up a potentially historic general election matchup if both advance through the June 2 top-two primary.

CO.title: Colorado Democrats censure Gov. Jared Polis over Tina Peters commutation
CO.summary: Colorado's Democratic Party formally censured Governor Jared Polis for commuting the sentence of Tina Peters, an election denier convicted of breaching Mesa County voting systems, with 90% of the State Central Committee supporting censure after Polis reduced her nine-year sentence amid pressure from President Trump.

CO.title: Colorado Democratic Party censures Gov. Jared Polis over commutation for Tina Peters
CO.summary: NPR reported on the Colorado Democratic Party's censure of Governor Polis for commuting election denier Tina Peters' prison sentence, with the party warning the action sends a dangerous message about accountability for election tampering.

CO.title: Colorado GOP governor primary pits MAGA candidates against establishment favorite
CO.summary: Colorado's three-way Republican gubernatorial primary ahead of the June 30 primary features state Rep. Scott Bottoms and businessman Victor Marx competing for MAGA voters while state Sen. Barbara Kirkmeyer draws establishment endorsements as the only non-MAGA candidate.

CT.title: Lamont signs law allowing no-excuse absentee voting in Connecticut
CT.summary: Governor Ned Lamont signed Public Act 26-42 into law, removing restrictions that previously limited absentee voting to specific circumstances such as illness or military service, making Connecticut the 37th state to allow no-excuse absentee voting effective immediately.

DC.title: DC voter guide: What to know before June primary for mayor, council, Congress
DC.summary: WTOP's voter guide to DC's June 16 primary covers the first-ever use of ranked-choice voting, the competitive seven-candidate open mayoral race, ballot drop boxes opening May 22, and the May 26 voter registration and party-change deadline.

DC.title: 2026 Election Guide: Everything DC voters need to know ahead of 2 June 16 elections
DC.summary: Comprehensive guide to DC's June 16 primary and At-Large Council special election covering ranked-choice voting mechanics, candidates in the first open mayoral race in 12 years, and key voter deadlines including the May 26 registration cutoff and mail ballot options.

DE.title: Department of Elections Announces Primary Election Party Change Deadline, Friday, May 29, 2026, 11:59 pm
DE.summary: Delaware's Department of Elections announced that voters wishing to participate in the September 15, 2026 closed primary must change their party affiliation by May 29 at 11:59 p.m., with county offices open until 6 p.m. on May 28 for in-person changes.

FL.title: NAACP calls for college sports boycott in states targeting Black voting power
FL.summary: The NAACP launched its 'Out of Bounds' campaign calling on Black student-athletes and fans to boycott public universities in Florida and other Southern states that enacted redistricting plans the group says dismantle Black voting representation following a Supreme Court ruling weakening the Voting Rights Act.

FL.title: NAACP urges public to boycott Florida, Georgia's college sports until redistricting is overturned
FL.summary: The NAACP urged fans, alumni, and prospective student-athletes to withhold support from Florida's major college sports programs, citing the state's congressional redistricting that the organization contends dilutes Black political representation and voting power.

GA.title: Several down-ballot statewide races will also go to a runoff
GA.summary: Following Georgia's May 19 primary, multiple statewide races headed to June 16 runoffs include both parties' lieutenant governor contests and the Republican secretary of state race, as no candidates secured the required majority of votes.

GA.title: NAACP urges public to boycott Florida, Georgia's college sports until redistricting is overturned
GA.summary: The NAACP is calling on fans, alumni, and recruits to withhold support from Georgia's major public university athletic programs in response to the state's congressional redistricting that the organization says reduces Black voting representation.

ID.title: About 30% of Idaho voters turned out for 2026 primary election, early data shows
ID.summary: Roughly 30.3% of Idaho's registered voters cast ballots in the May 19 primary election, surpassing most Idaho primaries since 2010. Turnout varied widely by county, from 21.8% in Teton County to nearly 51.9% in Bear Lake County.

ID.title: Independent challenger calls on Risch to do three public debates ahead of Idaho's general election
ID.summary: Independent U.S. Senate candidate Todd Achilles called on incumbent Sen. Jim Risch to participate in three statewide public debates ahead of the November general election, after Risch won the Republican primary with nearly 67% of the vote.

IL.title: Illinois county clerks are preparing for mail voting amid continued attacks, changes
IL.summary: Illinois county clerks are working to inform voters about postal rule changes, the SAVE Act, and a Supreme Court ruling on mail ballot deadlines ahead of the November general election. Despite ongoing federal challenges to mail voting, over 18% of Illinois voters cast ballots by mail in 2024, with permanent vote-by-mail rolls continuing to grow.

IN.title: Banks, Rokita drop support for Morales, urge him to suspend secretary of state campaign
IN.summary: U.S. Senator Jim Banks and Attorney General Todd Rokita withdrew their endorsements of incumbent Secretary of State Diego Morales and urged him to suspend his 2026 re-election campaign, citing 'self-inflicted wounds.' Morales, who oversees Indiana elections, refused to drop out ahead of the Republican state convention.

IA.title: Here's how we know why Iowa has competitive races in 2026
IA.summary: Despite Republicans maintaining a nearly 200,000 registered voter advantage in Iowa, both parties are investing heavily in the state's 2026 U.S. Senate, gubernatorial, and congressional races. National Republican PACs have pledged nearly $30 million to defend Ashley Hinson's open Senate seat, and Vice President Vance visited Iowa to boost Rep. Zach Nunn's re-election bid.

KS.title: Democratic gubernatorial candidate Ethan Corson joins forces with Salina business director
KS.summary: Kansas Democratic gubernatorial candidate Ethan Corson announced Renee Duxler, Salina Area Chamber of Commerce President, as his running mate for lieutenant governor, setting the Democratic ticket ahead of the August 4, 2026 primary.

KS.title: SCHMIDT PICKS RUNNING MATE
KS.summary: Kansas Republican gubernatorial candidate and Insurance Commissioner Vicki Schmidt announced Kansas Farm Bureau President Joe Newland as her lieutenant governor running mate ahead of the August 4 primary.

KS.title: What Kansas governor candidates have named their running mates in leadup to the 2026 midterms?
KS.summary: Multiple Kansas gubernatorial candidates announced running mates ahead of the August 4 primary with the June 1 filing deadline approaching, including Republicans Schmidt and Stacy Rogers and Democrat Corson each naming lieutenant governor choices.

LA.title: By the numbers: Analyzing Letlow's first-place Senate primary finish
LA.summary: Data analysis of Rep. Julia Letlow's 45% first-place finish in Louisiana's May 16 Senate primary, setting up a June 27 runoff against state Treasurer John Fleming after incumbent Sen. Bill Cassidy was eliminated with about 25% of the vote.

LA.title: Louisiana could close primary elections to no-party voters. Here's what might change.
LA.summary: Louisiana is considering legislation that would allow the Democratic and Republican parties to exclude unaffiliated 'no-party' voters from primary contests for congressional and other races, a major change to the state's semi-closed primary system that critics say could disenfranchise voters.

LA.title: Louisiana Democrats, GOP might get to exclude 'no-party' voters from their primary elections
LA.summary: Louisiana's House Bill 906 passed a Senate committee 4-3, putting the state one vote away from allowing parties to exclude unaffiliated voters from primary elections starting in 2027, after the House already approved it 67-19.

ME.title: Longshot Senate hopeful tells Maine Democrats Graham Platner isn't their only option
ME.summary: Brunswick Democrat David Costello continues his longshot U.S. Senate primary campaign ahead of the June 9 election, arguing voters should consider him as an alternative to frontrunner Graham Platner, who is heavily favored after Gov. Janet Mills suspended her campaign.

ME.title: Election Preview
ME.summary: Maine Public Radio political reporters preview the June 9 primary races for governor, U.S. Senate and Congress, discussing candidates, ranked-choice voting procedures, and key voting deadlines including the May 26 party enrollment change cutoff.

MD.title: Trio of GOP candidates for governor — out of nine total — meet in debate
MD.summary: Three of nine Republican gubernatorial candidates — Shannon Wright, John Myrick and Douglas Larcomb — participated in a Maryland Public Television debate ahead of the June 23 primary, while frontrunners Dan Cox and Ed Hale skipped the event, leaving the field largely unrepresented.

MA.title: Markey, Moulton agree to August debate in US Senate primary fight
MA.summary: Sen. Ed Markey and Rep. Seth Moulton have agreed to a primary debate on August 20, co-hosted by the Boston Globe, WCVB, and WBUR, marking a formal milestone in the increasingly competitive Massachusetts Democratic Senate primary ahead of the September 1 primary election.

MA.title: Markey v. Moulton: Senate race may be 'closer than people think'
MA.summary: A recent Emerson College poll shows incumbent Sen. Ed Markey leading challenger Rep. Seth Moulton by just five percentage points in the Massachusetts Democratic Senate primary, with political observers saying the race is more competitive than most anticipated.

MI.title: Former Detroit Mayor Mike Duggan ends independent bid for Michigan governor
MI.summary: Former Detroit Mayor Mike Duggan withdrew from the Michigan governor's race on May 21, citing national headwinds favoring Democrats and his inability to close the gap in polls and fundraising, reshaping the election contest ahead of the August primary.

MI.title: Mike Duggan drops governor bid in Michigan election shocker
MI.summary: Bridge Michigan reports on Duggan's abrupt exit from the Michigan governor's race, noting his departure is expected to consolidate the major-party contest between Democratic Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson and Republican John James.

MN.title: Democratic group launches ICE attack against Rep. Angie Craig in Minnesota Senate primary
MN.summary: The Democratic Lieutenant Governors Association launched a $2 million ad campaign attacking Rep. Angie Craig for her immigration enforcement votes, backing Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan in the open Minnesota Senate primary seat ahead of the DFL State Convention May 29-31.

MO.title: Gov. Mike Kehoe's decision on ballot timing could shape Missouri's 2026 elections
MO.summary: Gov. Mike Kehoe faces a deadline to decide which constitutional amendments will appear on Missouri's August 4 primary ballot versus the November general election, a strategically significant choice affecting voter turnout on measures covering abortion, taxes, and other issues.

MO.title: Missouri voters could face as many as nine ballot measures in 2026
MO.summary: Missouri could see up to nine statewide ballot measures in 2026 — the most since 2014 — including proposals on abortion rights, income tax replacement, initiative petition protections, state parks funding, and congressional redistricting.

MO.title: Missouri voters could face as many as nine ballot measures in 2026
MO.summary: Missouri voters may face up to nine statewide ballot measures in August and November 2026, as Gov. Kehoe decides which measures to place on the lower-turnout August primary ballot.

MT.title: Three things to know ahead of the 2026 Montana primaries
MT.summary: Montana Public Radio outlines key facts for voters heading into the June 2 primary, including the court-blocked Election Day voter registration changes and the impact of absentee ballots already mailed.

MT.title: Montana election officials working to get word out about updates to same-day registration
MT.summary: Following a court injunction blocking Senate Bill 490, Montana county election officials are conducting outreach to inform voters that same-day voter registration remains available through the June 2 primary, reversing guidance that had been prepared under the now-blocked law.

NE.title: How did Denise Powell beat an Omaha dynasty in NE-02?
NE.summary: An analysis of the Democratic primary for Nebraska's 2nd Congressional District, where political outsider Denise Powell defeated longtime Omaha political figures, with implications for the general election race in one of the nation's most competitive House districts.

NV.title: 2026 Primary Election Guide: What you need to know
NV.summary: A comprehensive guide to Nevada's June 9 primary election covering registration deadlines, how to vote by mail, early voting dates starting May 23, and key races on the ballot for governor, Congress, and state legislature.

NV.title: 2026 Primary Election Guide: Voting sites
NV.summary: Lists early voting and Election Day polling locations across Nevada for the June 9 primary, including Clark County Government Center and other sites, with schedules to help voters plan their participation.

NJ.title: Attorney General Davenport Announces Safeguards to Protect the Right to Vote During the 2026 Primary Election
NJ.source: New Jersey Office of Attorney General
NJ.summary: New Jersey Attorney General Jennifer Davenport announced a Voter Protection Initiative for the June 2 primary, including measures to address voting rights and civil rights issues during early voting (starting May 26) and on Election Day, along with an expanded polling site protective zone.

NJ.title: Union County Board of Elections Reminds You to Plan Your Vote for the June 2 Primary Election
NJ.summary: Union County's Board of Elections issued a reminder to voters about key deadlines and options for the June 2 primary, including early voting from May 26-31 and mail-in ballot request deadlines.

NM.title: New 'dark money' group backs array of New Mexico House Democratic candidates
NM.summary: A new 501(c)4 nonprofit called New Chapter, New Mexico is spending roughly $85,000 on ads backing and opposing Democratic candidates in 10 state House races ahead of the June 2 primary, without disclosing its donors or leadership.

NM.title: NM House candidate faces state ethics complaint over coordinating with dark money group
NM.summary: House District 30 candidate Veronica Mireles faces an ethics complaint accusing her of illegally coordinating with New Chapter, New Mexico, a newly formed dark money group backing multiple candidates in the June 2 primary without disclosing its funders.

NM.title: Bernalillo County DA Bregman says he's running for NM governor because he's 'tired of mediocrity'
NM.summary: Democratic gubernatorial candidate Sam Bregman addressed a town hall outlining his priorities of education, healthcare, and public safety for the June 2 primary race against former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland.

NY.title: Full Debate: Three Democratic candidates for New York state comptroller face off in debate
NY.summary: Incumbent Thomas DiNapoli faced primary challengers Raj Goyle and Drew Warshaw in a 60-minute debate on Spectrum News, covering the state pension fund, economic development, and Albany reform ahead of the June 23 Democratic primary.

NY.title: DiNapoli touts record while opponents crave change in N.Y. comptroller debate
NY.summary: Post-debate coverage found DiNapoli defending his nearly two-decade record as state comptroller while challengers Drew Warshaw and Raj Goyle pressed for change, with the Democratic primary set for June 23.

NC.title: NC voters set to weigh in on limiting state income tax and property taxes in November
NC.summary: The North Carolina House approved two constitutional amendments on May 20 that would cap the state income tax rate at 3.5% and limit property tax increases, sending both measures to voters in the November 2026 general election.

NC.title: NC Senate moves constitutional amendment on local property tax increases to the November ballot
NC.summary: North Carolina's Senate advanced a constitutional amendment to the November ballot that would require the legislature to limit how much local governments can raise property taxes, passing along party lines 31-15.

NC.title: North Carolinians to vote on income, property tax limits after lawmakers OK ballot questions
NC.summary: After both chambers passed the measures on May 20, North Carolina voters will decide in November whether the state constitution should cap the income tax at 3.5% and limit local property tax rate increases, with votes split along party lines.

NC.title: North Carolina voters to decide on two measures related to property and income tax limits on the November 2026 ballot
NC.summary: Ballotpedia details the two North Carolina constitutional amendments approved May 20 — capping income tax at 3.5% and limiting property tax increases — that will appear on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot.

ND.title: Dems, secretary of state disagree on process to replace candidate after lawmaker's death
ND.summary: North Dakota Democrats and Secretary of State Michael Howe are in dispute over how to replace Rep. Liz Conmy, who died in an April plane crash, on the District 11 ballot ahead of the June 9 primary, with the party seeking to invoke a 2020 precedent.

ND.title: District 11 Democrats to choose new nominee after Conmy death
ND.summary: The Democratic-NPL Party in North Dakota's House District 11 held a listening session on May 20 and is moving to choose a replacement nominee for Rep. Liz Conmy's seat ahead of the June 9 primary, with a replacement expected to be named by May 22.

ND.title: North Dakota Democrats plan write-in candidate to replace Conmy
ND.summary: Facing a dispute with the secretary of state over ballot replacement rules, North Dakota Democrats announced plans to run a write-in candidate in the June 9 primary for the seat left vacant by the death of Rep. Liz Conmy.

OH.title: An amendment on photo ID is likely to make the ballot with Ohio GOP leaders behind it
OH.summary: Ohio House and Senate Republican leaders are backing joint resolutions to put a constitutional amendment requiring voter photo ID on the November 2026 ballot, needing a three-fifths vote in both chambers by August 5.

OH.title: Ohio Republicans trying to get voter photo ID on the ballot, enshrined in state constitution
OH.summary: Ohio Republican lawmakers introduced House Joint Resolution 9 and Senate Joint Resolution 10 to codify existing voter photo ID requirements into the state constitution, requiring 60 House and 20 Senate votes by August 5 to place the measure before November voters.

OK.title: Deadline approaches for Oklahoma voter registration ahead of primary election
OK.summary: May 22 is the final deadline for Oklahomans to register to vote ahead of the June 16 primary election, with registration available online, by mail, or in person at county election boards.

OK.title: Key dates approaching for Oklahoma primary elections
OK.summary: With the June 16 Oklahoma primary approaching, the article outlines key deadlines including the May 22 voter registration cutoff, the June 1 absentee ballot request deadline, and early voting dates of June 11-13.

OK.title: Oklahoma Voice launches voter guide ahead of June 16 primary election
OK.summary: Oklahoma Voice released a voter guide covering candidates on the June 16 primary ballot, including a nonpartisan state question that would gradually raise Oklahoma's minimum wage to $15 an hour by 2029.

OR.title: Changed political environment will shake up Kotek-Drazan rematch
OR.summary: Following their primary wins, incumbent Gov. Tina Kotek and Republican Christine Drazan are set for a November rematch, with analysts noting the political environment has shifted since their narrow 2022 race.

PA.title: PA election 2026: Primary winners, losers; full results
PA.summary: A comprehensive recap of Pennsylvania's May 19 primary showing Democratic wins in key congressional swing districts, including Bob Harvie in the 1st District and Chris Rabb in the 3rd District in Philadelphia.

PA.title: PA primary election results: Who won US House races?
PA.summary: Spotlight PA reports on Democratic nominees winning in four swing congressional districts as Pennsylvania shapes up as a key battleground in November's fight for control of the U.S. House.

PA.title: Primary results spell the end for four PA House incumbents
PA.summary: Four Pennsylvania state House incumbents lost their primary races, with results indicating significant shifts in the composition of the state legislature ahead of November's general election.

RI.title: McKee facing uphill battle in WPRI poll. Block may have a chance. AG race is wide open.
RI.summary: A new WPRI/Emerson College poll shows Helena Foulkes leading Gov. Dan McKee by 20 points in the Democratic gubernatorial primary, with McKee holding a net favorability of -39 among all likely voters.

RI.title: 12 News/Emerson Poll: Foulkes leads McKee by double-digits in RI gov primary
RI.summary: The WPRI/Emerson College poll of 565 likely Democratic primary voters found Foulkes at 40% to McKee's 20%, with 37% undecided ahead of Rhode Island's September 9 Democratic gubernatorial primary.

RI.title: McKee shrugs off 12 News/Emerson poll showing big lead for Foulkes
RI.summary: Gov. Dan McKee dismissed the polling showing a 20-point deficit to challenger Helena Foulkes in the Democratic primary, while Foulkes brushed off McKee's criticism of her business record at CVS Health.

SC.title: SC Senate begins redistricting debate and adjourns early evening, as Dems, ACLU push back
SC.summary: The South Carolina Senate opened floor debate on a redistricting bill that would redraw congressional maps to eliminate the state's only majority-Black district held by Rep. Jim Clyburn, then adjourned without taking action as Democrats and the ACLU pushed back.

SC.title: Bill redrawing SC congressional voting lines advances in Senate as cost estimates double
SC.summary: The South Carolina Senate Judiciary Committee advanced the redistricting bill 15-7, with cost estimates for delaying the primary to August now doubled, and early voting set to begin May 26 adding urgency to the timeline.

SC.title: SC Senate opens heated debate on redistricting plan as questions mount over map's origins
SC.summary: South Carolina senators questioned Senate Judiciary Chairman Luke Rankin about the origins of the redistricting map, which was crafted by the National Republican Redistricting Trust, as floor debate opened on the plan to reshape the state's seven congressional districts.

SC.title: South Carolina redistricting: Lawmakers take next step to pass gerrymandered map as election looms
SC.summary: The South Carolina Senate Judiciary Committee advanced a new congressional map that would dismantle the state's lone majority-Black district held by Rep. Jim Clyburn, with the full Senate set to vote as early voting approaches on May 26.

SD.title: Advance voting for South Dakota primary election picks up after delayed start
SD.summary: Advance voting for South Dakota's June 2 primary is on track to match or surpass 2024 levels despite a weeklong delay caused by a short window between candidate petition filing deadlines and the start of advance voting.

TN.title: Three-judge panel to rule on NAACP challenge of redrawn Tennessee district map
TN.summary: A three-judge state court panel heard oral arguments on May 21 over whether Tennessee's legislature exceeded its authority when it redrew congressional districts during a special session, with the NAACP arguing the new map violates the state constitution and dilutes Black voting power in Memphis.

TX.title: Cornyn, Paxton make dueling campaign stops in Houston area during GOP primary runoff for Senate
TX.summary: Sen. John Cornyn and Attorney General Ken Paxton made final Houston-area campaign appearances during the last days of early voting, with Paxton leveraging his Trump endorsement and Cornyn arguing he is the best Republican to beat Democratic nominee James Talarico in November.

UT.title: Did Democrats win a congressional seat in Utah ahead of midterms?
UT.summary: A court-ordered congressional map giving Democrats a safe Salt Lake City-based seat has put Utah at the center of the national redistricting battle, with Democrats projecting a net gain of six seats nationally as Utah's June 23 primary approaches.

VT.title: Vermont voters to decide on equality amendment
VT.summary: Vermont's proposed Proposal 4 equal protection constitutional amendment, which passed both legislative chambers with strong bipartisan support, is headed to voters on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot.

VT.title: Vermonters to Vote on Equal Protection Amendment to State Constitution
VT.summary: Vermont's Proposal 4, a constitutional amendment ensuring equal protection under the law regardless of race, sex, religion, disability, and other characteristics, has received final legislative approval and will appear on Vermont's November 2026 ballot.

WA.title: US Supreme Court may look at WA redistricting case
WA.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court could weigh in on Washington's Yakima Valley legislative redistricting case following the court's ruling weakening the Voting Rights Act; Secretary of State Hobbs warned overturning district lines before the August 4 primary would be a 'recipe for chaos.'

WI.title: 2020 election misinformation continues to ripple through Wisconsin politics
WI.summary: Wisconsin officials and politicians reacted to the FBI probe into the 2020 presidential election, with Democrats warning the investigation could intimidate election administrators ahead of the 2026 midterms and Republicans supporting the federal inquiry.

WV.title: 'I'm the head,' Morrisey insists to disjointed West Virginia GOP
WV.summary: Governor Morrisey asserted control of the West Virginia Republican Party amid intraparty divisions following the May 12 primary where his backed candidates unseated multiple GOP incumbents, with both parties now focused on the November general election.

WV.title: Two Primary Races Go To Recount
WV.summary: Two West Virginia House of Delegates races from the May 12 primary will proceed to official recounts after canvassing confirmed margins as slim as six votes, potentially affecting who appears on the November general election ballot.

AL.title: As litigation continues, 21 candidates qualify for August Alabama congressional primaries
AL.summary: Twenty-one candidates — 14 Republicans and 7 Democrats — qualified by the May 22 deadline to run in special August 11 primary elections for Alabama's 1st, 2nd, 6th, and 7th congressional districts, which were reshuffled after the Supreme Court allowed the state to revert to its 2023 redistricting map that eliminates a second majority-Black district.

AK.title: Curveball vote could snarl effort to reimpose campaign finance restrictions in Alaska
AK.summary: The Alaska Legislature passed HB 16 to impose new campaign contribution limits, but a failed effective-date clause vote means the law could take effect mid-election season rather than January 1; if Gov. Dunleavy vetoes the bill, a similar measure goes to voters on the August primary ballot.

AZ.title: Supreme Court faces new criticism for redistricting decisions so close to the 2026 elections
AZ.summary: Legal scholars and voting rights advocates are criticizing the Supreme Court for issuing redistricting rulings — including the Alabama map decision — so close to the 2026 elections, with Arizona among states where the weakened Voting Rights Act may spur new legal challenges to existing legislative district maps.

AR.title: Twenty-one states set at least one requirement on ballot initiative petition circulators
AR.summary: A new Ballotpedia analysis highlights that Arkansas is among 21 states with requirements on ballot initiative petition circulators, relevant context as Arkansas voting-rights groups contest 2025 laws that critics say make it far harder to gather signatures for citizen-initiated measures.

AR.title: What to expect in Arkansas primary runoff elections
AR.summary: Arkansas held its May 19 primary elections, sending multiple down-ballot races including the Secretary of State Republican primary to a runoff; Tom Cotton won the Senate primary outright and Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders ran unopposed.

CA.title: My Ballot Never Showed Up. How Can I Still Vote in the 2026 California Primary?
CA.summary: With California's June 2 primary approaching and vote centers now open for early in-person voting as of May 23, KQED explains options for voters whose mail ballots did not arrive, including same-day registration and provisional balloting at county election offices.

CT.title: Connecticut Moves to Strengthen Voter Privacy in Sweeping Election Bill
CT.summary: Connecticut's new election law prohibits using voter registration data for commercial purposes, exempts cast ballots from public-records disclosure while keeping vote totals and audits public, and restricts the full birth date visible in voter files — provisions intended to protect voter information from misuse.

FL.title: Florida moving toward stricter voting requirements: What you need to know
FL.summary: Florida's SAVE Act — signed April 1 and already facing multiple federal lawsuits — will require proof of citizenship for new and updated voter registrations and restrict acceptable voter ID forms, though key provisions are delayed until January 1, 2027, after this year's elections.

FL.title: State Voting Laws Roundup: May 2026
FL.summary: The Brennan Center's May 2026 roundup notes Florida among states that enacted restrictive voting laws this cycle, with Florida, Kentucky, and Mississippi requiring citizenship documents from some voters; at least 9 states enacted 12 restrictive laws between January and May 1, 2026.

GA.title: These statewide candidates are headed to June runoffs
GA.summary: After no candidate cleared 50% in Georgia's May 19 primary, multiple statewide races — including both Republican and Democratic Secretary of State primaries — head to June 16 runoffs; the Secretary of State race is closely watched because the winner will oversee voter registration and election certification in a key battleground state.

MD.title: Maryland Rushes to Reprint, Resend 500,000 Mail Ballots
MD.summary: Maryland election officials moved to reprint and resend over 500,000 mail-in primary ballots after a vendor printing error caused some voters to receive the wrong party's ballot ahead of the June 23 gubernatorial primary; replacement ballots were to be mailed by May 29 with safeguards in place to prevent double-counting.

MN.title: Following conclusion of legislative session, MN eyes consequential November elections
MN.summary: With Minnesota's 2026 legislative session concluded, attention turns to November when every House and Senate seat is on the ballot; the DFL holds the Senate by one vote and the House is tied 67-67, making election outcomes critical to state policy direction.

MO.title: Missouri governor moves votes on taxes, constitutional amendments to August primary
MO.summary: Gov. Mike Kehoe placed four constitutional amendments on the August 4 primary ballot, including Amendment 4 which would require citizen-initiated constitutional amendments to win a majority in every congressional district rather than just statewide, significantly raising the bar for voter-driven ballot initiatives.

NH.title: What to watch for on 'committee of conference' week
NH.summary: New Hampshire's legislature enters its final conference committee week, with HB 1541 — requiring the secretary of state to supply all voting precincts with secure ballot storage containers — among the election-related bills still under negotiation.

NM.title: New Mexico Election 2026: trail notes
NM.summary: Campaign trail roundup covering the June 2 primary, including a legal dispute over a Republican gubernatorial candidate's unauthorized use of Trump's image and campaign materials. New Mexico is in the early-voting window for its first-ever semi-open primary, which allows unaffiliated voters to participate without changing their registration.

NV.title: Early voting begins May 23 for Nevada's primary
NV.summary: Early in-person voting for Nevada's June 9 primary election opens May 23 through June 5; Nevada automatically mails ballots to all active registered voters, and the closed primary allows only registered party members to vote in party contests.

NV.title: Early voting begins Saturday for Nevada's primary election in Washoe County
NV.summary: Washoe County early voting locations open May 23 for the June 9 Nevada primary, with mail ballots already distributed to active registered voters across the state.

NY.title: Senate Advances Reforms to Protect Election Integrity and Support Election Workers
NY.summary: The New York State Senate advanced a package of election-integrity bills including the New York Election Officer Protection Act (S.8646), which prohibits intimidation of election workers, and measures expanding portable early-voting locations and mandating uniform training for Board of Elections commissioners ahead of the June 23 primary.

OH.title: How changes to Ohio's voting laws affected the May 2026 election
OH.summary: Ohio's May 5 primary was the first election under a new law eliminating the four-day mail-ballot grace period, requiring ballots to be received by Election Day; officials reported about 10% of requested ballots did not return, within the historical range, though it is too early to assess the full impact on voter participation.

OK.title: Voter registration deadline is May 22
OK.summary: May 22 was the final day for Oklahomans to register to vote ahead of the June 16 closed primary, which will include races for governor, U.S. Senate, and State Question 832 — an initiative that would gradually raise the state minimum wage from $7.25 to $15 by 2029.

PA.title: PA's 2026 primary election goes well despite a few incidents
PA.summary: Pennsylvania's May 19 primary went smoothly statewide with no major machine malfunctions, though isolated incidents included an explosive device detonated near a Lehigh County polling place and more than 200 independent voters in York County who did not receive mail ballots for a special state House election.

PA.title: PA primary election results: Gaming-targeted senators win
PA.summary: Three Republican state senators targeted by more than $8 million in skill-games industry spending survived their primary challenges in Pennsylvania; progressive Chris Rabb won the Democratic nomination in the 3rd Congressional District in a rebuke of the Philadelphia Democratic establishment.

SC.title: Divisions in SC Senate derail push to speed redistricting vote
SC.summary: Republican senators in South Carolina's special session failed to invoke cloture to fast-track a congressional redistricting bill, meaning it is unlikely to reach the governor before early voting begins May 26 — with over 2,500 absentee ballots already cast and Election Commission officials warning a primary delay could cost more than $5 million.

SC.title: South Carolina governor calls for a special session on redistricting
SC.summary: Gov. Henry McMaster called a special legislative session to redraw congressional maps after the Senate failed to reach the two-thirds vote needed to extend its regular session; the proposed map would eliminate South Carolina's only majority-minority congressional district, held by Rep. James Clyburn.

SC.title: South Carolina redistricting debate continues into weekend
SC.summary: The South Carolina redistricting debate stretched into the Memorial Day weekend with the Senate still unable to advance a map that would delay U.S. House primaries from June 9 to August 18 while establishing new district lines favored by Trump allies.

SD.title: Advance voting for South Dakota primary election picks up after delayed start
SD.summary: Advance voting for South Dakota's June 2 primary is outpacing 2024 totals in some counties despite a weeklong delay caused by a calendar quirk that compressed the window between candidate filing deadlines and the start of absentee voting. Lincoln County has already surpassed its entire 2024 pre-primary absentee ballot total.

TX.title: Early voting to end on Friday for Texas primary runoff election
TX.summary: Early voting for Texas's May 26 primary runoff election concludes Friday, May 22, with 38 races on the ballot statewide. The contest features the high-profile Republican U.S. Senate runoff between incumbent John Cornyn and Attorney General Ken Paxton, who received a Trump endorsement one week before Election Day.

UT.title: Utah's new voter registration records privacy law will affect 1.3 million voters — Here's what you need to know
UT.summary: Utah's Senate Bill 153 takes effect May 25, making voter registration information for approximately 1.3 million previously private-status voters publicly available. The law ends Utah's unique opt-out voter privacy system; only voters qualifying as at-risk under specific criteria can keep their data protected.

WA.title: Bill strengthening protections on Washington's voter database takes effect
WA.summary: Washington's Senate Bill 5892 takes effect, making it a class C felony for election officers to disclose voters' private identifying information such as Social Security numbers or driver's license numbers, and designating the Secretary of State as the sole agency authorized to respond to voter database requests from federal agencies.

WY.title: Filing deadline looms as Natrona County's 2026 races take shape
WY.summary: With Wyoming's candidate filing deadline approaching May 29, major statewide races including governor, U.S. Senate, and secretary of state are taking shape under sweeping new election rules including closed-primary party affiliation requirements, compressed absentee ballot windows, and new residency verification mandates.

WY.title: Filing deadline looms as Laramie County's 2026 races take shape
WY.summary: Laramie County's candidate field for 2026 is crystallizing ahead of Wyoming's May 29 filing deadline, with significant open-seat races for governor and other statewide offices operating under Wyoming's new closed-primary system that eliminated crossover voting.

LA.title: Louisiana congressional map bill advances to House
LA.summary: After a House committee approved an amended version of Senate Bill 121 on a party-line 10-7 vote, Louisiana's controversial congressional redistricting bill advanced to the full House floor. The map, which would give Republicans a 5-1 advantage in congressional districts by eliminating one majority-Black district, must be approved by June 1 under a court-ordered deadline following the Supreme Court's ruling that the state's previous map was an unconstitutional racial gerrymander.

LA.title: Committee forwards congressional redistricting map to full House
LA.summary: Louisiana's House and Governmental Affairs Committee forwarded the congressional redistricting map to the full House for a final vote, after hours of public testimony opposing the plan to eliminate a majority-Black congressional district. Governor Landry previously signed a separate bill shifting the postponed U.S. House primaries to November 3 after the Supreme Court struck down the existing map.

MD.title: DOJ civil rights chief requests Maryland retain records regarding mail-in ballot error
MD.summary: The Justice Department's civil rights chief Harmeet Dhillon formally notified Maryland election officials to preserve all records related to the erroneous distribution of approximately 500,000 mail-in primary ballots that were sent to some voters for the wrong party. Maryland's top election official maintained that no fake or illegal ballots were distributed and that safeguards prevent duplicate voting, as the state rushes to resend replacement ballots ahead of the June 23 primary.

MS.title: 'We're ready to fight': Thousands protest Mississippi redistricting and rally for voting rights
MS.summary: Thousands gathered in Jackson on May 20 to protest redistricting efforts that would reduce Black voting representation, following the U.S. Supreme Court's Callais ruling weakening the federal Voting Rights Act. Rep. Bennie Thompson and NAACP CEO Derrick Johnson urged voters to mobilize ahead of November midterms.

MS.title: Mississippi Day of Action focuses on redistricting and voting rights
MS.summary: Mississippi's Day of Action event mobilized voters against redistricting proposals that advocates say would reduce Black representation in Congress and the state legislature following the Supreme Court's Callais decision weakening federal Voting Rights Act protections.

MS.title: NAACP, SPLC, Mississippi Democrats march, rally to protest Callais, redistricting
MS.summary: The NAACP, SPLC, and Mississippi Democrats organized a march and rally in Jackson protesting the Supreme Court's Callais redistricting ruling and looming Republican efforts to redraw Mississippi's congressional districts in ways that could eliminate Rep. Bennie Thompson's majority-Black district.

MT.title: Montana voter registration ruling deemed 'big win' for youth vote
MT.summary: Youth voter advocates celebrated the Montana district court ruling blocking Senate Bill 490, which would have cut off Election Day voter registration at noon. Voters can now register through polls closing at 8 p.m. for the June 2 primary, with advocates noting same-day registration is especially important for young and mobile voters.

NJ.title: New Jersey Senate Panel Approves State Voting Rights Bill
NJ.summary: The New Jersey Senate Judiciary Committee approved the John R. Lewis Voter Empowerment Act in a party-line vote, advancing a state-level voting rights bill that would require state attorney general pre-clearance for election rule changes in jurisdictions with a history of discrimination and expand language access for voters.

NV.title: Early voting kicks off for Nevada's June primary
NV.summary: Early in-person voting began May 23 across Nevada ahead of the June 9 primary election, running through June 5. Nevada is a universal vote-by-mail state, and about 130 early voting sites are available statewide, with the registration deadline set for May 27.

NV.title: Nevada primary election shifts into high gear as early voting begins
NV.summary: Early voting opened statewide in Nevada on May 23 for the June 9 closed primary election, setting the stage for competitive governor and congressional races. Nevada's Secretary of State Francisco Aguilar launched voter outreach resources including interactive polling maps and text message notifications.

SC.title: SC Senate advances redistricting map, sets final vote for Tuesday
SC.summary: The South Carolina Senate passed a congressional redistricting map on second reading on May 23, setting a final vote for May 26 — the first day of early voting — on a plan that would eliminate Rep. James Clyburn's majority-Black district and give Republicans all seven U.S. House seats.

SC.title: S.C. redistricting map passes second reading, final vote set for Tuesday
SC.summary: South Carolina senators on May 23 advanced a redrawn congressional map that would delay U.S. House primaries to August 18, with lawmakers and voting officials warning the plan could expose the state to a multimillion-dollar lawsuit if signed into law after early voting begins.

TN.title: First challenge to Tennessee's congressional map heard in court
TN.summary: A three-judge Tennessee state panel heard opening arguments in the NAACP's challenge to the redrawn congressional map that split Memphis and Shelby County into three districts, eliminating the state's only majority-Black district. Judges did not immediately rule.

TX.title: Inside the closing week of the Texas GOP Senate runoff
TX.summary: As the May 26 Republican Senate runoff approaches, the race between incumbent Sen. John Cornyn and AG Ken Paxton tightened after Trump's endorsement of Paxton; the winner will be the GOP nominee for the November general election.

VA.title: Lessons from Virginia's redistricting wars: Supreme Court nullification and options for November
VA.summary: After the US Supreme Court rejected Virginia Democrats' emergency appeal on May 15, Democrats regrouped to assess congressional options for November with the existing 6-5 district split remaining in place; several Democrats who had launched campaigns in hypothetical new districts ended their bids.

WI.title: Court dismisses Trump administration lawsuit for Wisconsin voter roll
WI.summary: A federal judge dismissed the DOJ's lawsuit seeking Wisconsin's detailed voter registration data, ruling that state voter rolls are not records subject to the Civil Rights Act of 1960, marking another legal defeat for the Trump administration's voter data collection effort.

WI.title: Judges in Maine and Wisconsin Dismiss Justice Department's Attempts to Force Turnover of Voter Rolls
WI.summary: Federal judges in Wisconsin and Maine dismissed DOJ suits that sought to compel states to hand over voter data including dates of birth and partial Social Security numbers, continuing a pattern of court defeats for the Trump administration's voter data collection effort across more than 30 states.

WI.title: Wisconsin Elections Commission sued over Madison ballot error
WI.summary: After a court ordered 23 late-arriving absentee ballots counted in April's Wisconsin Supreme Court election, a new lawsuit challenged the Elections Commission's initial directive to reject those ballots, prompting Madison to adopt new absentee ballot courier protocols ahead of November.

DC.title: DC voter guide: What to know before June primary for mayor, council, Congress
DC.summary: WTOP published a comprehensive voter guide for D.C.'s June 16 primary, covering the mayoral race, council seats, and congressional races using ranked-choice voting for the first time. Ballot drop boxes opened May 22, the voter registration deadline is May 26, and early voting runs June 8–14.

DE.title: Independent Party Endorses Katz, Urges Supporters to Act Before May 29 Deadline
DE.summary: Delaware's Independent Party endorsed Republican U.S. Senate candidate Dr. Mike Katz and urged supporters to change their party registration to Republican by the May 29 closed-primary deadline in order to vote for him in the September 15 primary.

HI.title: Hawaii law aims to curb corporate influence in elections but faces hurdles
HI.summary: Hawaii's new first-of-its-kind law restricting corporate political spending faces questions about whether out-of-state corporations could fill the void left by in-state entities. Legal experts anticipate court challenges before the law's July 2027 effective date.

ID.title: Coin toss will decide Jerome County election race that ended in tie
ID.summary: A Jerome County, Idaho race from the May 19 primary ended in a tied vote between two candidates, with the winner to be decided by a coin flip scheduled for May 29 after official canvass results are certified. Under Idaho law, a coin toss resolves tied primary races.

KY.title: Voter turnout varied widely across Kentucky in May 19 primary
KY.summary: Participation in Kentucky's May 19 primary ranged dramatically by county, with Owsley County recording the highest turnout at 51.9% and several larger-population counties among the lowest.
