Statewide, about 863,999 votes were cast, representing an 18.9% increase over the 2022 midterm primary.

MD.title: Trump calls for DOJ investigation after mail ballot error in Maryland
MD.summary: President Trump called for a Justice Department investigation into a vendor coding error that sent approximately 500,000 Maryland voters primary ballots for the wrong party. State election officials said no illegal ballots were distributed and that replacement ballots would be mailed to all affected voters by May 29.

NJ.title: New Jersey primary election 2026: What to know before you vote
NJ.summary: New Jersey's June 2 primary is approaching, with early voting opening May 26 through May 31 and mail ballot applications due by May 25. The primary features competitive U.S. House races including a special congressional election in the 11th District.

PA.title: Pa. election 2026: Primary winners, losers; full results
PA.summary: Pennsylvania's May 19 primary produced key results including progressive Chris Rabb winning the Democratic nomination in Philadelphia's 3rd District, and two sitting state House incumbents defeated. Gov. Josh Shapiro and Republican Stacy Garrity each won uncontested primaries for the fall governor's race.

SC.title: Early voting for South Carolina's primary opens May 26. Here's when and where to vote early
SC.summary: Early voting for South Carolina's June 9 primary opened May 26 at county election offices statewide, running through June 5. Congressional primaries may be delayed to August if a pending redistricting bill passes, meaning June votes for U.S. House candidates would not count.

TX.title: Cornyn not ready to give up his Texas Senate seat in GOP runoff against Paxton: 'I refuse to lose and I'm going to fight to win this'
TX.summary: Senator John Cornyn made a final campaign push ahead of the May 26 Republican Senate runoff against Attorney General Ken Paxton, who holds a narrow polling lead with Trump's endorsement. Cornyn stated he refuses to concede, calling the race a test of character.

WY.title: 100+ candidates file early as Wyoming election season starts; deadline May 29
WY.summary: More than 100 candidates filed for Wyoming state and federal offices within the first two days of the 2026 candidate filing period, with open seats including governor, secretary of state, and two congressional seats. Candidates must file by May 29 to appear on the August 18 primary ballot.

CA.title: California almost killed the Board of Equalization. Now lawmakers want seats on it
CA.summary: With several competitive races for seats on California's Board of Equalization on the June 2026 primary ballot, CalMatters reports on the board's history and the contested election dynamics, including candidates backed by incumbents seeking to consolidate control of the five-member panel that oversees tax appeals.

CA.title: California Voter Guide 2026
CA.summary: CalMatters published an updated undecided voter guide for California's June 2026 primary covering statewide races, ballot measures, and key contested contests ahead of the election.

GA.title: Twelve Georgia legislative races advance to runoffs
GA.summary: Following Georgia's May 19 primary, twelve state legislative races failed to reach the 50% majority needed to avoid a runoff, sending five state Senate seats and seven House district races to the June 16 runoff election. Voters who participated in the May primary must stick with that party's ballot for the runoff.

GA.title: Everything to know about Georgia's June runoff election
GA.summary: A comprehensive voter guide to Georgia's June 16, 2026 primary runoff covering major statewide races including governor and U.S. Senate, early voting dates beginning June 8, absentee ballot request deadlines, and rules on which party's runoff ballot voters may choose.

IA.title: GOP gubernatorial candidate Adam Steen addresses death threat against campaign
IA.summary: Republican gubernatorial candidate Adam Steen spoke at a campaign event in Ames about a death threat received prior to a campaign stop in Oskaloosa, as he continues campaigning ahead of Iowa's June 2 primary election. Steen is one of five Republican candidates vying for the party's gubernatorial nomination.

IA.title: Sen. Zach Wahls, Rep. Josh Turek call for voters' support ahead of primary
IA.summary: Democratic U.S. Senate candidates Zach Wahls and Josh Turek made their cases to voters at the Des Moines Farmer's Market in the final days before Iowa's June 2 primary, with both seeking to become the Democratic nominee for the open Senate seat previously held by Joni Ernst.

IN.title: RACE FOR NOMINATION: Indiana Republicans split over SOS candidates
IN.summary: Top Indiana Republicans are divided over the race for secretary of state, with four candidates vying for the nomination at the June 19-20 GOP convention in Fort Wayne: incumbent Diego Morales, U.S. Sen. Jim Banks' regional director Max Engling, businesswoman Jamie Reitenour, and Knox County clerk David Shelton.

KS.title: Kansas City's August election will have 5 bond and tax measures
KS.summary: Kansas City voters will face five ballot questions in the August 4, 2026 election, including four bond measures totaling $1.7 billion for water infrastructure, affordable housing, and civic facilities, plus a sales tax renewal funding economic development.

KY.title: A dozen Louisville voters were wrongly prevented from voting in a Metro Council race
KY.summary: About a dozen voters in Louisville's Wilder Park neighborhood were given the wrong ballot during the May 19 primary and were unable to vote in their Metro Council District 21 race; the Jefferson County Clerk's Office launched a full review of voter district assignments after LPM News flagged the issue.

LA.title: Data, race and partisanship in redistricting: Louisiana must verify before it votes
LA.summary: As Louisiana's congressional redistricting bill moves toward a full House vote, concerns are raised about the accuracy of population and voter registration data behind the proposed new map, which would eliminate one of the state's two majority-Black districts, amid a deadline tied to early voting beginning May 26.

MI.title: Who's on the ballot for Michigan's governor in the 2026 election? Here's a list
MI.summary: A roundup of all confirmed candidates running for Michigan governor in 2026, ahead of the August 4 primary, following Mike Duggan's withdrawal as an independent candidate on May 21.

MI.title: Who's running for Michigan secretary of state in 2026? What to know about the candidates
MI.summary: Coverage of candidates seeking Michigan's secretary of state office in 2026, a particularly notable race as incumbent Jocelyn Benson is running for governor.

MI.title: What to know about the candidates running for Michigan attorney general in 2026 election
MI.summary: Overview of candidates running for Michigan attorney general in the 2026 election cycle, ahead of the August 4 primary.

MS.title: Mississippi redistricting could change who represents you
MS.summary: Reports on how Mississippi's ongoing redistricting debate, following the Supreme Court's weakening of the Voting Rights Act, could reshape which voters are represented by which legislators.

NE.title: Lindstrom explains potential bid for Nebraska governor, dissatisfaction with state's direction
NE.summary: Former GOP state senator Brett Lindstrom discusses his potential nonpartisan gubernatorial bid in Nebraska's 2026 general election, expressing frustration with partisan gridlock after the May 12 primary.

NJ.title: Here's what New Jersey voters need to know for the June primary when Congress is on the ballot
NJ.summary: With NJ in-person early voting opening May 26 and the June 2 primary approaching, this voter guide covers candidates, voting options, deadlines, and ID requirements for all 12 congressional district races and the U.S. Senate seat on the ballot.

NV.title: The early voting blog, Primary 2026
NV.summary: Nevada's June 9 primary early voting is underway with nearly 40,000 ballots cast in the first two days—about 1.5% of active voters—showing no unusual enthusiasm on either side, with Republicans and Democrats tracking at roughly equal participation rates.

OR.title: David Brock Smith wins GOP primary for US Senate in Oregon, will face Democratic incumbent Merkley
OR.summary: State Sen. David Brock Smith emerged from a seven-candidate Republican field to win the Oregon U.S. Senate primary, completing the last major race called from Oregon's May 19 primary and setting up a November challenge to incumbent Democratic Sen. Jeff Merkley.

SC.title: SC Senators return to redistricting decision as early voting begins
SC.summary: South Carolina senators returned to debate on a proposed congressional redistricting map as the two-week early voting period for June 9 primaries began, with the Senate voting on whether to advance a new map that would also delay congressional primaries to August 18.

SC.title: Early voting begins Tuesday as South Carolina redistricting debate continues
SC.summary: Early voting opened in South Carolina's primary elections while the state Senate continued debating a congressional redistricting proposal to eliminate the lone Democratic congressional seat held by Rep. Jim Clyburn.

TX.title: Texas primary runoff elections: races to watch on May 26
TX.summary: Texas voters headed to the polls for primary runoff elections, headlined by the high-profile GOP Senate battle between incumbent Sen. John Cornyn and Attorney General Ken Paxton, who received a late Trump endorsement.

TX.title: 2026 Texas primary runoff election results
TX.summary: Live coverage and results from Texas's May 26 primary runoff elections, covering 38 unresolved races where no candidate received a majority in the March 3 primary, including the Cornyn vs. Paxton Senate contest.

TX.title: KXAN Voter Guide: What to know for the May 2026 primary runoff elections
TX.summary: Voter guide for the May 26 Texas primary runoff elections covering polling locations, voting hours, key contested races including the U.S. Senate GOP runoff and multiple congressional primaries.

AL.title: Federal court blocks new Alabama congressional map
AL.summary: A three-judge federal panel blocked Alabama from using its GOP-drawn 2023 congressional map for the 2026 elections, ruling it remains intentionally discriminatory against Black voters and ordering the state to continue using the court-approved special master map.

AL.title: Federal court blocks Alabama plan for new congressional districts that could help Republicans
AL.summary: Federal judges blocked Alabama's attempt to redraw its congressional districts using a map that would eliminate one of the state's two majority-minority districts, preserving the existing court-ordered map through the 2026 elections and prompting an immediate state appeal.

AL.title: Judges block Alabama redistricting maps that would dilute Black vote in midterms
AL.summary: Federal judges issued a preliminary injunction preventing Alabama from using congressional district maps found to violate the Fourteenth Amendment by intentionally discriminating against Black voters, setting up a likely emergency Supreme Court appeal.

AL.title: State officials react to federal court's blockage of Alabama congressional redistricting plan
AL.summary: Alabama state officials responded to the federal court ruling blocking the new congressional map, with the state attorney general announcing an immediate appeal to the U.S. Supreme Court.

AZ.title: State Voting Laws Roundup: May 2026
AZ.summary: The Brennan Center's May 2026 roundup notes that Arizona is among nine states that have enacted at least 5 restrictive voting laws since 2021, providing context for ongoing voting access debates as the state's July primary approaches.

CA.title: Last-minute voter guide for California governor election
CA.summary: CalMatters published a last-minute guide for undecided California voters ahead of the June 2 primary, with early in-person voting underway statewide since May 23, covering the crowded governor's race and other key statewide contests.

CA.title: California almost killed the Board of Equalization. Now lawmakers want seats on it
CA.summary: CalMatters reported on a California legislative effort to place lawmakers on the elected Board of Equalization, an office appearing on the June 2 primary ballot as millions of Californians cast early ballots.

CO.title: KUNC 2026 Northern Colorado Primary Election Voter Guide
CO.summary: KUNC published a comprehensive voter guide for Colorado's June 30 primary, covering competitive congressional and statewide races in Northern Colorado and how unaffiliated voters — now the largest voter bloc — can participate in either party's primary.

DC.title: D.C. candidates share their plans for getting rid of rats
DC.summary: Candidates running in Washington D.C.'s June 16 primary are campaigning on various local issues; mayoral candidate Janeese Lewis George introduced legislation creating a public rat-abatement tracking dashboard, as voters prepare to use ranked-choice voting for the first time.

DC.title: Meet the candidates vying to succeed Eleanor Holmes Norton in Congress
DC.summary: The Washington Post profiles the field of candidates running in D.C.'s June 16 primary to succeed retiring Delegate Eleanor Holmes Norton, a consequential congressional race that will be decided under the district's newly implemented ranked-choice voting system.

DE.title: Primary Election Party Change Deadline is Friday, May 29th
DE.summary: WGMD reported on Delaware's upcoming May 29 party change deadline for the September 15 primary, reminding registered voters in the closed-primary state that they must switch to the Democratic or Republican party by 11:59 p.m. Friday to vote in their preferred primary.

DE.title: Independent Party Endorses Katz, Urges Supporters to Act Before May 29 Deadline
DE.summary: The Independent Party of Delaware endorsed Republican U.S. Senate candidate Dr. Mike Katz and urged members to change their party registration to Republican before the May 29, 2026 deadline to participate in Delaware's closed September 15 primary.

GA.title: Here is how to vote in Georgia's June 16, 2026, primary runoff election
GA.summary: The AJC published a voter guide for Georgia's June 16 primary runoff explaining eligibility rules (party selection locked from May primary), photo ID requirements, early voting from June 8–12, and instructions for checking registration.

IA.title: As Iowa's 2026 Primary approaches, Pate touts election security
IA.summary: Iowa Secretary of State Paul Pate held a news conference with officials from multiple state and federal agencies to announce security preparations for the June 2 primary election, stating no evidence of unauthorized intrusions into Iowa election systems has been found.

IA.title: Iowa Democrats to propose changes for their 2028 Caucuses
IA.summary: Iowa Democratic Party leaders unveiled a plan for their 2028 caucuses featuring paper-based presidential preference voting and an early mail option, which they planned to present to national Democrats starting May 27 as Iowa competes for an early-state slot in the 2028 presidential nominating calendar.

IL.title: Lawsuit Challenges Illinois Congressional District Map
IL.summary: Former state Rep. Jeanne Ives and the Public Interest Legal Foundation filed a federal lawsuit arguing Illinois's Voting Rights Act of 2011 unconstitutionally mandates race as a primary criterion in redistricting, citing the U.S. Supreme Court's Callais decision; the state has three weeks to respond.

LA.title: 5 GOP senators back Julia Letlow in Louisiana runoff after Bill Cassidy defeat
LA.summary: Five sitting Republican U.S. senators endorsed Julia Letlow ahead of the June 27 Senate runoff against state Treasurer John Fleming, reinforcing Letlow's frontrunner status in Louisiana's closed GOP primary following incumbent Sen. Bill Cassidy's May 16 defeat.

MA.title: Young Massachusetts voters anticipate the 2026 Massachusetts primary election
MA.summary: Reporting on how young Massachusetts voters are engaging with the upcoming 2026 primary elections, including perspectives on key races for U.S. Senate and governor, and ballot measures such as the same-day voter registration initiative.

MD.title: What to know about the mail ballot mix-up in Maryland
MD.summary: An explainer on Maryland's mail ballot printing error — what caused it, who was affected among the 500,000+ mail ballot requesters, how replacement ballots are being sent, and what safeguards against duplicate voting are in place ahead of the June 23 gubernatorial primary.

ME.title: In 1st District primary, Republicans diverge on their approach to Trump
ME.summary: With early voting underway ahead of Maine's June 9 primary, the two leading Republican candidates for the 1st Congressional District seat are navigating conflicting stances on President Trump as they seek to differentiate themselves to voters ahead of the primary.

MI.title: Michigan Democrats reintroduce state Voting Rights Act
MI.summary: Michigan Senate Democrats reintroduced legislation to create a state-level Voting Rights Act (Senate Bills 961–964) in response to the U.S. Supreme Court's Louisiana v. Callais decision that gutted Section 2 of the federal Voting Rights Act.

MT.title: Montana election officials working to get word out about updates to same-day registration
MT.summary: After a court blocked Senate Bill 490 that would have curtailed Election Day voter registration, Montana county election officials are doing outreach to clarify that voters can still register through 8 p.m. on Election Day for the June 2 primary.

ND.title: Issue spotlight: North Dakota's US House candidates weigh in on elections, mail-in voting
ND.summary: North Dakota's US House candidates shared their stances on elections and mail-in voting ahead of the June 9 primary, including views on the SAVE Act, noncitizen voting concerns, and whether they would accept the 2026 election results.

ND.title: Voting absentee? Mind your signatures, North Dakota election officials say
ND.summary: North Dakota election officials warn absentee voters ahead of the June 9 primary that ballots may be rejected if signatures on the application and return envelope do not match, and explain the process voters can use to cure a rejected signature.

ND.title: Voting absentee? Mind your signatures, North Dakota election officials say
ND.summary: State election officials outline absentee voting procedures and signature-matching requirements for the June 9 primary, including a 2025 law change eliminating the grace period for late-arriving mail ballots that were previously counted if postmarked before Election Day.

NV.title: The early voting blog, Primary 2026
NV.summary: The Nevada Independent's running blog on early voting tallies shows more than 52,600 ballots cast through May 26, including over 11,600 in-person votes over Memorial Day weekend, with turnout projected to remain low statewide.

TN.title: Court rules against NAACP in congressional districts case
TN.summary: A Tennessee state court three-judge panel ruled against the NAACP's challenge to the new congressional map that divided Memphis into three districts, finding that plaintiffs lacked standing and that all constitutional claims were without merit, leaving federal litigation as the remaining avenue for opponents.

VA.title: 16 statewide candidate filing deadlines in the next two weeks
VA.summary: Virginia's May 26 filing deadline for U.S. House party candidates is highlighted among sixteen imminent state deadlines, with the state's August 4 primary set under pre-referendum district maps after the state Supreme Court voided the redistricting amendment.

AR.title: Republicans running for House District 44 seat in Pope, Van Buren counties aim to cut property taxes
AR.summary: Four Republican candidates are competing in a special election for Arkansas House District 44, vacated after the death of Rep. Stan Berry. Early voting began for the June 2 special election, with candidates focused on property tax cuts and education issues.

AR.title: Candidates for late Arkansas lawmaker's seat tout tax cut support
AR.summary: Candidates vying in the June 2 special election for Arkansas House District 44 are campaigning on property tax cuts ahead of early voting for the special election to fill the seat left vacant by the death of Rep. Stan Berry.

FL.title: Florida redistricting ruling protects DeSantis' map for now
FL.summary: A Leon County Circuit Court judge ruled to keep Gov. DeSantis's congressional redistricting map in place while lawsuits continue, finding plaintiffs had not shown a substantial likelihood of success, meaning Florida will likely use the new GOP-favorable map in 2026 elections.

FL.title: DeSantis-appointed judge allows Florida to use GOP gerrymander in 2026
FL.summary: A DeSantis-appointed circuit court judge declined to block the new congressional map from use in 2026 elections despite pending legal challenges from voting rights groups, allowing the partisan gerrymander to remain in place for the upcoming midterms.

FL.title: Florida court keeps new districts in place ahead of midterms
FL.summary: A Florida state court judge ruled against blocking the new congressional map that would give Republicans up to four additional seats, keeping the redistricting plan in effect for the 2026 midterm elections while litigation continues.

IN.title: Morales lashes back over loss of Indiana secretary of state race support
IN.summary: Indiana Secretary of State Diego Morales publicly struck back at fellow Republican officeholders calling for his resignation amid controversy over his hiring of a former non-citizen as chief of staff, as he fights to secure delegate support ahead of the June 20 state Republican convention where party delegates will decide the secretary of state nomination.

KY.title: Hot-ticket federal races fuel rise in Kentucky primary voter turnout
KY.summary: Kentucky's May 19 primary saw voter turnout of 25.67%, the highest midterm primary rate for Republicans since 2014, driven by competitive federal races including the open U.S. Senate seat left by Mitch McConnell's retirement and the Trump-endorsed primary challenge against Rep. Thomas Massie.

MD.title: Maryland Election Official Warns Voters Not To Trust 'Social Influencers' After Ballot Chaos
MD.summary: As replacement ballots arrived in mailboxes following a printing vendor error that sent over 500,000 Maryland voters the wrong-party primary ballot, State Administrator of Elections Jared DeMarinis publicly countered growing misinformation and warned voters not to trust social media influencers, stating no fake or illegal ballots were distributed ahead of the June 23 gubernatorial primary.

MI.title: Michigan Democrats and Republicans want to pass new election laws if they win the 2026 midterms
MI.summary: Democrats want to pass the Michigan Voting Rights Act, expanding language access and voter assistance, while Republicans are pushing proof-of-citizenship requirements for voter registration. Which agenda advances depends on which party wins a trifecta in November 2026.

MO.title: Missouri governor places tax overhaul on August ballot, and abortion ban in November
MO.summary: Gov. Mike Kehoe placed four constitutional amendments on Missouri's August 4 primary ballot, including Amendment 4, which would require initiative-petition constitutional amendments to pass in all eight congressional districts — a significant change to the ballot measure process.

MO.title: Missouri voters could face as many as nine ballot measures in 2026
MO.summary: Missouri voters could face up to nine statewide ballot measures in August and November 2026, including a possible veto referendum on the state's gerrymandered congressional redistricting plan. If all nine qualify, it would be the most statewide measures in Missouri since 2014.

MS.title: Congressional Black Caucus presses companies to oppose redistricting
MS.summary: The Congressional Black Caucus called on more than 250 major corporations to oppose Republican-led redistricting efforts in Southern states aimed at eliminating majority-Black congressional districts, following a Supreme Court ruling weakening the Voting Rights Act.

MS.title: Mississippi redistricting debate intensifies after Supreme Court ruling
MS.summary: Mississippi's redistricting debate is intensifying after the Supreme Court weakened the Voting Rights Act, with lawmakers discussing maps that could eliminate Rep. Bennie Thompson's majority-Black congressional district. Experts note the compressed 2026 election calendar makes pre-election redistricting extremely difficult.

MT.title: Democratic and Republican appetite for ticket splitting in Montana elections is low, poll indicates
MT.summary: A Montana Free Press-Eagleton poll found that 63% of registered Montana voters say they are unlikely to vote for a candidate from a different party than they usually support, complicating prospects for independent and Democratic candidates hoping to win over Republicans ahead of the June 2 primary.

ND.title: Early voting and absentee ballot deadlines approaching in Ward County
ND.summary: With North Dakota's June 9 primary approaching, Ward County election officials remind voters of absentee ballot deadlines; a new state law means ballots arriving after Election Day will not be counted even with an Election Day postmark, reversing prior practice.

NH.title: Judge weighs Trump administration's demand for confidential NH voter data
NH.summary: A federal judge heard arguments over the Trump administration's demand that New Hampshire turn over its confidential statewide voter database, including partial Social Security and driver's license numbers. The state asked for dismissal, calling the request beyond the limits of federal oversight; the case is one of about 20 similar suits the administration is pursuing nationwide.

NM.title: Early voting continues through Saturday for New Mexico's first semi-open primary election on June 2
NM.summary: Early voting for New Mexico's June 2 primary continues through May 30, marking the state's first semi-open primary allowing unaffiliated voters to choose a party ballot; May 26 was also the last recommended day to mail in an absentee ballot.

NM.title: Nearly 95,000 New Mexicans vote early in primary election
NM.summary: Nearly 94,930 voters — about 6.6% of New Mexico's electorate — cast early ballots for the June 2 primary as of May 26, with approximately 8,800 unaffiliated 'decline to state' voters participating for the first time under the new semi-open primary system.

NV.title: Early voting (and vote by mail) now underway for Nevada's June primary
NV.summary: Nevada's early in-person voting period is underway through June 5, with more than 41,000 mail ballots already returned and over 11,600 in-person votes cast over Memorial Day Weekend. May 27 is the final day to register or update registration for the June 9 primary.

OR.title: Oregon primary election roundup
OR.summary: A roundup of Oregon's May 19 primary results as ballot counting continued, with Republican Christine Drazan winning the gubernatorial primary to face Democratic incumbent Gov. Tina Kotek in November, and a gas tax transportation funding measure soundly rejected by 83% of voters.

SC.title: Clyburn's district stays intact as South Carolina Republicans scrap redistricting
SC.summary: South Carolina Republicans abandoned a plan to redraw the majority-Black 6th Congressional District after record-breaking first-day early voting turnout of over 44,000 voters on May 26 prompted Republican senators to reject the redistricting bill ahead of the June 9 primary.

SC.title: South Carolina's Trump-backed redistricting push fails in the state Senate amid GOP opposition
SC.summary: The South Carolina Senate voted against advancing a new congressional map despite pressure from President Trump, as record-setting early voting turnout — over 44,000 ballots statewide on day one — prompted key Republican senators to abandon the mid-election redistricting effort.

SD.title: South Dakota GOP primary preview: U.S. Senate
SD.summary: Preview of the June 2 Republican primary U.S. Senate race, where incumbent Sen. Mike Rounds seeks a third term against challenger Justin McNeal, with advance voting underway ahead of the primary.

SD.title: South Dakota GOP primary preview: U.S. House
SD.summary: Preview of the June 2 Republican primary U.S. House race in South Dakota, covering candidates and key issues ahead of the upcoming primary election.

TX.title: 4 takeaways from the Texas runoff primary elections
TX.summary: Analysis of the May 26 Texas runoff results, where Ken Paxton defeated incumbent Sen. John Cornyn in the GOP Senate primary — making Cornyn the first Texas Republican senator to lose renomination — and other key congressional race outcomes.

UT.title: These new laws took effect in Utah on Wednesday
UT.summary: Reports on 373 new Utah laws taking effect on May 27 including SB153, which makes voter registration records (names, addresses, party affiliation, voting history) public for roughly 1.3 million previously-protected voters unless they qualify for the new at-risk exemption status.

WI.title: Deadline approaching to file nomination papers to run for office
WI.summary: Wisconsin Elections Commission reminder that June 1 is the deadline for candidates to file nomination papers and declarations of candidacy for the August 11 partisan primary and November general election, along with a note that circulators of nomination papers must now reside in Wisconsin under a new statute.

AL.title: Alabama GOP runoff candidates make cases to Shelby County voters
AL.summary: Republican candidates in statewide primary runoff elections — including races for U.S. Senate, Attorney General, and Lieutenant Governor — made their pitches to Shelby County voters on May 26, three weeks before the June 16 runoff election.

AZ.title: Drop boxes at center of Maricopa County election dispute
AZ.summary: The feud between Maricopa County Recorder Justin Heap and the Board of Supervisors over ballot drop box authority escalated ahead of the July 21 primary, with the Arizona Attorney General rejecting Heap's claims that election workers could face felony charges for handling board-approved drop box ballots.

CO.title: Restore Our Roads submits 180,000 signatures for transportation funding initiative
CO.summary: Proponents of Initiative 175 submitted over 180,000 petition signatures to qualify the road-funding constitutional amendment for the November 2026 ballot; the Secretary of State has until June 25 to verify whether the required 124,000+ signatures are valid.

IN.title: New recount director picked for review of two narrow Indiana Senate primaries
IN.summary: Indiana's bipartisan Recount Commission approved a new recount director after the original appointment resigned, as the review of two extremely close Republican state Senate primary races — decided by margins of three votes or fewer — moves forward.

ME.title: Susan Collins trails Graham Platner by 9 points in Maine Senate race, new poll finds
ME.summary: A new University of New Hampshire Survey Center poll shows Democratic challenger Graham Platner leading incumbent Republican Sen. Susan Collins by 9 points in Maine's Senate race, ahead of the June 9 primary and November general election.

MO.title: Four Missouri amendments set for August ballots – What would they do?
MO.summary: An explainer on the four constitutional amendments Missourians will vote on August 4, covering state park funding renewal, county assessor elections, initiative petition supermajority requirements, and a plan to eliminate the state income tax.

MT.title: Seth Bodnar expects to clear signature threshold for independent U.S. Senate campaign
MT.summary: Independent U.S. Senate candidate Seth Bodnar says he has gathered sufficient signatures to qualify for the November general election ballot, adding a notable independent contender to Montana's open Senate seat race.

NH.title: NH Democrats pitch DNC on NH's place at the head of the 2028 primary calendar
NH.summary: Top New Hampshire Democrats testified before the DNC Rules Committee in Washington, arguing the state should retain its first-in-the-nation presidential primary status in 2028, citing its large bloc of undeclared voters as uniquely testing candidates across party lines.

NJ.title: Early in-person voting begins for NJ congressional primaries
NJ.summary: NJ Urban News reported on active early voting across New Jersey ahead of the June 2 primary, with federal races including all 12 House seats and Sen. Cory Booker's open seat at the top of the ballot and strong Democratic mail-in participation.

NY.title: The 2026 state legislative primary races to watch
NY.summary: City & State New York previewed the most competitive state legislative primaries ahead of the June 23 primary election, highlighting races driven by retirements, a new cap on legislators' outside income, and progressive vs. establishment Democratic clashes.

NY.title: Senate Advances Reforms to Protect Election Integrity and Support Election Workers
NY.summary: The New York State Senate advanced a package of election administration bills including anti-voter-suppression penalties, an election worker protection act barring intimidation and doxxing of poll workers, and a mandatory training curriculum for election commissioners.

NC.title: North Carolinians to vote on income, property tax limits after lawmakers OK ballot questions
NC.summary: North Carolina's GOP-led General Assembly passed two constitutional amendments that will ask voters in November to permanently cap the income tax rate and limit local governments' ability to raise property taxes.

NC.title: 2 tax amendments will be on the ballot for North Carolina voters this November
NC.summary: WLOS reported on both constitutional amendments approved by the NC legislature that will appear on November's general election ballot, explaining the income tax cap and property tax limit proposals and the partisan dynamics behind their passage.

OK.title: Voter Guide: 2026 Oklahoma Primary Election
OK.summary: Oklahoma Voice launched a comprehensive voter guide for the June 16 primary election, covering candidates for governor, U.S. Senate, and other statewide offices, along with a ballot measure to raise the minimum wage to $15 by 2029.

OK.title: Oklahoma voters facing deadlines for upcoming election cycle
OK.summary: Coverage of key voter registration and absentee ballot deadlines ahead of Oklahoma's June 16 primary, noting the May 22 voter registration deadline and explaining implications for young voters turning 18.

AZ.title: After months of delay, Maricopa County recorder refers alleged noncitizen voters to AG
AZ.summary: Maricopa County Recorder Justin Heap referred 207 alleged noncitizen voters to the Arizona Attorney General's Office after months of delay and pressure from AG Kris Mayes. The referral has implications for voter roll integrity ahead of Arizona's July 21 primary.

CA.title: Newsom signs bill to protect California elections from Trump
CA.summary: Governor Gavin Newsom signed Senate Bill 73, restricting law enforcement from interfering with election administration and creating criminal penalties for unauthorized seizure of voted ballots. The law was prompted by Riverside County Sheriff Chad Bianco's seizure of over 650,000 ballots and takes effect immediately ahead of California's June 2 primary.

DC.title: D.C. Voter Guide 2026: Who's running to replace Eleanor Holmes Norton as D.C. delegate?
DC.summary: WAMU published a voter guide covering DC's historic June 16, 2026 primary, where voters will for the first time use ranked-choice voting and choose a new Congressional delegate to replace the retiring Eleanor Holmes Norton.

DE.title: Delaware judge rules corporations can vote in some municipal elections
DE.summary: A Delaware Superior Court judge dismissed an ACLU lawsuit, ruling that corporations, LLCs, trusts and other 'artificial entities' may vote in some Delaware municipal elections where they own property, upholding a Fenwick Island town charter provision.

FL.title: Judge rules Florida's new congressional map will remain intact ahead of midterms
FL.summary: A Leon Circuit Court judge rejected challenges from Common Cause and Equal Ground Education Fund, allowing Florida's redrawn congressional map to stand for the 2026 midterms, with opponents vowing to appeal before candidate qualifying begins.

GA.title: Georgia Runoff Elections: Who's on the ballot, how can you vote?
GA.summary: WSB-TV published a voter guide for Georgia's June 16, 2026 primary runoff, detailing early voting dates (June 8-12), the absentee ballot request deadline of June 5, and major races on the ballot including governor, U.S. Senate, and Secretary of State.

GA.title: Chris Carr endorses Rick Jackson in Georgia GOP governor's runoff
GA.summary: Georgia Attorney General Chris Carr endorsed Rick Jackson over Lt. Gov. Burt Jones ahead of the June 16 Republican gubernatorial runoff election; the winner will face Democratic nominee Keisha Lance Bottoms in November.

HI.title: Honolulu attorney John Choi announces run for lieutenant governor
HI.summary: Honolulu civil trial attorney John Choi filed his nomination papers with the Hawaii Office of Elections on May 27, entering the Democratic primary for lieutenant governor ahead of the June 2 candidate filing deadline and the August 8 primary election.

IA.title: Feenstra touts support from Branstad, GOP officials ahead of primary
IA.summary: Republican gubernatorial candidate Randy Feenstra campaigned with former Gov. Terry Branstad and state GOP officials five days before Iowa's June 2 primary, which will also decide nominees for U.S. Senate and all four congressional seats.

ID.title: Jesse Human wins coin toss to break election tie
ID.summary: A tied Republican precinct committeeman race in Jerome County, Idaho was resolved by a coin toss on May 26 under Idaho Code 34-1210, with challenger Jesse Human defeating incumbent Brian Smith after both received 75 votes in the May 19 primary.

ID.title: Coin toss decides tied race for Caribou County commissioner
ID.summary: George Hulse won the Republican nomination for Caribou County Commissioner District 2 after a coin toss broke a tie with Tracy Davis, each having received 469 votes in Idaho's May 19 primary, under Idaho's tied-election statute.

KS.title: Kansas voters face approaching deadlines as new election rules take effect
KS.summary: Kansas voters have less than a week to change party affiliation ahead of the June 1 deadline before the August 4 primary. New state rules have eliminated the three-day grace period for mail-in ballots, requiring ballots to be received by 7 p.m. on election day to count.

MA.title: In Massachusetts governor's race, it's the economy, stupid. For Healey, it's abortion, too.
MA.summary: Governor Maura Healey is linking abortion access to economic concerns as part of her reelection pitch, facing two Republican challengers ahead of the November general election, with reproductive health care becoming a central campaign issue alongside cost-of-living concerns.

MN.title: U.S. Senate hopeful Craig heads straight to primary, paving way for Flanagan's DFL endorsement
MN.summary: U.S. Rep. Angie Craig announced she will bypass the DFL Party convention and take her Senate candidacy directly to the August 11 primary, clearing the way for Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan to win the party endorsement, though both will still face each other in the primary.

MN.title: Not on Angie's list: Seeking DFL Party endorsement
MN.summary: Roll Call covers Angie Craig's decision to skip the DFL state convention in the Minnesota U.S. Senate race, reflecting divisions between moderate and progressive wings of the Democratic party ahead of the pivotal open-seat contest.

MN.title: Minnesota Congresswoman Angie Craig no longer seeking DFL endorsement in Senate race
MN.summary: Minnesota Rep. Angie Craig officially decided not to seek the DFL party endorsement for the open U.S. Senate seat, with Peggy Flanagan's campaign reporting she was on track to win about 75% of convention delegates. Both candidates will compete in the August 11 primary.

MT.title: Montana's primary election is Tuesday; here's how to vote
MT.summary: Ahead of Montana's June 2 primary, the Secretary of State's office urged absentee voters to drop ballots off in person rather than mail them, and reminded voters of new requirements including photo ID at polling places and writing their birth year on mail ballot return envelopes.

NC.title: Republican lawmakers consider shortening NC's early voting period
NC.summary: Two bills in the North Carolina General Assembly would cut early in-person voting from 17 days to as few as 10 and eliminate a Sunday voting day statewide, with Democrats warning it would disproportionately harm Black voters ahead of the 2026 election cycle.

NE.title: U.S. Senate nominee Cindy Burbank might have to sue to get her name off the general election ballot
NE.summary: After winning the Democratic Senate primary, Cindy Burbank faces a legal obstacle to removing her name from the November ballot after pledging to drop out to support independent Dan Osborn, with the Secretary of State's office seeking guidance from the Attorney General.

NM.title: NM judge rules Republican Party of New Mexico Chair Barela must leave post
NM.summary: A New Mexico district court judge issued a preliminary injunction ordering GOP Chair Amy Barela to vacate her position, ruling that simultaneously serving as party chair and running as a primary candidate constituted a conflict of interest that could unfairly influence the June 2 primary election.

NM.title: Judge orders New Mexico GOP chair Amy Barela to step down, citing primary race conflict
NM.summary: A Bernalillo County District Court ruling ordered NM Republican Party Chair Amy Barela to step down before the June 2 primary; First Vice Chair Mike Nelson was set to take over pending appeal.

NM.title: Judge bars Barela from serving as New Mexico Republican Party chair
NM.summary: A court order barred Amy Barela from the NM GOP chairperson role amid a party rules dispute over whether she could hold party leadership while running as a candidate in the same June 2 primary.

OH.title: Ohio Republicans Trying to Get Voter Photo ID on Ballot, Enshrined in State Constitution
OH.summary: Ohio House and Senate Republicans introduced joint resolutions to place a constitutional amendment requiring voter photo ID on the November 2026 ballot, seeking to enshrine into the state constitution existing statutory ID requirements in place since 2023; a three-fifths vote in each chamber would be needed.

TN.title: Tennessee mid-decade redistricting survives first legal challenge
TN.summary: A three-judge state panel dismissed the NAACP's legal challenge to Tennessee's redrawn congressional map, which split the majority-Black city of Memphis across three districts. Three federal court challenges remain pending ahead of the August 6 primary.

VT.title: As Vermont legislative session stretches on, adjournment is a moving target
VT.summary: Vermont's extended legislative session is complicating election preparation, with the May 28 candidate filing deadline for the August 11 primary forcing legislators to collect required voter signatures while still in session.

WI.title: Lawsuit seeks to require Wisconsin clerks to let voters fix problems with their absentee ballots
WI.summary: The League of Women Voters of Wisconsin sued the Wisconsin Elections Commission seeking a court order requiring all municipal clerks to notify voters when their absentee ballot certificates have missing information and allow them to fix the problem, arguing the current optional practice leads to inconsistent treatment of voters statewide.

WY.title: Wyoming lawmakers request another batch of election bills
WY.summary: The Wyoming Corporations, Elections and Political Subdivisions Committee advanced 14 election bill requests for potential consideration, including proposals for pen-and-paper-only ballot marking and moving the party affiliation change deadline to January 1. Secretary of State Chuck Gray identified about 30 previously failed election bills he wants reconsidered ahead of the August 18 primary.

DC.title: A federal judge in D.C. declines to block Trump's executive order on voting by mail
DC.summary: A federal judge declined to temporarily block President Trump's executive order restricting mail-in voting, leaving in place a March directive that uses Social Security data to compile voter eligibility lists and limit mail ballot delivery in all states.

AL.title: Alabama Files Emergency Appeal to U.S. Supreme Court Over Congressional Redistricting Map
AL.summary: Alabama officials filed an emergency appeal to the U.S. Supreme Court seeking to use their GOP-drawn congressional map in the 2026 midterms, after a three-judge federal panel blocked it for intentionally discriminating against Black voters.

CA.title: Becerra leads race for governor, Hilton and Steyer in close race for second, poll shows
CA.summary: A UC Berkeley IGS poll released May 29 shows Xavier Becerra leading California's gubernatorial primary with 25%, with Republican Steve Hilton at 21% and Democrat Tom Steyer at 19%, four days before the June 2 primary.

DE.title: Political party change deadline nears ahead of Delaware primary elections
DE.summary: Delaware voters have until Friday, May 29 at 11:59 p.m. to change their party registration to participate in the September 15 primary election, as the state's closed primary requires voters to be registered with a party.

TX.title: How the Talarico-Paxton race could play out
TX.summary: Democrat James Talarico launched his general election Senate campaign on May 28 targeting Republican Ken Paxton's corruption record, as Democrats see an unusual opportunity in Texas following Paxton's divisive primary runoff win over incumbent Sen. John Cornyn.

AK.title: 3 things to watch as Alaska's election filing deadline approaches
AK.summary: With the June 1 candidate filing deadline imminent, Alaska's August 18 primary ballot is taking shape; 20 gubernatorial candidates are in the race, including late entrants like former Gov. Bill Walker, with ranked-choice voting to be used in November's general election.

AK.title: Former Alaska Gov. Bill Walker files for possible run in 2026 governor's race
AK.summary: Former Alaska Governor Bill Walker filed a letter of intent for the 2026 gubernatorial race, saying he would most likely enter the contest ahead of the June 1 candidate filing deadline for the August 18 primary election.

AL.title: Gov. Ivey calls special primary election for Alabama-drawn State Senate map
AL.summary: Governor Kay Ivey called a special primary election for August 11, 2026 for State Senate Districts 25 and 26 after a federal appeals court allowed Alabama to use its 2021-drawn state senate map, voiding the May 19 primary results for those districts.

AL.title: Court clears Alabama to use previously replaced 2021 state Senate map; Ivey calls special elections
AL.summary: The 11th Circuit Court of Appeals cleared Alabama to use its 2021 state senate map for Senate Districts 25 and 26, prompting Governor Ivey to call a special primary election for August 11 and void the earlier May 19 primary results for those seats.

AZ.title: Legislative candidates face fierce competition ahead of July primaries
AZ.summary: Arizona legislative candidates are ramping up campaigns with less than two months until the July 21 primary, the first under the state's newly enacted law permanently moving the primary election from August to July to help meet federal military and overseas ballot deadlines.

AZ.title: Legislatures in Arizona, California, and Rhode Island will decide on legislatively referred ballot measures in June
AZ.summary: The Arizona Legislature is among several that will vote on referring additional ballot measures to voters before the July primary, as the June legislative calendar shapes the fall ballot in Arizona.

CA.title: California contests for governor, LA mayor head toward primary election with no clear leaders
CA.summary: On the eve of California's June 2 primary, top-two open primary races for governor and Los Angeles mayor remained highly competitive with multiple candidates lacking a commanding lead, the first major statewide election under new election-security laws.

CA.title: Candidates for LA mayor and California governor make weekend push
CA.summary: California gubernatorial and Los Angeles mayoral candidates made final campaign stops ahead of the June 2 top-two primary election, which will also be the first conducted under a new law banning unauthorized law enforcement access to ballots and voting systems.

CO.title: CPR News' voter guide to the Colorado 2026 primary election
CO.summary: With ballots now available for Colorado's June 30 primary, this guide covers voting procedures, key races for U.S. Senate, governor, and all 65 state House seats, including rules for unaffiliated voters who make up over half the state's electorate.

CO.title: Colorado primary election guide 2026: How to vote and what to vote on
CO.summary: Colorado's June 30 primary election will feature races for U.S. Senate, governor, attorney general, and all 65 state House seats; ballots are being mailed to voters starting June 8 under the recently expanded mail-ballot window enacted to guard against postal delays.

DC.title: Your Guide to Ranked Choice Voting in the DC Primaries
DC.summary: Washington, D.C. will use ranked-choice voting for the first time in its June 16 primary election, where seven Democratic mayoral candidates are competing; voters approved Initiative 83 in 2024, though the DC Council funded only ranked-choice implementation — not open primaries — for this cycle.

DE.title: Primary Election Party Change Deadline is Friday, May 29th
DE.summary: Delaware's Department of Elections reminded voters that May 29 is the last day to change party affiliation ahead of the September 15 closed primary, noting that about one-third of registered Delaware voters are unaffiliated and currently barred from participating in partisan primaries.

FL.title: Florida's new congressional map to remain intact, judge rules
FL.summary: A Leon County circuit court judge upheld Florida's redrawn congressional map, rejecting challenges who argued the DeSantis-directed map violated the state's Fair Districts Amendment; voting rights groups immediately announced plans to appeal to the Florida Supreme Court.

FL.title: Judge says Florida can use new congressional map for Midterms, voting rights groups appeal
FL.summary: After a circuit court judge declined to block Florida's redrawn congressional districts, voting rights organizations including the League of Women Voters and Common Cause announced they will pursue an appeal to the Florida Supreme Court ahead of candidate qualifying, which opens June 8.

GA.title: It's almost time to vote again: Georgia's primary runoff election just weeks away
GA.summary: A comprehensive voter guide covering Georgia's June 16 runoff election, including contested Republican primaries for governor and U.S. Senate, early voting dates of June 6–12, and absentee ballot request procedures.

GA.title: GOP governor and Senate battles intensify as runoff nears
GA.summary: With the June 16 runoff approaching, Republican candidates for governor and Senate are escalating campaigning; Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms, who won her primary outright, is appearing with incumbent Sen. Jon Ossoff to build a unified Democratic coalition ahead of November.

HI.title: Judge won't block Trump's mail-in voting executive order for now
HI.summary: A federal judge declined to immediately block Trump's executive order targeting mail-in voting, directly affecting Hawaii, which mandates mail-in voting by state law and is among 19 states suing over the order; Hawaii officials say they have no plans to change course regardless of any future ruling.

IA.title: Three Democrats compete in Iowa 4th Congressional District primary
IA.summary: Three Democratic candidates are competing in Iowa's June 2 primary for the open 4th Congressional District seat vacated when Rep. Randy Feenstra stepped down to run for governor; the Republican nominee, Trump-endorsed Chris McGowan, is running unopposed.

IA.title: Two Republicans aim to become candidate to flip state auditor seat to GOP control
IA.summary: Lt. Gov. Chris Cournoyer and Iowa County Supervisor Abigail Maas are vying in the June 2 Republican primary for state auditor, seeking to flip the seat currently held by Democrat Rob Sand, who is running for governor.

ID.title: Idaho election officials randomly pick eight counties for primary election audits
ID.summary: Following the May 19 primary, Idaho's Secretary of State randomly selected eight counties for post-election hand-count audits covering at least 2,100 ballots; official results will be certified by the State Board of Canvassers on June 9.

IN.title: Candidates focused on convention delegates in upended GOP secretary of state race
IN.summary: After incumbent Secretary of State Diego Morales lost support from top Republicans due to a hiring controversy, four candidates are competing for roughly 1,800 GOP delegate votes at the June 20 state convention — a race with direct implications for the office that oversees Indiana elections.

IN.title: It's a new race for secretary of state
IN.summary: The Indiana secretary of state's race was dramatically reshuffled as Sen. Jim Banks recruited his own staffer to challenge Morales, with cascading Republican withdrawals; the upheaval also energizes Indiana Democrats heading into their June 6 convention.

LA.title: Louisiana lawmakers pass a congressional map to dismantle a majority-Black district
LA.summary: Louisiana Republicans passed a new congressional map eliminating one of the state's two majority-Black districts, giving the GOP a 5-1 advantage in the congressional delegation. The map was signed by Gov. Jeff Landry hours after passing the state legislature, following the Supreme Court's Louisiana v. Callais ruling.

LA.title: Louisiana House passes new congressional map, sending bill back to Senate
LA.summary: The Louisiana House passed a revised congressional redistricting map and sent it back to the Senate for final approval, advancing legislation that would dismantle a majority-Black district and create an additional Republican-leaning seat ahead of the 2026 midterms.

LA.title: Louisiana passes new congressional map to eliminate majority-Black district, give GOP another seat
LA.summary: Louisiana enacted a new congressional map designed to help Republicans pick up a seat while eliminating one of the state's two majority-Black House districts. More lawsuits are expected over the new map, which critics say could itself face racial gerrymandering challenges.

MA.title: Markey wins Mass. Democrats' endorsement as Moulton clears ballot hurdle in Senate race
MA.summary: Sen. Ed Markey won the Massachusetts Democratic Party's endorsement with nearly 73% of delegate support at the state convention, while Rep. Seth Moulton cleared the 15% threshold needed to appear on the September 1 primary ballot, setting up a contested Democratic Senate primary.

MA.title: In contested US Senate race, Markey beats Moulton for endorsement of Mass. Dems at convention
MA.summary: At the Massachusetts Democratic state convention, incumbent Sen. Ed Markey secured the party's endorsement over challenger Rep. Seth Moulton, who still qualified for the primary ballot by crossing the 15% delegate threshold, in a race framed around generational change ahead of the September primary.

MD.title: MD ballot error: Original mail-ins to be counted if replacements not returned
MD.summary: Maryland elections administrator confirmed that original mail-in ballots sent in error — where some voters received the wrong party's primary ballot — will be counted if voters do not return the replacement ballots mailed to them, as the state works to ensure all voters can participate in the June 23 primary.

MD.title: Maryland elections head: Original ballots will count if replacement isn't sent
MD.summary: Maryland elections Administrator Jared DeMarinis clarified that original mail-in ballots will be quarantined and potentially counted if no replacement ballot is returned, as officials work to balance voter access with election integrity before the June 23 primary.

ME.title: Republican Primary Set for Maine House District 3
ME.summary: Two Republican candidates will face each other in the June 9 primary for Maine House District 3 after incumbent Rep. Mark Babin announced he will not seek reelection, setting up a contested race ahead of the state primary election.

ME.title: New poll shows Democrat Platner leading GOP Sen. Collins by 9 points in Maine
ME.summary: A University of New Hampshire poll shows Democratic Senate candidate Graham Platner leading incumbent Republican Sen. Susan Collins 51% to 42%, with Platner also holding a dominant lead in the Democratic primary ahead of the June 9 primary election.

MI.title: MDOS announces changes to automatic voter registration process to comply with Michigan election law
MI.summary: Starting June 1, Michigan residents automatically registered to vote through Secretary of State transactions will receive a mailed opt-out notice, a change stemming from legislation Gov. Whitmer signed in 2023 that updates how the state handles automatic voter registration.

MI.title: Changes to automatic voter registration process take effect June 1
MI.summary: Michigan's updated automatic voter registration opt-out process takes effect June 1, requiring the Department of State to mail confirmation letters with prepaid opt-out forms to all newly automatically registered voters, replacing the prior in-person opt-out system.

MN.title: What you need to know about the DFL, GOP conventions this weekend
MN.summary: A preview of the Minnesota DFL and Republican state conventions held May 29-30, explaining how party endorsements work, the key races at stake including governor and U.S. Senate, and how endorsed candidates can still face primary challenges on August 11.

MN.title: Klobuchar fights off challenge from left, wins DFL convention nod in bid for governor
MN.summary: Sen. Amy Klobuchar won the DFL endorsement for Minnesota governor at the May 30 state convention despite a challenge from progressive delegates, while Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan secured the DFL Senate endorsement, setting both up for the August 11 primary.

MN.title: Kendall Qualls wins GOP endorsement for governor
MN.summary: Kendall Qualls secured the Republican Party endorsement for Minnesota governor after ten rounds of convention voting, defeating House Speaker Lisa Demuth to become the endorsed GOP candidate heading toward the August 11 primary.

MO.title: Judge to decide Monday whether Missouri tax overhaul stays on August ballot
MO.summary: A Cole County judge will rule on whether Amendment 5 — proposing to replace Missouri's income tax with expanded sales taxes — can stay on the August 4 primary ballot, with opponents arguing single-subject constitutional violations and a misleading ballot summary.

MO.title: Missouri could be stuck using an invalid congressional map in the 2026 midterms
MO.summary: Secretary of State Denny Hoskins has delayed certifying a citizen referendum on Missouri's gerrymandered congressional map, risking the August primary being conducted under a constitutionally barred map and triggering post-election litigation.

MS.title: Redistricting affects millions of Americans
MS.summary: A review of Republican-led redistricting efforts ahead of November elections, with Mississippi context including pressure on Gov. Reeves to call a special session to redraw maps following the Supreme Court's Callais ruling.

MS.title: Callais redistricting ruling leaves unanswered questions
MS.summary: An examination of the Supreme Court's Callais decision and its unresolved implications for Mississippi, including whether intentional prevention of majority-Black districts is now constitutionally permissible.

MT.title: Read the instructions if you want your vote to count
MT.summary: Hundreds of Montana mail ballots were rejected before the June 2 primary after voters submitted multiple party ballots; election officials urge voters to use only one of the three party ballots received (Democratic, Libertarian, Republican) and destroy the others.

ND.title: North Dakota Republican incumbents join Fedorchak for candidate tour
ND.summary: With early in-person voting underway ahead of the June 9 primary, Republican statewide incumbents joined Rep. Julie Fedorchak on a statewide tour; the Secretary of State noted primary turnout typically runs around 22%, as Fedorchak faces a primary challenge from Alex Balazs.

NE.title: Nebraska Board of State Canvassers set to certify primary election results
NE.summary: Nebraska's Board of State Canvassers will meet June 8 to officially certify the May 12 primary results; no automatic recounts are anticipated, though contingency recount dates of June 10 and 15 are reserved if needed.

NH.title: New Hampshire is moving its state primary. Will it improve the state's politics?
NH.summary: Gov. Kelly Ayotte signed a law moving New Hampshire's state primary from September to June starting in 2028, expanding the primary-to-general gap from two months to five and shifting candidate filing deadlines from June to March.

NH.title: New Hampshire primary moved to June, starting in 2028
NH.summary: Analysis of New Hampshire's new law moving state primaries to the second Tuesday in June beginning in 2028, which supporters say will reduce incumbent advantage by giving challengers five months to campaign before the general election.

NJ.title: New Jersey's primary election is Tuesday. Here's what to watch.
NJ.summary: Preview of New Jersey's June 2 primary featuring a packed 12-candidate Democratic field in the 12th District, competitive contests to flip Republican-held seats, and a Republican Senate primary to challenge incumbent Cory Booker.

NM.title: New Mexico Election 2026: trail notes
NM.summary: With nearly 140,000 early ballots cast ahead of New Mexico's June 2 primary — the state's first semi-open primary allowing independent voters to participate without re-registering — campaigns are in their final days of mobilization.

NM.title: Will independents turn out for New Mexico's first semi-open primary?
NM.summary: Early voting data shows only about 4% of New Mexico's 330,000-plus independent voters have cast ballots in the state's inaugural semi-open primary, with advocates attributing the low turnout to a lack of outreach from the Secretary of State's office.

NV.title: What are the issues, endorsements, and candidates impacting the 2026 primary election?
NV.summary: Nevada public radio examines key races and voter concerns ahead of the June 9 primary, including competitive open congressional seats, Trump endorsement dynamics, and affordability as voters' top issue.

NY.title: New York Democrats unveil their own mid-decade redistricting scheme, targeting future elections
NY.summary: New York Democratic leaders announced plans to advance two constitutional amendments through the legislature before the June 4 session end, enabling mid-decade redistricting and altering the independent redistricting commission's composition in response to Republican-led redistricting efforts.

NY.title: NY Democrats Plan to Pass Redistricting Amendments Ahead of 2028
NY.summary: Assembly Speaker Carl Heastie confirmed two redistricting constitutional amendments were on track for passage before the legislature adjourned, aiming to eventually allow Democrats to redraw congressional maps ahead of the 2028 elections.

OH.title: An Ohio House committee reviewed the voter photo ID amendment. No one spoke for it
OH.summary: A nearly three-hour Ohio House committee hearing on House Joint Resolution 9 — which would put a constitutional voter photo ID requirement on the November ballot — drew no in-person supporters; of 80 written testimonies submitted, only two were in favor while 78 opposed the measure.

OK.title: Oklahoma Voice launches voter guide ahead of June 16 primary election
OK.summary: Oklahoma Voice published a comprehensive voter guide for the June 16 primary election covering all races plus State Question 832 on the minimum wage, noting that all Oklahoma primaries remain closed to non-party voters in 2026 and 2027 following the State Election Board's December 2025 decision.

RI.title: Legislatures in Arizona, California, and Rhode Island will decide on legislatively referred ballot measures in June
RI.summary: Rhode Island's legislature faces a June 30 adjournment deadline to refer measures to voters, with a Right to Public Education constitutional amendment — already passed 36-0 by the Senate — still pending before the House State Government & Elections Committee and needing a House vote to reach the November ballot.

SC.title: EARLY VOTING TRACKER: Record turnout continues for SC primaries
SC.summary: South Carolina's June 9 primary early voting continued to break records, with over 100,000 ballots cast through late May and Democrats turning out at high rates, many citing redistricting concerns as motivation.

SC.title: Democrats point to SC's early voting records in pitch to stay first in 2028
SC.summary: South Carolina Democrats are using the state's record-breaking primary early voting numbers — over 56,000 ballots on day one alone — as an argument for maintaining South Carolina's first-in-the-nation status in the 2028 presidential primary.

SD.title: Election 2026: Five candidates, two seats — District 8 Republican primary to decide South Dakota House race outright
SD.summary: With five Republicans competing for two open South Dakota House seats in District 8 and no general election opposition, the June 2 primary will serve as the de facto general election for these seats.

SD.title: Secretary of State emphasizes safety of South Dakota's election processes
SD.summary: Ahead of the June 2 primary, South Dakota Secretary of State Monae Johnson detailed the state's election security measures: paper-only ballots, photo ID requirements, post-election audits, and no internet connections for tabulating machines.

UT.title: Utah's top election official checked for noncitizens on state's voter rolls. Here's what she found
UT.summary: Utah Lt. Gov. Deidre Henderson's citizenship audit of over 2 million registered voters found 27 confirmed noncitizens now removed from rolls and a software glitch that had allowed some noncitizens to register online, as Utah implements new documentary proof-of-citizenship requirements under HB209 for the 2026 general election.

VT.title: Vermont Gov. Phil Scott is running for reelection
VT.summary: Republican Gov. Phil Scott filed for a sixth two-year term just before the candidate deadline, setting up a contested gubernatorial race in Vermont's August 11 primary and November 3 general election.

VT.title: With two major vacancies, who will lead the Vermont House and Senate?
VT.summary: Both Vermont's House and Senate leaders announced they will not seek reelection, creating major leadership vacancies to be decided in the 2026 elections as the legislature extended its session into late May.

WA.title: WA Secretary of State Responds to USPS Proposed Rule on Ballot Mail
WA.summary: Washington Secretary of State Steve Hobbs pushed back against a Trump administration USPS proposed rule that would require states to share voter lists and mail-ballot barcodes with the Postal Service for federal elections, asserting the President has no constitutional authority over state elections.

WA.title: USPS seeks to require states to submit lists of voters
WA.summary: The Postal Service's new proposed rule would require states to provide voter names and unique ballot barcodes for all federal mail-in ballots, with Washington state officials warning it threatens voter privacy and state sovereignty over elections; the public comment period runs through July 2.

WI.title: Wisconsin Pushes USPS To Fix Absentee Mail Before Next Elections
WI.summary: The bipartisan Wisconsin Elections Commission formally demanded USPS take extraordinary measures to prevent absentee ballot delivery failures ahead of 2026 fall elections, after two-thirds of clerks statewide reported problems in April — including 269 ballots arriving in Milwaukee the morning after Election Day.

WI.title: Officials worry about USPS speed with absentee ballot delivery
WI.summary: Wisconsin election officials raised alarms that USPS mail delays disproportionately affect military and overseas absentee voters and could disenfranchise citizens in upcoming 2026 elections, following what one veteran clerk called the worst delivery failures in nearly three decades.

WI.title: Wisconsin warns USPS over 'unusually long' mail voting delays
WI.summary: Wisconsin Elections Commission formally warned USPS of widespread absentee ballot delivery failures during the April 2026 election, calling for corrective action before upcoming 2026 general election ballots are mailed.

WY.title: Primary election candidates set for Natrona County, state races
WY.summary: Following the close of Wyoming's May 29 candidate filing deadline, the field was set for the August 18 primary with open races for governor, secretary of state, and two congressional seats — among the most consequential Wyoming election contests in years.

AL.title: In amicus brief election experts warn Alabama map switch could upend 2026 vote
AL.summary: A bipartisan coalition of election officials and experts warned the U.S. Supreme Court that Alabama's emergency bid to revive its 2023 congressional map could force local officials to complete months of voter reassignment work in as little as one business day, risking voter confusion and uncounted ballots. The brief supported the Milligan plaintiffs urging the Court to deny Alabama's request for a stay of the federal injunction blocking the map.

AL.title: Alabama groups urge Supreme Court to halt congressional map
AL.summary: Challengers to Alabama's redistricting push urged the Supreme Court not to allow the state to use a congressional map a lower court found likely discriminated against Black voters, arguing justices should keep the court-ordered lines used in 2024. Civil rights groups warned that changing district boundaries now would trigger electoral chaos ahead of the state's August special primary.

AK.title: Alaska primary ballot set: 17 governor candidates, competitive U.S. Senate race and legislature at a crossroads
AK.summary: Following the June 1 filing deadline, Alaska's August 18 primary ballot is set with 17 candidates for the open governor's race — including last-minute entrant former Gov. Bill Walker — after Lt. Gov. Nancy Dahlstrom unexpectedly dropped out. The cycle will also feature a third attempt to repeal Alaska's ranked-choice voting and top-four primary system on the November ballot.

AK.title: Candidate slate finalized for Alaska's statewide elections
AK.summary: The June 1 filing deadline finalized a competitive slate for Alaska's 2026 elections, including a crowded open governor's race and a U.S. Senate race where Democrat Mary Peltola is challenging incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan. Alaska will again use its top-four primary and ranked-choice general election system, though voters will also decide on a ballot initiative to repeal that system.

AZ.title: Arizona Secretary of State's Office accidentally released personal data of 373 protected voters
AZ.summary: Staff at the Arizona Secretary of State's Office accidentally publicly released home addresses and phone numbers of 373 voters enrolled in the state's address confidentiality program — including domestic violence victims and law enforcement officials — with the error going undetected for nearly nine months. The office acknowledged staff failed to follow existing policies that should have prevented the breach.

CA.title: What we know so far about LA and OC voter turnout in the 2026 primary election
CA.summary: With California's June 2 statewide direct primary underway, midday turnout stood at 16% statewide, with L.A. County at about 10% and Orange County at about 22% of registered voters. Republicans have returned proportionally more pre-election mail ballots (21%) than Democrats (16%), with final results not expected until counting concludes around June 26.

CO.title: Colorado elections clerk released from prison after governor commutes sentence
CO.summary: Former Mesa County Clerk Tina Peters was released from prison after Democratic Gov. Jared Polis commuted her nine-year sentence for election equipment tampering, making her eligible for parole after serving less than a quarter of her term. Colorado Secretary of State Jena Griswold warned the release would embolden the election denier movement, and the state Democratic Party formally censured Polis.

DC.title: See a Ranked Choice Ballot from the District of Columbia
DC.summary: A sample ranked choice voting ballot from Washington, D.C. was published ahead of the city's historic June 16 primary — its first-ever use of ranked choice voting, approved by 73% of voters via Initiative 83 in 2024. The ballot allows voters to rank up to five candidates by preference for mayoral, council, congressional delegate, and attorney general races.

GA.title: Georgia's political June: Runoffs, redistricting and a pivotal month ahead
GA.summary: Georgia faces a dense political calendar in June: Republicans hold high-stakes June 16 runoffs for governor and U.S. Senate, while Gov. Kemp called a special legislative session beginning June 17 to redraw congressional and legislative maps following the Supreme Court's Callais ruling.

HI.title: Last Day to File as a Candidate for the 2026 Elections
HI.summary: Hawaii's Office of Elections announced June 2 as the final day to file nomination papers for the 2026 elections, covering more than 100 offices including governor, lieutenant governor, and all state legislative seats, with the primary election scheduled for August 8.

IA.title: Democrats and Republicans think control of Congress runs through Iowa
IA.summary: Both parties view Iowa's June 2 primary as a critical midterm battleground, with open governor and Senate seats drawing national attention; Trump-endorsed Rep. Ashley Hinson leads the Republican Senate primary and Rep. Randy Feenstra is favored in the Republican gubernatorial contest after a late presidential endorsement.

IA.title: Who's running in Iowa's primary? Your voter guide for the June 2 election
IA.summary: Iowa voters head to the polls June 2 to choose party nominees for governor, U.S. Senate, congressional seats, and state legislative offices; polls are open 7 a.m.–8 p.m. and same-day voter registration is available at polling places.

ID.title: Idaho election officials randomly pick eight counties for primary election audits
ID.summary: Idaho Secretary of State officials randomly selected eight counties for post-primary paper ballot audits comparing hand counts to reported results, with all audits scheduled before the June 9 State Board of Canvassers certification meeting.

ID.title: Eight Idaho counties randomly chosen for post-primary election audit
ID.summary: Following Idaho's May 19 primary, which drew about 30% voter turnout, election officials selected eight counties for paper ballot audits to verify results before the State Board of Canvassers certifies the election on June 9.

IN.title: Electability, future of party on minds of delegates as Democrats choose secretary of state nominee
IN.summary: Indiana Democrats gather at their June 6 state convention to choose a secretary of state nominee, pitting well-funded Beau Bayh against progressive challenger Blythe Potter, as both parties seek to fill an office shaken by controversy over Republican incumbent Diego Morales.

IN.title: Secretary of State race getting national attention ahead of the Indiana Republican Convention
IN.summary: Indiana's Republican secretary of state race has drawn national attention ahead of the June 20 convention, as incumbent Diego Morales faces four challengers after U.S. Sen. Jim Banks and other prominent Republicans withdrew their endorsements amid spending and management controversies.

KS.title: Kansas online voter registration remains down ahead of party change deadline
KS.summary: Kansas's online voter registration system was down due to a Department of Revenue systems outage just before the June 1 noon deadline to change party affiliation for the August 4 primary, with officials directing voters to paper registration forms.

KS.title: Kansas Online Voter Registration now restored following systems outage
KS.summary: Kansas restored its online voter registration system Sunday evening after a roughly 24-hour outage, in time for voters to change party affiliation before the June 1 noon deadline ahead of the August 4 primary election.

LA.title: Louisiana approves new congressional map, dismantling majority-Black district
LA.summary: Louisiana Republican lawmakers passed and Gov. Jeff Landry signed a new congressional map eliminating one of the two majority-Black congressional districts, giving the GOP a 5-1 advantage in the delegation. Civil rights groups pledged legal challenges, calling the map a racial gerrymander.

MD.title: Replacement mail-in ballots for Maryland primaries being sent to voters this week
MD.summary: Maryland's Board of Elections mailed replacement ballots after a vendor coding error sent some voters the wrong party's primary ballot for the June 23 primary. Officials confirmed safeguards prevent duplicate voting and all affected voters will receive a correct replacement.

MD.title: Trump calls for DOJ investigation after mail ballot error in Maryland
MD.summary: President Trump called for a Justice Department probe into Maryland's mail-in ballot vendor error, alleging fraud without evidence. Maryland election officials maintained no fraudulent ballots were distributed and that the error was a coding mistake by the state's print vendor.

ME.title: Two Maine primary races may come down to a ranked-choice runoff. Here's how the process works
ME.summary: Maine Public explained ranked-choice voting ahead of the June 9 primary, noting the crowded Democratic and Republican gubernatorial races and the Democratic U.S. Senate primary may all require multiple rounds of tabulation. Voters can rank candidates by preference; if no one wins a first-round majority, lower-ranked candidates are eliminated and votes redistributed.

ME.title: How ranked-choice voting will work in Maine's wide-open June primaries
ME.summary: With Maine's primary one week away, the Bangor Daily News explained how ranked-choice voting applies across multiple June 9 primary races, noting that candidates in the crowded gubernatorial contests are openly coordinating second-choice strategies with rivals.

MI.title: MDOS announces changes to automatic voter registration process to comply with Michigan election law
