MO.summary: KCUR's coverage of the ongoing legal dispute in which Missouri courts have repeatedly rewritten Secretary of State Hoskins' ballot descriptions for measures including the redistricting referendum, raising concerns about fair voter access to accurate ballot information ahead of the August 4 primary.

NC.title: GOP groups claim victory in dispute over NC 'never resident' voters
NC.summary: A Wake County Superior Court judge ruled that U.S. citizens born overseas to North Carolina parents who never actually lived in the state cannot register or vote in any North Carolina election, a significant change to voter eligibility rules.

NC.title: Judge confirms GOP victory in voting dispute over 'never residents'
NC.summary: A North Carolina judge formally confirmed the ruling barring 'never resident' overseas voters from casting ballots in state and federal elections, affecting overseas military-adjacent families whose parents last lived in North Carolina but who themselves never established residency there.

ND.title: Prevailing PSC candidates say campaign work not done with Dem opponents on horizon
ND.summary: Republican candidates who won North Dakota's June 9 Public Service Commission primary races are looking ahead to November matchups against Democratic opponents, in a state where Democrats are contesting all major statewide races for the first time since 2020.

NE.title: Second former Nebraska lawmaker mulling nonpartisan run, including for secretary of state
NE.summary: Former state Sen. Bob Krist is considering a nonpartisan candidacy for Nebraska secretary of state, which could reshape the November contest between Republican Scott Petersen — who upset incumbent Bob Evnen in the primary — and Democrat Sarah Slattery in a race that will determine who oversees Nebraska's elections.

NH.title: 2026 NH elections to watch: Governor, US and state Senate, House fields are set
NH.summary: With New Hampshire's June 12 candidate filing deadline closed, the fields for the September 8 primary are set across all major races — including an open U.S. Senate seat, governor, both U.S. House seats, the Executive Council, and the state legislature.

NV.title: Who voted in Nevada's 2026 primary? Turnout up slightly, still about 20%
NV.summary: Following Nevada's June 9 primary, overall voter turnout came in around 20% — slightly above 2024 — with mail ballots accounting for about 60% of votes cast and roughly 46,000 more Nevadans voting than in the prior primary cycle.

NY.title: Early Voting Underway in New York for June Primaries
NY.summary: Early voting began June 13 for New York's June 23 primary election, with over 16,000 ballots cast in New York City alone on the first day; competitive races include NY-10 (Goldman vs. Lander) and a contested state comptroller primary.

OH.title: Ohio voters to decide voter ID amendment in November, one of five voter ID ballot measures in 2026
OH.summary: Ohio lawmakers advanced a constitutional amendment requiring photo ID for both in-person and absentee voting to the November 2026 ballot, while also passing a separate bill requiring absentee voters to submit a copy of their photo ID starting in 2027.

OK.title: State Election Board Offers Tips and Reminders Ahead of June 16 Primary
OK.summary: Oklahoma's State Election Board reminded voters of requirements for the June 16 primary: closed party primaries, mandatory photo ID, and early voting open June 11-13; over 635 positions are on the ballot including governor, U.S. Senate, and State Question 832 on raising the minimum wage.

OK.title: Oklahoma Voice launches voter guide ahead of June 16 primary election
OK.summary: Oklahoma Voice released a comprehensive voter guide for the June 16 primary covering all statewide and federal candidates, including 9 Republican gubernatorial candidates, the open U.S. Senate race, and State Question 832 on raising the minimum wage to $15 per hour.

PA.title: Democratic registration drops in key midterm districts
PA.summary: Democrats lost more than 275,000 registered voters across 28 competitive congressional districts from November 2024 to May 2026, including Pennsylvania swing districts, a trend with potential implications for Democratic competitiveness in the November 2026 elections.

RI.title: TGIF: Ian Donnis' Rhode Island politics roundup for June 12, 2026
RI.summary: The weekly Rhode Island politics roundup covers the close of the legislative session with the Rhode Island Voting Rights Act failing to advance to a floor vote, and previews the September 9 Democratic gubernatorial primary between incumbent Dan McKee and challenger Helena Foulkes.

SC.title: Democratic Party runoff in 1st Congressional District may go without debate before June 23
SC.summary: Mac Deford accepted a debate invitation from two Lowcountry TV stations while fellow Democratic runoff candidate Nancy Lacore declined, potentially leaving South Carolina's 1st Congressional District June 23 runoff without a head-to-head forum before voters decide.

SD.title: Early voting begins in South Dakota governor runoff
SD.summary: Early in-person voting opened for South Dakota's historic first gubernatorial runoff between Republican Gov. Larry Rhoden and businessman Toby Doeden, after neither cleared the 35% threshold in the June 2 primary; the runoff is scheduled for July 28.

TX.title: Election results: June 13 North Texas runoff
TX.summary: Voters across North Texas returned to the polls on June 13 for local municipal runoffs resulting from the May 2 Uniform Election Date, including races for mayoral and city council positions across the region.

TX.title: Terry Lynne leads Jaime Rivas by 25 votes in razor-thin Farmers Branch mayoral runoff, unofficial returns show
TX.summary: Incumbent Mayor Terry Lynne narrowly edged Jaime Rivas by just 25 votes (50.32% to 49.7%) in the June 13 Farmers Branch mayoral runoff, one of the tightest local races in Texas's June 13 runoff elections.

UT.title: 2026 primary elections in Northern Utah: candidate profiles for Weber, Davis counties
UT.summary: Candidate profiles for competitive Weber and Davis county races ahead of Utah's June 23 primary election, where mail-in ballots were mailed June 2 and must be received by 8 p.m. on Election Day under a new state law tightening mail ballot deadlines.

WI.title: Democrats make their pitch for governor at annual state convention
WI.summary: All seven Democratic candidates for Wisconsin governor spoke at the WisDems Convention in Madison, making their cases to succeed term-limited Gov. Tony Evers ahead of the August 11 primary.

WI.title: Wisconsin Democrats make their case in crowded governor primary
WI.summary: Seven Democratic governor candidates pitched voters on affordability and beating the Republican nominee at Wisconsin's Democratic Party annual state convention, with the August 11 primary approaching.

AK.title: Senate candidate with same name as incumbent Dan Sullivan ineligible for ballot, official rules
AK.summary: Alaska's Division of Elections director ruled that a U.S. Senate candidate named Dan Sullivan cannot appear on the August 18 primary ballot, finding his candidacy was filed to confuse voters and not in good faith as a genuine bid for office.

AK.title: Alaska candidate with same name as Sen. Dan Sullivan disqualified by election official
AK.summary: Alaska's election director formally disqualified a Republican Senate candidate sharing the name Dan Sullivan with the incumbent senator, citing his attempt to register using the senator's middle initial as evidence of intent to mislead voters.

AZ.title: Republican legislators put measure to change voting procedures on November ballot
AZ.summary: Arizona Republicans approved a ballot referral requiring mail-ballot voter ID, restricting voting centers, and requiring citizenship-only voting, sending it directly to November voters and bypassing Governor Hobbs's veto authority.

CA.title: California Secretary of State Announces Certification of Congressional District 1 Special Primary Election Results
CA.summary: California Secretary of State Shirley Weber certified the June 2 Congressional District 1 Special Primary Election results on June 11, with the winner advancing to a special general election to fill the remainder of the congressional term.

CA.title: Vote counting winding down in LA and OC
CA.summary: As of June 12, Los Angeles County reported approximately 37.7% voter turnout in the June 2 primary with outstanding ballots still under signature verification, while Orange County estimated 43% and statewide turnout reached 40.3%.

DC.title: AP Decision Notes: What to expect in the Washington, DC, primary
DC.summary: AP overview of DC's unprecedented June 16 primary, the first to use ranked-choice voting, with voters choosing among competitive Democratic fields for mayor, House delegate, and four council seats amid federal intervention in the district.

FL.title: Candidates across the state swarm ballot as qualifying period ends; some win by default
FL.summary: After Florida's candidate qualifying closed June 12, Rep. Byron Donalds leads the Republican field for governor with Trump's endorsement, while David Jolly is the Democratic frontrunner; hundreds of candidates qualified for legislative and congressional seats under a new Republican-leaning map.

HI.title: The Elections Commission Is Struggling To Elect A New Leader
HI.summary: Hawaii's Elections Commission is deadlocked over choosing a new chair before current chair Mike Curtis's term expires June 30, raising concerns about election oversight and continuity heading into the August 8 primary election.

ID.title: Idaho primary election results certified
ID.summary: Idaho's State Board of Canvassers certified primary election results on June 9, officially opening the window for candidates to request recounts; 11,087 Idahoans registered and voted on Election Day following county-level audits across all 44 counties.

LA.title: No-party voters still have access to Louisiana's closed primaries, for now
LA.summary: In Louisiana's first year of closed party primaries, unaffiliated voters who chose a party in May's primary can vote in the June 27 runoffs, but the long-term status of no-party voter access to the closed primary system remains legally uncertain.

NM.title: Board of Canvass Certifies 2026 Primary Election Results
NM.summary: Bernalillo County's Board of Canvass officially certified the results of New Mexico's June 2 primary election on June 15, completing post-election certification for the state's most populous county following the historic first semi-open primary.

NY.title: More than 16,500 New Yorkers cast ballots on first day of early voting
NY.summary: More than 16,500 New Yorkers voted on the first day of early voting (June 13) for the June 23 primary, led by Manhattan at 7,581 ballots; competitive races include the NY-10 Goldman vs. Lander contest.

NY.title: More than 44,000 New Yorkers cast ballots in first three days of early voting
NY.summary: Through June 15, over 44,000 NYC residents had cast early ballots for the June 23 primary, with Manhattan leading at 19,216 and Brooklyn at 11,438; early voting continues through June 21 before Primary Day.

VA.title: Wittman seeks to keep 1st District seat, as Democratic challengers face crowded primary
VA.summary: Democratic contenders are lining up to challenge longtime Republican incumbent Rob Wittman in Virginia's 1st congressional district, with early voting for the August 4 primary beginning June 18.

VA.title: Early Voting for Aug. 4 Primary Election Begins June 18
VA.summary: Virginia Beach and other Virginia localities announced that early in-person voting for the August 4 primary election begins June 18, with absentee ballots to be mailed no later than June 19 and a voter registration deadline of July 24.

WA.title: These new Washington laws take effect Thursday
WA.summary: More than 200 new Washington state laws took effect June 11, including major expansions to the state's Voting Rights Act: HB 1750 bars election policies creating material disparate burdens on protected-class voters, HB 1710 reinstates preclearance requirements.

WA.title: More than 200 new laws now in effect in Washington state
WA.summary: Washington state's package of new laws effective June 11 includes significant voting rights enhancements: preclearance requirements for jurisdictions with histories of discrimination and tighter rules for challenging voter registrations.

WY.title: Wyoming Supreme Court considers constitutionality of crossover-voting ban
WY.summary: Wyoming Supreme Court justices heard oral arguments challenging the constitutionality of the state's crossover-voting ban and party affiliation restrictions. Plaintiffs argue the laws violate Wyoming constitutional provisions requiring open, free, and equal elections.

AL.title: A voter guide to Alabama's primary runoffs
AL.summary: A comprehensive voter guide covering Alabama's June 16 primary runoff elections for five statewide Republican contests including U.S. Senate (Barry Moore vs. Jared Hudson), Attorney General (Katherine Robertson vs. Jay Mitchell), and Lieutenant Governor (John Wahl vs. Wes Allen).

AL.title: What to know: Alabama 2026 Primary Runoff Election
AL.summary: A pre-election explainer for Alabama's June 16 primary runoff detailing the five statewide races and multiple legislative runoffs, runoff rules requiring a majority vote, and what voters need to know before heading to the polls.

AL.title: Alabama Runoff Election Day 2026: What Central Alabama Voters Need to Know
AL.summary: Alabama voters headed to polls June 16 for statewide and local primary runoff elections with polls open 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Statewide Republican runoffs include U.S. Senate, Attorney General, Lieutenant Governor, Agriculture Commissioner, and Public Service Commission.

AL.title: Trump-Backed US Rep. Barry Moore Battles Ex-Navy SEAL Jared Hudson in GOP Senate Runoff in Alabama
AL.summary: Trump-endorsed Rep. Barry Moore and former Navy SEAL Jared Hudson faced off in the Republican primary runoff for Alabama's open U.S. Senate seat on June 16, with the winner set to face a Democrat in November for the seat vacated by Tommy Tuberville, who is running for governor.

AL.title: Alabama Senate Primary Runoff Election 2026 Live Results
AL.summary: Live results coverage of Alabama's June 16 Republican U.S. Senate primary runoff between Trump-backed Rep. Barry Moore and ex-Navy SEAL Jared Hudson, determining the GOP nominee who will face the Democratic nominee in November for the seat Tommy Tuberville is vacating.

AK.title: Alaska election official threatens to disqualify Republican who shares name with Sen. Dan Sullivan
AK.summary: Alaska's Division of Elections director threatened to disqualify a U.S. Senate candidate named Dan J. Sullivan from the August primary ballot, citing concerns that he registered as a Republican only days before filing and that his campaign materials appeared designed to mimic incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan's branding to confuse voters.

AK.title: Alaska formally disqualifies namesake challenger to Sen. Dan Sullivan from appearing on the ballot
AK.summary: The Alaska Division of Elections officially removed a same-named Senate candidate from the August primary ballot, with the elections director concluding the filing was intended to create voter confusion rather than represent a legitimate candidacy for the U.S. Senate seat.

AK.title: How a change to mail-in voting could impact Alaska's most rural voters
AK.summary: Changes to Alaska's mail-in voting procedures could disproportionately affect small rural communities that rely heavily on absentee ballots, where weather delays and mail delivery challenges already complicate participation in elections.

AZ.title: This week at the Arizona Legislature: Which ballot measures will go before voters in November?
AZ.summary: KJZZ previewed the final days of Arizona's 2026 legislative session and the pending ballot measures on voting procedures, including the voter ID for mail ballots referendum, that lawmakers were poised to send to November voters.

AZ.title: Key dates and essential information for Arizona's Primary Election
AZ.summary: A comprehensive voter guide for Arizona's July 21 primary covering key deadlines: voter registration closes June 22, early voting begins June 24, and mail ballot requests are due by July 10. Also notes a new 2026 rule allowing mail ballot drop-off voters to skip signature verification by showing ID at drop-off.

AZ.title: Here are the 10 measures lawmakers sent to the Arizona ballot in November
AZ.summary: Arizona's Republican-controlled legislature passed 10 ballot referendums for November including voter ID requirements for mail ballots, transgender bathroom restrictions, and school voucher reforms, significantly adding to the measures voters will decide in 2026.

AZ.title: Arizona ballot measure to change voting rules will be decided in 2026 election
AZ.summary: Republican legislators placed HCR 2001 on the November 2026 ballot, which would require all voters including mail voters to show government-issued ID and would require voters to request a mail ballot before each biennial general election rather than staying on a continuous early voting list.

AZ.title: Republican legislators put measure to change voting procedures on November ballot
AZ.summary: The Arizona Legislature voted along party lines to place the Fast, Accurate, Secure, Transparent Election Results Act on the November ballot — a measure that would add voter ID requirements for mail ballots and other voting procedure changes — circumventing Governor Hobbs's veto power.

AR.title: Republican nominee selected to run for late Arkansas lawmaker's House seat
AR.summary: Bill Teeter was selected as the Republican nominee for the House District 44 special election after winning the June 2 primary following the death of Rep. Stan Berry. Teeter is set to face Nikki Phillips in a June 30 runoff, though Phillips indicated she may withdraw.

CA.title: Hernandez strengthens second-place hold in bid for runoff with Wahab for Congressional District 14
CA.summary: As vote-counting from California's June 2 primary continued, BART Director Melissa Hernandez consolidated her second-place position among candidates for the vacant CD-14 seat, setting up a two-Democrat field alongside front-runner state Sen. Aisha Wahab for the June 16 special primary.

CA.title: Republican Steve Hilton advances to November governor's election
CA.summary: After several days of post-primary ballot-counting, Republican Steve Hilton was confirmed as advancing to the November general election to face Democrat Xavier Becerra for California governor, while billionaire Tom Steyer, who spent $215 million on his campaign, was eliminated.

CA.title: Vote counting winding down in LA and OC
CA.summary: Statewide voter turnout in California's June 2 primary reached 40.3%, with LA County at 37.7% and Orange County at about 43%; approximately 140,000 outstanding vote-by-mail ballots remained to be counted in LA County as late as June 13.

CA.title: Aisha Wahab takes early lead in race to replace ex-congressman Eric Swalwell in CA's 14th Congressional District
CA.summary: California held a special primary on June 16 to fill the congressional seat vacated by Eric Swalwell. State Sen. Aisha Wahab led early results with about 34% of the vote, with BART Director Melissa Hernandez in second at 16%; since no candidate cleared 50%, a two-Democrat runoff is set for August 18.

CO.title: Colorado Secretary of State candidates tout their experience at Democrat gathering
CO.summary: Democratic candidates for Colorado Secretary of State — state Sen. Jessie Danielson and Jefferson County Clerk Amanda Gonzalez — made their pitches at DemFest, with both emphasizing support for election clerks and fighting election misinformation ahead of the June 30 primary.

CO.title: County Clerks May Begin Mailing Ballots for the 2026 Primary Election
CO.summary: Colorado county clerks began mailing ballots to all active registered voters on June 8 for the June 30 primary, with unaffiliated voters receiving both Democratic and Republican ballots. The deadline for initial mail ballots to reach voters was June 12, with 137 voting centers and 437 drop boxes opening later in June.

CO.title: Record-breaking fundraising, billionaire-backed super PACs shape Colorado governor's race
CO.summary: The Colorado Democratic gubernatorial primary has drawn record-breaking outside money, with billionaire-backed super PACs pouring millions into the Bennet-Weiser race in the final weeks before the June 30 primary.

CO.title: Michael Bennet, Phil Weiser clash over ambition and housing in last major debate before Democratic primary
CO.summary: U.S. Sen. Michael Bennet and AG Phil Weiser faced off in their final debate ahead of the June 30 primary, clashing over housing affordability, healthcare, and how each would resist the Trump administration.

CO.title: Michael Bennet loans his campaign for governor $1M as support from Michael Bloomberg surpasses $4.6M
CO.summary: Michael Bennet loaned his campaign $1 million while Michael Bloomberg's super PAC support for Bennet surpassed $4.6 million, with the PAC spending heavily on ads in the final stretch before the June 30 Democratic primary for governor.

CT.title: Finished with fundraising, Josh Elliott goes on the road
CT.summary: Josh Elliott's campaign to challenge Gov. Ned Lamont in the August 11 Democratic primary reached a fundraising milestone, topping $335,500 to qualify for a $3.75 million public grant under Connecticut's Citizens' Election Program; Elliott then pivoted to grassroots outreach around the state.

DE.title: Delaware seeks state-level voting rights legislation post U.S. Supreme Court decision
DE.summary: Delaware lawmakers introduced HB444, the Delaware John Lewis Voting Rights Act, as the first state-level response to the U.S. Supreme Court's Callais v. Louisiana ruling that weakened federal voting rights protections, banning election practices that suppress or discriminate against voters.

DE.title: AG Jennings defeats Koch billionaire-backed effort to upend Delaware's election transparency laws
DE.summary: A federal district court rejected Americans for Prosperity's First Amendment challenge to the Delaware Elections Disclosure Act, which requires third-party campaign advertisers to disclose donors, preserving Delaware's campaign finance transparency requirements.

DE.title: Millsboro incumbents keep seats in 2026 council election
DE.summary: All three incumbent Millsboro town council members retained their seats in the June 13 municipal election, with Ron O'Neal defeating challenger Stephen Webster in District 2 by a 104-87 margin, while Gary Mack and Marty Presley ran unopposed.

DE.title: ACLU of Delaware appeals dismissal of its case against Fenwick Island
DE.summary: The ACLU of Delaware appealed to the Delaware Supreme Court after a judge dismissed its lawsuit challenging Fenwick Island's town charter, which allows corporations, LLCs, and trusts that own property in the town to cast votes in local elections in violation of the Delaware Constitution's Elections Clause.

FL.title: Florida Supreme Court rejects challenge to new GOP-drawn congressional maps
FL.summary: The Florida Supreme Court issued a 6-1 ruling declining to block the new DeSantis-backed congressional redistricting map, saying it lacked jurisdiction while the case remains in lower courts. The decision locks in a map expected to shift Florida's congressional delegation to a 24-4 Republican advantage.

FL.title: Byron Donalds continues fundraising domination in Florida governor's race
FL.summary: As Florida's candidate qualifying period closed, Trump-endorsed Republican Rep. Byron Donalds officially entered the governor's race with $65.8 million combined cash on hand, far outpacing rival candidates ahead of the August 18 primary.

FL.title: Candidates across the state swarm ballot as qualifying period ends; some win by default
FL.summary: Florida's candidate qualifying period closed June 12, setting the field for the August 18 primary under the new Republican-drawn congressional map, with hundreds of candidates qualifying and some races decided by default where no opponent filed.

FL.title: How Florida's new congressional map is shaking up the 2026 election
FL.summary: Florida's newly redrawn congressional districts, with 21 of 28 reworked, are scrambling incumbent matchups and forcing voters into new districts ahead of the August 18 primary, with the Florida Supreme Court's refusal to block the map now confirmed.

GA.title: Georgia's vote-counting method will soon be banned. Lawmakers will try to find a fix this week
GA.summary: Georgia lawmakers prepared to convene a special legislative session on June 17 to address the looming July 1 deadline banning QR codes in ballot tabulation, with no approved replacement system in place and counties weighing a switch to hand-marked paper ballots.

GA.title: Georgia primary runoff elections live results 2026: Collins, Dooley vie for Senate
GA.summary: Georgia held its June 16 primary runoff elections featuring Republican contests for U.S. Senate (Collins vs. Dooley) and governor (Jones vs. Jackson), with approximately 485,000 Georgians having cast early ballots, reflecting higher Republican than Democratic early turnout.

ID.title: State of Idaho certifies May 2026 primary election results
ID.summary: Idaho's State Board of Canvassers officially certified the May 19 primary election results without changes to any races, with statewide voter turnout at 30.1%, slightly above the 2024 primary, setting up November general election matchups.

IN.title: Indiana rejects, cancels voter registration for more than half of flagged immigrant Hoosiers
IN.summary: Indiana has rejected or canceled voter registrations for more than 60% of immigrants challenged under the state's new proof-of-citizenship law, with 644 prospective voters rejected and 981 existing registrations canceled, prompting voting rights groups to seek emergency court relief ahead of November.

IA.title: Defeated GOP challenger urges voters to oppose Hinson in Iowa Senate race
IA.summary: Former Iowa Republican Senate primary candidate Jim Carlin announced he will not endorse primary winner Rep. Ashley Hinson, urging his supporters not to vote for her in the November general election against Democrat Josh Turek in what has become a competitive Senate race.

KS.title: Judge refuses to block election official from dissolving No Labels Kansas party
KS.summary: A Kansas judge declined to block Secretary of State Scott Schwab's move to dissolve the No Labels Kansas party and remove its candidates from the November ballot, clearing the way for the State Objections Board to formally uphold the decision.

KS.title: Kansas State Objections Board strikes No Labels party from ballot, along with Democrat in House race
KS.summary: The Kansas State Objections Board upheld the secretary of state's decision not to recognize the No Labels Kansas party, denying two candidates ballot access for the general election, and also rejected a Democrat's challenge after her mailed filing arrived hours past deadline.

LA.title: Early voting starts for June 27 party runoffs
LA.summary: Early voting opened in Louisiana for the June 27 party runoffs for U.S. Senate, Public Service Commission, and state school board, with polls open through June 20; only registered party members who voted in the May 16 primary are eligible to participate in their party's runoff.

LA.title: Early voting underway for Oklahoma primary, Louisiana runoff elections
LA.summary: Early voting was underway across Louisiana for the June 27 party primary runoffs, including the Republican U.S. Senate contest between Julia Letlow and John Fleming, as the state navigates a changed election calendar following Supreme Court-ordered congressional redistricting.

LA.title: Louisiana voters head to the polls in Senate runoffs
LA.summary: Louisiana voters were heading to early voting sites ahead of the June 27 U.S. Senate party runoffs, with Republican frontrunner Julia Letlow facing John Fleming and Democrats choosing between Gary Crockett and Jamie Davis as party nominees for the November general election.

ME.title: Three Maine races are headed to ranked-choice voting. Here's what happens next.
ME.summary: The Maine Secretary of State announced three primary races — Democratic governor, Republican governor, and Democratic Congressional District 2 — will proceed to ranked choice voting tabulation after no candidate won a majority of first-choice votes on June 9, with counting set to begin June 12 in Augusta.

ME.title: Ranked-choice voting counting continues in key Maine races
ME.summary: Ranked-choice vote counting is underway in Augusta for Maine's 2026 gubernatorial and congressional primaries, with Nirav Shah leading the Democratic governor race at 27% followed closely by Hannah Pingree, Troy Jackson, and Shenna Bellows, and Bobby Charles holding a lead in the Republican race.

ME.title: Maine Secretary of State's Office announces additional races for Ranked Choice Voting tabulations, recounts
ME.summary: The Maine Secretary of State announced that two additional legislative races — House District 58 Republican and Senate District 4 Republican — will proceed to ranked-choice voting tabulation, while three other races will go to recounts, extending Maine's post-primary certification process.

MD.title: Early voting begins for Maryland's 2026 Primary election. Here are the key races to watch.
MD.summary: In-person early voting opened June 11 across Maryland for the 2026 Gubernatorial Primary Election, running through June 18, with voters choosing among eight Republican and two Democratic candidates for governor ahead of the June 23 primary.

MD.title: Maryland's 2026 primary: Early voting, mail-in deadlines and more
MD.summary: A comprehensive guide to Maryland's 2026 primary election logistics including early voting dates running June 11-18, the June 16 mail-in request deadline, same-day voter registration at early voting centers, and the key statewide contests on the June 23 primary ballot.

MI.title: Michigan Senate Democrats adopt state voter bill of rights
MI.summary: The Michigan Senate passed four bills creating the Michigan Voting Rights Act along party lines, aimed at protecting ballot access for voters of every language, race, and ability, in response to weakened federal voting protections and threats to restrict mail-in voting ahead of the November midterms.

MN.title: Candidates Certified for 2026 Primary Election
MN.summary: The Minnesota Secretary of State certified all candidates for federal and state offices in the August 11 Primary Election, with some minor party and independent candidate petitions finalized by June 16; absentee voting for the primary opens June 26.

MN.title: Minnesota Poll: DFL leads for governor, senate, but undecided voters still a factor
MN.summary: A KARE 11/Star Tribune poll of 800 registered voters (conducted June 8-10) found DFL candidates lead Minnesota's top races, with Amy Klobuchar ahead of Republican rivals for governor by 11-17 points, though a large share of undecided voters remains a significant factor.

MN.title: Minnesota DFL primary for U.S. Senate heats up between Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan and Rep. Angie Craig
MN.summary: The Minnesota DFL Senate primary is heating up between DFL-endorsed Lt. Governor Peggy Flanagan and four-term Congresswoman Angie Craig, with Flanagan holding a polling edge but Craig leading in fundraising with nearly $5 million cash on hand ahead of the August 11 primary.

MS.title: National redistricting battle turns to statehouses and city councils
MS.summary: Following the Supreme Court's Louisiana v. Callais ruling narrowing Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, the redistricting battle is turning to state legislatures and local governments, with Mississippi Republicans potentially pursuing legislative redistricting before 2027 elections.

MO.title: Missouri courts keep rewriting 'unfair' ballot language as fights over direct democracy intensify
MO.summary: Missouri courts have now rejected or rewritten Secretary of State Denny Hoskins' ballot summary language five times on measures involving abortion, redistricting, public education, private-school funding, and the initiative-petition process, as fights over direct democracy intensify ahead of multiple 2026 ballot measures.

MO.title: Local election officials go with Missouri's gerrymandered congressional map despite uncertainty
MO.summary: Missouri local election officials began mailing August 4 primary ballots to military and overseas voters using the contested Republican-drawn congressional map, even as the Secretary of State has not yet officially certified a referendum challenge that has qualified with sufficient signatures.

MT.title: Campaign behind Montana ballot initiative to add nonpartisan judicial elections to the state constitution submits signatures for November
MT.summary: The campaign behind Montana Constitutional Initiative 132 submitted more than 100,000 signatures to county officials — well above the 60,241 required — to place a measure on the November ballot that would enshrine nonpartisan judicial elections in the Montana Constitution.

NE.title: Nebraska secretary of state plans to comply with presidential election order
NE.summary: Secretary of State Bob Evnen announced Nebraska will comply with Trump's executive order on election integrity for the November general election, including providing voter mail lists to the federal government, though the state already meets many of the order's requirements.

NE.title: Dan Osborn's Senate campaign submits 12,700 petition signatures, all but confirming a place on Nebraska's general election ballot
NE.summary: Independent U.S. Senate candidate Dan Osborn submitted over 12,700 petition signatures to the Nebraska Secretary of State, well exceeding the 4,000 required to appear on the November ballot as a third-party candidate against incumbent Sen. Pete Ricketts.

NE.title: Nebraska's third party voices are growing. What does that mean for this election cycle?
NE.summary: Nebraska is seeing a rise in independent candidates ahead of the 2026 general election, with political scientists noting more voters and candidates willing to run outside the two-party system, exemplified by Dan Osborn's high-profile Senate bid.

NV.title: Nevada 2026 primary results: Lombardo and Ford set to face-off for governor
NV.summary: Gov. Joseph Lombardo won the Republican primary with around 90% of the vote, while Democratic Attorney General Aaron Ford won his primary with about 63%, setting up a competitive November governor's race in this battleground state.

NV.title: 15 big takeaways from Nevada's 2026 primary elections
NV.summary: Trump's endorsements went undefeated in Nevada's primary, overall turnout was about 20%, and women made a strong showing with both attorney general candidates advancing to the general election being female.

NV.title: Who voted in Nevada's 2026 primary? Turnout up slightly, still about 20%
NV.summary: Nevada's 2026 primary saw approximately 20% voter turnout, a slight increase over the prior cycle, driven by competitive local races including one Assemblymember losing reelection by just 44 votes.

NV.title: Nevada Secretary of State issues second update on 2026 primary ballot count
NV.summary: Nevada's Secretary of State reported that most counties had tabulated more than 90% of mail ballots from the June 9 primary, with ballot processing continuing through June 13 and a signature cure deadline of June 15 for eligible voters.

NH.title: Hitting the trail: Candidate filing period continues at NH State House
NH.summary: New Hampshire's candidate filing period for the September 8 primary is underway, with notable filings including Rep. Chris Pappas for U.S. Senate and Gov. Kelly Ayotte for reelection, with the deadline set for June 12.

NH.title: 2026 Candidate Filing Update: Who's in? Who's Out?
NH.summary: A roundup of New Hampshire's candidate filings for the September 8 primary covering the open U.S. Senate seat, with former Sen. John Sununu and Scott Brown expected on the Republican side and Rep. Chris Pappas running for Democrats.

NJ.title: How did Democrat Adam Hamawy win the 12th Congressional District in N.J.?
NJ.summary: Analysis of how political newcomer Adam Hamawy defeated 12 other candidates in New Jersey's 12th Congressional District Democratic primary, credited in part to the elimination of the controversial county-line ballot system and a pro-Palestinian super PAC's $1.5 million in spending.

NJ.title: Justin Murphy's Chances Against Cory Booker In NJ Senate Race
NJ.summary: After winning the Republican Senate primary with just 33% of the vote, Justin Murphy faces a steep climb against incumbent Cory Booker in a state that has not sent a Republican to the U.S. Senate since 1972, with prediction markets giving Booker over a 90% chance of winning.

NM.title: Trail Notes: One NM election cycle ends…another begins
NM.summary: A post-primary roundup noting that 24.6% of New Mexico's 1.4 million registered voters participated in the June 2 primary, with the State Board of Canvass scheduled to certify results on June 23 and endorsement dynamics following Deb Haaland's gubernatorial primary victory.

NM.title: Independent NM governor candidate sues Secretary of State over 'unjust burden' to make ballot
NM.summary: Independent candidate Ken Miyagishima filed suit against the New Mexico Secretary of State, arguing that ballot-access requirements for independent gubernatorial candidates are an unconstitutional burden compared to major-party candidates.

NY.title: New York Democrats unveil their own mid-decade redistricting scheme, targeting future elections
NY.summary: New York legislative Democrats advanced a constitutional amendment that would allow mid-decade redistricting and remove the state's ban on partisan gerrymandering, aimed at netting two to three additional congressional seats in 2028 if eventually approved by voters.

NY.title: New York Lawmakers Approve Amendment Allowing Mid-Decade Redistricting and Partisan Map-Drawing
NY.summary: The New York Legislature approved on party-line votes a constitutional amendment permitting mid-decade congressional redistricting and removing the prohibition on partisan gerrymandering, marking the first of two required legislative passages before a voter referendum can be held.

NY.title: How and when to vote early in New York's 2026 primary election
NY.summary: New York's primary early voting period opened June 13, with the NYC Board of Elections reporting over 16,000 ballots cast on the first day. Election Day is June 23, with competitive races including Brad Lander vs. Rep. Dan Goldman in NY-10 and a crowded field in NY-12.

NC.title: NC House elections bill adds requirements for overseas voters, allows for more partisan staff
NC.summary: North Carolina's sweeping elections omnibus bill would require military and overseas voters to submit documentation of their most recent NC address with registration applications, and would allow political parties to place additional partisan staff inside county election offices.

NC.title: NC House starts moving sweeping elections bill, plans to pass it this week despite opposition
NC.summary: North Carolina House Republicans fast-tracked HB 958, a 37-page omnibus elections bill that would allow any county resident to challenge another's right to vote, ban ranked-choice voting, give the state auditor power to select counties for post-election audits, and ban overseas 'never-resident' voters from state elections.

NC.title: Proposed NC election law would increase secrecy for political donors, change audit rules
NC.summary: North Carolina's HB 958 would raise campaign finance disclosure thresholds to shield more donors from public reporting and create a new statewide post-election audit process, while also prohibiting election officials from encouraging voter turnout.

ND.title: Cass County turnout drives early in-person voting in North Dakota primary
ND.summary: Cass County accounted for an outsize share of North Dakota's early voting ahead of the June 9 primary, with nearly double the early voters compared to 2024, driven largely by the competitive Fargo mayoral race rather than statewide contests.

ND.title: 2026 North Dakota primary election results in statewide and legislative races
ND.summary: Incumbent U.S. Rep. Julie Fedorchak won the Republican primary with 73% of the vote against challenger Alex Balazs, while several sitting state legislators lost their primary races; total turnout across the June 9 primary was 125,101 votes.

ND.title: Voter turnout in North Dakota at about 21% for primary
ND.summary: North Dakota's June 9 primary saw roughly 21% voter participation — 125,101 total ballots — on par with historical averages, with absentee and early voting accounting for about 41% of all ballots cast.

OH.title: Ohio Republican lawmakers pass bill requiring absentee voters show a copy of their ID to vote
OH.summary: The Ohio House passed 61-27 a bill requiring absentee voters to provide a copy of a driver's license or state ID beginning with the November 2027 general election, sending it to Gov. Mike DeWine for his signature.

OH.title: Ohio Republican lawmakers send constitutional amendment requiring voter photo ID to ballot
OH.summary: Ohio lawmakers passed SJR 10 on a 61-27 vote to place a constitutional amendment on the November 2026 ballot that would require photo ID for in-person voting, with an alternative verification process included for voters with religious objections to being photographed.

OH.title: Ohio voters to decide voter ID amendment in November, one of five voter ID ballot measures in 2026
OH.summary: Ohio will join Nevada, North Carolina, and Wisconsin as one of multiple states with voter ID measures on the November 2026 ballot, placing the state at the center of a national debate over election access and photo identification requirements.

OH.title: Ohio will be one of six states with a voter ID measure on the ballot this year
OH.summary: An updated count identifies six states with voter ID constitutional amendments or measures on the November 2026 ballot, with Ohio's measure covering both in-person photo ID requirements and new mail-in ballot identification rules.

OK.title: Oklahoma primary elections: What voters need to know
OK.summary: A voter guide published ahead of Oklahoma's June 16 primary covering closed primary rules, the three-day early voting window (June 11-13), photo ID requirements for all voters, and the major open-seat races for governor and U.S. Senate.

OK.title: Oklahoma primary election results 2026 live updates
OK.summary: The Washington Post's live updates covered Oklahoma's June 16 primary contests, including Trump-endorsed Rep. Kevin Hern's run for the open U.S. Senate seat vacated by Markwayne Mullin and a crowded gubernatorial primary to succeed term-limited Gov. Kevin Stitt.

PA.title: Pennsylvania begins audit of statewide primary election results
PA.summary: Pennsylvania's Department of State launched a post-election risk-limiting audit following the May 19 primary, using a publicly conducted dice roll to generate a random audit seed, with counties required to complete the audit and certify results before June 8.

PA.title: Post election audits confirm Pennsylvania Primary's accuracy
PA.summary: Pennsylvania completed a risk-limiting audit of its May 19 primary election, with the contested Republican lieutenant governor race selected for audit and results confirmed accurate as counties certified their results to the Department of State.

RI.title: Better luck next year, Rhode Island Voting Rights Act. Here's why it stalled this session.
RI.summary: Rhode Island's Voting Rights Act (S 3143 / H 8334), sponsored to protect minority voters against suppression and racial gerrymandering, failed to advance before the 2026 legislative session ended, with advocates vowing to reintroduce it in 2027.

SC.title: South Carolina results: Evette and Wilson head to runoff
SC.summary: Following South Carolina's June 9 primary, Lt. Gov. Pamela Evette (Trump-endorsed) and Attorney General Alan Wilson advanced to a June 23 Republican gubernatorial runoff. State Rep. Jermaine Johnson won the Democratic gubernatorial primary.

SC.title: South Carolina primary results: Rep. Nancy Mace fails to advance in governor's race
SC.summary: Rep. Nancy Mace failed to advance in the Republican governor's race in South Carolina's June 9 primary, setting up a June 23 runoff between Lt. Gov. Pamela Evette and Attorney General Alan Wilson. The primary also included a contested U.S. Senate primary featuring incumbent Lindsey Graham.

SC.title: South Carolina early voting for runoff races will not take place on Juneteenth, state says

NV.title: Nevada primary election results 2026
NV.summary: Full results from the Nevada 2026 primary election, including races for U.S. Senate, governor, and congressional seats.

NV.title: Jim Marchant wins Nevada Republican Secretary of State primary
NV.summary: Election denier Jim Marchant won the Nevada Republican Secretary of State primary, setting up a rematch against Democratic incumbent Cisco Aguilar.

NV.title: Nevada mail ballot signature cure deadline approaches
NV.summary: Nevada voters who returned mail ballots with signature issues had until the cure deadline to fix the problem and have their votes counted.

NV.title: Who voted in Nevada: An analysis of 2026 primary turnout
NV.summary: An analysis of who voted in Nevada 2026 primary election, examining turnout by party, county, and demographic group.

NY.title: More than 16,500 New Yorkers vote on day one of early voting
NY.summary: More than 16,500 New York City voters cast ballots on the first day of early voting for the June primary, with competitive Democratic primaries for mayor and other offices.

NY.title: More than 44,000 New Yorkers have voted in first three days of early voting
NY.summary: Early voting participation in New York City reached more than 44,000 ballots in the first three days, with several competitive primary races driving turnout.

NY.title: Early voting in NYC reaches 62,000 in fourth day
NY.summary: Early voting in New York City continued to grow, reaching 62,000 ballots cast through the fourth day of the early voting period.

NY.title: Few voters show up to early vote for Mamdani despite leading in polls
NY.summary: Despite polling well in the New York City mayoral primary, candidate Zohran Mamdani has seen modest early voting turnout at his targeted polling sites.

NY.title: New York lawmakers approve redistricting reform amendment
NY.summary: New York legislators approved a constitutional amendment to reform the redistricting process, reducing partisan influence in drawing district lines.

OH.title: Ohio voter photo ID constitutional amendment to go on November ballot
OH.summary: Ohio legislators voted to put a constitutional amendment on the November ballot that would require photo ID for voting, going beyond the current state law.

OH.title: Ohio absentee voter ID bill advances through legislature
OH.summary: Ohio lawmakers advanced a bill that would require voters casting absentee ballots to provide additional identification, tightening mail voting rules.

OH.title: FBI searches Ohio voting rights organization
OH.summary: Federal agents searched the offices of an Ohio voting rights organization as part of an investigation, drawing condemnation from civil rights groups.

OH.title: FBI searches Ohio voter registration group amid investigation
OH.summary: The FBI conducted a search of an Ohio voter registration organization, raising concerns among voting rights advocates about the targeting of civic groups.

OH.title: Ohio voter ID constitutional amendment headed to November ballot
OH.summary: Ohio voter photo ID constitutional amendment was officially certified for the November ballot, setting up a high-profile election law vote.

OK.title: What is on the Oklahoma primary ballot for June 16
OK.summary: A voter guide to the races and questions on the Oklahoma primary ballot, including the U.S. Senate race, state questions, and competitive legislative primaries.

OK.title: Oklahoma early voting turnout up ahead of June primary
OK.summary: Oklahoma saw higher early voting turnout than recent comparable elections ahead of the June 16 primary, driven by competitive races at the top of the ballot.

OK.title: Oklahoma voters reject minimum wage increase in primary election
OK.summary: Oklahoma voters rejected a state question that would have raised the minimum wage, one of several measures decided in the June primary.

OK.title: Tom Hern wins Oklahoma Republican Senate primary
OK.summary: Rep. Tom Hern won the crowded Oklahoma Republican U.S. Senate primary, securing the nomination to succeed retiring Sen. James Lankford.

OK.title: Oklahoma primary turnout down from peak years
OK.summary: Oklahoma primary turnout, while higher than very recent cycles, remains lower than the peak years of the Trump era, according to post-election analysis.

OR.title: Nonaffiliated Oregon candidate files for Congress using new independent process
OR.summary: A nonaffiliated Oregon candidate filed for a congressional seat using a new process that allows independent candidates to appear on the November ballot without running in a primary.

OR.title: Oregon certifies 2026 primary election results
OR.summary: Oregon officials certified the results of the May 2026 primary election, finalizing nominees for statewide and congressional races.

PA.title: Pennsylvania certifies 2026 primary election results
PA.summary: Pennsylvania certified the results of the May 2026 primary election, setting the field for November contests including the U.S. Senate and governor races.

PA.title: Democratic voter registration drops in Pennsylvania ahead of midterms
PA.summary: Democratic voter registration in Pennsylvania has declined relative to Republicans since 2024, raising concerns for party officials ahead of key 2026 races.

RI.title: Rhode Island Voting Rights Act stalls in legislature
RI.summary: A Rhode Island state Voting Rights Act failed to advance in the legislature before the session deadline, disappointing voting rights advocates.

RI.title: Rhode Island assembly will not vote on state Voting Rights Act this session
RI.summary: The Rhode Island General Assembly adjourned without taking up the state Voting Rights Act, which had been a priority for progressive legislators.

RI.title: Rhode Island Democrats endorse Foulkes over incumbent legislators
RI.summary: Rhode Island Democrats endorsed Erin Foulkes in a state legislative primary over incumbent representatives, reflecting divisions within the party.

RI.title: McKee faces home-turf snub in Cumberland ahead of governor primary
RI.summary: Gov. Dan McKee was denied his hometown Democratic committee endorsement in Cumberland ahead of the governor primary, a politically embarrassing snub.

SC.title: South Carolina governor runoff: Evette and Wilson head to runoff
SC.summary: South Carolina Republican governor primary headed to a runoff between Lt. Gov. Pamela Evette and Attorney General Alan Wilson after no candidate reached 50 percent.

SC.title: South Carolina runoff rules: A voter guide
SC.summary: A guide to South Carolina runoff election rules, including eligibility, dates, and voting options for the July runoff races.

SC.title: Early voting for South Carolina runoffs: How to cast your ballot
SC.summary: A guide to early voting options for South Carolina July runoff elections, including locations, hours, and absentee voting procedures.

SC.title: South Carolina runoff early voting begins this week
SC.summary: Early voting opened for South Carolina July runoff elections, giving voters an opportunity to cast ballots ahead of the July 14 runoff date.

SC.title: South Carolina governor runoff early voting opens
SC.summary: Early voting opened at South Carolina county election offices for the July governor runoff between Pamela Evette and Alan Wilson.

SD.title: Sioux Falls mayor race reveals Republican fractures ahead of primary
SD.summary: The competitive Sioux Falls mayoral race is exposing divisions within the South Dakota Republican Party ahead of the state primary election.

SD.title: South Dakota governor runoff early voting begins
SD.summary: Early voting started for South Dakota June governor runoff election, with Republican candidates competing for the nomination.

SD.title: Sioux Falls mayor candidates face off in Q&A as Republican fractures grow
SD.summary: Sioux Falls mayor candidates participated in a Q&A event that highlighted the growing ideological divide within the South Dakota Republican Party.

TN.title: Tennessee court upholds redistricting, dismisses NAACP challenge
TN.summary: A Tennessee court dismissed a redistricting challenge from the NAACP, upholding the Republican-drawn legislative maps.

TN.title: Tennessee NAACP plaintiffs vow to appeal redistricting ruling
TN.summary: NAACP plaintiffs in a Tennessee redistricting case said they will appeal after a state court upheld the Republican-drawn maps.

TN.title: NAACP files federal injunction against Tennessee congressional map
TN.summary: The NAACP filed a federal court injunction seeking to block Tennessee new congressional map, arguing it illegally dilutes Black voting power.

TX.title: Texas Secretary of State appointment creates uncertainty
TX.summary: Texas faces uncertainty over its Secretary of State appointment as the Legislature considers changes to the election oversight role.

TX.title: Texas election officials take over Val Verde County voter registration
TX.summary: Texas state election officials took over voter registration operations in Val Verde County, citing concerns about administration of the county rolls.

TX.title: Texas state takeover of Val Verde voter registration: What to know
TX.summary: Details on the Texas state takeover of Val Verde County voter registration, including what triggered the intervention and what it means for county voters.

UT.title: Utah 1st Congressional District primary: Candidate profiles
UT.summary: Profiles of the candidates competing in Utah 1st Congressional District Republican primary, a competitive race in northern Utah.

UT.title: How to vote in Utah primary election 2026
UT.summary: A guide to voting in the 2026 Utah primary election, including registration status, voting locations, and mail ballot options.

UT.title: Summit County early voting opens for Utah primary
UT.summary: Summit County opened early voting sites for the Utah primary election, allowing residents to cast ballots before election day.

UT.title: Democratic ballots in high demand in Utah 1st Congressional District
UT.summary: An unusually high number of voters in Utah 1st Congressional District are requesting Democratic primary ballots, signaling interest in the competitive race.

UT.title: Republicans may decide Utah-1 Democratic primary as crossover interest surges
UT.summary: Crossover voting could play a decisive role in Utah 1st Congressional District Democratic primary as Republicans and independents request Democratic ballots.

VA.title: Virginia primary early voting begins at registrar offices
VA.summary: Virginia opened early in-person voting at local registrar offices ahead of the June 17 primary election, which features competitive primaries for governor and other statewide offices.

VA.title: Virginia Beach announces early voting locations for primary
VA.summary: Virginia Beach announced early voting locations and hours for the upcoming primary election, giving residents options to cast ballots before election day.

WA.title: Initiative to repeal Washington income tax surcharges gathers signatures
WA.summary: Organizers of a Washington state initiative to repeal recently enacted income tax surcharges are gathering signatures to qualify the measure for the November ballot.

WI.title: Madison deputy city clerk reassigned after losing track of ballots
WI.summary: A Madison deputy city clerk was reassigned after ballots were lost or mishandled during the primary election, raising concerns about election administration.

WI.title: Wisconsin Elections Commission considers ballot access changes
WI.summary: The Wisconsin Elections Commission is weighing changes to ballot access rules that would affect how third-party candidates qualify for future elections.

WI.title: Wisconsin Democratic governor straw poll shows competitive primary
WI.summary: A straw poll of Wisconsin Democrats shows a competitive governor primary, with no candidate holding a commanding lead ahead of the August primary.

WV.title: West Virginia certifies 2026 primary election results
WV.summary: West Virginia officials certified the results of the May 2026 primary election, finalizing nominees for U.S. Senate, governor, and other statewide races.

WV.title: West Virginia primary results officially certified
WV.summary: West Virginia Secretary of State certified the May primary results, setting up general election contests including the U.S. Senate race.

WV.title: West Virginia preliminary report shows increased unaffiliated voter participation
WV.summary: A preliminary post-election report shows a notable increase in West Virginia voters registered as unaffiliated participating in the May primary.

WY.title: Weston County gets new election clerk as 2026 cycle begins
WY.summary: Weston County, Wyoming installed a new election clerk ahead of the 2026 election cycle, bringing fresh administration to the rural county elections.

WY.title: Wyoming voters switching to Republican registration ahead of 2026
WY.summary: Wyoming is seeing an uptick in voters switching their registration to Republican ahead of the 2026 primary, which is the decisive contest in the heavily GOP state.

WY.title: Five Republicans and two Democrats vie for Wyoming U.S. Senate seat
WY.summary: Wyoming has a contested U.S. Senate primary with five Republican candidates and two Democrats competing for the seat held by retiring Sen. John Barrasso.

AZ.title: Arizona Court of Appeals rules in Maricopa County election dispute as primary draws near
AZ.summary: A 2-1 Arizona Court of Appeals ruling blocked Maricopa County Recorder Justin Heap from immediately taking over key election IT systems and databases ahead of early voting for the July 21 primary, keeping control with the Board of Supervisors. Recorder Heap announced plans to seek emergency intervention from the Arizona Supreme Court.

AZ.title: Arizona appeals court blocks Maricopa County election changes ahead of July 21 primary
AZ.summary: The Arizona Court of Appeals stayed a lower court order that had sided with Recorder Justin Heap in the ongoing dispute over who controls election operations in Maricopa County, citing the Purcell principle against last-minute changes close to an election.

CA.title: California billionaire tax proposal qualifies for the November ballot
CA.summary: State officials announced that a citizen initiative to impose a one-time tax on the wealthiest Californians has gathered enough signatures to appear on the November 2026 ballot, adding a high-profile direct democracy measure alongside contested congressional and gubernatorial races.

CA.title: California election results: Governor and key 2026 races
CA.summary: Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra advanced to the November governor's race following the June 2 primary; Democrats' redistricting strategy to net five U.S. House seats is being tested as competitive congressional primaries finalize their November matchups.

DC.title: US Judge Allows Challenges to Trump's Mail-In Voting Order Ahead of November Elections
DC.summary: A federal judge in Boston ruled that Democratic-led states and voting rights groups can proceed with lawsuits challenging Trump's executive order on mail-in voting ahead of the 2026 midterms, while narrowing the cases to only cover 2026 elections. The ruling keeps alive the possibility of blocking the order before November.

DE.title: Two voting-related Constitutional Amendments advance in General Assembly
DE.summary: Two Delaware constitutional amendments restoring voting rights for returning citizens passed the House 30-10 and will now move to the Senate, requiring approval in a second legislative session before voters ratify the changes.

DE.title: Delaware House Bill 430 could ban corporations from voting in municipal elections statewide
DE.summary: HB 430, the first leg of a constitutional amendment, advanced through the Delaware House to prohibit corporations and other artificial entities from voting in any Delaware election at any level, in response to a court ruling permitting corporate voting in some municipal elections.

GA.title: Georgia's GOP-led legislature ditches redistricting plans amid voting rights concerns
GA.summary: Georgia House Speaker Jon Burns announced legislators would not redraw congressional or legislative maps during Governor Kemp's special session, citing pending legal cases and the need for more time after the Supreme Court's Voting Rights Act ruling. Civil rights advocates celebrated the decision.

GA.title: On redistricting, Georgia GOP lawmakers concluded today's election risks outweighed future gains
GA.summary: Georgia Republicans calculated that pushing redistricting in a contentious special session risked mobilizing opposition voters ahead of November, deciding the near-term political risks of redrawing maps outweighed potential long-term gains for their party.

GA.title: Voting machine changes postponed to 2028 under new GOP bill
GA.summary: Georgia's Senate Ethics Committee advanced legislation to delay the state's QR code ballot-counting ban until 2028, extending a deadline originally set by a 2024 law that lacked funding to implement new voting machines before the 2026 elections.

GA.title: Georgia's QR codes for counting votes likely to remain for midterms as lawmakers delay action
GA.summary: Georgia lawmakers are advancing a bill to delay replacing the state's QR code-based ballot-marking devices until 2028, meaning the widely criticized voting technology will remain in use for the upcoming November midterm elections.

GA.title: Georgia voting rights advocates celebrate redistricting decision
GA.summary: Civil rights groups celebrated after Georgia Republicans abandoned redistricting efforts during the special session, with Sen. Raphael Warnock and coalition allies crediting grassroots pressure for preventing maps that advocates said would dilute minority voting power.

HI.title: Automatic Voter Registration bill signed into law, set to begin Jan. 1, 2027 in Hawaii
HI.summary: Governor Josh Green signed SB 2239 (Act 67) into law, establishing automatic voter registration statewide beginning January 1, 2027: eligible residents will be automatically registered when applying for or renewing a Hawaii driver's license or state ID unless they opt out.

HI.title: Voter registration going from opt-in to opt-out
HI.summary: Hawaii's newly signed automatic voter registration law shifts the state from an opt-in to an opt-out system tied to driver's license applications, and will also automatically update address records for already-registered voters, taking effect January 1, 2027.

MA.title: Record number of measures remain in play for 2026 ballot
MA.summary: Massachusetts ballot initiative organizers faced a June 17 deadline to submit second-round signatures for a record-breaking slate of up to 12 potential 2026 ballot measures, including proposals for same-day voter registration and a top-two primary system, after the legislature declined to act on any of the certified initiatives.

MD.title: Maryland leaders raise additional concerns about ballot mix-up as early voting ends
MD.summary: As Maryland's early voting period ended June 18, election watchdog groups raised additional concerns about voter confusion and potential participation dropoff resulting from the mail-in ballot printing error, calling for further investigation into the handling of more than 565,000 replacement ballots.

ME.title: Maine resolves ranked choice primaries, setting up the governor's race and a key House contest
ME.summary: Maine's ranked-choice tabulation concluded June 18, with Democrat Hannah Pingree winning the gubernatorial nomination and Matt Dunlap narrowly winning the 2nd Congressional District Democratic primary over Joe Baldacci, setting the November general election matchups.

ME.title: Maine governor, congressional nominations decided after ranked choice voting
ME.summary: Maine's ranked-choice voting tabulation resolved the state's primary races, with Republican Bobby Charles set to face Democrat Hannah Pingree for governor in November, providing a clear illustration of how Maine's ranked-choice system continues to shape election outcomes in multi-candidate primary fields.

MN.title: Candidates Certified for 2026 Primary Election
MN.summary: The Minnesota Secretary of State announced certification of all candidates for federal and state offices for the August 11 primary election. Early in-person and mail voting for the primary begins June 26; same-day registration remains available on Election Day.

NC.title: Advocates say a sweeping elections bill moving through the NC House undermines voting rights
NC.summary: Multiple voting rights organizations including Common Cause NC, Democracy NC, and the NC Black Alliance publicly opposed House Bill 958, warning it would undermine voting access through expanded ballot challenges and new restrictions on military and overseas voters requiring photo ID with absentee ballots.

NC.title: NC election law overhaul bill vote delayed as voting rights advocates ramp up opposition
NC.summary: The North Carolina elections omnibus bill (HB 958) was pulled from the House Rules Committee agenda, delaying an anticipated floor vote as mounting advocacy opposition and constituent pressure prompted Republican leadership to slow the bill's progress.

NV.title: Primary election results certified; Romero to face Chadwick in Henderson mayor race
NV.summary: Clark County governments voted to officially certify the June 9 primary election results on June 18 after an audit found no tabulation errors; Washoe County commissioners also certified their results 4-1, finalizing Nevada's primary election outcomes statewide.

NY.title: Attorney General James Announces Election Protection Hotline Ahead of June Primary Elections
NY.summary: New York AG Letitia James announced the Election Protection Hotline for voters experiencing problems during the June 23 primary and ongoing early voting period (June 13-21). The office has also taken legal action to protect against voter registration purges and ensure equitable early voting access.

OH.title: What changes to absentee voting will Ohioans see during the 2026 election?
OH.summary: Ohio's new law eliminates the prior 4-day postmark grace period, requiring all absentee ballots to be received by boards of elections before polls close on Election Day. The law also adds new steps for verifying voter registrations against state and federal databases.

PA.title: Pennsylvania Must Count Undated Mail-In Ballots, Federal Court Rules
PA.summary: A federal court ruled that Pennsylvania cannot reject mail-in ballots with missing or incorrect handwritten dates on return envelopes, finding such rejections violate the First and Fourteenth Amendments. The ruling affects how counties must handle defective mail ballots going into the November 2026 general election.

SC.title: South Carolina early voting for runoff races will not take place on Juneteenth, state says
SC.summary: South Carolina election officials confirmed that early voting for the June 23 primary runoff is restricted to June 17-18 only, as state law bars early voting on the Juneteenth state holiday. The two-day window applies to the Republican gubernatorial, attorney general, and agriculture commissioner runoffs.

TN.title: U.S. Appeals Court stops felon voter restoration change from going through
TN.summary: The Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals issued an injunction blocking a lower federal court ruling that had found Tennessee violated federal voting law by requiring extra documentation from formerly incarcerated people seeking to restore their voting rights. The appeals court cited proximity to upcoming elections and questioned the NAACP's standing.

UT.title: There's still time to vote in Utah's primaries — but use a drop box, not the mail, officials say
UT.summary: Utah election officials are urging primary voters to use ballot drop boxes ahead of the June 23 election due to a new state law requiring ballots to be physically received by county clerks by 8 p.m. on Election Day, eliminating any mail delivery grace period.

VA.title: Early voting underway for August primaries for Virginia congressional candidates
VA.summary: Early in-person voting for Virginia's August 4 primary officially began June 19, with offices closed for the Juneteenth holiday having opened June 18. Virginia moved its primary from June to August via HB 29 signed in February, and absentee ballots are being mailed starting June 19.

VA.title: Virginia dual party primary: Early voting begins this week
VA.summary: Early voting opened across Virginia for the August 4 primary featuring both Democratic and Republican congressional races: Democrats in five House districts and Republicans in U.S. Senate and three House races, the first primary under Virginia's newly rescheduled August calendar.

VT.title: Vermont Governor Signs S.298, An Act Relating to Voter Protections
VT.summary: Governor Phil Scott signed S.298 into law, creating new voter protection measures including strengthened penalties for election interference, a new criminal offense for intimidating voters or election officials, and updated rules on voter checklist use and campaign security disclosures.

WI.title: Wisconsin redistricting lawsuits may get ruling after 2026 elections
WI.summary: With both active lawsuits challenging Wisconsin's congressional maps either dismissed or stalled, legal experts say any judicial remedy is essentially off the table for the 2026 midterms. Voters will go to the polls under heavily Republican-advantaged maps despite Wisconsin being a competitive state.

WI.title: Wisconsin court dismisses challenge to Republican gerrymandered congressional map
WI.summary: A three-judge federal panel dismissed a lawsuit challenging Wisconsin's congressional maps, ruling it lacked jurisdiction over partisan gerrymandering claims. The dismissal effectively ends any realistic path to fairer maps before November 2026, leaving the current Republican-advantaged districts in place.

WV.title: Secretary of State Kris Warner Announces Certification of 2026 Mid-Term Primary Election
WV.summary: West Virginia's 2026 primary election was certified on June 10 after all 55 counties submitted results. Turnout was 21.02%, and this was the first primary since Republicans closed their party's primary to unaffiliated voters following a 2024 decision by the WV GOP state executive committee.

WV.title: State Primary Election Results Officially Certified
WV.summary: West Virginia Public Broadcasting reported on certification of the 2026 primary, noting early voting participation was more than 8% higher than in the 2022 midterm primary. The Democratic Party primary remained open to unaffiliated voters while the Republican primary was closed for the first time in decades.

CO.title: Looking for areas where Michael Bennet and Phil Weiser differ on policy? There aren't many.
CO.summary: A Colorado Sun analysis of the Democratic governor primary finds Bennet and Weiser broadly aligned on policy, leaving electability and experience as the key differentiators for voters as the June 30 primary ballot deadline approaches.

DE.title: State level voting rights act clears Delaware's House
DE.summary: The Delaware House passed House Bill 444, the Delaware John Lewis Voting Rights Act, on June 19 and sent it to the state Senate. The law would empower the state AG to sue over voter suppression and provide language assistance to voters with limited English proficiency.

DE.title: Delaware House passes John Lewis Voting Rights Act, Senate review next
DE.summary: WDEL reports on the House passage of the Delaware John Lewis Voting Rights Act (HB 444), establishing new protections against voter suppression, vote dilution, voter intimidation, and election access barriers. The bill now awaits Senate action before the legislative session closes.

IN.title: Beau Bayh outlines campaign platform for Indiana secretary of state race
IN.summary: Democratic secretary of state nominee Beau Bayh detailed his election administration platform after winning the June 6 convention nomination, positioning himself against Republican incumbent Diego Morales ahead of the November general election for the office that oversees Indiana's elections.

KS.title: 'Coordinated effort': Kansas Republican leaders have a plan to cancel the 2026 U.S. Senate election
KS.summary: A Democratic state legislator alleged that Kansas Republican leadership, coordinating with Sen. Roger Marshall's office, deliberately inserted language into SB 105 to cancel or delay a 2026 Senate election if Marshall leaves for a Trump administration post. Legal experts question whether the provision conflicts with the U.S. Constitution's 17th Amendment.

OR.title: Gov. Kotek won't debate Drazan with Oregon newspaper group
OR.summary: Oregon Gov. Tina Kotek declined to participate in a gubernatorial debate hosted by the Oregon Newspaper Publishers Association, instead challenging Republican challenger Christine Drazan to three specific debates in Medford, Portland, and Eugene ahead of the November general election.

PA.title: New Pa. poll shows Shapiro leading handily against Garrity, trouncing Trump in popularity
PA.summary: A Franklin & Marshall College poll conducted June 8-14 found incumbent Gov. Josh Shapiro leading Republican challenger Stacy Garrity 50% to 28% in Pennsylvania's 2026 governor's race. The survey also showed Shapiro with stronger job approval ratings than President Trump among Pennsylvania registered voters.

TX.title: The Texas GOP wants closed primaries. Here's what that would mean for voters.
TX.summary: Gov. Greg Abbott publicly backed a push to require voter party registration and close Texas's primaries to non-Republicans at the Texas GOP convention, calling it a top legislative priority for 2027. The proposal would require Texans to register with a party — a significant departure from the state's current open primary system.

AR.title: Pete Buttigieg rallies for Chris Jones in Little Rock
AR.summary: Former U.S. Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg endorsed Democratic congressional candidate Chris Jones at a Little Rock rally, calling Arkansas's 2nd Congressional District race against Republican Rep. French Hill a nationally significant contest ahead of the November general election.

AR.title: Buttigieg says Arkansas voters can send message about Trump by flipping GOP-held House seat
AR.summary: At a packed Little Rock event, Pete Buttigieg urged Arkansas voters to oust Rep. French Hill in the 2nd Congressional District and said the competitive race is drawing national attention as a potential Democratic pickup seat in the 2026 midterms.

CO.title: Democratic ballots outpace Republicans' as Colorado's primary vote starts to trickle in
CO.summary: With Colorado's June 30 primary underway by mail, county clerks reported receiving over 230,000 ballots, with Democratic primary ballots outnumbering Republican returns in early counts, though most unaffiliated voter ballots had yet to be processed.

CO.title: Bernie Sanders endorses DeGette challenger Melat Kiros in Colorado's 1st CD Democratic primary
CO.summary: Sen. Bernie Sanders endorsed first-time candidate Melat Kiros in her primary challenge against 15-term incumbent Rep. Diana DeGette ahead of Colorado's June 30 primary, adding national progressive attention to the Denver congressional race.

CO.title: DeGette spars with challengers Kiros, James in final Colorado 1st District candidate forum
CO.summary: Rep. Diana DeGette and her Democratic primary challengers Melat Kiros and Wanda James held a final candidate forum in Denver 10 days before Colorado's June 30 primary election, with DeGette defending her incumbency against democratic socialist challenger Kiros.

CO.title: Registered voters on the eve of the 2026 primaries
CO.summary: An analysis of Colorado's registered voter rolls ahead of the June 30 primary examines party registration trends and the dominant unaffiliated bloc — which now makes up more than half the electorate — that will shape outcomes in contested races.

DC.title: Preliminary results from the first ranked choice voting election in Washington, DC
DC.summary: FairVote released preliminary round-by-round RCV tabulation results from DC's first-ever ranked choice voting primary held June 16, finding 99.6% of mayoral voters cast valid ballots and 71% of voters whose first choice was eliminated had their vote transfer to a finalist.

DC.title: Chair of DC elections gives update on tabulating ranked choice votes
DC.summary: DC Board of Elections chair explained the multi-round RCV tabulation process after releasing the first round-by-round tallies from the June 16 primary, with an additional release planned for June 24 and final results expected on or after June 26 once remaining mail ballots are counted.

FL.title: DeSantis clashes with Florida GOP over absence of gubernatorial debate
FL.summary: Gov. Ron DeSantis publicly criticized the Republican Party of Florida for canceling its planned gubernatorial debate after only Trump-endorsed Rep. Byron Donalds met the party's polling and fundraising thresholds, saying the decision is counterproductive and harms the Republican primary process.

FL.title: 'What a farce:' DeSantis blasts Florida Republican Party over debate controversy
FL.summary: Gov. DeSantis escalated his criticism of the Florida GOP's decision to exclude three Republican gubernatorial candidates from a June 27 debate event, accusing the party chair of insulting the intelligence of Republican voters with opaque qualification criteria ahead of the August 18 primary.

GA.title: QR code deadline extension bill clears Senate in a Saturday vote
GA.summary: The Georgia Senate passed a bill along party lines extending the July 1 deadline to remove QR codes from ballot counting until January 2028, while also mandating hand recounts for top-ticket races and creating a committee to select the state's next voting system. Democrats opposed the measure, citing exclusion from the new oversight committee.

GA.title: Georgia lawmakers won't redraw electoral maps during special session
GA.summary: Georgia House Republicans declined Gov. Brian Kemp's call to redraw congressional and state legislative maps during the June special session, shelving the mid-decade redistricting effort despite the Supreme Court's Callais ruling weakening Voting Rights Act protections. The decision means Georgia will use existing maps for the 2026 midterm elections.

LA.title: Voter guide: Louisiana's June 27 primary runoff election
