LA.summary: Louisiana voters head to the polls June 27 for Senate party primary runoffs, with Republican Julia Letlow facing John Fleming and Democrat Jamie Davis facing Gary Crockett to determine nominees for the seat vacated by Bill Cassidy. Only registered party members who voted in the May primary, plus no-party voters who selected a party ballot then, are eligible to participate.

MA.title: Mass. high court blocks proposal to slash income tax from November ballot
MA.summary: The Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court removed a ballot initiative to cut the state income tax from 5% to 4% from the November 2026 ballot, ruling the attorney general's summary was significantly misleading for omitting the measure's effect on capital gains taxes. More than 100,000 residents had signed petitions to place the measure before voters.

MA.title: Mass. income tax question is off the ballot this fall. Now what?
MA.summary: Following the SJC's ruling striking the income tax cut question from the 2026 ballot, attention turns to the remaining ballot initiatives — including rent control and all-party primaries — which still face pending court challenges. The legislature has until July 1 to pass the rent control bill before backers take it to voters.

MD.title: Unaffiliated voters air grievances on eve of primary they're excluded from
MD.summary: More than 1 million unaffiliated Maryland voters are barred from participating in the June 23 closed primary, prompting advocates to renew calls to open the state's partisan primaries as the election approaches. Unaffiliated voters can only cast ballots in the primary for nonpartisan offices such as the State Board of Education.

MD.title: Early voting ends with light turnout at polls, thousands of mail-in ballots so far
MD.summary: Maryland's early voting period closed June 19 with more than 138,000 in-person ballots cast and nearly 165,600 mail-in ballots received ahead of the June 23 gubernatorial primary. Watchdog groups Secure the Vote and the Maryland Freedom Caucus raised continuing concerns about the May vendor error that sent roughly 500,000 wrong-party ballots to voters.

MD.title: Maryland leaders raise additional concerns about ballot mix-up as early voting ends
MD.summary: As Maryland's early voting period ended, lawmakers and watchdog groups raised unresolved concerns about the May ballot mix-up that sent nearly 500,000 wrong-party mail-in ballots to voters, with some households reporting receiving multiple live ballots. The State Board of Elections maintained that all ballots are safe and voting integrity is intact.

ME.title: How ranked-choice voting produced surprises in all of Maine's big primaries
ME.summary: Analysis of Maine's June 9 primaries shows RCV altered outcomes in all major races, with final tabulations released June 19 revealing that candidates who led in first-round counts did not always win once lower-ranked ballot redistributions were applied.

ME.title: Maine Secretary of State's Office announces ranked choice tabulations
ME.summary: Maine's Elections Division completed and released official RCV tabulation results for five June 9 primary races, including the Democratic and Republican gubernatorial contests and the 2nd Congressional District Democratic primary.

MI.title: Michigan election critics push for investigations ahead of 2026 vote
MI.summary: Vocal critics of Michigan's election administration are working with the Trump administration's DOJ and seeking investigations into voting matters in the battleground state, adding to election-integrity tensions ahead of the 2026 midterms.

MI.title: Thumbs Up or Thumbs Down? Michigan Senate Advances State Voting Rights Act, But It Faces a Challenge in the GOP-Led House
MI.summary: The Michigan Senate passed the Michigan Voting Rights Act (SB 961-964) on a 20-17 party-line vote to prohibit discriminatory voting access restrictions and establish a Voting Rights Assistance Fund, but the bill faces uncertain prospects in the Republican-led House.

MO.title: Missouri voters passed a sales tax cap. Under Amendment 4, it would have failed
MO.summary: An analysis illustrates the stakes of Amendment 4 on Missouri's August ballot: a past voter-approved constitutional amendment that passed with 57% statewide would have failed under the proposed new rule requiring majority support in each of Missouri's eight congressional districts.

MT.title: Democratic Senate candidate says she's 'in it to win it'
MT.summary: Democratic Senate nominee Alani Bankhead reaffirmed she will not drop out of Montana's open U.S. Senate race despite calls to step aside for independent Seth Bodnar, who simultaneously announced cross-partisan endorsements from former Sens. Jon Tester and Max Baucus and former Republican Gov. Marc Racicot.

MT.title: Divided Montana Senate field helps Republicans
MT.summary: New polling shows Republican Kurt Alme leading Montana's open Senate race with 44% to Democrat Alani Bankhead's 25% and independent Seth Bodnar's 20%, with the split center-left vote likely benefiting Alme's chances in November.

NC.title: Sweeping election bill stalls after backlash
NC.summary: North Carolina's sweeping elections omnibus bill HB 958 was unexpectedly pulled from the House Rules Committee after intense opposition from the governor, Democratic lawmakers, and protesters, leaving uncertain its proposed changes including a ban on ranked-choice voting and expanded ballot-challenge rules.

NJ.title: New Jersey congressman absent from Capitol Hill for months set to return June 30
NJ.summary: Republican Rep. Tom Kean Jr. of New Jersey's competitive 7th Congressional District announced he will return to Congress on June 30 after a three-month medical absence, raising questions about his 2026 re-election campaign against Democratic challenger Rebecca Bennett in a top-targeted district.

OH.title: A week after the FBI searched an Ohio voting-rights group, questions remain
OH.summary: One week after FBI agents raided the Cleveland offices of the Ohio Organizing Collaborative and seized electronic devices from staff, federal officials have provided no on-the-record explanation for the search warrant. Critics, including two congresswomen, have called the raid voter intimidation targeting a group that registers voters in communities of color ahead of the November midterms.

SC.title: AP Decision Notes: What to expect in South Carolina's state primary runoff
SC.summary: South Carolina holds its statewide primary runoff on June 23 deciding Republican nominees for governor (Lt. Gov. Pamela Evette vs. AG Alan Wilson), attorney general, and agriculture commissioner, plus the Democratic nominee in the 2nd Congressional District. Registered voters who sat out the June 9 primary are eligible to vote in either party's runoff.

UT.title: AP Decision Notes: What to expect in Utah's state primary
UT.summary: Utah voters head to the polls June 23 to nominate congressional candidates under a new court-ordered map that created a Democratic-friendly district in Salt Lake City and scrambled the reelection plans of the state's all-Republican delegation. The new boundaries could produce an additional Democratic seat in November, with former Rep. Ben McAdams among the key contenders in the new 1st Congressional District.

VT.title: Vermont enacts vote denial prohibition, campaign finance changes in 2026 session
VT.summary: Vermont Governor Phil Scott signed S.298, the Vermont Voter Protections Act, on June 8, establishing new prohibitions on voting policies that deny or abridge the right to vote based on race, color, language minority status, or disability. The law also authorizes the attorney general to file civil actions against violators, allows candidates to use campaign funds for security measures, and strengthens penalties for election interference and voter intimidation.

WV.title: Democrats, Republicans weigh in on Boone County registration flip
WV.summary: West Virginia Republicans and Democrats are reacting to Boone County becoming the first county in state history where registered Republicans outnumber registered Democrats, with Republicans holding a narrow 4,892 to 4,887 edge. Democrat registration has fallen 50.1% since 2016 while Republican registration has surged 149.6%, reflecting a broader partisan realignment ahead of November's general election.

WV.title: Registered Republicans surpass Dems in Boone County, WV, for first time; Dems keep focus on turnout
WV.summary: Registered Republicans outnumber registered Democrats in Boone County, West Virginia for the first time in the county's history, as Democrats plan statewide voter registration drives through summer to boost turnout ahead of the November general election. The shift represents a decade-long trend of partisan realignment in a county that was once a Democratic stronghold rooted in organized labor and the coal industry.

WY.title: Wyoming's secretary of state race attracts newcomers and political veterans
WY.summary: Four Republican candidates and one Democrat are competing for Wyoming's secretary of state post, an office that oversees the state's elections, ahead of the August 18 primary. The race will determine who oversees Wyoming's 2026 general election administration.

WY.title: Five Republicans, 2 Democrats vie for US Senate in Wyoming primaries
WY.summary: Five Republican and two Democratic candidates have filed to run for Wyoming's open U.S. Senate seat in the August 18 primaries, with Rep. Harriet Hageman considered the frontrunner among GOP candidates. Wyoming's 2026 cycle is defined by a large number of open seats including governor, secretary of state, and two of the state's three congressional positions.

CO.title: In-Person Voting for the 2026 Primary Election Available Starting June 22
CO.summary: The Colorado Secretary of State announced 137 in-person voting centers and 437 drop boxes are now open statewide for the June 30 primary. Eligible Coloradans can register and vote in person at any voting center through 7 p.m. on Election Day.

IN.title: Engling captures Republican bid for Indiana secretary of state
IN.summary: Max Engling won the Republican nomination for Indiana Secretary of State at the GOP state convention in Fort Wayne, capturing 53% of the delegate vote on the second ballot. Engling will face Democrat Beau Bayh in November in a race that will determine who oversees Indiana elections.

MD.title: Marylanders go to the polls for pivotal primaries in governor, congressional races
MD.summary: Maryland voters head to the polls June 23 for competitive Democratic and Republican gubernatorial primaries, along with several congressional races. Democrats outnumber Republicans 2-to-1 statewide, making the Democratic primary the decisive contest for governor.

MN.title: Absentee voting begins this week in Minnesota's primary election
MN.summary: Absentee voting for Minnesota's August 11 primary opens Friday, June 26, allowing voters to cast ballots by mail or in person at local election offices. Minnesota voters will need a witness who is a U.S. citizen aged 18 or older by Election Day, or a notary.

NY.title: More than 170,000 New Yorkers cast ballots during early voting
NY.summary: Early voting in New York City ended June 21 with 172,743 check-ins recorded across the five boroughs, led by Manhattan with 67,369 ballots. Voters head to the polls June 23 for primary races in several congressional districts and city contests.

TX.title: James Talarico leads Ken Paxton in Texas Senate race poll after GOP runoff
TX.summary: A new poll shows Democrat James Talarico leading Republican Ken Paxton 47%-44% in Texas's U.S. Senate race, with Cook Political Report shifting the race rating from 'Likely Republican' to 'Lean Republican' following Paxton's runoff win over incumbent John Cornyn.

AK.title: Challenger with same name as Alaska U.S. Sen. Dan Sullivan sues to stay on ballot
AK.summary: The disqualified same-named Dan Sullivan challenger filed a lawsuit seeking reinstatement on the August 18 primary ballot, arguing election officials lacked legal authority to remove him; with ballots set to print June 28, the case creates time pressure for a court ruling.

AR.title: Supreme Court allows Voting Rights Act ruling in Arkansas to stand, limiting voter assistance protections
AR.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court declined to review an Arkansas case, leaving intact an 8th Circuit ruling that private groups cannot sue to enforce Section 208 of the Voting Rights Act — which allows voters with disabilities or limited literacy to receive polling assistance from a person of their choice — affecting Arkansas and six other Midwestern states.

GA.title: Georgia Democrats blast requirement to recount votes by hand in bill that would keep ballot QR codes
GA.summary: As Georgia's QR code bill moves to the House, Democrats sharply criticized the hand recount amendment, arguing it will slow certification and create opportunities to challenge legitimate vote tallies when hand and machine tallies differ slightly.

HI.title: Senate Bill 2239 signed into law, establishing updated automatic voter registration in Hawaiʻi
HI.summary: Coverage of Hawaii's newly signed automatic voter registration law confirms it will automatically update existing registrants' address records when they renew driver's licenses or state IDs, and that new registrants must document U.S. citizenship.

MD.title: On primary Election Day in Maryland, voters are deciding several highly competitive races
MD.summary: Maryland's June 23 primary drew voters to polls open 7am–8pm for governor, all eight U.S. House seats, and county executive races in Montgomery and Prince George's counties. The state offered same-day registration, early voting June 11–18, and mail-in ballot options for the first primary since redistricting reshaped several congressional districts.

MA.title: Massachusetts high court clears ballot question that would eliminate party-based primaries
MA.summary: The Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court rejected a legal challenge to the top-two 'jungle primary' ballot question, clearing the major election reform for a statewide vote on November 3. Under the proposed system all candidates appear on a single primary ballot open to voters of any party affiliation, with the top two advancing to the general election.

MA.title: High court clears ballot question that would eliminate party-based primaries
MA.summary: The Massachusetts SJC dismissed a challenge by Democratic Party officials, ruling that the top-two primary initiative does not unconstitutionally burden voting rights or the right to seek elected office, clearing the proposal for the November 3 ballot.

MI.title: Michigan primary absentee voting begins this week
MI.summary: Michigan residents can begin casting absentee ballots for the August 4 primary as the state constitution requires clerks to have ballots available and dropboxes accessible 40 days before Election Day. Competitive governor and U.S. Senate primaries are on the ballot for both parties.

MN.title: Early voting in the 2026 primary election starts June 26. What do voters need to know?
MN.summary: Early voting for Minnesota's August 11 primary opens June 26, with voters able to request mail ballots or visit local election offices. About 150,000 Minnesotans in mail-ballot precincts will be automatically sent ballots, and in-person early voting at polling places with tabulators begins July 24.

NH.title: A tale of two senators: Sununu, Brown both hope to reclaim job they once held
NH.summary: Former U.S. Senators John Sununu (backed by Trump) and Scott Brown are leading the Republican field for New Hampshire's open Senate seat, with the September 8 primary to determine who faces Democrat Chris Pappas in one of the nation's most competitive Senate races of 2026.

NH.title: Who's running to represent New Hampshire in the U.S. Senate?
NH.summary: New Hampshire's open Senate seat has attracted Republicans Sununu and Brown, Democrat Chris Pappas, and multiple independent and third-party candidates ahead of the September 8 primary, in a race that could help determine control of the U.S. Senate.

NM.title: NM ethics watchdog looks into dark money group that propped up state House Democratic candidates
NM.summary: The New Mexico State Ethics Commission voted unanimously to seek information — through a lawsuit if necessary — from New Chapter New Mexico, a PAC that spent more than $400,000 in the June 2 Democratic primary without disclosing its donors. The commission is empowered to enforce the state Campaign Reporting Act.

SC.title: South Carolina heads back to the polls today: What to know about voting in the 2026 primary runoffs
SC.summary: South Carolina voters returned to the polls for statewide primary runoffs including the Republican gubernatorial race between Lt. Gov. Pamela Evette (Trump-backed) and Attorney General Alan Wilson. Polls were open 7 a.m. to 7 p.m., with more than 72,500 early ballots already cast during the abbreviated two-day early voting window.

UT.title: Here are Utah's 2026 primary election results
UT.summary: Utah held its June 23 primary — the first conducted under new citizenship verification and ballot deadline laws — covering all 75 state House seats, 15 Senate seats, and competitive congressional primaries in newly redrawn districts.

WA.title: Postal Service skips hearing with WA lawmakers on mail-in ballot rules
WA.summary: USPS officials canceled their appearance before a Washington state House panel hours before a June 22 hearing on proposed federal rules that would condition ballot delivery on states sharing voter lists with the federal government. Washington officials characterized the proposed rule as federal overreach violating states' constitutional authority over elections.

DC.title: ACLU to monitor election certification as part of $50 million midterm effort
DC.summary: The ACLU announced a $50 million commitment to the 2026 midterms including a new program to deploy more than 100 staff and 3,000 volunteers to monitor ballot counting and election certification in battleground states. The organization has filed more than 80 lawsuits in two dozen states over voting rights issues including redistricting, mail ballot restrictions, and federal interference in state elections.

AK.title: Alaska legislators probe decision to remove candidate from the ballot
AK.summary: Members of Alaska's House Judiciary and State Affairs committees held an investigatory hearing about the Division of Elections' decision to remove Dan J. Sullivan — a retired teacher from Petersburg sharing the name and party of incumbent U.S. Sen. Dan Sullivan — from the August primary ballot. Lt. Gov. Nancy Dahlstrom initially declined to appear before a legislative subpoena but later agreed to testify at a follow-up hearing scheduled for July 22.

AK.title: Sen. Dan Sullivan's same-named challenger sues to stay in Alaska primary race
AK.summary: Dan J. Sullivan, a retired teacher from Petersburg, filed suit in Alaska Superior Court arguing the Division of Elections lacked legal authority to remove him from the August 18 primary ballot. His attorneys contend the disqualification violates state and federal law, and with ballots set to be printed June 28, the case carries urgent implications for Alaska's high-profile Senate race.

AK.title: Alaska Senate candidate with same name as Sullivan sues to stay on primary ballot
AK.summary: The Hill reports on Dan J. Sullivan's Superior Court challenge to his disqualification from Alaska's nonpartisan primary, noting that ballots are due to be printed June 28 for the August 18 primary and that the incumbent Sen. Dan S. Sullivan is in one of the most consequential Senate races of the 2026 cycle against Democrat Mary Peltola.

AL.title: Tuberville files motion to dismiss Montgomery County residency lawsuit
AL.summary: Former Auburn football coach and U.S. Senate candidate Tommy Tuberville filed a motion to dismiss a lawsuit challenging his Montgomery County residency, which is a requirement to appear on the Alabama ballot; the case could affect his eligibility in the November election.

AL.title: Tuberville seeks to dismiss residency challenge, halt discovery process
AL.summary: Attorneys for Tommy Tuberville filed motions June 23 seeking to dismiss the residency lawsuit and halt discovery, arguing the court lacks jurisdiction; the case centers on whether Tuberville is a legitimate Montgomery County resident as required to appear on the Alabama Senate ballot.

AZ.title: Last Chance: Arizona Voter Registration Deadline is TODAY, June 22
AZ.summary: Arizona's voter registration deadline for the July 21 primary election was June 22 at 11:59 p.m. Voters who missed the deadline cannot participate in the primary, which features contested races for governor, secretary of state, and two open congressional seats.

AZ.title: Monday marks last day to register to vote in Arizona's primary election
AZ.summary: Arizona's June 22 midnight voter registration deadline closed the books for the July 21 primary. Early voting begins June 24, with Maricopa County expanding to 17 more early voting locations than in 2022 and introducing a streamlined drop-off process allowing mail ballot voters to skip signature verification by showing ID.

CO.title: Sportsbooks have spent about $1.5M on Democratic, Republican statehouse primaries in Colorado
CO.summary: With Colorado's primary election one week away on June 30, the Colorado Sun reports that sports betting companies — including DraftKings, FanDuel, and Fanatics — have funneled roughly $1.5 million through a state-level super PAC into legislative primary races, the majority targeting Democratic contests, raising questions about outside spending influence on state elections.

FL.title: June's numbers are in: Byron Donalds rolls toward the Sunshine State Showdown with a $65 million machine
FL.summary: Trump-endorsed Republican gubernatorial frontrunner Byron Donalds raised $1.8 million in early June, bringing his total political operation to nearly $65 million heading into the June 27 Sunshine State Showdown in Hollywood, where GOP candidates will appear on stage ahead of the August 18 primary.

IA.title: Turek leads Hinson in Iowa Senate poll of likely general election voters
IA.summary: An internal poll released June 22 shows Democratic Senate candidate Josh Turek narrowly leading Republican Rep. Ashley Hinson 47% to 45% among likely Iowa general election voters, with the open U.S. Senate seat emerging as a competitive race in the 2026 midterms.

IA.title: Turek criticizes Hinson's vote for Medicaid cuts at healthcare event
IA.summary: Democratic Senate nominee Josh Turek held a healthcare roundtable in Des Moines on June 22, attacking Republican opponent Rep. Ashley Hinson's congressional votes on Medicaid, drawing contrasts ahead of the November general election for Iowa's open U.S. Senate seat.

IN.title: Banks-endorsed adviser wins Republican nomination for Indiana Secretary of State at party convention
IN.summary: Max Engling, an aide to U.S. Sen. Jim Banks, won the Republican nomination for Indiana Secretary of State at the June 20 GOP convention in Fort Wayne, defeating incumbent Diego Morales on the second ballot. Engling will face Democrat Beau Bayh and others in November for the office that serves as Indiana's chief elections administrator.

IN.title: Republicans choose Max Engling in upset for secretary of state nomination
IN.summary: Indiana Republicans picked Max Engling at the state GOP convention as their secretary of state candidate, capping a rapid rise after incumbent Diego Morales lost key party endorsements. The nomination sets up a November contest for control of the office overseeing Indiana elections.

IN.title: Max Engling wins Indiana GOP Secretary of State nomination
IN.summary: Max Engling secured the Republican nomination for Indiana Secretary of State at the state convention, defeating incumbent Secretary of State Diego Morales who had lost the backing of key Republican leaders including Sen. Jim Banks. Engling's campaign includes pledges to push for closed primaries and other election reforms.

KS.title: Kansas GOP leaders' alarming plot to cancel U.S. Senate elections unfolded in plain sight last year
KS.summary: A 2025 Kansas law coordinated by Republican legislative leaders and Sen. Roger Marshall's office could prevent voters from electing a U.S. Senate replacement until 2028 if Marshall vacates his seat after May 1, raising serious questions about voter access to Senate elections and potential 17th Amendment conflicts.

MA.title: SJC blocks rent control question from ballot
MA.summary: Massachusetts' Supreme Judicial Court threw out a ballot question that would have allowed voters to enact statewide rent control, ruling that its exemption for religious-facility housing constituted an impermissible reference to religion under Article 48 of the state Constitution. The measure had gathered more than 157,000 voter signatures.

MA.title: Rent control question disqualified due to religious exemption
MA.summary: GBH News covers the SJC's unanimous ruling striking the rent control initiative from Massachusetts' November 2026 ballot, explaining that the proposal's carve-out exempting religiously affiliated housing units made the measure constitutionally ineligible for the citizen-initiative process under the state's Declaration of Rights.

MA.title: Top Mass. court shuts down rent control ballot question
MA.summary: WAMC reports on the Massachusetts high court's decision disqualifying the rent control ballot initiative that would have capped annual rent increases at 5% or the CPI, whichever is lower. The ruling narrows the set of questions Massachusetts voters will decide in November, leaving housing policy advocates without a statewide ballot vehicle this cycle.

ME.title: Sophie Warren officially secures Democratic nomination for Maine Senate after recount
ME.summary: Following a June 22 recount of the Democratic primary for Senate District 30, Rep. Sophia Warren officially secured the nomination over Rep. Eleanor Sato, concluding one of three close races stemming from Maine's June 9 primary that required recounts.

MO.title: Absentee voting begins in Missouri for primary election
MO.summary: Missouri began accepting absentee ballot requests June 23 for the August 4 primary. Voters with qualifying excuses (surgery, military service, travel) may now vote by mail or in person; no-excuse absentee voting opens July 21. The primary ballot includes constitutional amendments and congressional races under a disputed gerrymandered map.

MO.title: Absentee voting begins in Missouri for August primary election
MO.summary: Missouri's August 4 primary absentee voting opened June 23 for voters with valid excuses. The ballot will include amendments to phase out the state income tax and change the initiative petition process, alongside primary races for congressional seats drawn under the state's legally contested gerrymandered map.

MT.title: Petition signatures for proposed statewide ballot issues submitted to Montana counties; election officials to verify and certify
MT.summary: Montana's June 19 signature submission deadline passed with several campaigns claiming enough signatures to qualify for the November ballot, including Montanans for Nonpartisan Courts (CI-132) with over 102,000 signatures and a dark-money restrictions initiative. County officials must verify signatures and submit them to the Secretary of State by July 17.

MT.title: The ballot questions likely to come before voters in November
MT.summary: Following the June 19 deadline, several Montana ballot initiatives appear on track for the November general election, covering judicial election reform (CI-132), restrictions on corporate campaign contributions, and property taxes. County officials begin the verification process before a July 17 forwarding deadline.

NE.title: Republican National Committee sues Nebraska over state election law
NE.summary: The Republican National Committee filed a federal lawsuit against Nebraska challenging a state election law that critics say allows nonresidents to register and vote in Nebraska elections, seeking to enjoin the law ahead of the November 2026 general election.

NE.title: RNC sues to stop Nebraska election law that allows nonresidents to vote
NE.summary: The RNC's lawsuit filed in federal court targets a Nebraska election law that the party argues permits nonresidents to register and cast ballots in the state; the suit asks for an injunction blocking enforcement of the law before the 2026 elections.

NH.title: New Hampshire primary races heat up
NH.summary: New Hampshire's candidate filing period for the September 8, 2026 state primary closed June 12, and the field of candidates is now set across all races. The open U.S. Senate seat (following Sen. Shaheen's retirement) and the governor's race are drawing competitive fields ahead of the fall primary.

NM.title: New Mexico Secretary of State Maggie Toulouse Oliver suspends Dem Lt. Gov. campaign, citing health
NM.summary: New Mexico Secretary of State Maggie Toulouse Oliver, who won the Democratic primary for lieutenant governor on June 2, suspended her campaign June 18 for health reasons. The Democratic state central committee now has until August 25 to appoint a replacement, disrupting the historic all-female Democratic ticket alongside gubernatorial nominee Deb Haaland.

NM.title: New Mexico lieutenant governor nominee suspends campaign
NM.summary: Maggie Toulouse Oliver's exit from New Mexico's lieutenant governor race, announced June 18, disrupted the projected first all-female Democratic ticket in state history. The Democratic Party must now select a replacement candidate by August 25 under state party rules.

NY.title: Here are New York's 2026 primary election results
NY.summary: NPR tracked results from New York's June 23 primary, in which voters decided Democratic nominations for key U.S. House seats — including the crowded eight-way race to succeed Rep. Jerry Nadler in NY-12 and the competitive challenge by former city Comptroller Brad Lander against incumbent Rep. Dan Goldman in NY-10 — as well as all 63 state Senate and 150 Assembly seats.

NY.title: PRIMARY ELECTION 2026: NYC voters cast ballots in numerous key U.S. House races
NY.summary: Voters across New York City headed to the polls on Primary Day with more than 330,000 already checked in as of 3 p.m., including the 276,593 who cast early ballots, in a primary centered on a wave of contested Democratic congressional races that could reshape New York's House delegation.

NY.title: New York State Primary Day 2026: Key congressional races and the Mamdani effect
NY.summary: ABC7 New York covered Primary Day voting across New York State, with polls open from 6 a.m. to 9 p.m., highlighting how NYC Mayor Mamdani's endorsements in multiple congressional contests turned the primary into a test of progressive versus establishment Democratic strength ahead of November.

NY.title: New York House District 12 primary election live results: Lasher, Bores run
NY.summary: The Washington Post tracked live results in the NY-12 Democratic primary to succeed retiring Rep. Jerry Nadler, where Assemblymembers Micah Lasher and Alex Bores emerged as the leading candidates in a crowded eight-way field including Jack Schlossberg and George Conway.

OH.title: Ohio will be one of six states with a voter ID measure on the ballot this year
OH.summary: Ohio joins five other states in placing a voter ID constitutional amendment on the November 2026 ballot; Ohio's measure (SJR 10) passed the legislature on party-line votes and would enshrine existing photo ID requirements in the state constitution while extending the requirement to absentee voters.

OK.title: June Primary Election — 2026 Election Results
OK.summary: The Oklahoma State Election Board certified June 16 primary results on June 23. Rep. Kevin Hern won the Republican Senate nomination outright with over 63% of the vote; the governor's race heads to an August 25 runoff between Mike Mazzei and Gentner Drummond; a Democratic Senate runoff between N'kiyla Jasmine Thomas and Jim Priest was also set for August 25.

RI.title: Deadlines for RI Candidates Filing for Office Are Approaching
RI.summary: Rhode Island's candidate filing window for the 2026 general election opened June 22, with candidates for state and federal office having a limited window to submit paperwork to appear on the November ballot; the article outlines key deadlines for prospective candidates.

SD.title: Runoff election polls open at 7 a.m. in Sioux Falls
SD.summary: Polls opened June 23 for the Sioux Falls mayoral runoff election, with voters choosing between the top two finishers from the initial mayoral contest; the runoff determines Sioux Falls' next mayor.

SD.title: Sioux Falls runoff absentee voting comes to a close
SD.summary: Absentee voting for the June 23 Sioux Falls mayoral runoff election closed June 22, as election officials prepared for Election Day; officials reported strong early voter turnout in the closely watched race.

TX.title: Ken Paxton and James Talarico are neck and neck in U.S. Senate race, new poll finds
TX.summary: A University of Texas/Texas Politics Project poll released June 23 shows Republican Ken Paxton leading Democrat James Talarico 43% to 42% in the Texas U.S. Senate race, a dramatic shift from April when Talarico led by 8 points, signaling Republican consolidation around Paxton following his upset runoff victory over Sen. John Cornyn.

VA.title: Civil rights group files motion to speed up Va.'s reform of voter registration process for ex-felons
VA.summary: A civil rights group filed a motion for an expedited court remedy as thousands of Virginians with certain past felony convictions remain unable to complete voter registration despite a court order requiring state compliance. With early voting for the August 4 primary already underway, affected applicants are left in limbo as Virginia's Department of Elections has declined to fully process their applications.

WI.title: Missy Hughes drops out of governor race, endorses Sara Rodriguez
WI.summary: Missy Hughes became the first Democratic gubernatorial candidate to exit Wisconsin's crowded primary on June 22, endorsing Lt. Gov. Sara Rodriguez. Hughes remains on the August 11 primary ballot because Wisconsin's candidate withdrawal deadline had already passed.

WI.title: Missy Hughes drops out of Wisconsin governor's race
WI.summary: Missy Hughes suspended her Wisconsin governor campaign June 22 and endorsed Lt. Gov. Sara Rodriguez, calling her the strongest candidate to defeat Republican frontrunner Tom Tiffany in November. The endorsement shifts the Democratic primary dynamics with six candidates remaining ahead of the August 11 vote.

WI.title: First Major Candidate Drops Out of Wisconsin Governor Race
WI.summary: Missy Hughes's departure from Wisconsin's Democratic governor primary on June 22 narrows the field to six active candidates, with a Democratic debate scheduled for July 28 at Marquette University and the primary set for August 11, 2026.

WV.title: Schedule set for official contesting of Harrison County House race election results
WV.summary: A formal schedule has been set for the official contest of election results in a Harrison County West Virginia House of Delegates race, following a challenge to the certified primary outcome; the proceeding will determine whether the certified results stand or are overturned.

AZ.title: Early voting in Arizona's primary elections kicks off
AZ.summary: In-person early voting for Arizona's July 21 primary election began June 24, with Maricopa County opening more than a dozen locations and adding 17 more early voting sites compared to the 2022 primary.

AZ.title: Your voter guide: Arizona primary election 2026
AZ.summary: A comprehensive voter guide for Arizona's July 21 primary outlines key races, voting options including early and mail-in ballots, and the new permanent July primary date signed into law by Governor Hobbs in February 2026.

CO.title: New challenge to Colorado Springs' April elections cites state Voting Rights Act
CO.summary: The League of Women Voters, Citizens Project, and Harvard Law School's Election Law Clinic challenged Colorado Springs' practice of holding mayoral and city council elections in low-turnout April odd-year elections as a violation of the state's new Colorado Voting Rights Act.

CT.title: Connecticut enacts no-excuse absentee voting, four other election bills in 2026
CT.summary: Connecticut enacted five new election laws in the 2026 session, including HB 5001 making Connecticut the 29th state with no-excuse absentee voting, along with a ballot cure process, automatic absentee ballot application lists, and increased penalties for harassing election workers.

CT.title: Several New Laws Take Effect July 1 In Connecticut
CT.summary: Among more than 80 new Connecticut laws taking effect July 1 is an election provision allowing voters to request permanent placement on an automatic absentee ballot application list, part of the recently enacted no-excuse absentee voting package.

GA.title: Scaled-back QR code bill headed to Gov. Brian Kemp's desk
GA.summary: Georgia lawmakers sent a revised bill to Gov. Kemp that delays the QR code tabulation ban to 2028 and narrows mandatory hand recounts to only the top two statewide races when the margin is under 0.5%.

GA.title: Georgia's QR codes for counting votes will remain for midterms after lawmakers vote to delay a fix
GA.summary: Georgia's legislature voted to delay its self-imposed ban on QR code ballot tabulation, pushing the deadline to 2028 while establishing a special committee to select the next voting system. The decision means Georgia's current Dominion machines will count ballots in the 2026 elections.

KS.title: Kansas poll of likely Democratic voters favors Holscher for governor, Hamilton for U.S. Senate
KS.summary: A Change Research poll of Democratic-leaning Kansas voters conducted June 11-15 shows pastor Adam Hamilton leading the Democratic U.S. Senate primary field and state Sen. Cindy Holscher ahead in the governor's race, setting the stage for competitive August 4 primaries.

KY.title: Andy Barr, Charles Booker win primary elections for Kentucky US Sen. Mitch McConnell's seat
KY.summary: Republican Rep. Andy Barr and Democrat Charles Booker won their respective primary elections for the Kentucky U.S. Senate seat being vacated by Mitch McConnell, setting up a November general election matchup in the first open Kentucky Senate race since 2010.

KY.title: Barr vs. Booker: Candidates in Kentucky's U.S. Senate race advance to November election
KY.summary: Trump-backed Andy Barr defeated Daniel Cameron in the Republican Senate primary while Charles Booker beat Amy McGrath on the Democratic side, advancing to a November general election for Kentucky's open U.S. Senate seat.

KY.title: Kentucky Senate seat: GOP's Andy Barr, Dem Charles Booker will square off
KY.summary: After Kentucky's June 18 primary, Republican Andy Barr and Democrat Charles Booker emerged as nominees who will compete in November for the U.S. Senate seat long held by Mitch McConnell.

MD.title: Takeaways from Maryland's 2026 primary election results
MD.summary: Post-primary analysis of Maryland's June 23 election found a mix of establishment wins and upsets, including a Black challenger defeating an incumbent in the Baltimore Sheriff's race, setting the stage for November contests.

MD.title: Maryland election results 2026 primary
MD.summary: The Baltimore Sun compiled full Maryland primary election results from June 23, 2026, covering races for governor, congressional seats, county executive positions, and state legislature.

MI.title: Michigan kicks off primary voting June 25 with absentee ballots
MI.summary: Michigan's August 4 primary election formally began with in-person absentee voting starting June 25, as Detroit mailed out 99,000 absentee ballots and no-reason absentee voting continues to drive high mail ballot usage across the state.

NV.title: Tracking 2026 Nevada ballot measures: What's up for a vote and what's still in limbo
NV.summary: The Nevada Independent tracked the status of 2026 ballot measures, including a voter ID constitutional amendment (Question 7, already heading to November after 73% approval in 2024) and an open primaries initiative needing nearly 149,000 valid signatures by a June 24 deadline.

ND.title: State Canvassing Board certifies results of June election
ND.summary: The North Dakota State Canvassing Board officially certified the June 9, 2026 primary election results, finalizing all state, judicial, and legislative contests after all 53 county canvassing boards submitted their tallies.

ND.title: 20.86% voter turnout in North Dakota primary election
ND.summary: Final certified data shows 125,225 ballots cast in North Dakota's June primary — a 20.86% turnout rate, on par with the state's 25-year historical average for primary elections.

OH.title: Ohio sec. of state candidates split on mail-in voter ID bill DeWine considering veto on
OH.summary: With Gov. DeWine weighing a veto of the absentee voter ID bill by June 25, secretary of state candidates in both parties diverged on the legislation, with Democrats urging a veto while some Republicans backed the new mail-ballot ID requirement.

RI.title: Gov. McKee and his main rival Foulkes officially declare their candidacy for September primary
RI.summary: Rhode Island Gov. Dan McKee and challenger Helena Foulkes both filed official candidacy paperwork for the September 8 Democratic gubernatorial primary, with recent polling showing McKee trailing Foulkes significantly despite a narrow win over her in their 2022 matchup.

SC.title: SC runoff election results: Candidates will face winners of primary in general election
SC.summary: A wrap-up of South Carolina's June 23 runoff election results, confirming Alan Wilson as the Republican gubernatorial nominee, David Stumbo as the GOP attorney general nominee, and 25-year-old Zyon Khalifa as the Democratic nominee in House District 2 — all set for November.

TN.title: Tennessee's 2026 candidate lists finalized for state and federal races
TN.summary: Tennessee finalized its 2026 candidate lists for state and federal races, with petition pickup beginning June 22 ahead of the August 6 primary — the first election under newly redrawn congressional maps that have drawn multiple federal lawsuits.

TN.title: Up Next, the August 6 Primary Election: More Open Seats, Competitive Races, and New Congressional Districts
TN.summary: Tennessee's August 6 primary features the first open governor's race since 2018, newly redrawn congressional districts splitting Memphis, and a July 7 voter registration deadline — a high-stakes election cycle shaped by ongoing redistricting litigation.

TX.title: Texas lawmakers seek fixes to statewide voter registration system
TX.summary: Texas lawmakers demanded assurances from the Secretary of State that the troubled TEAM voter registration and election management system — relaunched last summer and reported to malfunction for voter lookups, precinct assignments, and mail ballot tracking — will be fixed before the November midterms.

TX.title: Texas lawmakers want fixes to statewide voter registration system ahead of midterms
TX.summary: County election officials in Travis, Austin, Jackson and other Texas counties have complained that the TEAM system continues to malfunction, forcing some to create their own spreadsheets to track voter rolls and mail ballot requests, with most of the state's 254 counties relying on TEAM.

UT.title: Data center backlash helps sink Utah Senate President Stuart Adams in primary
UT.summary: Analysis of how public outcry over a large out-of-state data center proposal contributed to Utah Senate President Stuart Adams' primary defeat on June 23, in an election conducted predominantly by mail across the state.

UT.title: The big takeaways from Utah's primary elections
UT.summary: Utah's June 23 primary produced major upsets including the Senate President's ouster, confirming Utah's all-mail voting model continues to produce robust statewide participation.

UT.title: Utah primary election day ends with concessions from several candidates
UT.summary: Multiple Utah candidates conceded the night of the June 23 primary, with the Senate President's surprise defeat headlining a night of notable primary outcomes across Utah's mail-ballot-based election system.

AK.title: Alaska judge orders emergency hearing in ballot fight involving two Dan Sullivans
AK.summary: An Anchorage Superior Court judge granted an emergency hearing in the case of Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., a retired teacher removed from the August 18 primary ballot by the Alaska Division of Elections for allegedly not filing in good faith, with a June 28 ballot certification deadline looming.

AK.title: Dan Sullivan candidate appeal likely to go to Alaska Supreme Court, with one week until ballot deadline
AK.summary: The ballot eligibility challenge by Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. — a retired teacher sharing a name with incumbent U.S. Sen. Dan Sullivan — is expected to escalate to the Alaska Supreme Court, with the case centering on whether the Division of Elections overstepped its authority in disqualifying the challenger.

AZ.title: Maricopa County supervisors approve election plan amid dispute with recorder
AZ.summary: The Maricopa County Board of Supervisors unanimously approved the county's 2026 primary and general election plan, with Recorder Justin Heap notably absent amid his ongoing feud with the board, covering more than 200 voting centers ahead of the July 21 primary.

AR.title: US Supreme Court further erodes Voting Rights Act by declining Arkansas case, advocates say
AR.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court declined to review an Arkansas case challenging Act 658, which limits voter assistance at polls, leaving in place an 8th Circuit ruling that bars private parties from suing to enforce Section 208 of the Voting Rights Act in seven states.

AR.title: Supreme Court declines review of case against Arkansas law limiting voter assistance
AR.summary: The Supreme Court refused to hear a challenge to Arkansas Act 658, which prohibits anyone other than a poll worker from assisting more than six voters, leaving private parties without the ability to sue under Section 208 of the Voting Rights Act in the 8th Circuit.

AR.title: Supreme Court declines to hear Arkansas case, further weakening Voting Rights Act
AR.summary: The Supreme Court denied certiorari in the Arkansas United case, meaning private plaintiffs in seven Midwestern states can no longer sue to enforce Voting Rights Act Section 208 protections for voters with disabilities or language barriers.

CA.title: Want faster election results? California Democrats won't clamp down on late voters
CA.summary: California's primary took more than a week to call the governor's race, but Democratic leaders say they support faster results without pursuing changes such as earlier mail-ballot deadlines that they argue would reduce voter access.

CA.title: Was a stun gun fired at an elections office run by an election-denying conspiracy theorist?
CA.summary: A journalist reported witnessing an apparent stun gun activation outside Shasta County's elections office run by registrar Clint Curtis, an election denier who appears to have lost his reelection bid in the June 2 primary, drawing fresh attention to the troubled office.

DC.title: Poll: 78% of DC voters say ranked choice voting is simple, 74% support ranking candidates
DC.summary: A SurveyUSA poll found that 78% of DC voters found ranked choice voting simple to complete and 74% support ranking candidates, following DC's first-ever use of RCV in its June 16 primary election.

DC.title: Appeals court deals biggest setback yet to Trump DOJ's demands for confidential voter roll data
DC.summary: The Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals ruled 2-1 that the DOJ lacks authority to compel Michigan to hand over its unredacted voter registration database, the first federal appeals court loss for the DOJ in its nationwide voter roll data campaign against more than 30 states.

DC.title: Trump keeps sabotaging legislation over a voting bill. Here's what's in it
DC.summary: President Trump canceled a bipartisan housing bill signing, demanding Congress first pass the SAVE America Act requiring documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote in federal elections — a bill that has cleared the House but lacks 60 Senate votes.

DE.title: Delaware House passes John Lewis Voting Rights Act, Senate review next
DE.summary: The Delaware House passed HB 444, the Delaware John Lewis Voting Rights Act, along party lines, sending it to the Senate; the bill would establish state-level protections against voter suppression and vote dilution, with the Attorney General empowered to bring enforcement lawsuits.

FL.title: Twelve candidates compete for open Florida congressional seat as Donalds exits for governor's race
FL.summary: With Rep. Byron Donalds vacating Florida's 19th Congressional District to run for governor, twelve candidates entered the Republican primary for the August 18 contest, including Madison Cawthorn, Catalina Lauf, Jim Oberweis, and Jim Schwartzel.

FL.title: 'The race is wide open': Poll shows Jim Schwartzel, Jim Oberweis leading crowded CD 19 field
FL.summary: A new poll shows media figure Jim Schwartzel at 13% and Jim Oberweis at just under 12% in Florida's CD-19 Republican primary, with 54% of voters still undecided ahead of the August 18 contest for the open seat.

FL.title: Meet the Florida Democrats running for governor against David Jolly
FL.summary: After Orange County Mayor Jerry Demings dropped out due to health problems, former Republican David Jolly emerged as the clear Democratic frontrunner for governor, with five other candidates qualifying to challenge him in the August 18 primary.

GA.title: Special session ends as lawmakers postpone mandated changes to Georgia's election system
GA.summary: Georgia's special legislative session concluded with passage of SB 3EX, extending the deadline to remove QR codes from ballot tabulation from July 1, 2026 to January 1, 2028, while adjourning without taking up redistricting.

GA.title: Georgia lawmakers delay a major change to the state's voting system
GA.summary: The Georgia legislature passed a bill extending the QR code ballot deadline to 2028, averting a crisis that would have left the state without a legally compliant voting system for the November midterms, amid partisan debate over hand-counting accuracy.

GA.title: Georgia Republicans backtrack on redistricting plans
GA.summary: Georgia House Speaker Jon Burns and Senate leaders rejected Gov. Brian Kemp's call to redraw congressional and state legislative maps during the special session, citing pending court cases and pressure from civil rights organizations protecting majority-minority districts.

GA.title: Georgia Republicans Cancel Redistricting Special Session
GA.summary: GOP legislative leaders scrapped redistricting plans during the special session, ending June 24 without new maps being drawn — attributed in part to massive voter mobilization by Black-led advocacy groups who rallied against plans that would have eliminated majority-minority districts.

GA.title: Special session ends with election fix
GA.summary: Georgia's special session concluded with passage of the QR code extension bill heading to Gov. Kemp's desk, which includes a hand recount requirement for top statewide races within a 0.5% margin, averting a legal crisis just days before the July 1 deadline.

HI.title: Civil Beat Election Forum: Congressional District 1 (Keohokalole vs. Case)
HI.summary: Civil Beat hosted a live public forum on June 24 for Hawaii's 1st Congressional District primary candidates, featuring Jarrett Keohokalole, as incumbent Ed Case declined to participate ahead of Hawaii's August 8 primary election.

IN.title: Indiana Republican platform now backs property tax elimination, closed primaries
IN.summary: Delegates at the Indiana GOP state convention approved a new party platform explicitly endorsing closed primary elections and property tax elimination, with the closed-primaries plank directly relevant to future voter eligibility rules if enacted into law.

MN.title: Minnesota primary elections 2026: What you need to know as voting begins
MN.summary: Early voting for Minnesota's Aug. 11 primary opens June 26, with major races for governor and U.S. Senate; the article explains all voting options including mail, in-person absentee, and a new option to feed ballots directly into tabulators at election offices.

MO.title: Missouri secretary of state sues to close records on redistricting referendum signatures
MO.summary: Missouri Secretary of State Denny Hoskins filed suit against the People Not Politicians PAC seeking a court declaration that he need not fulfill a Sunshine Law request for records on how his office is reviewing over 305,000 signatures on a referendum petition challenging the state's new congressional map.

MS.title: Voter voices: 'I thought that was my voter registration'
MS.summary: Mississippi voters share experiences of confusion following the mailing of new voter registration cards reflecting redistricted precincts, with some residents finding they were not registered when they showed up to vote.

MS.title: Judge rules against DeSoto County redistricting lawsuit
MS.summary: U.S. District Judge Glen H. Davidson ruled that plaintiffs failed to prove DeSoto County's 2022 district maps were drawn to intentionally dilute Black voting power under Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, with the ACLU calling the decision 'deeply disappointing.'

MS.title: Judge rules against effort to create majority-Black DeSoto County districts
MS.summary: A federal judge sided with DeSoto County in a Voting Rights Act lawsuit challenging the county's district maps as racially discriminatory, finding that the Mississippi NAACP and co-plaintiffs did not provide sufficient evidence of intentional vote dilution.

MS.title: Federal Judge rules DeSoto County did not discriminate on redistricting maps
MS.summary: Federal Judge Glen H. Davidson rejected claims that DeSoto County's Board of Supervisors and Election Commission drew maps intended to prevent Black candidates from winning elected office, after a two-week bench trial.

MT.title: The ballot questions likely to come before voters in November
MT.summary: Following the June 19 signature submission deadline, Montana Free Press surveyed which proposed ballot measures collected enough signatures to potentially qualify for the November 2026 general election, including initiatives on nonpartisan courts and campaign finance limits.

MT.title: Campaign behind Montana ballot measure to guarantee impartial, predictable, transparent, and expeditious processes for ballot initiatives submits signatures
MT.summary: The campaign behind a Montana ballot measure aimed at protecting the citizen initiative process submitted its signatures to county election officials, seeking qualification for the November 2026 general election ballot.

NC.title: Sweeping election law bill passes key NC House committee, but more changes possible
NC.summary: The NC House Rules Committee advanced House Bill 958 — a sweeping 37-page elections omnibus — on a 14-9 party-line vote, with House Speaker Destin Hall saying the full chamber would vote the following day.

NC.title: Proposed NC election law would increase secrecy for political donors, change audit rules
NC.summary: NC Republicans' omnibus elections bill would raise donor disclosure thresholds to increase campaign-finance secrecy and give the Republican state auditor new discretion to select counties for post-election audits.

NC.title: Election bill fate could depend on late NC legislator negotiations
NC.summary: Bipartisan talks were underway over House Bill 958, with lawmakers negotiating over the ballot-challenge window length and a provision banning election officials from making statements encouraging voter turnout.

NC.title: Protests in Raleigh as NC lawmakers push for election law changes
NC.summary: Hundreds of protesters gathered at the NC General Assembly as Republicans advanced the elections omnibus bill that Democrats and voting rights groups say would restrict ballot access and increase partisan control over elections.

NE.title: RNC Sues Over 'Never Residents' Voting in Nebraska Elections
NE.summary: The RNC filed a lawsuit in Lancaster County challenging a 2010 Nebraska law allowing U.S. citizens who have never resided in Nebraska but have a parent registered to vote there to cast ballots in the state, arguing it violates residency requirements.

NH.title: Weeks before election, state appeals ruling striking down proof-of-citizenship voting law
NH.summary: With New Hampshire's September 8 primary less than 11 weeks away, the state AG appealed a ruling striking down HB 1569 requiring documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote, seeking a stay while the case goes to the 1st Circuit.

NJ.title: Mixed reception for bill allowing candidates' names to be rotated on ballot
NJ.summary: A New Jersey Assembly committee held a hearing on a bill to allow candidate name rotation on primary ballots, with voting rights advocates and election officials raising concerns about partisan discretion and the creation of over 500 different ballot styles per county.

NM.title: New Mexico primary election: Four contested races head to vote recounts
NM.summary: New Mexico's State Canvassing Board certified June 2 primary results and ordered automatic recounts in four close races, including a state House District 66 Republican primary where the top two candidates were separated by just eight votes.

NV.title: Nevada officials praise federal judge's blocking of Trump elections executive order
NV.summary: A federal judge permanently barred the Trump administration from implementing key parts of its elections executive order, including proof-of-citizenship requirements for voter registration, in a lawsuit co-led by Nevada; AG Aaron Ford and SoS Francisco Aguilar hailed the ruling.

NY.title: Three New York Democrats backed by Mamdani win House seat primaries; 2 incumbents lose
NY.summary: Three progressive candidates endorsed by NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani won Democratic House primaries, defeating incumbents Dan Goldman and Adriano Espaillat while Claire Valdez took an open seat, marking a significant progressive shift in New York City's congressional delegation.

NY.title: N.Y. House Democrat Espaillat loses 13th District primary to Avila Chevalier
NY.summary: Five-term Rep. Adriano Espaillat, chair of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, lost his NY-13 primary to democratic socialist Darializa Avila Chevalier by roughly 2,000 votes with 94% reporting.

NY.title: Incumbent NY Comptroller DiNapoli Defeats Primary Challengers
NY.summary: Incumbent state Comptroller Tom DiNapoli won the Democratic primary with roughly 60% of the vote, defeating challengers Drew Warshaw and Raj Goyle in his first primary contest in 20 years.

NY.title: 5 takeaways from New York 2026 primary election results
NY.summary: New York primary voters unseated numerous Democratic incumbents with Mayor Zohran Mamdani's endorsed candidates sweeping multiple congressional races, widely described as a significant progressive wave with implications for the November general elections.

NY.title: New York primary could forecast future for Democrats. Here's what you need to know
NY.summary: NPR analyzed New York's June 23 primary results, noting progressive wins in safe Democratic seats while more moderate candidates prevailed in competitive districts, setting up a test of whether the party's leftward shift translates to general-election success.

RI.title: Declared safe: Most state lawmakers unopposed after filing deadline passes
RI.summary: After the June 24 declaration-of-candidacy deadline, nearly two-thirds of Rhode Island General Assembly incumbents seeking reelection faced no challengers, with 44 of 75 House members running unopposed.

TX.title: Will Texas' new top voting official be a 'disruptor'? Locals are preparing for it
TX.summary: Texas election officials and voting rights advocates are preparing for the likely appointment of state Rep. Nate Schatzline — a pastor with no election administration experience who has repeated baseless fraud claims — as Secretary of State just months before competitive midterm elections.

WA.title: With mail-in voting under threat, election officials say Washington voters should use drop boxes or mail ballots a week before Election Day
WA.summary: Washington election officials are urging voters to use drop boxes or mail ballots at least a week early, citing a pending Supreme Court ruling in Watson v. RNC that could eliminate the state's grace period for accepting mail ballots postmarked by but received after Election Day.

AK.title: Alaska judge facing June 30 deadline to rule in 'sham candidate' Sullivan court case
AK.summary: An Alaska Superior Court judge must decide before June 30 — when ballots must begin printing — whether Petersburg's Dan Sullivan, a retired teacher who shares the name of incumbent U.S. Sen. Dan S. Sullivan, can remain on the August primary ballot. The Division of Elections disqualified him on June 15, ruling his candidacy was not filed in good faith and was intended to confuse voters.

CO.title: Phil Weiser leads Michael Bennet in new poll, with Colorado's Democratic primary for governor coming down to undecided voters
CO.summary: A new Public Policy Polling survey shows Attorney General Phil Weiser leading U.S. Sen. Michael Bennet 45%–36% among likely Democratic primary voters, with 19% still undecided, five days before Colorado's June 30 primary election that will determine the Democratic nominee for governor.

CO.title: Primary Election Ballots Returned: June 25, 2026
CO.summary: Colorado's Secretary of State reported 578,570 ballots returned statewide as of June 25, with five days remaining before the June 30 primary election; officials warned it is too late to mail ballots and urged voters to use the 437 drop boxes or 137 in-person voting centers open across the state.

KS.title: Democratic candidates for Kansas governor pitch campaign priorities to voters
KS.summary: Democratic gubernatorial candidates Curt Skoog, Ethan Corson, and Cindy Holscher pitched voters on healthcare, rural economic development, and data center concerns ahead of the August 4 Kansas primary. Skoog presented his 'THRIVE Kansas' plan while Corson launched nearly $1 million in TV ads and Holscher called for a statewide pause on data center construction.

KY.title: Latest Beshear PAC report shows continuing signs of a presidential run
KY.summary: Gov. Andy Beshear's super PAC filed a May FEC report showing spending concentrated in early presidential primary states including Iowa, South Carolina, and New Hampshire, consistent with preparations for a 2028 presidential run. The PAC also paid for Beshear's political travel and consultants, signaling his political activities as Kentucky's 2026 election cycle heads toward the November general election.

LA.title: Louisiana early voting sees steep decline ahead of June 27 election
LA.summary: In-person early voting for Louisiana's June 27 Republican and Democratic Senate primary runoffs fell nearly 40% from the May primary, with roughly 151,637 voters casting early ballots statewide. The sharp decline signals potentially low overall turnout for the Republican U.S. Senate runoff between U.S. Rep. Julia Letlow and State Treasurer John Fleming.

LA.title: Voter guide: Louisiana's June 27 primary runoff election
LA.summary: WWL-TV published a comprehensive voter guide for Louisiana's June 27 party primary runoffs covering poll hours (7 a.m.–8 p.m.), voter eligibility, absentee ballot deadlines (request by June 23, return by June 26), and the key statewide races including the Republican U.S. Senate runoff between Julia Letlow and John Fleming.

MD.title: Maryland election results 2026 primary
MD.summary: The Baltimore Sun's running results roundup updated June 25, covering vote totals across Maryland's June 23 primary for governor, congressional, state legislative, county executive, and local races statewide.

MD.title: Concessions, victory laps mark the day after a 'smooth' Maryland primary contest
MD.summary: The day after Maryland's primary, losing candidates — including David Trone in the 6th District — formally conceded, while officials described the overall election administration as smooth despite a prior mail-ballot party mismatch issue that prompted a lawsuit seeking to delay certification.

ME.title: See how ranked-choice ballots moved to Pingree, Charles and Dunlap
ME.summary: The Portland Press Herald analyzed how ranked-choice voting reallocated ballots through multiple rounds in Maine's June 9 gubernatorial and 2nd Congressional District primaries, resulting in come-from-behind wins for Hannah Pingree and Matt Dunlap. The breakdown illustrates how backup choices from eliminated candidates determined outcomes in races where no one initially held a majority.

ME.title: How Maine differs from the other state with ranked-choice voting
ME.summary: The Portland Press Herald examined differences between Maine's and Alaska's ranked-choice voting systems following the completion of Maine's 2026 primary tabulation, contextualizing Maine's multi-week counting process and the three major races resolved by RCV.

ME.title: Inside the 17-hour final day of Maine's ranked-choice voting count
ME.summary: The Maine Monitor reported from inside the final marathon session of Maine's ranked-choice voting tabulation, which involved a printer jam, spreadsheet issues, mixed-up memory sticks, and a livestream failure. The 17-hour session ultimately confirmed Hannah Pingree and Bobby Charles as gubernatorial nominees and Matt Dunlap as the Democratic 2nd District nominee.

MI.title: How to vote in Michigan's 2026 primary election
MI.summary: Votebeat published a voter guide explaining absentee ballot procedures, voter ID requirements, drop-box access, and key deadlines for Michigan's August 4 primary, as clerks statewide were required to make ballots available starting June 25.

MI.title: Michigan absentee ballots becoming available statewide ahead of August primary
MI.summary: Michigan clerks were required by the state constitution to make absentee ballots available by June 25 — 40 days before the August 4 primary — opening a six-week voting window for governor, U.S. Senate, U.S. House, and state legislative races.

MI.title: As ballots go out, what to know about voting in Michigan's Aug. 4 primary
MI.summary: Bridge Michigan's voter guide covers how to request and return absentee ballots, where to vote early, registration deadlines, and what is on the August 4 Michigan primary ballot as ballots go out statewide.

MO.title: Missouri secretary of state sues to close records on redistricting referendum signatures
MO.summary: Missouri Secretary of State Denny Hoskins filed a lawsuit seeking a court order shielding his office from disclosing records about how it is reviewing signatures for the referendum challenging the Republican-gerrymandered congressional map, as People Not Politicians claimed preliminary tallies show enough verified signatures to make the November ballot.

NC.title: Roy Cooper leads Michael Whatley by 14 points in new NC Senate race poll
NC.summary: A Catawba College-YouGov poll of 1,000 North Carolina voters shows Democrat Roy Cooper leading Republican Michael Whatley 48% to 34% in the closely watched open U.S. Senate race, with Cooper holding advantages across city, suburban, and rural voters.

NC.title: Michael Whatley's Michigan roots largely disappear from his bio as he runs for Senate in North Carolina
NC.summary: An NBC News review found that Republican Senate candidate Michael Whatley has repeatedly claimed he 'grew up' in Blowing Rock, NC, but records show he was born in Michigan and lived there through early high school — raising questions about his stated North Carolina identity in the Senate race.

ND.title: North Dakota Supreme Court tosses ballot measure, finding term limits proposal unconstitutional
ND.summary: The North Dakota Supreme Court ruled that the Legislature's resolution placing a term-limits amendment on the November ballot was unconstitutional, finding the Legislature cannot propose changes to a constitutional provision voters enacted through the initiative process. The court directed the Secretary of State not to place the measure on the ballot.

NJ.title: Rep. Tom Kean, missing for months, is back home in New Jersey
NJ.summary: Rep. Thomas Kean Jr. (R-NJ-7), absent from Congress since March 5 due to an undisclosed medical condition, was spotted at his Westfield, NJ home on June 25. A spokesperson confirmed he plans to return to Congress on June 30 and will disclose his medical condition at that time, amid a competitive re-election race against Democrat Rebecca Bennett.

NY.title: NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani basks in the glow of big primary wins. Here's what they could mean.
NY.summary: Mayor Zohran Mamdani's three endorsed congressional candidates — Brad Lander (NY-10), Darializa Avila Chevalier (NY-13), and Claire Valdez (NY-7) — all won their June 23 Democratic primaries, unseating two incumbents. The article examines what the progressive sweep means for the fall general election and New York's competitive districts.

OH.title: Ohio Gov. Mike DeWine vetoes bill requiring mail-in voters show a copy of their ID to vote
OH.summary: Gov. DeWine vetoed House Bill 472, which would have required Ohioans to provide a photo ID copy when casting a mail-in ballot, saying the requirement would burden voters without meaningfully deterring fraud. The veto came as Ohio Republican legislators separately advanced a resolution to place voter ID requirements in the state constitution on the November ballot.

SD.title: Doeden and Rhoden will share the stage on Friday
SD.summary: Both Republican gubernatorial runoff candidates Toby Doeden and incumbent Gov. Larry Rhoden are confirmed to deliver remarks at the South Dakota Republican Party Convention in Rapid City on Friday night, marking what may be their final joint appearance before the July 28 runoff election. The Rhoden campaign has declined to debate Doeden before the runoff.

TN.title: Former congressman squares off with state House member in 6th District GOP primary
TN.summary: Former U.S. Rep. Van Hilleary and state Rep. Johnny Garrett are competing for the Republican nomination in Tennessee's newly redrawn 6th Congressional District, one of the seats reconfigured under the May 2026 special-session redistricting that split Memphis's majority-Black district. The August 6 primary is the first election under the new map.

TN.title: Tennessee's 2026 candidate lists finalized for state and federal races
TN.summary: Tennessee's Secretary of State released the finalized candidate list for the August 6 primary after the filing deadline. Key races include the open governor's seat featuring Sen. Marsha Blackburn and Rep. John Rose, plus contested primaries across newly redrawn congressional districts.

UT.title: "Cost me the election": Data centers trigger voter backlash
UT.summary: Utah Senate President Stuart Adams lost his June 23 Republican primary after championing the Stratos Project, a massive proposed data center near the Great Salt Lake. His defeat and that of two Box Elder County commissioners signals that data center opposition has become a significant voting issue capable of reshaping elections in Utah.

UT.title: Data center controversy unseats powerful Utah lawmaker
UT.summary: Utah Senate President Stuart Adams lost his GOP primary to challenger Stephanie Hollist after shepherding the controversial Stratos data center project through approvals, becoming the first sitting Utah Senate president to lose a primary in modern history.

VT.title: Why H. Brooke Paige appears 4 times on the Vt. Republican primary ballot
VT.summary: As Vermont Republicans struggle to recruit candidates, H. Brooke Paige is running simultaneously for secretary of state, treasurer, attorney general, and auditor to block Democrats from claiming GOP nominations via write-in campaigns. He plans to withdraw from three races after the August 11 primary and focus on the secretary of state contest against Democratic incumbent Sarah Copeland Hanzas.

WI.title: Wisconsin officials, voting rights advocates address fears about election security
WI.summary: Wisconsin election officials and voting rights advocates are preparing for potential disruptions ahead of the state's August primary and November general election, addressing fears that federal actors could interfere with polling places or election administration. Law Forward and other groups are focused on preventing federal seizure of 2020 election ballots, building clerk-law enforcement trust, and countering Trump's election executive orders.

WI.title: Judge blocks key pillars of Trump executive order restricting mail voting in 2026 election
WI.summary: U.S. District Judge Indira Talwani blocked key provisions of President Trump's executive order on elections, ruling unconstitutional his attempts to create centralized citizen voter lists and give USPS authority to limit mail ballot delivery. Wisconsin was among the 24 plaintiff jurisdictions covered by the injunction, which applies to the 2026 election cycle.

WY.title: Wyoming Supreme Court will not intervene in Gray voter data complaint
WY.summary: The Wyoming Supreme Court declined to intervene in a dispute over the Attorney General's Office handling of an election complaint against Secretary of State Chuck Gray. A Cheyenne lawyer had asked the high court to appoint a special prosecutor after two independent evaluations declined to bring criminal charges against Gray for sharing confidential voter registration data — including Social Security numbers — with the U.S. Department of Justice.

CA.title: California leaders yet to reach deal to keep billionaire tax off the ballot. Time is running out
CA.summary: State leaders were negotiating with SEIU-United Healthcare Workers West ahead of the June 25 deadline to withdraw the billionaire tax initiative from the November ballot, but no agreement had been reached. Governor Newsom opposed the measure, arguing a one-time 5% tax on California's roughly 200 billionaires would harm the state's economy.

CA.title: California billionaire tax proposal qualifies for the November ballot
CA.summary: California Secretary of State Shirley Weber announced that the SEIU-backed initiative to levy a one-time 5% tax on the roughly 200 California billionaires formally qualified for the November 3 ballot after signature verification was completed. The measure, estimated to generate $100 billion primarily for healthcare, has divided California Democrats, with Governor Newsom among those opposed.

CA.title: Billionaire tax, affordable housing: See the measures on California's November ballot
CA.summary: With the June 25 qualification deadline passed, California voters will decide on 14 statewide ballot measures in November, including a billionaire wealth tax, an $11 billion affordable housing bond, and voter ID requirements. Several measures were withdrawn after last-minute deals between interest groups and state lawmakers, while the billionaire tax remained on the ballot after negotiations collapsed.

CA.title: California's billionaire tax is headed to voters — and so are the measures to kill it
CA.summary: After the health care union behind the billionaire tax failed to reach a withdrawal deal by the June 25 deadline, the initiative will appear on the November ballot alongside two counter-measures funded by a coalition of billionaires including Google co-founder Sergey Brin. The counter-initiatives, backed by more than $100 million, include a constitutional amendment to ban retroactive taxation that would effectively nullify the billionaire tax if both pass.

CT.title: Dem Primaries Set; Congressional, Probate Petitioners Come Up Short
CT.summary: The Connecticut Secretary of the State's office published the list of Democratic and Republican primary candidates who will appear on August 11 ballots. Challenger candidates in several congressional and probate races, including a democratic socialist who sought to unseat 18-term Rep. Rosa DeLauro, failed to collect enough petition signatures to force primaries.

DE.title: Bills head to governor's desk: EVs rebates, voter protections, "captive audiences"
DE.summary: Delaware legislation clarifying that violence at or near a polling place — directed at voters, campaign volunteers, or election officials during canvassing or counting — constitutes a class G felony when carried out with intent to interfere with the election process passed the Senate and headed to Governor Matt Meyer's desk. Senate sponsor Sen. Tizzy Lockman noted the offense was already in state law but poorly worded in code.

DE.title: Delaware Legislature Races Toward June Deadline With Wide-Ranging Bills on Taxes, Elections, Guns, Immigration, and Health Care
DE.summary: With Delaware's General Assembly set to adjourn June 30, multiple election-related bills face a last-chance vote, including HB 188 (opening primaries to unaffiliated voters), HB 444 (the Delaware John Lewis Voting Rights Act, House-passed and pending Senate action), and constitutional amendments on same-day voter registration and restoring voting rights for people who have completed felony sentences.

DE.title: Immigrant protections and referenda reform head to governor, gun vendor bill back to senate
DE.summary: Referendum reform legislation (SB 322) passed both Delaware chambers and headed to Governor Meyer with days left in the session, as remaining election-related constitutional amendments — including on same-day voter registration, early voting, and no-excuse absentee voting — remained pending with the June 30 adjournment deadline looming.

GA.title: Georgia election bill deadlines: New law delays ballot QR code removal
GA.summary: Gov. Brian Kemp signed SB 3EX into law on June 25, extending the deadline for Georgia to remove QR code-based ballot tabulation from July 1, 2026 to January 1, 2028. The law also adds a mandatory hand recount provision limited to governor and lieutenant governor races when the margin falls within 0.5 percent.

HI.title: Dramatic Shakeup Coming To Hawai'i County Council
HI.summary: Following the close of candidate filing, at least four new members are expected to join the Hawai'i County Council after challengers lined up against three of five incumbents across multiple districts. Notable entrants include UFC Hall of Famer BJ Penn and former council member Eileen O'Hara, with the August 8 primary serving as the decisive contest in this heavily Democratic county.

ID.title: Idaho PACs spent more than $4.2M on primary races
ID.summary: Idaho political action committees spent more than $4.2 million on the May 2026 primary races, with most money flowing into Republican legislative contests between hardline conservative candidates and more mainstream Republicans. The top spender, "Defend and Protect Idaho," put more than $752,800 into supporting 23 Republican primary candidates and opposing 14 others.

IA.title: Libertarian candidates ask court to put them back on 2026 ballot
