IA.summary: Iowa Libertarian gubernatorial candidate Nicholas Gluba and his running mate Jules Cutler filed a petition for judicial review in Polk County District Court, asking a judge to reverse the State Objection Panel's decision removing them from the November ballot. The campaign argues that a Secretary of State employee wrongly told Cutler her affidavit of candidacy was not needed on the June 2 filing deadline.

IA.title: Iowa Libertarian candidates sue to get back on the ballot
IA.summary: Iowa Libertarian candidates Nicholas Gluba (governor) and Jules Cutler (lieutenant governor) filed suit in Polk County District Court seeking reinstatement to the November 2026 ballot after the State Objection Panel removed them for a missed affidavit deadline. The Gluba-Cutler campaign collected more than 8,000 petition signatures — more than double the 3,500 required — to qualify for the ballot.

IA.title: Sand announces 100 Iowa Republicans backing his governor bid
IA.summary: Democratic gubernatorial nominee Rob Sand launched the "Rob-Publicans" coalition, announcing endorsements from more than 100 registered Iowa Republicans and over 1,800 donations from Republican voters. The campaign highlights Sand's crossover appeal in what forecasters rate as a competitive toss-up governor's race against Republican Zach Lahn.

IA.title: Elections forecaster shifts Iowa governor's race to 'Toss-Up'
IA.summary: Inside Elections became the third major national election forecaster to shift Iowa's 2026 gubernatorial race to "Toss-Up," citing Democratic nominee Rob Sand's overwhelming fundraising advantage over Republican Zach Lahn and Lahn's vulnerabilities as a first-time candidate in a state seeing a political environment ready for change after a decade of Republican rule.

LA.title: Senate runoff polls show tighter gap between Fleming and Letlow
LA.summary: New polling ahead of Louisiana's June 27 Republican U.S. Senate runoff shows the gap between Rep. Julia Letlow and state Treasurer John Fleming has narrowed significantly since the May primary, where Letlow led by 17 points, with surveys now showing a near-deadlock between the two candidates.

LA.title: Fleming and Letlow seek GOP's nomination in Senate race
LA.summary: A profile of the two Republican candidates competing in Louisiana's June 27 U.S. Senate runoff, covering their backgrounds, campaign positions, and key policy differences — including carbon capture pipeline policy — driving the race.

LA.title: Fleming and Letlow trade attacks as they compete for Louisiana's open U.S. Senate seat
LA.summary: Republican Senate runoff candidates Julia Letlow and John Fleming exchanged sharp attacks in the days before the June 27 vote, with Fleming citing dishonest PAC ads and Letlow decrying $15 million in negative advertising against her, while the two also clashed over carbon capture pipeline policy.

LA.title: Jamie Davis, Gary Crockett compete in Democratic U.S. Senate runoff in Louisiana
LA.summary: Jamie Davis and Gary Crockett are competing in Louisiana's June 27 Democratic U.S. Senate primary runoff, with the winner set to make history as the first Black U.S. Senate campaign finalist in Louisiana since Reconstruction; Davis, a Tensas Parish farmer, holds the party endorsement and significant fundraising advantages.

LA.title: Crockett and Davis face off in Saturday's Democratic runoff for U.S. Senate
LA.summary: KALB previews the Louisiana Democratic U.S. Senate primary runoff between Gary Crockett and Jamie Davis scheduled for June 27, outlining the candidates' backgrounds and the stakes of the contest ahead of Election Day.

MS.title: Judge rules against effort to create majority-Black DeSoto County districts
MS.summary: Senior U.S. District Judge Glen Davidson ruled that plaintiffs in a 2024 voting rights lawsuit failed to prove that DeSoto County's electoral maps diluted Black voting power, dismissing the case. The decision follows the U.S. Supreme Court's ruling in Louisiana v. Callais, which substantially weakened Voting Rights Act protections against racially discriminatory redistricting.

NE.title: Republican National Committee sues Nebraska over state election law
NE.summary: The RNC and two Nebraska voters filed a lawsuit challenging a 2010 state law that allows U.S. citizens who have never resided in Nebraska to vote in state elections if they have a parent registered there, calling it unconstitutional. The suit seeks an expedited ruling before the November general election and mirrors a similar RNC action that succeeded in North Carolina.

OH.title: Will Ohio Republicans override Gov. DeWine's voter photo ID veto?
OH.summary: Following Gov. Mike DeWine's veto of House Bill 472, which would have required photo ID for mail-in voting, Ohio Republican lawmakers are weighing a veto override. At least four Republicans who voted for the bill said they would not support an override, making the effort unlikely before the legislature's summer recess.

OH.title: Republican officials irked by DeWine veto on absentee voter ID bill
OH.summary: Ohio Republican county officials and state lawmakers expressed frustration after Gov. DeWine vetoed legislation requiring photo identification for mail-in ballots, calling it a missed opportunity to strengthen election security. DeWine argued the bill would create unnecessary burdens for mail voters without meaningfully reducing fraud.

PA.title: Philadelphia residents like Josh Shapiro most, but continue to sour on John Fetterman, poll shows
PA.summary: A new Philadelphia Inquirer/Suffolk University CityView poll found 62% of Philadelphians view Gov. Josh Shapiro favorably, while just 24% view Sen. John Fetterman favorably — with only 17% of Democrats holding a positive view amid his repeated crossovers to support Trump.

PA.title: Shapiro and Garrity open to a 2026 PA governor debate
PA.summary: Spokespeople for both Gov. Josh Shapiro and Republican challenger Stacy Garrity told Spotlight PA the candidates are willing to participate in at least one debate ahead of November's general election, marking the first potential gubernatorial debate in Pennsylvania since 2018.

PA.title: Trump was welcomed to Pa. by Stacy Garrity. He didn't mention her at all.
PA.summary: President Trump visited the Mack Trucks plant in Macungie, Pennsylvania to campaign for vulnerable GOP Rep. Ryan Mackenzie in the competitive 7th Congressional District, but conspicuously failed to mention GOP gubernatorial nominee Stacy Garrity despite her endorsement of him.

PA.title: Pennsylvania Is the Key To the Battle For the House
PA.summary: Pennsylvania's four competitive U.S. House races — the most of any state — make it the pivotal battleground in the fight for congressional control this fall, with districts ranging from Bethlehem's Latino-heavy 7th to the Pocono Mountains 8th testing whether Republicans can hold gains made in 2024.

RI.title: 5 Democrats, 5 Republicans declare candidacy for Rhode Island governor
RI.summary: Following the June 24 filing deadline, five Democrats including incumbent Gov. Dan McKee, five Republicans, and nine independents filed declarations of candidacy for governor with the Rhode Island Secretary of State. Candidates must next collect 1,000 valid petition signatures by July 10 to qualify for the September 9 primary.

RI.title: Local Dems endorsement count has Foulkes leading 12-2
RI.summary: Helena Foulkes leads incumbent Gov. Dan McKee 12-to-2 in endorsements from municipal Democratic committees following the close of candidate filing for the 2026 governor's race, with Foulkes backed by committees in Providence, Warwick, Cranston, and Woonsocket. The tally underscores Foulkes' momentum heading into the September 9 Democratic primary.

SC.title: Alan Wilson wins GOP nomination for South Carolina governor after dual Trump endorsement
SC.summary: Attorney General Alan Wilson won the Republican gubernatorial runoff over Lt. Gov. Pamela Evette by a nearly 2-to-1 margin, advancing to face Democratic nominee Jermaine Johnson in November in South Carolina's first open governor's race since 2010. President Trump had initially endorsed Evette but issued a co-endorsement of both candidates before the June 23 runoff.

SC.title: Wilson wins GOP nomination for South Carolina governor after Trump hedges his bet on race
SC.summary: PBS NewsHour reported on Wilson's commanding June 23 runoff victory and the unusual dynamics of Trump's dual endorsement, noting Evette quickly conceded and endorsed Wilson as the Republican nominee heading into the November general election.

SD.title: Gubernatorial runoff candidates to speak at SD GOP Convention
SD.summary: South Dakota's Republican gubernatorial runoff candidates, Gov. Larry Rhoden and political newcomer Toby Doeden, are scheduled to address delegates at the South Dakota GOP state convention in Rapid City. The convention, running June 25-27, is where delegates will nominate candidates for constitutional offices ahead of the November general election.

WI.title: Riding primary momentum, democratic socialists eye a battleground state breakthrough
WI.summary: After progressive candidates swept New York congressional primaries, Wisconsin state Rep. Francesca Hong's democratic-socialist gubernatorial bid is drawing fresh attention as a test of whether left-wing candidates can win in competitive swing states. Hong has polled at or near the top of the crowded Democratic primary field ahead of the August 11 primary.

WV.title: Commissioners set hearings in contested Harrison County election case
WV.summary: The Harrison County Commission set a schedule for the formal contest of the District 71 House of Delegates Republican primary, in which incumbent Del. Laura Kimble lost to challenger Tim McNeely by six votes after a recount. Kimble alleges that unaffiliated voters were improperly allowed to cast ballots in the closed Republican primary, with a July 1 hearing and decision expected by July 6.

AK.title: Judge allows namesake challenger to Sen. Dan Sullivan to appear on Alaska ballot
AK.summary: An Anchorage Superior Court judge ruled that Dan J. Sullivan — a retired teacher with the same name and party as incumbent U.S. Sen. Dan S. Sullivan — is eligible to appear on the August 18 Alaska Senate primary ballot, overturning the Division of Elections' disqualification on 'good faith' grounds as unconstitutional.

AK.title: Judge finds Alaska Division of Elections' removal of Dan J Sullivan from US Senate race unlawful
AK.summary: Superior Court Judge Thomas Matthews ruled the Alaska Division of Elections acted unlawfully in disqualifying U.S. Senate challenger Dan J. Sullivan, with the state immediately appealing to the Alaska Supreme Court ahead of the ballot-printing deadline.

AK.title: US Senate challenger, incumbent with same name to appear on Alaska ballot
AK.summary: A court ruling placed both challenger Dan J. Sullivan (retired teacher) and incumbent Sen. Dan S. Sullivan on the Alaska Senate primary ballot, raising voter confusion concerns as both are Republicans in Alaska's top-four nonpartisan primary leading to a ranked-choice general election.

AZ.title: Lawsuits are challenging 5 ballot measures from Arizona Republican lawmakers
AZ.summary: Opponents filed lawsuits against five measures referred to Arizona's November ballot by the Republican-led Legislature, including an election measure that would require voters to show photo ID and mandate in-precinct ballot tabulation, arguing the measures unconstitutionally bundle unrelated topics in violation of Arizona's anti-log-rolling rule.

CA.title: California unions, hospitals strike deal — but billionaire tax heads to ballot
CA.summary: California hospitals and the SEIU United Healthcare Workers West union pulled two competing ballot initiatives before the state filing deadline, but a union-backed measure to levy a one-time 5% wealth tax on California billionaires to fund healthcare and education remained on track for the November 2026 ballot after Gov. Newsom failed to broker a deal to remove it.

CO.title: Republicans sue Colorado to block votes by some overseas U.S. citizens
CO.summary: The Republican National Committee sued Colorado Secretary of State Jena Griswold, challenging the state's policy of allowing overseas U.S. citizens who have never personally lived in Colorado to register and vote using a parent's or spouse's former Colorado residency. The suit was filed four days before the June 30 primary as part of a broader RNC campaign targeting similar overseas voter policies in six states.

CO.title: RNC sues Jena Griswold over 'never-resident' overseas Colorado voters
CO.summary: The RNC, joined by Douglas County Clerk Sheri Davis and U.S. Rep. Jeff Crank, filed a 24-page complaint arguing that Colorado's UOCAVA voter policy unconstitutionally allows approximately 40,000 overseas 'never-residents' to vote in state elections, with Secretary Griswold calling the suit a 'sad and unpatriotic' attempt to disenfranchise eligible voters.

CO.title: Voting rights groups are suing Colorado Springs over when the city holds its elections
CO.summary: Common Cause Colorado, Citizens Project, and the League of Women Voters of the Pikes Peak Region filed suit alleging that Colorado Springs' off-year April municipal elections violate the state Voting Rights Act by depressing turnout among Black and Hispanic voters, who participate at roughly half the rate of white voters in those contests compared to November elections.

DC.title: Pennsylvania's voter rolls are safe from DOJ's grab, rules federal judge, bringing Justice Dept record to 0-10
DC.summary: A federal judge dismissed the Trump Justice Department's lawsuit seeking Pennsylvania's unredacted voter registration database, the tenth consecutive federal court loss in the administration's nationwide campaign to obtain sensitive state voter data. The DOJ has sued 31 jurisdictions including Washington D.C. seeking voter rolls to build a national voter database.

DC.title: A federal judge tossed a Justice Department lawsuit seeking Pennsylvania voters' private information
DC.summary: Federal judge Cathy Bissoon dismissed the Trump DOJ's demand for Pennsylvania's voter rolls, writing that public statements from officials revealed the data collection's intended purpose was to 'weaponize' voter information in future elections and as an immigration enforcement tool, raising serious concerns about federal overreach into election administration.

FL.title: 6 takeaways from Florida GOP's Sunshine State Showdown
FL.summary: Florida Republican gubernatorial candidates clashed at the party's Sunshine State Showdown on June 27, which substituted for a cancelled formal debate after the Republican Party of Florida determined only frontrunner Byron Donalds met its fundraising and polling qualifications ahead of the August 18 primary.

FL.title: Fact-checking Florida Republicans' Sunshine State Showdown
FL.summary: PolitiFact fact-checked claims by Florida Republican gubernatorial candidates at the June 27 Sunshine State Showdown event, which replaced the cancelled GOP debate, with key races for governor and all 28 U.S. House seats set for the August 18 primary under a newly redrawn congressional map.

GA.title: Georgia election board gives final approval to new rule requiring hand counting of ballots
GA.summary: The Georgia State Election Board gave final approval to a new rule requiring hand counting of ballots at polling places on election night, drawing criticism from election integrity advocates who argued it could complicate ballot verification.

GA.title: Georgia's 13th Congressional District Special Election: Voter Registration Deadline Is June 29
GA.summary: Voters in Georgia's 13th Congressional District have until June 29 to register or update their registration for the upcoming special election to fill the vacated congressional seat.

HI.title: New Law Makes Hawaii Automatic Voter Registration Opt-Out
HI.summary: A new Hawaii law (Act 67/SB 2239), signed in May and taking effect January 1, 2027, will shift the state to an automatic voter registration opt-out system, automatically registering eligible residents to vote unless they choose to opt out.

HI.title: Dramatic Shakeup on Hawaii County Council After Primary Results Certified
HI.summary: Hawaii County Council saw a significant reshuffling of seats following certification of primary election results, with several incumbents losing their bids for re-election in a development that signals major changes in county governance heading into the general election.

IA.title: Republicans target Iowa Libertarian candidates, urging them to drop out of congressional races
IA.summary: Iowa Republicans are pressuring Libertarian congressional candidates to withdraw from the 2nd and 3rd Congressional District races, citing concerns that Libertarian votes could tip close November contests away from Republicans. The pressure campaign follows the State Objection Panel's removal of two Libertarian gubernatorial candidates from the ballot.

IA.title: LISTEN: Sec. RFK, Jr. tries to convince Iowa candidate to drop out of race
IA.summary: Audio released by The Washington Post captured U.S. Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. calling Iowa Libertarian congressional candidate Rick Stewart and urging him to drop out of the 2nd Congressional District race, describing himself as a White House liaison. Stewart declined to withdraw.

IA.title: Iowa Libertarian Gubernatorial Candidate Files Ballot Access Lawsuit
IA.summary: Libertarian gubernatorial nominee Nicholas Gluba filed a state court lawsuit challenging his removal from Iowa's November ballot, arguing he and running mate Jules Cutler relied in good faith on a Secretary of State employee's incorrect guidance about filing requirements.

IN.title: Review of Ballots Done in Senate District 23 Recount — And Now We Wait
IN.summary: The manual recount of ballots in Indiana's Senate District 23 race has been completed, but results are being withheld pending legal proceedings following an extremely close margin in the Republican primary.

IN.title: Hendricks County to Conduct Recount in Close Republican Primary Race
IN.summary: Hendricks County election officials are set to conduct a recount in a tight Republican primary race, following a petition from one of the candidates, adding to a series of post-primary ballot reviews across Indiana.

KS.title: Kansas GOP gubernatorial candidate Philip Sarnecki inflates personal record on voting frequency
KS.summary: Kansas Republican gubernatorial candidate Philip Sarnecki claimed to have missed only two elections in 20 years, but public records show he skipped six elections, including the 2022 primary featuring the abortion constitutional amendment. Sarnecki declined to explain the discrepancies.

LA.title: Trump-backed Julia Letlow wins Louisiana GOP Senate runoff, completing president's revenge plot against Bill Cassidy
LA.summary: U.S. Rep. Julia Letlow won the Republican Senate nomination in Louisiana's June 27 runoff, defeating state Treasurer John Fleming 57% to 43%. Letlow will face Democratic nominee Jamie Davis in November for the seat vacated by Sen. Bill Cassidy.

LA.title: Letlow, Davis win Senate primary runoffs in Louisiana; will face off in November
LA.summary: Julia Letlow and Jamie Davis won their respective party runoffs in Louisiana's June 27 primary, setting the November general election matchup for Bill Cassidy's Senate seat. Statewide runoff turnout was approximately 17%, with Democratic participation falling 43% compared to the earlier primary.

LA.title: Louisiana Senate election by the numbers: See turnout figures, where Letlow won
LA.source: The Times-Picayune / The New Orleans Advocate
LA.summary: A detailed breakdown of Louisiana's June 27 Senate runoff shows 316,538 Republican ballots cast and a 43% drop in Democratic participation compared to the May primary, with overall statewide turnout at roughly 17%. Letlow won across Republican strongholds statewide.

MD.title: Maryland election results 2026 primary
MD.summary: The Baltimore Sun published updated primary election returns from Maryland's June 23 gubernatorial primary, covering results for governor, congressional races, and local offices as canvassing of mail-in and provisional ballots continued through late June.

MN.title: Early voting for Minnesota's August 11 primary election begins with key races to sort out
MN.summary: Early voting kicked off June 26 for Minnesota's August 11 primary, with crowded fields in both the governor's and U.S. Senate races; voters can cast absentee ballots by mail or in person through August 10, and a new early-voting option lets voters feed ballots directly into tabulators up to 18 days before the primary.

MN.title: Early primary voting begins today. Here's what you need to know.
MN.summary: Minnesota's early voting period for the August 11 primary opened June 26, with all statewide offices on the ballot including governor, U.S. Senate, attorney general, secretary of state, and state auditor; the article details registration deadlines, voting locations, and Minnesota's open-primary rules.

MN.title: How to vote early in Minnesota's August primary
MN.summary: Axios Twin Cities published a voter guide explaining early voting options for Minnesota's August 11 primary, covering absentee mail ballots, in-person early voting at local offices, registration deadlines, and the open-primary rules that allow voters to choose any party's ballot without prior registration.

MO.title: Millions of dollars pour into Missouri ballot fights over taxes and majority rule
MO.summary: Campaigns for and against Missouri's Amendment 4 and Amendment 5 on the August 4 primary ballot have raised $14.5 million combined. Amendment 4 would require citizen initiatives to win majorities in all eight congressional districts, while Amendment 5 would expand sales taxes to replace the personal income tax.

MS.title: Mississippi Democrats seeking new midterm election voters
MS.summary: Mississippi Today reports on Democratic efforts to register and mobilize new voters ahead of the November U.S. Senate contest between Democratic nominee Scott Colom and incumbent Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, noting that midterm turnout will be significantly lower than in presidential election years.

MT.title: Nonpartisan courts initiative qualifies for ballot
MT.summary: Montanans for Nonpartisan Courts announced it gathered more than 102,000 signatures from 57 House districts to qualify CI-132 for Montana's November 2026 general election ballot, which would add nonpartisan judicial elections to the Montana Constitution, preserving a practice in place since 1936.

NC.title: How an under-the-radar GOP official is shaping local voting plans in North Carolina
NC.summary: State Auditor Dave Boliek, whose office gained authority over the State Board of Elections from the Republican-controlled legislature, is weighing in on county early voting plans for the November general election, prompting concern from voting rights advocates who say he is exceeding his statutory role in ways that could reduce early voting access.

NE.title: Nebraska Supreme Court rules voter data case is moot because feds already have records
NE.summary: The Nebraska Supreme Court dismissed a challenge to the transfer of the state's voter registration data to the U.S. Department of Justice, ruling the matter moot because the data — including voter names, birth dates, addresses, driver's license numbers, and partial Social Security numbers — had already been released by Secretary of State Bob Evnen.

NJ.title: Could more ineligible voters be on NJ's rolls? New guilty plea fuels debate
NJ.summary: A French citizen's guilty plea for illegally voting in New Jersey's 2022 election renewed debate over the state's automatic voter registration system, with critics arguing that automatic registration at the MVC creates risks of placing noncitizens on voter rolls.

NJ.title: French Citizen Pleads Guilty to Voting in U.S. Election After New Jersey Auto-Registered Him, Lawyer Says
NJ.summary: Eliezer Kadoch, a French citizen from Toms River, admitted to illegally casting a ballot in New Jersey's 2022 federal midterm election, with his attorney claiming he mistakenly believed he was permitted to vote after being automatically registered when he obtained a New Jersey driver's license.

NM.title: Forward Party candidates file for New Mexico general election; ballot spots uncertain
NM.summary: A slate of five Forward Party candidates, including former Democratic state legislator Bob Perls running for U.S. Senate, filed to run in the November general election on the independent/minor party filing deadline, though their ballot access is pending certification by the Secretary of State by June 30.

NM.title: No Independents' Day: Political outsiders take a beating
NM.summary: Independent gubernatorial candidate Ken Miyagishima and other political outsiders faced steep ballot access hurdles in New Mexico, as a state court denied his petition to lower the 14,200-signature requirement for independent statewide candidates — far more than the roughly 2,500 signatures required for major-party candidates.

NV.title: Nevada will have its fewest ballot measures since 2012 after citizen initiatives fail to qualify
NV.summary: No citizen initiatives qualified for Nevada's November 2026 general election ballot after the June 24 signature deadline passed without any petitions submitted, leaving just two constitutional amendments that voters must ratify a second time after approving them in 2024.

RI.title: RI GOP endorses Aaron Guckian for governor
RI.summary: Rhode Island Republicans voted at the state party convention to endorse Aaron Guckian for governor, with Guckian defeating rival Tom Pelino 72-44 in the delegate vote, setting up the Republican primary field ahead of the 2026 governor's race.

RI.title: Nesi's Notes: June 27
RI.summary: WPRI's weekly political roundup covers Rhode Island's election landscape after the candidate filing deadline, including the governor's race field and post-GOP convention dynamics heading into the September primary.

TN.title: Stockard on the Stump: Senators say no state House, Senate redistricting on their radar
TN.summary: Two key Tennessee Republican senators told the Tennessee Lookout there is no interest in redrawing state House and Senate districts, in the aftermath of the contentious mid-decade congressional redistricting that split Memphis's majority-Black district ahead of the August 6 primary.

TX.title: Dolores Huerta makes surprise show at Texas Democratic Convention
TX.summary: Civil rights icon Dolores Huerta addressed Texas Democrats at the state party convention in Corpus Christi, urging activists to maximize voter turnout among Latino voters and labor communities ahead of November's elections.

TX.title: Talarico looks for momentum with Black voters at Dem convention
TX.summary: Democratic U.S. Senate nominee James Talarico worked to build support among Black voters at the Texas Democratic Convention, with Black elected officials saying the candidate has more engagement work to do before November's race against Republican Ken Paxton.

TX.title: Texas Democrats rally supporters at Corpus Christi convention
TX.summary: The Texas Democratic Convention closed in Corpus Christi with a rally featuring Sen. Bernie Sanders as keynote speaker, sending thousands of delegates home with instructions to register voters and canvass ahead of the November midterms.

TX.title: Texas Democrats leave convention united in effort to end GOP's 30-year hold on Texas
TX.summary: Following the three-day Texas Democratic Convention, party members departed Corpus Christi committed to voter registration and turnout ahead of November elections, where polls show a competitive U.S. Senate race between Republican Ken Paxton and Democrat James Talarico.

VT.title: What to know about early voting
VT.summary: Vermont Public's daily news podcast explains what voters need to know about early voting and absentee ballots for Vermont's August 11 primary election, including the in-person early voter registration period that opened June 27 at local town clerk offices.

WA.title: 'Stop the Income Tax' Initiative Clears Signature Threshold
WA.summary: Let's Go Washington announced it had collected more than enough signatures to qualify its initiative to repeal Washington's new 9.9% tax on incomes above $1 million for the November 2026 ballot, with the signature sheet submission deadline falling on June 28 before the July 2 official filing deadline with the Secretary of State.

WI.title: Wisconsin officials, voting rights advocates address fears about election security
WI.summary: Wisconsin election officials and voting rights advocates addressed voter fears about election security ahead of the 2026 fall elections, with Law Forward staff counsel explaining their focus areas including threats of federal ballot seizures and preventing Trump executive orders from affecting Wisconsin's election processes.

AL.title: Judge Has Not Dismissed Tuberville Residency Challenge as Case Moves Toward Key Hearing
AL.summary: A Montgomery County judge declined to dismiss a lawsuit challenging Tommy Tuberville’s Alabama residency and his eligibility to run for governor, scheduling a key hearing for June 29 to consider motions to dismiss from Tuberville’s attorneys.

AL.title: Status hearing on Tuberville residency lawsuit canceled, motion to dismiss expected
AL.summary: A scheduled status hearing in the Tuberville gubernatorial eligibility lawsuit was canceled, with the court instead expecting Tuberville and Secretary of State Wes Allen to file motions to dismiss questioning whether courts have jurisdiction over the residency challenge.

AL.title: Tuberville residency fight heads to court
AL.summary: A legal challenge to Republican gubernatorial nominee Tommy Tuberville’s eligibility advanced to court, with plaintiffs arguing he does not meet Alabama’s constitutional requirement of seven consecutive years of state residency prior to the general election.

AL.title: Republican ballot numbers drop, Democrat ballot numbers increase as voter turnout declines
AL.summary: Post-runoff analysis shows overall turnout fell in Alabama’s June 16 primary runoff, with Republican ballots dropping from 425,779 in the 2022 midterm runoff to 310,000 while Democratic ballot numbers rose.

AL.title: Judge hears arguments challenging Alabama residency of GOP gubernatorial nominee Tommy Tuberville
AL.summary: A Montgomery County Circuit Court judge heard oral arguments on June 29 on motions to dismiss the Tuberville residency lawsuit; the judge did not rule immediately and said she hopes to issue a decision within the next few days.

AK.title: Alaska Supreme Court orders a spot on the ballot for 2nd Dan Sullivan
AK.summary: The Alaska Supreme Court ordered that Dan J. Sullivan, a retired teacher who shares a name and party with incumbent Sen. Dan Sullivan, must appear on the August 18 primary ballot, ruling the Division of Elections acted unconstitutionally by removing him for failing to file in good faith.

AZ.title: U.S. Supreme Court will take up 2 Trump-backed Arizona election laws
AZ.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court agreed on June 29 to hear appeals involving two Arizona election laws — one requiring documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote on a state form, and another on procedures for election officials to review voter rolls — with arguments expected in the fall term.

AR.title: Love vows order halting school vouchers if elected Arkansas governor
AR.summary: Democratic gubernatorial nominee Fred Love said at an Arkansas Press Association convention debate that he would issue an executive order blocking the state’s school voucher program if elected, as the November contest between Love, incumbent Sanders, and Libertarian Colt Shelby takes shape.

AR.title: Gubernatorial challengers talk ideas as Sanders skips debate
AR.summary: Democratic and Libertarian nominees for Arkansas governor debated education, prisons, and data centers at the Arkansas Press Association annual convention while incumbent Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders declined to attend, citing a scheduled TV debate.

CO.title: Democratic ballot returns driving strong Colorado primary turnout, early data shows
CO.summary: More than 639,000 total ballots had been returned ahead of Colorado’s June 30 primary, with Democratic returns outpacing Republicans by the widest margin since 2020 and Democrats on track for their highest June primary turnout in years.

CO.title: What happens on June 30 when the primary race polls close?
CO.summary: CPR News answered key questions for Colorado voters about the June 30 primary, including how same-day registration works, when results will be released, and what competitive races for governor and Congress are being decided.

CT.title: New CT laws taking effect July 1: Absentee ballots, zoning, AI
CT.summary: Connecticut’s no-excuse absentee voting law takes effect July 1, 2026, making Connecticut the 29th state to allow all voters to request an absentee ballot without providing a reason. The law also keeps voters on an automatic absentee registry for all future elections and restricts mask-wearing within 250 feet of polling places.

ID.title: Idaho PACs spent more than .2M on primary races
ID.summary: Idaho political action committees spent over .2 million on the May 19 primary races, led by “Defend and Protect Idaho” which spent 52,800 supporting or opposing 37 Republican primary candidates. PAC contributions in Idaho face no legal caps unlike direct candidate contributions, highlighting outside money’s significant role in state elections.

MD.title: Maryland primary election live returns
MD.summary: The Baltimore Sun compiled partial and unofficial vote counts from Maryland’s June 23 primary election, showing results across statewide offices, all eight congressional districts, and county-level races. Final results including additional mail-in canvasses and provisional ballots are expected by July 6, 2026.

MA.title: As Mass. ballot initiatives multiply, critics want to limit them
MA.summary: Eight initiative petitions are headed to Massachusetts voters on the November 2026 ballot, including proposals on all-party primaries and Election Day voter registration. State legislative leaders have grown frustrated with the ballot initiative process and are calling for systemic reforms.

MA.title: Bernie Sanders backs Markey in Mass. Senate race
MA.summary: Vermont Sen. Bernie Sanders endorsed Sen. Ed Markey for reelection in Massachusetts, boosting Markey ahead of the September 1 Democratic primary against Rep. Seth Moulton. The primary winner will face Republican John Deaton in the November general election.

MI.title: Voting in the primary? Here’s a guide to your ballot.
MI.summary: Michigan Public published a voter guide for the August 4 primary covering absentee ballot deadlines, candidate information for governor and U.S. Senate races, and how to find voting locations. Absentee ballots began distribution on June 25 and must be received by 8 p.m. on Election Day to count.

MO.title: VOTER GUIDE: August 4 primary election in Missouri
MO.summary: Missouri voters head to the polls August 4 for the primary election, with absentee voting already underway and a July 8 voter registration deadline. The ballot includes over 1,136 positions and multiple constitutional amendments including Amendment 4 on initiative petition approval rules and Amendment 5 on phasing out state income tax.

MO.title: Heartland Votes: Missouri’s August Primary Election Guide
MO.summary: KFVS12 published a comprehensive voter guide to Missouri’s August 4 primary covering key races for U.S. House, State Auditor, and local offices, along with information on how to vote and the absentee ballot process.

MT.title: Bodnar’s big gamble: Why the independent is pushing for Montana’s nonpartisan era
MT.summary: Seth Bodnar, the independent U.S. Senate candidate and former University of Montana president, is raising over .1 million and building a broad coalition he calls the “sensible majority” to challenge both major parties in Montana’s November Senate race.

NV.title: RNC sues Nevada, amping up nationwide campaign against overseas voters
NV.summary: The Republican National Committee filed a lawsuit against Nevada’s Secretary of State challenging a state law that allows certain U.S. citizens born abroad who have never lived in Nevada to vote through a parent’s state registration.

NH.title: Weeks before election, State of NH appeals ruling striking down proof-of-citizenship voting law.
NH.summary: New Hampshire’s Attorney General’s Office asked a federal court to stay the May ruling striking down the state’s proof-of-citizenship voter registration law, seeking to keep the requirement in effect during the appeals process ahead of the September 8 primary.

NM.title: Deb Haaland endorses Stephanie Garcia Richard as her running mate
NM.summary: Democratic gubernatorial nominee Deb Haaland endorsed New Mexico State Land Commissioner Stephanie Garcia Richard as her preferred running mate for lieutenant governor after the prior nominee Maggie Toulouse Oliver withdrew for health reasons; the state Democratic Party will officially select the replacement at its July 25 central committee meeting.

NY.title: Democratic rift over the party’s future widens amid the left’s New York victories
NY.summary: Following the June 23 New York primary in which Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s endorsed democratic socialist candidates defeated two Democratic incumbents, a deepening intraparty schism emerged over the direction of the Democratic Party and the role of progressive versus establishment factions heading into the November midterms.

ND.title: State canvassing board certifies election results
ND.summary: North Dakota’s State Canvassing Board officially certified the 2026 primary election results after receiving submissions from all 53 county canvassing boards, with 125,225 voters participating and a 20.86% statewide turnout in the June 9 primary.

OH.title: Will Ohio Republicans override Gov. DeWine’s absentee ballot voter photo ID veto?
OH.summary: Ohio Republicans are evaluating whether to override Governor DeWine’s June 25 veto of House Bill 472, which would have required absentee mail-in voters to submit a photo ID copy; with 65 House Republicans holding the 60 votes needed to override, party leaders are weighing next steps.

OK.title: Sam Wargin Grimaldo Sworn Into Office
OK.summary: Sam Wargin Grimaldo, a Democrat, was sworn into the Oklahoma House of Representatives on June 26 to represent House District 92 in Oklahoma City, after winning both the special election and the regular Democratic primary on June 16 to succeed Rep. Forrest Bennett who resigned to lead the Oklahoma AFL-CIO.

OR.title: Nearly every proposed Oregon initiative won’t make it onto the November ballot
OR.summary: With a July 2 signature deadline looming, nearly all of the roughly 90 proposed citizen initiatives for November 2026 will fail to qualify for the ballot. Only one initiative — a vegan animal-rights measure — has collected sufficient signatures, a stark contrast to recent election cycles.

PA.title: Judge dismisses Department of Justice lawsuit seeking Pennsylvania voters’ private information
PA.summary: A federal district judge dismissed the DOJ’s case seeking Pennsylvania’s unredacted voter roll — including driver’s license numbers and partial Social Security numbers — ruling the request was a “fishing expedition” aimed at creating an unlawful national voter database. The DOJ has sued 30 states and may appeal.

PA.title: Signals Point to US Supreme Court Taking On Pennsylvania Mail Ballot Date Dispute
PA.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court invited the Solicitor General to weigh in on the Pennsylvania mail ballot envelope dating requirement case — a strong signal the court will hear the dispute in its next term. The case centers on whether Pennsylvania may discard thousands of mail ballots lacking a handwritten date on the outer envelope.

TX.title: Ruling that blocks Trump use of system to hunt noncitizen voters won’t stop ongoing investigations
TX.summary: A federal judge blocked the Trump administration from using the SAVE database to flag noncitizens on voter rolls nationwide, but the ruling does not halt existing Texas investigations already underway. Texas had flagged approximately 2,700 of its 19 million registered voters, and election officials note consistent evidence of ineligible voters impacting elections has not been found.

UT.title: One of Utah’s hottest Democratic races shows how far left voters are willing to go
UT.summary: Analysis of the June 23 Democratic primary results in Utah’s court-ordered new 1st Congressional District examines where Democratic primary voters stand ideologically. Former Rep. Ben McAdams won the primary over Bernie Sanders-endorsed state Sen. Nate Blouin, setting up a competitive fall race in a district created by redistricting.

WI.title: Green Bay says it may have issued duplicate ballots in a second election this year
WI.summary: Green Bay officials discovered some voters in eight wards may have received two absentee ballots for the August primary — the second such error this year after a duplicate-ballot incident ahead of the April Supreme Court election. City Clerk Celestine Jeffreys assured voters only one ballot per eligible voter will be tabulated, and the Wisconsin Elections Commission will address the April complaint at its July 9 meeting.

DC.title: The Supreme Court upholds grace periods for mail-in ballots, siding against the GOP
DC.summary: The Supreme Court ruled 5-4 in Watson v. Republican National Committee that states may count mail ballots postmarked by Election Day even if they arrive afterward, upholding Mississippi’s grace-period law and rejecting a GOP challenge. Justice Amy Coney Barrett wrote the majority opinion joined by Chief Justice Roberts and the three liberal justices, with broad implications for election administration nationwide.

AL.title: Republican ballot numbers drop, Democratic ballot numbers increase as voter turnout declines
AL.summary: Analysis of June 16 primary runoff turnout data shows statewide turnout fell to 10.72%, with Republican ballots declining from 88% to 77% of total cast compared to the 2022 runoff, while Democratic ballots rose — continuing a trend from the May 19 primary where Democratic participation surged.

AK.title: Alaska Supreme Court orders a spot on the ballot for 2nd Dan Sullivan
AK.summary: The Alaska Supreme Court upheld a lower court ruling allowing Dan J. Sullivan of Petersburg — a retired teacher sharing the incumbent senator's name — to appear on the August 18 nonpartisan primary ballot, just hours before a ballot-printing deadline; the court sent the case back to determine how the two candidates' names will be listed.

AK.title: Alaska Supreme Court allows namesake challenger to U.S. Sen. Dan Sullivan to appear on the ballot
AK.summary: In a ruling issued three hours after oral arguments, the Alaska Supreme Court preserved Dan J. Sullivan's place on the U.S. Senate primary ballot; the Division of Elections announced the challenger will appear as 'Sullivan, Daniel J. Jr.' with no party affiliation, while the incumbent appears as 'Sullivan, Dan S.' with party and incumbent notation.

AK.title: Man with same name as Alaska Sen. Dan Sullivan can appear on primary ballot, state's Supreme Court rules
AK.summary: The Alaska Supreme Court upheld a Superior Court ruling allowing a same-named challenger to share the August 18 Senate primary ballot with incumbent Sen. Dan Sullivan, rejecting the Division of Elections' finding of bad faith; the case drew briefs from 14 states and raises questions about Alaska's nonpartisan ranked-choice primary system.

AZ.title: Supreme Court takes up dispute over Arizona voting restrictions
AZ.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court agreed to hear Mi Familia Vota v. Fontes, a challenge to two Arizona election laws — a documentary proof-of-citizenship requirement for voter registration and a provision allowing pre-election purges of noncitizen registrations — that lower courts found violated the National Voter Registration Act; oral arguments expected in fall 2026.

AZ.title: Supreme Court will hear Arizona case that could badly weaken key federal law protecting voter registration
AZ.summary: The Supreme Court granted certiorari in Mi Familia Vota v. Fontes to consider whether Arizona's proof-of-citizenship voter registration requirement and pre-election voter roll purge mechanism are preempted by the NVRA; a ruling is expected in spring 2027 and could significantly affect voter registration nationwide.

AZ.title: AZ Supreme Court upholds voter-approved dark money law — but it wasn't a total win for supporters
AZ.summary: The Arizona Supreme Court issued a 4-3 ruling upholding Proposition 211, the Voters' Right to Know Act approved by 72% of voters in 2022, which requires disclosure of donors giving ,000+ to groups spending over 0,000 on campaigns; the court remanded a narrower free-speech challenge to lower courts.

AR.title: Last call for citizen-led petition signatures!
AR.summary: With the July 3, 2026 petition deadline one week away, Arkansas ballot initiative groups held final signature-collection events to qualify two proposed constitutional amendments for the November ballot: the Arkansas Ballot Measure Rights Amendment and the Arkansas Education Rights Amendment, each requiring over 90,700 valid signatures from at least 15 counties.

CA.title: Voting Rights Groups Applaud Ruling Declaring 2026 Executive Order Interference with Voter Rolls and Mail-In Ballots Unconstitutional and Unlawful
CA.summary: A federal district court declared key sections of President Trump's March 2026 executive order unconstitutional in a case led by California and 22 other states, barring federal agencies from interfering with how plaintiff states maintain voter rolls or conduct mail voting and blocking the U.S. Postal Service from withholding mail ballots.

CO.title: It's primary Election Day in Colorado. Here's what you need to know to vote and find results.
CO.summary: Colorado held its June 30 primary covering governor, U.S. Senate, eight House seats, and state legislative races. The article details voting rules: same-day registration is available, ballots must be returned to drop boxes or voting centers rather than mailed, and ID is required for first-time and in-person voters. Unaffiliated voters may receive both party ballots but submit only one.

CO.title: Democratic ballot returns driving strong Colorado primary turnout, early data shows
CO.summary: More than 327,000 Democratic primary ballots were processed by the eve of the June 30 primary — the highest Democratic primary turnout in years — with unaffiliated voters comprising nearly 40% of all ballots cast, driven by competitive races for governor (Bennet vs. Weiser) and U.S. Senate (Hickenlooper vs. Gonzales).

CO.title: Colorado Votes 2026: Full primary election results
CO.summary: Rocky Mountain PBS provided comprehensive results coverage for Colorado's June 30 primary, including the Democratic governor race between Sen. Michael Bennet and AG Phil Weiser, the Senate primary between incumbent John Hickenlooper and challenger Julie Gonzales, and attorney general, secretary of state, and congressional primaries.

CT.title: New CT laws taking effect July 1: Absentee ballots, zoning, AI
CT.summary: Connecticut's no-excuse absentee voting law takes effect July 1, 2026, enabling all eligible voters to request mail ballots for any election without providing a reason; voters may also enroll for automatic future ballot applications. The law additionally restricts masks within 250 feet of a polling place unless for weather or medical reasons.

DE.title: Delaware legislators look to pass several bills on final day of legislative session
DE.summary: On Delaware's final legislative day, three major election bills were considered: HB 444 (the John Lewis Voting Rights Act) to bar voter suppression and vote dilution; HB 180 to restore voting rights to people who have completed felony sentences; and HB 430 to ban corporations from casting ballots in municipal elections.

FL.title: LWV Palm Beach County launches nonpartisan 'Every Vote Counts!' campaign ahead '26 Elections
FL.summary: The League of Women Voters of Palm Beach County launched a nonpartisan voter registration and education drive ahead of Florida's August 18 primary and November 3 general election, including community outreach at schools and churches, printed and online VOTE411 guides launching July 10, and a public Election Expo scheduled for September 28.

HI.title: Incumbent Faces Councilman In Race For State's Biggest House District
HI.summary: State Rep. Jeanne Kapela faces Hawaii County Council member Matt Kaneali'i-Kleinfelder in the August 8 Democratic primary for House District 5, the state's largest by area. Mail-in primary ballots are set to arrive July 21, making this one of the first contested legislative primaries heading into the November general election.

ID.title: In rural Idaho, medical marijuana ballot initiative hits setback after signatures turned in late
ID.summary: An Idaho judge ruled that signatures delivered to Minidoka County after the 5 p.m. May 1 statutory deadline cannot be counted, potentially preventing the medical marijuana initiative from qualifying for the November 2026 ballot. The ruling came as county clerks were completing the June 30 deadline to certify signature totals for both the marijuana and reproductive freedom ballot initiatives.

ID.title: These new laws are set to go into effect in Idaho on July 1
ID.summary: Senate Bill 1322, taking effect July 1, requires voters using a signed affidavit as voter ID to provide their date of birth or Idaho driver's license number before receiving a ballot, tightening Idaho's voter identification requirements at the polls. A second election-related law (SB 1356) changes Ada County Highway District commissioner elections from district-based to countywide elections starting in 2027.

IL.title: Linda Holmes, a 20-year Illinois Senate Democrat, will step down from ballot
IL.summary: Illinois Senate Assistant Majority Leader Linda Holmes filed paperwork to remove her name from the November 2026 ballot after 20 years in the 42nd District, citing her multiple sclerosis diagnosis. Her departure triggers a party-selection process in which Democratic county chairs — Kane County holding 41% of the vote — will choose her replacement for the general election ballot.

IA.title: These new laws are taking effect in Iowa July 1
IA.summary: Three voting-related laws take effect in Iowa on July 1: HF 2501 eliminates the option for a registered voter to attest to another voter's identity when ID is unavailable; SF 2218 requires all new voter registrants to swear citizenship under penalty of perjury; and HF 2694 requires legislative approval for any future changes to election laws even between legislative sessions.

KS.title: U.S. Sen. Roger Marshall of Kansas promises to refuse Trump administration appointment
KS.summary: Kansas Sen. Roger Marshall appeared on NBC's Meet the Press pledging to remain on the November ballot and decline any Trump administration appointment, responding to a 2025 Kansas law that would allow Republicans to fill a Senate vacancy without an election for two years. His statement directly addressed Democratic Senate candidate Adam Hamilton's criticism that Kansas GOP leaders were plotting to circumvent the August primary.

KS.title: Kansas U.S. Senate candidate Erik Murray wants 'solutions not chaos' on healthcare and the economy
KS.summary: Profile of Erik Murray, one of 11 Democratic candidates competing in the August 4 primary for Kansas's U.S. Senate seat, discussing his priorities including healthcare, education, and economic opportunity as the primary field races to challenge Republican incumbent Roger Marshall.

KY.title: Trump DOJ suffers first appeals court loss — after nine lower court failures — in floundering voter roll crusade
KY.summary: The Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals ruled against the Trump DOJ's attempt to obtain unredacted voter registration data from Michigan, marking the first appellate defeat after nine district court losses. The ruling is binding on the pending DOJ lawsuit against Kentucky Secretary of State Michael Adams (also in the Sixth Circuit), making dismissal of the Kentucky case nearly certain.

MA.title: As Mass. ballot initiatives multiply, critics want to limit them
MA.summary: Eight initiative petitions are headed to the Massachusetts November 2026 ballot after the Legislature declined to approve any of them; lawmakers and critics are debating whether to reform or restrict the ballot initiative process, including proposals to ban per-signature payments to signature gatherers.

MA.title: Bernie Sanders backs Markey in Mass. Senate race
MA.summary: Vermont Sen. Bernie Sanders endorsed incumbent Ed Markey for reelection in the Massachusetts Democratic Senate primary, adding to a string of progressive endorsements as Markey faces Rep. Seth Moulton ahead of the September 1 primary; three debates are scheduled before the vote.

MD.title: Jawando wins Democratic primary for Montgomery Co. executive after Friedson concedes race
MD.summary: Will Jawando won the Democratic primary for Montgomery County Executive after rival Andrew Friedson conceded following the completion of mail-in ballot canvassing. Jawando, who won with roughly 40% of the vote to Friedson's 34%, will face Republican Esther Wells in the November general election.

MD.title: Maryland primary election live returns
MD.summary: Continuously updated compilation of unofficial Maryland primary election vote counts as the state's mail-in ballot canvassing continued into late June. Non-provisional ballots cast in-person are complete; final results including provisional ballots are expected July 6, covering statewide, congressional, General Assembly, and local races from the June 23 primary.

ME.title: New Maine U.S. Senate poll: A tight race with challenges for Collins, Platner
ME.summary: A New York Times/Portland Press Herald/Siena poll of 608 likely Maine voters shows Democrat Graham Platner leading Republican incumbent Susan Collins 49% to 47%, within the margin of error. The poll reveals that independent voters — nearly a third of Maine's electorate — favor Platner by 8 points, with both candidates facing distinct challenges heading into November.

ME.title: Graham Platner and Susan Collins are neck and neck, Times/Press Herald/Siena poll shows
ME.summary: Coverage of the Times/Press Herald/Siena poll showing the Maine U.S. Senate race is effectively tied at 49%-47%. The article details the challenges each candidate faces: Platner struggles with character questions and college-degree gaps, while Collins risks losing voters who see her as too aligned with Trump.

MI.title: Voting in the primary? Here's a guide to your ballot.
MI.summary: Michigan Public released a comprehensive guide to voting in the August 4, 2026 primary, detailing absentee ballot distribution (started June 25), Democratic and Republican candidate lineups for governor and U.S. Senate, and crossover voting rules that could invalidate ballots if a voter switches parties.

MI.title: Voter guide 2026: How to vote in Michigan's Primary election
MI.summary: BridgeDetroit published a nonpartisan voter guide for Detroit-area residents covering registration deadlines, absentee and early voting options, drop box locations, and photo ID requirements for Michigan's August 4, 2026 primary election.

MN.title: MN Sec. of State says Supreme Court ruling on mail-in ballots won't affect Minnesota elections
MN.summary: Minnesota Secretary of State Steve Simon clarified that the Supreme Court's ruling in Watson v. RNC (upholding states' ability to count postmark-valid mail ballots after Election Day) does not affect Minnesota, because Minnesota already requires mail ballots to arrive by Election Day with no grace period — meaning no change in Minnesota election procedures.

MO.title: VOTER GUIDE: August 4 primary election in Missouri
MO.summary: KMOV published a comprehensive voter guide for Missouri's August 4 primary covering four constitutional amendments on the statewide ballot, voter registration deadline of July 8, absentee voting procedures, poll hours, and key congressional and county races.

MO.title: Heartland Votes: Missouri's August Primary Election Guide
MO.summary: KFVS12 published a southeast Missouri-focused voter guide for the August 4 primary detailing four constitutional amendments, voter registration and absentee voting deadlines, U.S. House District 8 candidates, and county-level races with links to sample ballots by county.

MS.title: U.S. Supreme Court upholds Mississippi mail-in ballot law
MS.summary: MPB reported on the Supreme Court's 5-4 decision upholding Mississippi's mail-in ballot grace period law, which allows ballots postmarked by Election Day to be counted up to five days afterward. Governor Tate Reeves and Attorney General Lynn Fitch stated they intend to change state law anyway to require ballots to arrive by 5 p.m. on Election Day.

NC.title: NC HB 958 (Election Law Changes) passes House 66-47
NC.summary: The North Carolina House passed House Bill 958 on a 66-47 vote, sending the 37-page elections omnibus bill to the Senate. The legislation includes new powers for State Auditor Dave Boliek to conduct county-level election audits, photo ID requirements for overseas and military absentee voters, a ban on 'never-resident' citizens voting in state elections, a statewide ranked-choice voting ban, and expanded ballot challenge rights.

NE.title: National 'Working Families Party' considering legal action against Nebraska 'Working People Party' organizers
NE.summary: A newly formed Nebraska Working People Party filed for ballot access, needing roughly 6,726 signatures by July 15 to place candidates on the November 2026 general election ballot. Nebraska Democrats allege it is a partisan spoiler effort, while the national Working Families Party is considering legal action against the organizers over name and brand confusion.

NH.title: Weeks before election, State of NH appeals ruling striking down proof-of-citizenship voting law
NH.summary: New Hampshire's Attorney General filed a motion seeking a stay of the federal court ruling that struck down the state's documentary proof-of-citizenship voter registration requirement, while simultaneously appealing to the 1st Circuit Court of Appeals; the outcome will determine voter registration rules for the September 8 primary and November general election.

NM.title: Deb Haaland endorses Stephanie Garcia Richard as her running mate
NM.summary: Democratic gubernatorial nominee Deb Haaland endorsed state Land Commissioner Stephanie Garcia Richard as her preferred lieutenant governor running mate, after the previous nominee Maggie Toulouse Oliver withdrew for health reasons. The formal selection requires a vote by the state Democratic Party Central Committee on July 25.

NM.title: NM Sen. Pope staying in Dem lieutenant governor race even after losing Haaland endorsement
NM.summary: State Sen. Harold James Pope Jr. announced he would remain in the race for the Democratic lieutenant governor nomination despite gubernatorial nominee Deb Haaland endorsing a different candidate, keeping the July 25 state Central Committee vote competitive and highlighting the unusual process of replacing a primary winner mid-cycle.

OH.title: Will Ohio Republicans override Gov. DeWine’s voter photo ID veto?
OH.summary: Following Governor DeWine's June 25 veto of House Bill 472, which would have required absentee voters to submit photo ID copies starting in 2027, Ohio Republican legislators assessed a potential veto override. At least four Republicans who supported the original bill said they would not back an override, making the required 60-vote threshold uncertain; the legislature is not scheduled to reconvene until after November.

OK.title: Sam Wargin Grimaldo Sworn Into Office
OK.summary: Democrat Sam Wargin Grimaldo was officially sworn in to represent Oklahoma House District 92 in south Oklahoma City on June 26, following his election in the June 16 primary. He fills the seat vacated by Rep. Forrest Bennett, who resigned to lead the Oklahoma AFL-CIO, bringing new Latino representation to the Oklahoma House.

OR.title: Nearly every proposed Oregon initiative won't make it onto the November ballot
OR.summary: Of roughly 90 proposed ballot initiatives for Oregon's November 2026 election, only one citizen petition is on track ahead of the July 2 signature-submission deadline. Organizers of most initiatives cited insufficient time, volunteers, and funding to gather the required tens of thousands of verified voter signatures.

PA.title: Judge dismisses Department of Justice lawsuit seeking Pennsylvania voters’ private information
PA.summary: A federal district judge in Pittsburgh dismissed the DOJ's lawsuit demanding Pennsylvania's unredacted voter registration database, ruling the government intended to build a 'nationwide voter-database' amounting to potential weaponization of voter data. Federal courts have now ruled against the DOJ in nine states on voter roll data requests; Gov. Shapiro praised the decision.

RI.title: The man who wasn't there gets attacked anyway at Grow Smart gubernatorial forum
RI.summary: Governor McKee skipped a Grow Smart Rhode Island gubernatorial forum at the annual Power of Place summit at RISD, citing a scheduling conflict. Opponents Helena Foulkes, Republican Aaron Guckian, and Independent Ken Block all attended and criticized McKee's absence and record during the event.

RI.title: McKee cuts into Foulkes' lead, but remains far behind in UNH poll
RI.summary: A new University of New Hampshire poll of likely Democratic primary voters shows Helena Foulkes leading at 42% vs. incumbent Gov. McKee at 22%, with 31% undecided. McKee has recovered from an April low of 11% but 77% of all Rhode Islanders still disapprove of his job performance ahead of the September 9 primary.

SC.title: Inside Alan Wilson's historic GOP primary victory over Pamela Evette
SC.summary: A detailed examination of how Attorney General Alan Wilson won the June 23 Republican governor runoff by 37+ percentage points over Lt. Gov. Pamela Evette, overcoming her initial primary lead and Trump's early endorsement, setting up a November general election matchup with Democratic nominee Jermaine Johnson.

SD.title: State's top election official loses nomination to challenger who supports hand-counting
SD.summary: At the South Dakota Republican Convention in Rapid City, incumbent Secretary of State Monae Johnson was defeated by Heather Baxter, who received 59% of delegate support and has campaigned on hand-counting paper ballots rather than using electronic tabulation machines, marking a significant shift in the state GOP's approach to election administration.

SD.title: New candidates announced as South Dakota's Republican Convention closes out
SD.summary: South Dakota's GOP convention concluded with delegates selecting nominees for six constitutional offices via a proportional voting process, including Secretary of State, Attorney General, Treasurer, Auditor, and commissioners. The gubernatorial nomination will be settled in the July 28 runoff between incumbent Larry Rhoden and businessman Toby Doeden.

SD.title: Results and process from 2026 GOP Convention in Rapid City
SD.summary: SDPB provided detailed vote tallies and explained the weighted delegate process used at South Dakota's Republican state convention. The competitive Secretary of State race — pitting hand-counting advocate Heather Baxter against incumbent Monae Johnson — was the central election-integrity flashpoint at the gathering.

TN.title: Tennessee Voter Registration Deadline Approaching for August Primary Election
TN.summary: Secretary of State Tre Hargett reminded eligible Tennesseans that the voter registration deadline for the August 6 primary is July 7, 2026. Tennessee does not allow same-day voter registration; early voting runs July 17–August 1 and registration is available through GoVoteTN.gov.

TN.title: Inside the race for Tennessee's 1st Congressional District
TN.summary: Three Democratic candidates — Kristi Burke, Herman Garcia, and David Kerr — are competing in the August 6 primary for the right to challenge two-term Republican incumbent Diana Harshbarger in Tennessee's deeply red 1st Congressional District. Harshbarger previously won with nearly 80% of the vote and significantly outpaces challengers in fundraising.

TX.title: Supreme Court won't hear challenge to Texas anti-voting law in loss for voters with disabilities
TX.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court declined to review a challenge to a Texas SB1 provision prohibiting voters from receiving paid assistance in filling out or submitting ballots, brought by voting group LUPE under Section 208 of the Voting Rights Act. The denial is a loss for Texas voters with disabilities who rely on compensated helpers to cast their ballots.

UT.title: One of Utah's hottest Democratic races shows how far left voters are willing to go
UT.summary: Post-primary analysis of the Utah 1st Congressional District Democratic primary, made possible by court-ordered redistricting that created a new Democratic-leaning seat in Salt Lake County. The race drew national attention as a progressive-versus-moderate contest, reflecting the shifting political dynamics created by Utah's redistricting saga.

WI.title: Green Bay sends duplicate absentee ballots to some voters for second time this year
WI.summary: Green Bay discovered a printing error sent duplicate absentee ballots to voters in eight wards ahead of the August primary — the second such incident in 2026. City Clerk Celestine Jeffreys said only one ballot per voter will be counted, and Republicans called for a state elections commission investigation.

WY.title: Trump keeps sabotaging legislation over a voting bill. Here's what's in it
WY.summary: Explains the SAVE America Act's five main components — documentary proof of citizenship to vote, photo ID for mail and in-person voting, DHS voter roll access, and penalties for noncompliant officials — and how Trump threatened to block unrelated legislation until Congress passes it.

DC.title: Supreme Court allows states to accept mail ballots after Election Day, rejecting Republican challenge to voting access
DC.summary: In Watson v. Republican National Committee, the Supreme Court ruled 5-4 that states may count mail-in ballots postmarked by Election Day even if received days later, upholding state grace-period laws. Justice Barrett joined Chief Justice Roberts and the three liberal justices; the ruling protects mail-ballot grace periods in 14 states plus DC ahead of the 2026 midterms.

DC.title: These House Republicans voted to block NDAA rule over SAVE America Act
DC.summary: Fourteen House Republicans joined Democrats in a 198-224 vote to kill a procedural rule pairing the SAVE America Act — which would require documentary proof of citizenship to register and vote federally — with the must-pass defense authorization bill, collapsing Speaker Johnson's strategy to advance the election-law overhaul.

AR.title: Bill Teeter to win Special Election Runoff for District 44 Arkansas House seat
AR.summary: Republican Bill Teeter won the June 30 special primary runoff for Arkansas House District 44, defeating Nikki Phillips 279-24 (roughly 92%), to hold the vacancy left by the March death of Rep. Stan Berry. Teeter will advance to an August 4 special general election and will run unopposed in November's general election.

CA.title: US Postal Service cannot carry out Trump order on mail ballot delivery, judge rules
CA.summary: A federal judge blocked the USPS from implementing a Trump executive order restricting mail ballot distribution nationwide, ruling it violated a prior settlement agreement. The ruling lands as California counties are in the final days of counting mail ballots from the June 2 primary, due to the Secretary of State by July 3; California also led a companion 23-state lawsuit against the same executive order.

CO.title: In Colorado primaries, a democratic socialist wins; Bennet's governor bid ends
CO.summary: Melat Kiros, a 29-year-old democratic socialist and political newcomer, defeated 29-year incumbent Rep. Diana DeGette in CO-1; Attorney General Phil Weiser won the Democratic gubernatorial primary over Sen. Michael Bennet.

CO.title: Colorado primary election results: Melat Kiros wins – key takeaways
CO.summary: Progressive and DSA-backed candidates swept several Colorado Democratic primaries, with Manny Rutinel also winning in the competitive CO-8 swing district, setting up a key November matchup against Republican incumbent Gabe Evans.

CO.title: Is the GOP race for Colorado governor heading into mandatory recount territory?
CO.summary: State Sen. Barb Kirkmeyer leads ministry leader Victor Marx by roughly 1,356 votes out of 466,000 cast in Colorado's Republican gubernatorial primary, with the margin potentially narrowing to the 0.5% mandatory recount threshold as ballot counting continues.

CT.title: New CT laws take effect July 1, including no-excuse absentee voting
CT.summary: Connecticut became the 29th state to allow no-excuse absentee voting as the law took effect July 1, enabling any eligible voter to request an absentee ballot without providing a reason, in time for the August primary election.

CT.title: New Connecticut laws take effect July 1. Here's what to know
CT.summary: Connecticut's no-excuse absentee voting law — the culmination of a 2024 constitutional amendment approved by voters — took effect July 1, along with new election-worker harassment protections and a task force to study voter participation.

DE.title: Delaware lawmakers pass flurry of bills in final session push
DE.summary: Delaware's General Assembly passed HB 430 (a constitutional amendment barring corporations and LLCs from voting) and HB 444 (the Delaware John Lewis Voting Rights Act), along with same-day voter registration (HB 88) failing to advance from the House.

DE.title: What Delaware lawmakers passed — and what failed — before the legislative session ended
DE.summary: A recap of Delaware's end-of-session legislative push shows HB 430 (banning artificial entities from voting, first leg of a constitutional amendment) and HB 444 (the Delaware John Lewis Voting Rights Act creating new voting protections) passed both chambers, while same-day voter registration failed.

GA.title: Georgia enacts legislation extending voting machine deadline, establishing automatic hand recounts
GA.summary: Governor Kemp signed SB 3EX, pushing the deadline for eliminating QR code ballot tabulation from July 1, 2026 to January 1, 2028, and establishing automatic hand recounts in statewide races with a margin under 0.5%, making Georgia the 29th state with automatic recount requirements.

HI.title: Vacancy Election Announced for Hawaii State Senate District 18
HI.summary: Following Senator Michelle Kidani's retirement effective June 30, Hawaii's Office of Elections proclaimed a vacancy election for Senate District 18 to be filled at the November 3, 2026 General Election, with political parties required to submit nominees by September 4.

IA.title: New Iowa laws go into effect July 1. Here's what you need to know
IA.summary: Among Iowa laws taking effect July 1: a new requirement that voters registering swear U.S. citizenship, and HF 2501 ending the option for another registered voter to attest to a voter's identity at the polls, tightening in-person voter verification.

IL.title: Supreme Court allows mail ballots to be counted after Election Day, based on postmark
IL.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled 5-4 in Bost v. Illinois State Board of Elections that states may count mail ballots arriving after Election Day if postmarked by Election Day, directly protecting Illinois's law allowing ballots received up to 14 days post-election to be counted.

IL.title: Supreme Court rejects GOP mail ballot challenge, but Illinois Dems warn voting rights 'still under attack'
IL.summary: Illinois Governor Pritzker and Senator Durbin praised the Supreme Court's ruling preserving Illinois's mail ballot counting window in Bost v. Illinois, while warning that ongoing Trump administration efforts and pending federal legislation continue to threaten voting access.

IN.title: More Republicans than Democrats file for school board races in central Indiana
IN.summary: Central Indiana school board candidates have filed under party labels for the first time under Indiana's new law (Senate Enrolled Act 287) making school board races partisan. Among early filers in the region, Republicans outnumber Democrats.

IN.title: Here's who's running for Hamilton County school boards — some chose a political party
IN.summary: WFYI reports on candidates filing for Hamilton County school board seats under Indiana's new partisan school board election law, detailing which candidates declared a party affiliation and which did not.

KS.title: Kansas U.S. Senate candidate Christy Davis
KS.summary: KCUR interviews Democratic Senate primary candidate Christy Davis, who is running in the crowded August 4 primary field and drawing on her USDA background to distinguish herself in a race aiming to end nearly a century of Republican control of Kansas's U.S. Senate seats.

KY.title: Jefferson County Clerk, state elections officials offer dueling takes on ballot errors
KY.summary: The Jefferson County Clerk is requesting a full audit of 600,000 voter address assignments after a precinct-assignment error prevented about 8 voters from casting ballots in the correct race in the Kentucky House District 44 primary, which was decided by just 5 votes. State election officials dispute the error's scope.

ME.title: The Supreme Court just flooded more money into Maine's Senate race
ME.summary: The Supreme Court's 6-3 ruling eliminating coordinated spending limits between political parties and candidates removes the cap on Maine Senate race coordination, immediately benefiting Republicans who already hold a 2-to-1 outside spending advantage over Democratic challenger Graham Platner in his race against incumbent Susan Collins.

MI.title: One of the country's largest grassroots networks is backing Abdul El-Sayed for US Senate
MI.summary: Indivisible, one of the largest national grassroots progressive networks, along with its Michigan affiliate Statewide Indivisible Michigan, endorsed Dr. Abdul El-Sayed in the competitive Democratic primary for Michigan's open U.S. Senate seat ahead of the August 4 primary.

MS.title: JULY 1: New Mississippi laws take effect today
MS.summary: Mississippi's SHIELD Act (SB 2588) took effect July 1, requiring local election officials to verify voter citizenship through the federal SAVE immigration database and mandating annual voter roll audits. A separate law (HB 859) also changed absentee ballot handling so completed ballots are fed directly into voting machines.

MS.title: New laws in Mississippi take effect on July 1. Here's a breakdown
MS.summary: Mississippi's SHIELD Act requires election officials to verify new voter registrants' citizenship through the federal SAVE database before confirming registration. Applicants who cannot be verified have 30 days to provide documentation such as a passport or birth certificate to their county circuit clerk.

MT.title: Montana GOP formalizes opposition to 'The Montana Plan'
MT.summary: The Montana Republican Party Executive Board passed a resolution opposing Initiative 194, a ballot measure that would prohibit corporations, nonprofits, and other entities from contributing to candidate campaigns and ballot measure elections in Montana.

NC.title: NC House passes election bill, but Senate path remains uncertain
NC.summary: The North Carolina House passed HB 958 on a 66-47 party-line vote, a sweeping election law overhaul that expands state oversight of county election boards, mandates federal database checks on all absentee and provisional ballots, bans ranked-choice voting, and converts senior State Board of Elections positions to at-will employment. Senate leaders have not committed to taking it up.

NC.title: 'Chasing ghosts': NC House approves elections bill expanding state oversight
NC.summary: Following the House's passage of HB 958, Democrats criticized the omnibus elections bill as addressing a nonexistent voter fraud problem, noting only 123 documented fraud cases in North Carolina since 1986. Key provisions give the state auditor power to select counties for post-election audits and require every absentee and provisional ballot to be cross-checked against federal databases.

NE.title: Party fever: Another political party is gathering signatures to get on Nebraska's ballot
NE.summary: Two new political groups — the America First Party and the Nebraska Working People Party — are racing to collect approximately 6,726 signatures each by a July 15 deadline to qualify as official parties on Nebraska's November 2026 ballot.

NH.title: Federal judge denies effort by Trump administration to get New Hampshire's detailed voter data
NH.summary: A federal judge rejected the Trump administration's attempt to obtain detailed voter registration data from New Hampshire, a state-specific ruling in the broader DOJ campaign to access state voter rolls.

NJ.title: NJ legislators approve bills on data centers, voting rights, and more
NJ.summary: New Jersey's legislature passed the John R. Lewis Voter Empowerment Act (S282/A1715), expanding voting access and rights protections for New Jersey residents.

NM.title: Lieutenant Governor showdown: Inside the process to fill the vacant Democratic candidacy
NM.summary: KUNM reports on the process by which New Mexico will fill the vacant Democratic lieutenant governor candidate slot on the ballot, raising questions about candidate selection and election administration procedures ahead of November.

NV.title: Nevada mail voting rules stand secure after Supreme Court rejects major Republican challenge
NV.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court declined to hear Watson v. RNC, leaving Nevada's mail ballot laws intact and rejecting a Republican challenge to the state's vote-by-mail rules.

NY.title: DiNapoli's first primary challenge put statewide public financing to the test
NY.summary: New York's public campaign finance matching funds program, administered by the state's Public Campaign Finance Board, faced its first major statewide test in the Democratic primary for state comptroller, revealing how the system performs at scale.

NY.title: NY Elections, Census, and Redistricting Update 06/29/26
NY.summary: A roundup of New York election news covering a federal lawsuit challenging the Even Year Election Law, a Siena poll showing 44% of New Yorkers oppose the redistricting amendment (21% approve), and ongoing Voting Rights Act litigation affecting New York districts.

OH.title: Why Ohio Democrats nearly caught Republicans in primary election turnout
OH.summary: Post-primary data shows Democrats cast 815,922 ballots vs. Republicans' 907,273 in Ohio's May 5 primary — a dramatic narrowing from 2022.
