Republican turnout fell while about 288,500 unaffiliated voters requested Democratic ballots, driven by shifts in Cleveland, Cincinnati, and Columbus.

OK.title: Gentner Drummond (R) and Mike Mazzei (R) campaign on experience and Trump support in the August 25 Republican runoff for Oklahoma governor
OK.summary: After the June 16 primary yielded no majority winner among nine Republican candidates, AG Gentner Drummond (25.9%) and Trump-endorsed former legislator Mike Mazzei (25.5%) face off in an August 25 runoff to become the Republican nominee for Oklahoma governor.

RI.title: In a new poll, R.I. Governor McKee is down 20 with 10 weeks until the primary
RI.summary: A University of New Hampshire poll of likely Democratic primary voters shows incumbent Gov. Dan McKee trailing challenger Helena Foulkes 42-22%, with McKee's job approval at just 19% and 77% disapproving, as the September 9 Democratic gubernatorial primary draws closer.

SD.title: Tribal elections include leadership shakeup in Flandreau
SD.summary: South Dakota tribal elections in 2026 include a major leadership change at the Flandreau Santee Sioux Tribe, where three candidates will compete in an August general election; the article also previews elections across nine South Dakota tribal nations throughout 2026.

TX.title: Supreme Court decision loosening campaign finance rules could be boon for Paxton in Senate race
TX.summary: A 6-3 Supreme Court ruling eliminating caps on coordinated spending between political parties and candidates could help Republican Senate nominee Ken Paxton close his significant fundraising gap against Democratic nominee James Talarico, by allowing national GOP committees to spend freely on his behalf in the Texas Senate race.

VA.title: Voting rights court battle in Virginia drags into early voting period
VA.summary: Federal court dispute about Virginia's compliance with a ruling restoring voting rights to people with certain felony convictions continues, with the ACLU reporting that ELECT officials are not fully processing registrations, leaving eligible voters in limbo during early voting for the August 4 congressional primaries.

VT.title: Gov. Scott's approval at a 4-year low, according to UNH poll
VT.summary: A UNH Survey Center poll shows 51% of Vermonters approve of Gov. Phil Scott's job performance, his lowest rating in four years. Scott holds early leads over Democratic gubernatorial challengers Amanda Janoo and Aly Richards ahead of the November election.

WA.title: Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson backs challengers to unseat top Washington Senate Democrat
WA.summary: Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson endorsed two candidates challenging incumbent Democrats — one attempting to unseat Senate Majority Leader Jamie Pedersen — ahead of Washington's August 4 primary election.

WI.title: Wisconsin Democratic primary for governor turns negative
WI.summary: With absentee ballots already distributed for the August 11 primary, negative campaigning has begun in Wisconsin's Democratic gubernatorial primary, as Mandela Barnes directly attacked Lt. Gov. Sara Rodriguez over utility company donations — the first candidate-on-candidate attack in the crowded six-person field.

WI.title: Military and overseas ballots for Racine's August 11 primary are already in the mail — here's how to vote
WI.summary: Federal law required Wisconsin to mail ballots to military and overseas voters at least 45 days before the August 11 primary. Regular absentee ballots won't go out until July 28; article details Racine voter registration deadlines, photo ID requirements, and early voting locations.

WY.title: Gubernatorial candidate sues over Wyoming's residency requirements
WY.summary: Gabriel Green, 30, a Sheridan resident born and raised in Wyoming, filed a lawsuit challenging his disqualification from the 2026 gubernatorial race. Secretary of State Chuck Gray disqualified him because he lived in Arizona from August 2022 to March 2024, violating Wyoming's constitutional requirement of five consecutive years of residency before the election.

AL.title: NAACP Alabama stresses voter education as election season heats up
AL.summary: Alabama NAACP leaders held a virtual Statewide Freedom Call to outline voter engagement strategies ahead of the August 11 special primary election, focusing outreach on the 2nd and 7th Congressional Districts affected by the court-ordered redistricting. State Conference President Ronald Ali said a senior field organizer is targeting voter engagement in those districts, while Legal Redress Chair Shalela Dowdy stressed education for voters navigating the new congressional map.

AK.title: Alaska Might Have Finally Solved Its Two Dan Sullivans Problem
AK.summary: Alaska's Division of Elections released sample ballots showing how it will distinguish incumbent Sen. Dan S. Sullivan from challenger Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. on the August 18 primary ballot, following the Alaska Supreme Court's ruling that the challenger must remain on the ballot. The incumbent will appear as 'Sullivan, Dan S. (Registered Republican) Incumbent' while the challenger will be listed as 'Sullivan, Daniel J. Jr.' without a party designation, a design the court directed elections officials to implement using existing ballot design law.

AZ.title: Mohave County will debut new ballot paper with added security measures in July primary
AZ.summary: Mohave County is implementing 'Ballot Guard' security paper featuring watermarks, embedded security fibers, and microprinting for the July 21 primary — the first use of such paper in an Arizona election. Initial testing showed a 3.6% multi-feed error rate that improved to 0.7% after the paper acclimated to the printing environment, meeting national standards for ballot tabulation accuracy.

AZ.title: AZ vote-by-mail initiative won't make November ballot after campaign withholds signatures
AZ.summary: The Protect the Vote Arizona campaign announced it will not submit roughly 439,000 raw signatures for the 'Free, Fair and Secure Elections Act,' a proposed constitutional amendment that would have enshrined vote-by-mail and extended early voting rights. The campaign cited concerns about disclosing voter data to Maricopa County Recorder Justin Heap, an official they oppose, and plans to redirect efforts toward opposing HCR 2001, the voter ID ballot measure already set for November.

AR.title: Challengers score victories in lawsuit against Arkansas' restrictions on citizen ballot initiatives
AR.summary: A federal court ruled in favor of challengers contesting Arkansas laws that restrict citizen ballot initiatives, finding key provisions governing petition circulators and signature gathering to be unconstitutional. The ruling marks a significant victory for direct-democracy advocates who argued the restrictions made it nearly impossible for citizens to place measures on the statewide ballot.

CT.title: Connecticut expands first responder benefits, no-excuse absentee voting among 80 new laws taking effect July 1
CT.summary: Connecticut's new no-excuse absentee voting law took effect July 1, allowing any registered voter to request an absentee ballot without providing a specific reason, joining 28 other states with such policies. The change is part of 80 new laws taking effect, implementing a constitutional amendment approved by voters in 2024.

FL.title: Do D.C. records prove Fishback's ineligibility in Florida governor race?
FL.summary: Lt. Gov. Jay Collins filed suit to remove Republican gubernatorial candidate James Fishback from the August 18 primary ballot, citing Washington D.C. voter registration and homestead property records as evidence he fails the state constitution's seven-year Florida residency requirement. A court ruling is needed by around July 4 to avoid affecting overseas ballot mailings.

HI.title: Unopposed For Reelection, Honolulu Budget Chair Isn't Afraid To Fight Admin
HI.summary: Honolulu City Council Budget Chair Val Okimoto, running unopposed for reelection on the August 8 primary ballot, has spent her first year clashing with Mayor Rick Blangiardi's administration over city budget priorities and council oversight, establishing a track record that will shape her uncontested return to the ʻAiea-Mililani district seat.

ID.title: These new laws are set to go into effect in Idaho on July 1
ID.summary: Among Idaho's 350-plus new laws taking effect July 1, SB 1322 tightens voter ID affidavit requirements by mandating that voters who lack photo ID and use a signed affidavit must now also provide their date of birth or Idaho driver's license number — information election judges must verify before issuing a ballot.

IL.title: Bailey campaign embraces artificial intelligence in new era of politics
IL.summary: Republican gubernatorial candidate Darren Bailey's campaign is flooding social media with AI-generated images and videos to drive engagement against Gov. JB Pritzker, while all three major candidates support a proposed Illinois bill that would require written or spoken disclaimers on AI-generated political ads, with fines for violations.

IL.title: New Illinois Republican Party chair hopes for 'JB fatigue' in tough midterm
IL.summary: Newly elected Illinois GOP Chair Bob Grogan is emphasizing state-specific issues like property taxes over national Trump themes as he tries to rebuild a party that has not won a statewide race in over a decade, facing a substantial fundraising gap against Democrats in the 2026 general election cycle.

LA.title: State Rep. Gabe Firment announces candidacy for Louisiana's 5th Congressional District
LA.summary: State Rep. Gabe Firment announced his candidacy for Louisiana's open 5th Congressional District, the seat being vacated by Julia Letlow who won the June 27 GOP Senate runoff. Firment, a Rapides Parish native who has served in the Louisiana House since 2019, chairs the House Insurance Committee and is the first candidate to formally enter the race.

LA.title: Republicans outnumber registered Democrats in Louisiana for first time in state history
LA.summary: For the first time in Louisiana history, Republicans outnumber registered Democrats in voter registration. As of July 1, the GOP holds 1,064,496 registered voters compared to Democrats' 1,062,135, a shift of roughly 2,300 voters, with approximately 820,000 no-party registrants. Gov. Jeff Landry celebrated the milestone while Democratic Party chairman Randal Gaines blamed the Republican policy agenda.

MD.title: Maryland primary election live returns
MD.summary: Partial and unofficial vote counts from Maryland's June 23 primary election, covering governor, attorney general, comptroller, General Assembly, all eight congressional districts, and local offices in six counties. Final results including second mail-in canvasses and provisional ballots are expected July 6. A Carroll County state's attorney race shifted by just two votes between candidates in the latest count.

MA.title: Markey's lead over Moulton still narrow in new Massachusetts Senate primary poll
MA.summary: A new UNH Survey Center poll shows Sen. Ed Markey leading Rep. Seth Moulton 41%-35% in the Massachusetts Democratic Senate primary, a narrower margin than April's 46%-33% split, with undecided voters jumping to 23%. Both candidates have three summer debates scheduled before the September 1 primary.

MI.title: Michigan Democrats use 'One Big Beautiful Bill' anniversary to renew attacks on GOP agenda
MI.summary: Michigan Democratic elected officials and AFL-CIO President Ron Bieber held a press event calling out Republican U.S. Senate candidate Mike Rogers for his support of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act and President Trump's agenda. The event marks Democrats' escalating campaign attacks on Rogers as the August 4 Senate primary approaches.

MO.title: Rep. Wesley Bell and former Rep. Cori Bush are again running against each other in the Democratic primary for Missouri's 1st Congressional District
MO.summary: Incumbent Rep. Wesley Bell and former Rep. Cori Bush face a rematch in the August 4 Democratic primary for Missouri's 1st Congressional District; Bell is backed by House Democratic leadership while Bush has the support of Sen. Bernie Sanders and Our Revolution.

NV.title: Affordable healthcare emerges as a voter priority in purple Nevada
NV.summary: Healthcare costs have emerged as the decisive electoral issue in Nevada's 2026 gubernatorial race between Republican Gov. Joe Lombardo and Democratic AG Aaron Ford, with most respondents saying healthcare costs will influence whom they vote for in November, particularly among Democratic and independent voters.

NV.title: Las Vegas City Council's Allen-Palenske, Brune take second oath of office; Diaz appointed as mayor pro tem
NV.summary: Two Las Vegas City Council members took their oaths of office for second terms on July 1 after winning re-election in June's local elections — Councilwoman Brune won a contested three-way race with 56.7% of the vote, while Councilwoman Allen-Palenske ran unopposed; Councilwoman Diaz was also unanimously appointed mayor pro tem.

NH.title: UNH poll shows tight races for governor and U.S. Senate
NH.summary: A new University of New Hampshire survey shows the 2026 races narrowing: Democrat Chris Pappas leads the Senate primary 53%-29% over Karishma Manzur (down from a 43-point April lead), Republican John Sununu leads the GOP primary 59%-20%, and Gov. Kelly Ayotte holds a 44%-39% edge over Democrat Cinde Warmington in the governor's race ahead of the September 8 primary.

NY.title: Mo Brown declares victory over longtime state Assemblyman Bill Magnarelli in Democratic primary for CNY seat
NY.summary: After absentee ballots were counted, Onondaga County Legislator Maurice 'Mo' Brown defeated 28-year incumbent Bill Magnarelli in the Democratic primary for New York's 129th Assembly District; with no Republican opponent, Brown is effectively assured the seat in November.

OR.title: Nearly every proposed Oregon initiative won't make it onto the November ballot
OR.summary: Nearly all proposed Oregon ballot initiatives failed to collect enough signatures by the July 2 deadline. Only IP28, an animal rights measure that would limit hunting and trapping, gathered sufficient signatures — approximately 138,335, surpassing the 117,173 required. An open primary initiative and several other measures fell short and will not appear on the November ballot.

PA.title: 'Dark money' group paid Democrat Janelle Stelson for disappearing podcast
PA.summary: Democrat Janelle Stelson, who is challenging Rep. Scott Perry in Pennsylvania's 10th Congressional District, received $45,000 from 'Voting for America,' a dark money nonprofit, for podcast production work. The podcasts Stelson produced for the group are no longer accessible online, raising questions about the arrangement as she seeks a rematch against Perry in a competitive district.

UT.title: Kevin O'Leary's company says J. Stuart Adams' election loss won't impact Box Elder data center plan
UT.summary: Following Utah Senate President J. Stuart Adams' upset primary loss to challenger Stephanie Hollist — driven largely by his support for the controversial Box Elder County data center — Kevin O'Leary's company says the project will proceed regardless, stating 'from our perspective, it is business as usual.' The piece examines whether Adams' historic defeat, the first for a sitting Utah Senate president in modern history, will have any practical effect on the massive proposed data center development.

VT.title: Vermont Public's 2026 primary election debates: How to listen, watch and submit questions
VT.summary: Vermont Public announced it will host two primary election debates in late July featuring Democratic candidates for governor and lieutenant governor, ahead of the August 11, 2026 primary. The station is inviting viewers to submit questions via email and provided details on how to watch and listen to the debates.

VT.title: This could be the year Democrats unseat Gov. Scott, pollster says
VT.summary: A University of New Hampshire pollster says Democrats could potentially defeat Gov. Phil Scott in November 2026 if they nominate a well-funded, prominent candidate, as Scott's approval rating has declined to 51%, his lowest in four years. However, 70% of likely primary voters remain unfamiliar with both Democratic challengers, Aly Richards and Amanda Janoo.

WV.title: Harrison County Commission hears arguments in Laura Kimble election challenge
WV.summary: The Harrison County Commission heard arguments in an election contest filed by Laura Kimble, who is challenging the results of a recent local race. The commission is serving as the adjudicating body for the election challenge under West Virginia law.

WV.title: Delegate Daniel Linville is named 'director of special projects' by Morrisey
WV.summary: West Virginia Delegate Daniel Linville resigned from the House of Delegates after being appointed director of special projects by Governor Patrick Morrisey. His resignation creates a legislative vacancy that will require a special appointment process to fill.

WI.title: WEC finds probable violation in April instance of duplicate absentee ballots being sent out
WI.summary: The Wisconsin Elections Commission found a probable violation stemming from an April incident in which the City of Green Bay sent duplicate absentee ballots to some voters. The commission is taking action against the municipality over the mailing error.

DC.title: Red states demand restored access to citizenship database for purging voters
DC.summary: A coalition of Republican-led states filed a legal demand seeking restored access to the federal SAVE citizenship verification database, which they use to identify and remove non-citizens from voter rolls. The states argue the database access is essential to their voter roll maintenance programs.

DC.title: A federal law bans late voter roll purges. Republicans are pushing to reinterpret it.
DC.summary: NPR reports on Republican efforts to reinterpret the National Voter Registration Act's 90-day quiet period that prohibits systematic voter roll purges close to federal elections. The push comes as several states face legal challenges over aggressive voter list maintenance programs in the run-up to the 2026 midterms.

DC.title: What the SCOTUS campaign finance ruling means, according to an expert
DC.summary: NPR reports on the Supreme Court's recent ruling loosening restrictions on coordinated spending between political parties and their candidates, and what it means for campaign finance in the 2026 elections. The decision could significantly increase the role parties play in funding and directing candidate campaigns.

AK.title: The Dan Sullivan saga in the Alaska Senate race is under investigation, sources say
AK.summary: The FBI, Alaska attorney general, and U.S. attorney's office are investigating whether the same-named challenger Dan J. Sullivan's campaign constitutes a conspiracy to confuse voters and deprive Alaskans of a fair election. Investigators are examining potential wire fraud and civil rights violations; Dan J. Sullivan denies any coordination with Democratic candidate Mary Peltola's campaign.

AL.title: Two Republicans vie for 7th congressional district nomination in special August primary
AL.summary: Republican voters in Alabama's 7th Congressional District will choose between former educator Ammie Akin and retired pastor David Perry for the party's nomination in the special August 11 primary. The winner will face 16-year Democratic incumbent Rep. Terri Sewell in the November general election.

DE.title: Attorney General Jennings announces two major victories striking down executive orders on elections
DE.summary: Delaware Attorney General Kathy Jennings announced that federal courts struck down two Trump executive orders affecting elections: EO 14248 (requiring states to obtain documented proof of citizenship for voter registration) and EO 14399 (creating a new election-enforcement commission). Both rulings are expected to prevent enforcement of the EOs ahead of the November 2026 elections.

GA.title: How the U.S. Supreme Court may have given Mike Collins a helping hand
GA.summary: Three recent U.S. Supreme Court rulings are expected to reshape Georgia's 2026 election landscape, with a campaign finance ruling loosening restrictions on coordinated party spending potentially benefiting Republican Senate challenger Mike Collins against Democratic incumbent Jon Ossoff. The ruling allows unlimited coordinated spending between candidates and party committees.

IA.title: New polling, national rankings point to competitive Iowa Senate race between Hinson, Turek
IA.summary: Multiple polls released in late June show the open Iowa Senate race between Republican Rep. Ashley Hinson and Democrat Josh Turek essentially tied; CNN moved Iowa onto its list of most competitive Senate contests nationally, reflecting new voter dynamics following Sen. Joni Ernst's retirement.

IL.title: Democratic chairs choose teachers union leader to replace Holmes on ballot
IL.summary: Illinois Democratic Party chairs from four counties selected Aurora teachers union president Jared Ploger to fill the 42nd Senate District seat on the November 2026 ballot after incumbent Sen. Linda Holmes announced she would resign due to worsening multiple sclerosis; Ploger will face Republican Edgardo Perez in the general election.

KY.title: Voters across Louisville may have gotten the wrong ballots – for years
KY.summary: A Louisville Public Media investigation found that voters in more than 1,800 Louisville households may have received incorrect ballots for multiple election cycles due to precinct assignment errors following 2022 redistricting, potentially affecting at least one state House race outcome; the Jefferson County Clerk's office will audit all 600,000 county addresses and complete corrections before October voter notification postcards are sent.

MD.title: Maryland delays approval of new $109M voting system after rise of transparency concerns
MD.summary: The Maryland Board of Public Works pulled a proposed five-year contract with Election Systems and Software from its agenda after advocates and lawmakers raised concerns about the $109 million price tag and the system's lack of full federal certification. The contract is now expected to come before the Board at its July 22 meeting.

MD.title: Maryland primary election live returns
MD.summary: Maryland's June 23 primary canvass continues with mail-in and provisional ballots still being counted across the state. Counts from in-person votes and first mail-in canvasses are complete, but final certification including second mail-in canvasses and provisional ballots is expected July 6.

MI.title: Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez endorses Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan Democratic primary
MI.summary: Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez endorsed Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan's contested Democratic Senate primary — her first endorsement in a disputed Senate primary — putting her at odds with Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, who backs Rep. Haley Stevens. El-Sayed, Rep. Stevens, and state Sen. Mallory McMorrow are competing for the Democratic nomination ahead of the August 4 primary.

NE.title: Respect Nebraska Voters coalition turns in more than 186,500 signatures for initiative seeking to 'protect' voter-passed laws
NE.summary: The Respect Nebraska Voters coalition submitted 186,500+ signatures for a constitutional amendment that would raise the threshold for the Legislature to change voter-approved laws from two-thirds (33 votes) to four-fifths (40 votes) of the 49-member unicameral.

NE.title: Nebraska group submits 186,000 signatures for ballot measure on initiative rights
NE.summary: Respect Nebraska Voters submitted over 186,000 petition signatures to protect voter-approved laws from legislative changes; the measure was prompted by the Legislature altering earned paid sick leave legislation that received 75% voter approval.

NJ.title: Governor Sherrill Signs Historic Legislation Making New Jersey First State to Enact Voting Rights Reform Following Supreme Court Decision
NJ.source: Office of the Governor of New Jersey
NJ.summary: Governor Mikie Sherrill signed the John R. Lewis Voter Empowerment Act (S282/A1715) into law, making New Jersey the first state to enact voting rights reform in direct response to the U.S. Supreme Court's decision in Louisiana v. Callais. The law strengthens protections against voter suppression and intimidation, expands language access for voters with limited English proficiency, and requires state attorney general preclearance for changes to local election procedures.

NM.title: All independent and minor party candidates for statewide office fall short of qualifying for ballot
NM.summary: Secretary of State Maggie Toulouse Oliver's office disqualified all eight independent and minor party candidates seeking New Mexico statewide offices for failing to collect sufficient voter signatures. The disqualifications highlighted a stark signature disparity: independents must submit more than 14,200 valid signatures to qualify for statewide office, compared to roughly 2,500 for major-party candidates, sparking renewed debate about ballot access equity.

NV.title: SCOTUS mail ballot ruling, Nevada's election results mishap with SOS Cisco Aguilar
NV.summary: Nevada Secretary of State Cisco Aguilar addressed the June 9 primary incident in which partial election results from nine counties were inadvertently transmitted to a media outlet's server roughly three hours before polls closed, with the data removed within about an hour after reporters alerted the office. Aguilar also reviewed the debut of new ballot marking devices in the 2026 primary and previewed the voter ID constitutional amendment (Question 7) and abortion rights amendment (Question 6) heading to Nevada voters in November.

NY.title: Seven votes separate Brooklyn GOP state Senate candidates as BOE count continues, court fight ensues
NY.summary: Two Republican candidates for Brooklyn's 22nd State Senate District nomination are separated by just seven votes in unofficial results, with trailing candidate Bernard Vaiselberg filing a lawsuit seeking a full manual recount and claiming a ballot scanner malfunctioned at a poll site. The Board of Elections plans to continue canvassing through certification expected July 14, with the race falling within the legal threshold requiring a mandatory manual re-canvass.

NY.title: NYC Board of Elections to certify primary results, 3 races to be manually recounted
NY.summary: The New York City Board of Elections will certify all June 23 primary results except three legislative races where margins are within the threshold triggering a mandatory manual re-canvass: the Democratic Assembly primary in Queens District 30 (two-vote margin), the Democratic Assembly primary in Manhattan's West Village District 66, and the Republican State Senate primary in Brooklyn's District 22. The manual re-canvass is scheduled to begin July 10.

VA.title: Election Guide: Virginia primaries set stage for mid-term congressional showdown
VA.summary: Comprehensive voter guide for Virginia's August 4 primary covering the U.S. Senate race (Mark Warner vs. Republican challengers), multiple U.S. House district primaries, voter registration deadline of July 24, and early voting period through August 1. The guide provides context on redistricting and the primary date move from June to August.

VT.title: Candidates for Vermont governor and lieutenant governor report large fundraising hauls
VT.summary: Campaign finance disclosures ahead of Vermont's August 11 primary show Democratic gubernatorial candidates Aly Richards ($365,867) and Amanda Janoo ($164,798) raising significant funds, while lieutenant governor candidates Molly Gray and Ryan McLaren each raised over $250,000 in the most recent reporting period.

WA.title: WA income tax foes file signatures to get repeal measure on ballot
WA.summary: Let's Go Washington submitted 511,408 signatures — nearly double the 309,000 required — to qualify Initiative IP26-645, which would repeal Washington's new 9.9% income tax on earnings over $1 million, for the November ballot. The certification process will take about two weeks, with legal challenges due by July 23.

WV.title: Harrison County Commission hears official contesting of House of Delegates race
WV.summary: The Harrison County Commission is reviewing a contested Republican House of Delegates primary result where incumbent Del. Laura Kimble lost to Tim McNeely by six votes. Kimble's legal team argues unaffiliated voters were allowed to participate in the closed Republican primary in violation of state election law, with the Commission scheduled to render a decision on July 6.

AK.title: DOJ launches investigation into Alaska candidate with same name as sitting senator
AK.summary: The Department of Justice, FBI, and Alaska state authorities launched a joint investigation into whether a conspiracy was formed to place a same-name Republican challenger (Dan J. Sullivan) on the Alaska U.S. Senate primary ballot to confuse voters and harm incumbent Sen. Dan S. Sullivan. Investigators are examining potential wire fraud and civil rights violations related to the election scheme.

AL.title: Spending in Alabama primary elections exceeds $40 million
AL.summary: Politicians in Alabama spent $40.6 million across the May 2026 primary and June primary runoff for state and federal offices, making it one of the costliest election cycles in state history. The attorney general race was the most expensive single contest, reflecting the heightened stakes in Alabama's 2026 cycle, which includes upcoming special congressional primaries in August.

AR.title: Signatures submitted for Arkansas ballot measure on initiative process
AR.summary: Protect AR Rights submitted 108,837 signatures to the Arkansas secretary of state's office for the Arkansas Ballot Measure Rights Amendment of 2026, which would prohibit the Legislature from repealing or changing voter-approved constitutional amendments. The petition requires at least 90,704 valid signatures from registered voters to qualify for the ballot.

AZ.title: Mohave County will debut new ballot paper with added security measures in July primary
AZ.summary: Mohave County is introducing new ballot paper featuring watermarks, embedded security fibers, and microprinting for the July 21 primary election, following a county supervisors vote to contract with Runbeck Election Services for the enhanced paper. A successful debut could prompt other Arizona counties to adopt the security-enhanced ballot stock for future elections.

CO.title: Why Melat Kiros was able to tap into the anti-establishment wave and Julie Gonzales was not
CO.summary: The Colorado Sun reports on how democratic socialist Melat Kiros defeated 30-year incumbent Rep. Diana DeGette in Colorado's June 30 congressional primary while fellow progressive Julie Gonzales lost her Senate primary challenge to incumbent John Hickenlooper. The results article examines voter patterns and candidate strategies that shaped the two competing primary outcomes.

CT.title: Josh Elliott swings big in first commercial
CT.summary: Democratic gubernatorial primary challenger Josh Elliott launched his first campaign commercial ahead of Connecticut's August 11 primary, while awaiting approval of a $3.75 million public financing grant from the State Elections Enforcement Commission. Elliott qualified for the primary ballot by clearing the 15% delegate threshold at the state convention.

DC.title: Courts have protected states' rights to manage elections, despite Trump's efforts
DC.summary: Federal courts have consistently rejected President Trump's attempts to expand executive authority over election administration, blocking executive orders on voting, striking down DOJ demands for state voter data 10 consecutive times, and rejecting efforts to eliminate mail-in ballot grace periods. In response, Trump has escalated pressure on Congress to pass the Save America Act, which would impose new federal voting requirements and mandate states submit voter data to the federal government.

DE.title: Measures on elections and voting that did – and didn't – pass the General Assembly this year
DE.summary: Delaware's 2026 legislative session passed constitutional amendments restricting voting to natural persons in local elections, allowing felons to vote immediately after sentence completion, and enacting the John Lewis Voting Rights Act prohibiting discriminatory election practices. Bills to allow same-day voter registration and unaffiliated voter participation in primaries both failed to reach the required two-thirds threshold.

FL.title: Voter registration deadline approaches for primary election
FL.summary: Florida voters have until July 20 to register or change party affiliation in order to participate in the August 18 primary elections, which will include school board seats, county commission positions, and local ballot referendums across South Florida. The article provides registration resources for Miami-Dade, Palm Beach, Broward, and Monroe counties.

FL.title: The Florida primary is on Aug. 18. Here's what Northeast Florida voters need to know
FL.summary: A voter guide for Northeast Florida covering the August 18 primary election deadlines including the July 20 voter registration cutoff, August 6 vote-by-mail request deadline, and August 8-15 mandatory early voting period. The article explains Florida's closed primary system and provides county-specific sample ballot links for Duval, St. Johns, Clay, Nassau, and Baker counties.

GA.title: Early voting begins in Georgia 13th District special election to serve rest of David Scott's term
GA.summary: Early in-person voting opened July 6 for the July 28 special election in Georgia's 13th Congressional District to fill the seat of the late Rep. David Scott. Six candidates—including Scott's daughter Marcye Scott and former school board chairman Everton Blair—are competing in the safely Democratic suburban Atlanta district.

GA.title: U.S. House District 13: Who is running to finish David Scott's term
GA.summary: The AJC profiles the six candidates—four Democrats and two Republicans—running in Georgia's 13th Congressional District special election as early voting opened on July 6 ahead of the July 28 election day to complete the late Rep. David Scott's term.

HI.title: Ballot drop boxes arriving on Oahu this week ahead of Aug. 8 primary
HI.summary: Ballot drop boxes for Hawaii's August 8 primary election began arriving at 17 designated Oahu locations this week, including two new sites at Salt Lake District Park and the Nanakuli Public Library. Primary ballots will be mailed to registered voters on July 21, with voter service centers opening July 27.

IA.title: Iowa Democrats and Republicans gain voters, independent voters decrease
IA.summary: Iowa's July voter registration data shows Democrats gained more than 27,000 registrants since June and Republicans added 17,000, while the unaffiliated pool fell by more than 32,000—a pattern analysts attribute to independents switching to a party to participate in the June 2 primary.

KS.title: Kansas City election guide 2026: What Kansas and Missouri voters need to know about their ballots
KS.summary: A voter guide ahead of the August 4 Kansas primary covers the open governor's race, a contested U.S. Senate primary where multiple candidates challenge Sen. Roger Marshall, and a constitutional amendment that would shift Kansas Supreme Court justices to partisan elections decided by voters.

KS.title: Kansas primary voting: Key dates, mail ballot deadline, poll hours for Aug. 4
KS.summary: With Kansas's August 4 primary approaching, voters are reminded of key deadlines: the voter registration deadline is July 14, advance in-person voting begins July 15 (with mail ballots going out the same day), and the deadline to request a mail ballot is July 28.

MA.title: Their signatures helped get Republican candidates on the ballot. They say they never actually signed.
MA.summary: Massachusetts voters whose names appear on nominating petitions submitted for Republican candidates say they never signed those documents, raising concerns about fraudulent signatures in the ballot access process for the November 2026 elections.

MD.title: View Maryland primary vote totals as count nears completion
MD.summary: The Baltimore Sun published near-complete vote tallies from Maryland's June 23 primary election, with the State Board of Elections posting results for all jurisdictions. The aggregated results cover governor, attorney general, all eight congressional districts, state legislative races, and local school board contests across Baltimore City and surrounding counties.

MI.title: Michigan lawmakers pass $84B budget, 67 bills in marathon session
MI.summary: Michigan's Legislature passed a $84 billion FY2027 budget but cut a proposed $43 million grant to replace aging statewide voting equipment from the final package. The House Fiscal Agency noted much of the election equipment has reached the end of its lifecycle, and election officials had sought the funding to replace machines past their expected lifespan.

MN.title: What you need to know about Minnesota's primary election, and how to vote early
MN.summary: Sahan Journal published a comprehensive voter guide for Minnesota's August 11 primary election as early voting is underway, covering competitive races for governor, U.S. Senate, U.S. House, and Hennepin County Attorney, along with voter registration deadlines and mail ballot procedures.

MO.title: Taxes, assessors and initiative petitions: Your guide to the August Missouri primary
MO.summary: A guide to the four ballot measures Missouri voters will decide in the August primary election, explaining each proposed constitutional amendment and its potential effects on state policy ahead of the August vote.

MO.title: Missouri has 4 amendments on the August 2026 ballot. Here's what they would do
MO.summary: KCUR's voter guide to Missouri's August primary ballot amendments explains what each proposed constitutional measure would do and what voters will be deciding, providing non-partisan information on the statewide ballot questions ahead of the August election.

NC.title: Issues reported with voter registration forms sent out in North Carolina, state says
NC.summary: North Carolina state officials confirmed problems with voter registration forms that were mailed out to residents, with the state board of elections acknowledging the issue and advising affected voters to check their registration status and resubmit correct paperwork if needed.

NC.title: State Board of Elections issues guidance after NC residents receive bogus voter registration mailers
NC.summary: The North State Journal reported on fraudulent or erroneous voter registration mailers sent to North Carolina residents; officials warned voters to verify registration directly with the State Board of Elections and not rely on information in the suspect mailers.

ND.title: North Dakota Supreme Court tosses ballot measure, finding term limits proposal unconstitutional
ND.summary: The North Dakota Supreme Court unanimously ruled that a legislatively-referred ballot measure to amend voter-approved 2022 term limits for state lawmakers is unconstitutional, finding it violates Article XV of the state constitution. The court directed the secretary of state not to place the measure on the November ballot.

NE.title: Effort to enact total abortion ban in Nebraska fails to submit signatures for a ballot initiative
NE.summary: A campaign seeking to place a total abortion ban on Nebraska's November ballot failed to submit the required number of valid signatures by the deadline, ending the effort to repeal the state's existing 12-week abortion limit. The failure means the abortion ban question will not appear on the 2026 ballot.

NJ.title: Readington fight isn't over as candidate seeks do-over recount
NJ.summary: Republican candidate Jon Kowal seeks a second recount in a Readington Township committee seat race, alleging inconsistencies in how mail-in ballots with handwritten marks were adjudicated during the first recount, where his opponent's margin widened from two to four votes.

PA.title: Voter Data Lawsuit Against Pennsylvania Appealed By DOJ
PA.summary: The DOJ appealed to the Third Circuit its dismissed lawsuit seeking access to Pennsylvania's unredacted voter registration data; civil rights groups including the League of Women Voters and ACLU had successfully argued the data request threatened voter privacy.

SC.title: Primaries end with a draw in SC House's ongoing intraparty GOP battle
SC.summary: Results of South Carolina House GOP primary runoffs show roughly a stalemate between the mainline Republican caucus and the hardline Freedom Caucus, continuing an ongoing intraparty power struggle that will shape the chamber's direction heading into the general election.

TN.title: Tennessee's voter registration deadline is tomorrow. Here's what to know.
TN.summary: Tennessee's voter registration deadline for the August 6 primary is July 7. The article covers eligibility requirements, registration methods, and key dates voters need to know before the upcoming primary election.

TX.title: Rep. Nate Schatzline resigns from Texas House to lead 'election integrity' policy in Gov. Abbott's office
TX.summary: Hardline conservative state Rep. Nate Schatzline resigned from the Texas House to become Gov. Greg Abbott's senior adviser on election policy. His priorities include closing Republican primaries to registered party members only and further restricting mail-in voting eligibility.

VA.title: Affordability, jobs, election integrity take center stage in Va.'s 7th Congressional District race
VA.summary: Preview of Virginia's 7th Congressional District race ahead of the August 4 primary, where Democratic incumbent Rep. Eugene Vindman faces three Republican challengers. Election integrity, cost of living, and jobs are the top campaign themes.

VT.title: Bolstered bloc of Vermont Republicans see bills repealed this year as a win
VT.summary: Following gains in the 2024 elections, Vermont Republicans now hold enough seats to block overrides of Gov. Scott's vetoes. The strengthened caucus successfully drove repeal of several progressive laws this session, marking a significant shift in Vermont's legislative balance of power.

WA.title: Signatures submitted for Washington initiative to repeal legislation establishing an income tax for households earning over $1 million and ban income taxes in general
WA.summary: The Let's Go Washington campaign submitted 511,408 signatures to place an initiative on the November 3 ballot to repeal SB 6346, which established a 9.9% tax on capital gains income for households earning over $1 million. The campaign needs 308,911 validated signatures to qualify.

WI.title: Wisconsin candidates share their favorite state fun fact ahead of 2026 election
WI.summary: Wisconsin Watch published a comprehensive voter guide for the August 11 primary covering all 325 state legislative candidates, noting a stark partisan response gap: roughly 90% of Democratic candidates responded to questionnaires versus about 40% of Republican candidates.

WY.title: Registering to vote in Wyoming? Here's what you need to know
WY.summary: Covers Wyoming's new voter registration requirements that took effect July 1, 2026, including a 30-day residency requirement, mandatory proof of citizenship documentation, and notarization requirements for mail-in registration.

AK.title: The Dan Sullivan saga in the Alaska Senate race is under investigation, sources say
AK.summary: The FBI, Alaska attorney general, and U.S. attorney's office are all investigating whether two or more people conspired to create a Senate candidacy under the name 'Dan Sullivan' to confuse voters and boost Democratic challenger Mary Peltola ahead of Alaska's August primary.

AZ.title: U.S. Supreme Court agrees to review Arizona's documentary proof of citizenship and noncitizen voter removal laws
AZ.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court agreed to review Arizona's laws requiring documentary proof of citizenship for voter registration and mandating removal of noncitizens from voter rolls under the NVRA, in the case RNC v. Mi Familia Vota. The decision could affect more than 43,000 registered Arizona voters currently flagged under those provisions.

CO.title: Victor Marx holds a steady lead over Barbara Kirkmeyer in Colorado Republican governor contest
CO.summary: Victor Marx held a narrow lead over state Sen. Barb Kirkmeyer in Colorado's still-undecided Republican gubernatorial primary, with both campaigns urging voters to cure rejected mail ballots before the July 8 deadline.

CO.title: Republican Victor Marx maintains slim lead over Barb Kirkmeyer in Colorado gubernatorial primary
CO.summary: With 97% of ballots counted a week after the June 30 primary, Victor Marx led Kirkmeyer by 1,950 votes (0.38%), narrowly below the automatic recount threshold, as the ballot cure deadline approached on July 8.

DC.title: In good sign for voters, court won't fast-track Trump DOJ voter roll appeals
DC.summary: The First Circuit Court of Appeals declined the Trump DOJ's request to expedite three voter roll cases involving Maine, Massachusetts, and Rhode Island, slowing the administration's push to obtain unredacted voter data before the 90-day pre-election quiet period begins August 5.

DC.title: Postal Service appeals court order blocking Trump's anti-mail voting order
DC.summary: The U.S. Postal Service filed to pause a federal court order blocking implementation of President Trump's executive order restricting mail-in voting, arguing the injunction prevents USPS from developing voter-list systems needed before the 2026 midterm elections.

FL.title: DeSantis allies break away, endorse Byron Donalds for Florida governor
FL.summary: Key DeSantis allies including CFO Blaise Ingoglia, Attorney General James Uthmeier, and Agriculture Commissioner Wilton Simpson endorsed Byron Donalds for governor while DeSantis has continued to withhold his own endorsement of any candidate.

FL.title: Donalds towers over a sleepy Florida governor's race
FL.summary: Byron Donalds commands the Florida Republican gubernatorial primary with over $90 million raised and 54% support among likely GOP primary voters, heading into the August 18 primary with no serious challenger in sight.

FL.title: Sarasota County voter registration deadline for August primary is July 20
FL.summary: Florida voters must register to vote or change their party affiliation by July 20 to participate in the August 18 primary election, with vote-by-mail requests due by August 6 and mandatory early voting running August 8-15.

GA.title: Judge rejects Justice Department attempt to get names of 2020 election workers in Fulton County
GA.summary: Federal Judge William Ray rejected the DOJ's April subpoena seeking identities and personal information of approximately 3,000 Fulton County 2020 election workers, calling the scope 'staggering' and finding it lacked a legitimate law enforcement purpose. The judge warned the subpoena could deter future election worker recruitment in Georgia.

HI.title: Oahu's 2026 elections: Ballot drop boxes now available
HI.summary: Seventeen official ballot drop boxes opened at designated locations across Oahu on Monday ahead of Hawaii's August 8 primary, with a Honolulu Hale drop box set to arrive July 8; primary ballots will be mailed to registered voters starting July 21.

IA.title: Iowa Democrats and Republicans gain voters, independent voters decrease
IA.summary: Iowa voter registration data shows Democrats gained over 27,000 new registrants to reach 527,675 total active voters while Republicans added 17,000 to reach 711,587, with registered independents falling by more than 32,000 as analysts attribute the shifts to voters switching party affiliation to participate in the June 2 primary.

IL.title: Rep. Harry Benton resigns, withdraws name from ballot amid ethics investigation
IL.summary: Illinois State Rep. Harry Benton, a two-term Democratic lawmaker from Plainfield, resigned from the House effective Friday after a legislative inspector general investigation concluded he engaged in sexual harassment, and also withdrew his name as the Democratic candidate for his House district from the November ballot.

KY.title: Some voters in Louisville, Kentucky, got wrong ballots for years
KY.summary: An investigation found that more than 1,800 Louisville households may have received incorrect ballots for years due to voter precinct misassignments following 2022 redistricting, potentially affecting the outcome of a five-vote Democratic primary race in House District 44 and prompting a full county audit.

KY.title: How we did it: Untangling voter assignment errors in Louisville
KY.summary: Louisville Public Media detailed the data analysis behind its finding that Jefferson County voter precinct assignment errors affected over 1,800 households, with the clerk's office launching a countywide manual audit to fix errors before November.

MA.title: Markey and Moulton will have first senate debate in Western Massachusetts
MA.summary: Sen. Ed Markey and Rep. Seth Moulton are set to hold their first Democratic Senate primary debate on July 8 at the WWLP broadcast studio in Chicopee, the first of three summer debates before the September 1 primary.

MD.title: Maryland lawmakers announce special session for redistricting
MD.summary: Maryland's Senate President and House Speaker announced a special legislative session August 3-5 to address congressional redistricting in response to court decisions affecting voting rights, with lawmakers expected to establish new constitutional standards for drawing district maps rather than redrawing current lines.

MD.title: Legislative races come into focus as ballot counting wraps on June 23 primary
MD.summary: Local election boards completed ballot counting from Maryland's June 23 primary, with results showing roughly five legislative incumbents lost their seats including Senate Majority Leader Nancy King and Sen. Dalya Attar; official certification of results is scheduled for July 23.

ME.title: Graham Platner faces Democratic calls to quit after sexual assault allegation
ME.summary: Maine Democratic Senate nominee Graham Platner faces mounting calls to withdraw from the race against Sen. Susan Collins after an ex-girlfriend alleged he forced nonconsensual sex in 2021; the DSCC announced it will not invest in the Maine Senate race if Platner remains the nominee.

ME.title: Democrats begin pulling Platner endorsements after Maine Senate candidate faces sexual assault allegation
ME.summary: Leading Senate Democrats and Sen. Bernie Sanders rescinded endorsements of Maine Senate candidate Graham Platner following a Politico report detailing an allegation from a former girlfriend; Maine Democratic leadership also called on Platner to withdraw.

ME.title: The behind-the-scenes scramble begins to replace Graham Platner as he weighs his future
ME.summary: As Platner weighs dropping out of Maine's Senate race, Democratic operatives are vetting potential replacements; state law allows a new nominee if Platner withdraws by July 13, with the party then having until July 27 to name a replacement candidate.

ME.title: Graham Platner has six days to decide whether to drop out — here's how that would work
ME.summary: With Platner facing a July 13 deadline to allow ballot replacement, potential Democratic substitute nominees include former Maine Senate President Troy Jackson, former Maine CDC Director Nirav Shah, and Secretary of State Shenna Bellows, all of whom ran in the Democratic gubernatorial primary.

ME.title: Who could replace Graham Platner if he drops out of the Maine Senate race
ME.summary: Democratic officials are assessing potential candidates to replace Maine Senate nominee Graham Platner ahead of the July 13 withdrawal cutoff; incumbent Sen. Susan Collins held a narrow lead over Platner in the most recent polling before the allegation became public.

MI.title: Mallory McMorrow suspends Senate campaign in Michigan
MI.summary: Michigan State Senator Mallory McMorrow suspended her Democratic primary campaign for U.S. Senate, narrowing the August 4 primary field to Rep. Haley Stevens and Dr. Abdul El-Sayed for the seat being vacated by retiring Sen. Gary Peters.

MI.title: Michigan voters can change their absentee ballots after McMorrow's exit
MI.summary: Michigan election officials are explaining how voters who already returned absentee ballots for McMorrow can 'spoil' and replace them before the August 4 primary, with key deadlines ranging from July 24 to August 3 depending on how the ballot was submitted.

MI.title: AG Nessel, Secretary Benson Respond to DOJ Primary Election Municipal Letters
MI.summary: Michigan AG Dana Nessel and Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson rejected DOJ letters announcing federal election monitors for Detroit, Lansing, and East Lansing's August primary, calling the allegations baseless and asserting that states, not the federal government, administer elections.

MI.title: DOJ to send election monitors to Detroit, Lansing, East Lansing
MI.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice plans to deploy federal election monitors to three predominantly Democratic Michigan cities for the August 4 primary, with Democratic officials calling the move politically motivated targeting of communities with high Democratic turnout.

MI.title: Michigan religious leaders speak against what they say are voter intimidation efforts
MI.summary: About 250 faith leaders from across Michigan gathered at the state Capitol to oppose DOJ plans to send election monitors to Detroit, Lansing, and East Lansing ahead of the August primary, calling the monitors a form of voter intimidation targeting Democratic communities.

MT.title: Mystery PAC That Boosted Bankhead Exits Montana Senate Race, Leaving a Financial Void
MT.summary: A political action committee that provided significant financial backing to Montana Senate candidate Bankhead has withdrawn from the race, creating a fundraising gap for the campaign heading into the general election.

NC.title: Wake County Democrats want to bring back NC State early voting site
NC.summary: Wake County Democrats are requesting $200,000 to restore the early voting site at NC State's Talley Student Union after the Republican-majority elections board relocated it to a more remote campus area, reflecting a statewide pattern of Republican-controlled boards blocking on-campus early voting.

NE.title: Election 2026: Early ballot applications for Nebraska Gubernatorial General Election to be sent
NE.summary: The Douglas County Election Commission announced it will mail early-voting applications for Nebraska's November 2026 general election in late July, with voters on the early-voting request list expected to receive their applications in early August; completed applications can be returned by drop box, mail, email, or fax.

NE.title: Nonpartisan candidate Macey Budke will run write-in campaign for Nebraska's 3rd District
NE.summary: Nonpartisan candidate Macey Budke announced she will run a write-in campaign for Nebraska's 3rd Congressional District rather than collect the 2,000 signatures needed by the August 3 deadline, citing the logistical challenge of canvassing a large rural district without party infrastructure or paid circulators.

NJ.title: Sherrill signs John Lewis Voter Empowerment Act into law, creating New Jersey's own voting rights statute
NJ.summary: Governor Meredith Sherrill signed the John Lewis Voter Empowerment Act into law, creating New Jersey's own state-level voting rights statute following a Supreme Court decision; the law establishes new voter protections and expands access to the ballot independent of federal voting rights law.

NJ.title: Bennett raises colossal $1.6 million in Q2 in bid to unseat Kean in NJ-7
NJ.summary: Democrat Rebecca Bennett raised $1.6 million in Q2 2026 for her campaign to unseat Republican incumbent Tom Kean Jr. in New Jersey's 7th congressional district, accumulating over $4.2 million total with $1.3 million cash on hand for one of the most competitive House races in the country.

NM.title: Haaland holds big cash advantage over Hull in New Mexico governor's race
NM.summary: Democratic gubernatorial candidate Deb Haaland holds a significant fundraising advantage over Republican candidate Ryan Hull in New Mexico's open governor's race, having raised approximately double what Hull raised in the month following the primary election.

NM.title: Independents sink before Election Day
NM.summary: All independent and minor-party candidates for New Mexico statewide office failed to gather enough petition signatures to qualify for the November ballot, leaving the general election races entirely between Democratic and Republican nominees.

NV.title: 'Democrats for Lombardo' might say more about the Dems on the list than Lombardo, expert says
NV.summary: Gov. Joe Lombardo's campaign announced a coalition of 120-plus registered Nevada Democrats backing his re-election bid against AG Aaron Ford, but political scientists say the group reflects its members' own views more than broad bipartisan support for Lombardo.

OH.title: Catching Our Eye: News Roundup July 2, 2026
OH.summary: A roundup of notable Ohio political and election news stories from early July 2026, covering legislative and campaign developments across the state.

OH.title: Ohio Democrats outraising Republicans in downballot statewide offices but still far behind in cash on hand, campaign finance filings show
OH.summary: New campaign finance filings show Ohio Democrats outpacing Republicans in fundraising for downballot statewide races, though Republican candidates retain a significant advantage in total cash on hand heading into November.

OH.title: Catching Our Eye: News Roundup July 7, 2026
OH.summary: A roundup of notable Ohio political and election news from mid-July 2026, covering the latest developments in state campaigns and legislative matters.

RI.title: Rhode Island SEIU Endorses Foulkes for Governor
RI.summary: The Service Employees International Union's Rhode Island chapter endorsed Foulkes in the governor's race, adding a major labor organization's backing to the Democratic primary campaign.

SD.title: Dell Rapids Republican Lawmaker May Get Plea Deal in Election Fraud Case
SD.summary: A Republican state lawmaker from Dell Rapids is reportedly in negotiations for a plea deal in an election fraud case, according to court and legal sources familiar with the proceedings.

TN.title: Tennessee's voter registration deadline is Tuesday. Here's what to know.
TN.summary: Tuesday, July 7 is the voter registration deadline for Tennessee's August 6 primary, which includes state and federal primaries and county general elections; voters can register online, by mail, or in person at county election commissions through the end of business day.

TN.title: Tennessee's voter registration deadline is today. Here's what to know.
TN.summary: Today is the final day to register to vote or update voter registration for Tennessee's August 6, 2026 primary election, covering all state and federal primaries plus county general elections; registration can be completed online, by mail, or in person at county election offices.

TX.title: Ken Paxton vowed to crack down on 'illegal voting.' He may have violated Texas election law.
TX.summary: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton faces allegations he violated state election law by voting in six elections over two years while registered at his estranged wife's Collin County home, despite appearing to have relocated to a Denton County property — contradicting Paxton's own office guidance that misrepresenting residence on election records is illegal.

TX.title: Senate Republican leaders to headline Ken Paxton fundraiser in Texas
TX.summary: U.S. Senate Majority Leader John Thune and more than a dozen GOP senators, including Ted Cruz and Tim Scott, will attend a July 22 fundraiser for AG Ken Paxton's Senate campaign — a reversal for national Republicans who spent $90 million trying to defeat Paxton in the primary against incumbent Sen. John Cornyn.

TX.title: Paxton and Talarico are in a cage match for a Senate seat. Suburban Collin County is a battleground.
TX.summary: The 2026 Texas Senate race between Republican Ken Paxton and Democrat James Talarico is expected to be highly competitive, with Collin County — a historically conservative Dallas suburb experiencing demographic shifts — identified as a key battleground after Talarico drew 4,000 supporters to a Plano rally.

UT.title: McAdams Win Could Give Utah Lawmakers Pause on Reviving Redistricting Fight
UT.summary: Democrat Ben McAdams's primary victory may discourage Utah Republican lawmakers from reviving redistricting legislation, as the result signals electoral vulnerability in competitive districts.

VA.title: Primary challengers try to map out route to victory against incumbent Rep. Beyer
VA.summary: Four Democratic challengers (Seifeldein, Dunigan, Duffin, Bruner) debated Rep. Don Beyer ahead of the August 4 primary in Virginia's 8th Congressional District, each mapping out distinct strategies to break through against a well-funded incumbent.

VA.title: Arlington Democrats plan straw polls for primaries, 2028 presidential race
VA.summary: The Arlington County Democratic Committee plans straw polls on July 11 for the 8th Congressional District primary and county board races, and also voted to support three November ballot amendments covering voting rights, abortion rights, and marriage equality.

VT.title: Vermont Secretary of State Shares Voting Information and Resources Ahead of Primary
VT.summary: Vermont's Secretary of State issued voter information and resources ahead of the state's upcoming primary election, including details on registration deadlines, polling locations, and absentee voting procedures.

WI.title: Wisconsin Supreme Court refuses to release voter records sought by conservative activist
WI.summary: The Wisconsin Supreme Court ruled 5-2 that the state must not release guardianship records sought by conservative activist Ron Heuer and the Wisconsin Voter Alliance, who claimed the records would help identify ineligible voters; Justice Protasiewicz wrote that state law clearly protects the records.

WV.title: Morrisey appoints Shane Stack to House District 4 seat
WV.summary: West Virginia Gov. Patrick Morrisey appointed Shane Thomas Stack of Triadelphia to fill the vacancy in House District 4 left by Bill Flanigan, who was elected to the state Supreme Court of Appeals; Stack is a business owner and former town treasurer with deep roots in the local community.

WY.title: US Senate candidate Benavidez shrugs off probation sentence
WY.summary: Wyoming Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Billy Benavidez, running in the August 18 primary, is serving one year of unsupervised probation after pleading guilty to breach of peace for harassing a Sheridan police officer, but dismissed the issue by telling voters to 'figure it out' themselves.

AK.title: 7 candidates vie for Southwest Alaska seat left open by House speaker's run for state Senate
AK.summary: Seven candidates are competing for the Southwest Alaska House seat vacated by Speaker Cathy Tilton, who is running for state Senate in the November election, triggering a special primary race for the open seat.

AR.title: Arkansas Advocate: Signatures submitted for ballot measure on initiative process
AR.summary: Organizers submitted signatures for a ballot measure aimed at changing Arkansas's citizen initiative process, which could affect how voters propose and pass laws through direct democracy in future elections.

CA.title: Who is Steve Hilton? Here's how he has rebranded himself multiple times
CA.summary: A profile of Republican California governor candidate Steve Hilton examining his repeated political rebrands — from UK Conservative Party advisor to Fox News host to California gubernatorial contender — as he competes in the 2026 governor's race.

CO.title: Colorado's Republican primary for governor may not be decided until Thursday at the earliest
CO.summary: Colorado's Republican gubernatorial primary between Victor Marx and Barb Kirkmeyer remained unresolved with mail ballots still being counted, and a winner was not expected to be declared until at least Thursday.

CT.title: Voting by mail in Connecticut: Here's what you need to know
CT.summary: A guide to Connecticut's mail-in and absentee voting process, explaining how voters can request ballots, key deadlines, and drop-off locations under the state's expanded vote-by-mail laws ahead of upcoming elections.

DC.title: DOJ warns criminal charges for state election officials if noncitizens vote
DC.summary: The Justice Department sent letters to all 50 states and Washington D.C. threatening election officials with criminal prosecution if they knowingly retain noncitizens on voter rolls or facilitate noncitizen ballot casting, giving states five days to respond and escalating federal pressure on state election administration ahead of the November midterms.

DE.title: Delaware Court of Chancery holds hearing for case between Wilmington City Councilmembers
DE.summary: The Delaware Court of Chancery held a hearing in a legal dispute between Wilmington City Councilmembers over an election matter, with the outcome potentially affecting the composition of the city council.

FL.title: Lt. Gov. Jay Collins pushes back on accusations his wife attacked DeSantis online
FL.summary: Florida Lt. Governor Jay Collins denied claims that his wife posted critical comments about Gov. Ron DeSantis online, amid his campaign for the 2026 Republican gubernatorial nomination in a crowded primary field.

GA.title: Advance voting continues for District 13 special election
GA.summary: Advance voting is underway for the July 28 special election in Georgia's 13th Congressional District, called after Rep. David Scott died in April 2026. Six candidates — four Democrats and two Republicans — are competing to serve the remainder of his term, with early voting running July 6–24 at four Clayton County locations.

ID.title: Supporters of ballot measure to end Idaho's strict abortion ban turn in nearly 110K signatures
ID.summary: Supporters of the Reproductive Freedom and Privacy Act initiative delivered nearly 110,000 signatures to the Idaho Capitol, seeking to qualify the measure for the November ballot; organizers say they surpassed the threshold requiring signatures from at least 6% of registered voters in 18 of Idaho's 35 legislative districts.

IN.title: Longtime citizen flagged, voter registration revoked in proof-of-citizenship ordeal
IN.summary: A naturalized U.S. citizen for nearly three decades had her Indiana voter registration canceled under HEA 1264, the state's proof-of-citizenship law, after a BMV system outage prevented timely verification — illustrating concerns about the law's effect on more than 1,600 Indiana voters whose registrations have been rejected or canceled.

LA.title: Republicans take lead in Louisiana registered voters; Democrats claim purge
LA.summary: As of July 1, 2026, Republicans surpassed Democrats in Louisiana voter registration for the first time in state history, with Republicans gaining nearly 15,000 voters over the past year while Democrats lost more than 33,000. Democratic officials allege a targeted voter purge; Republican Secretary of State Nancy Landry's office denies removing any voters from the rolls.

MA.title: Boston DSA's November focus is on ballot questions
MA.summary: Boston's Democratic Socialists of America formed a campaign committee to support Massachusetts ballot questions on same-day voter registration and public records transparency in the November 2026 election, reflecting grassroots mobilization around voting-related ballot initiatives.

MD.title: Moore calls on Platner to drop out, more Maryland hopefuls concede, in political notes
MD.summary: Several Maryland candidates who fell short in the June 23 primary officially conceded their races as local election boards finalized tallies and reported results to the state Board of Elections, which has until July 23 to certify the primary results.

ME.title: As Calls Mount for Graham Platner to Drop Out of Senate Race, What Happens Next in Maine?
ME.summary: Maine Democratic Senate nominee Graham Platner faces mounting pressure to withdraw following a sexual assault allegation, with a July 13 deadline for the state party to name a replacement in the pivotal race against Republican Sen. Susan Collins that could determine Senate control.

MI.title: Feds sending monitors to Detroit, Lansing and East Lansing for August primaries
MI.summary: The DOJ announced plans to station federal election monitors in three Michigan cities for the August 4 primary, citing alleged 2024 irregularities; Michigan Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson and AG Dana Nessel called the claims unsubstantiated, with Detroit's city clerk describing the rationale as "thin gruel."

MI.title: DOJ intends to send election monitors to 3 Michigan cities for August primary
MI.summary: The Department of Justice plans to deploy federal election monitors to Detroit, Lansing, and East Lansing during Michigan's August 2026 primary, with state officials pushing back on DOJ claims that voters were denied provisional ballots and encountered long lines in November 2024.

MN.title: Red state? Blue state? Here are the races that will likely determine party control at the Minnesota Legislature
MN.summary: An examination of the most competitive Minnesota legislative districts heading into the August 11 primary and November election, covering suburban and rural rematches that will determine which party controls the closely divided state House and Senate.

MO.title: Wednesday July 8th final day to register to vote in Missouri for primary election
MO.summary: July 8 is the final deadline for Missourians to register to vote in the August 4 primary election, which features competitive congressional races and four constitutional amendments including a proposal to phase out the state income tax over five years.

MS.title: DeSoto County residents file lawsuit over majority-Black judicial subdistrict
MS.summary: DeSoto County residents filed a lawsuit challenging Mississippi's majority-Black judicial subdistrict, with a hearing scheduled for July 22, adding to the state's ongoing legal battles over redistricting and minority voting representation.

MT.title: Financial backer of Democratic Senate nominee backs out of Montana
MT.summary: Progressive Vet PAC, which spent over .5 million supporting Democratic Senate nominee Alani Bankhead in the primary, exited Montana's Senate general election race and declared no Democrat has a viable path to winning, leaving Bankhead's campaign without major outside financial support for November.

NC.title: North Carolina Republican operative shaping the state's early voting plans is reassigned
NC.summary: State Auditor Dave Boliek reassigned veteran GOP operative Dallas Woodhouse after NBC News reporting revealed Woodhouse was using his government position to pressure county election officials to alter their early voting schedules ahead of the 2026 midterms.

NH.title: Trump DOJ to deploy election monitors in 6 states amid intense pressure campaign
NH.summary: The Trump Justice Department announced it will send federal election monitors to 15 jurisdictions across six states — including New Hampshire — for the 2026 primary season, coinciding with its broader pressure campaign on state election officials over noncitizen voting concerns ahead of the September 8 New Hampshire primary.

NJ.title: New Jersey becomes the 11th state to enact a state-level voting rights act
NJ.summary: Governor Mikie Sherrill signed Assembly Bill 1715 on July 2, establishing New Jersey as the 11th state with a state-level voting rights statute that prohibits voting policies that deny or abridge the right of protected-class members to vote, with most provisions taking effect August 15, 2026.

NV.title: Lawsuit filed over 'never-resident' citizens voting rights
NV.summary: The Republican National Committee, Nevada Republican Party, and Jim Marchant filed suit challenging a Nevada law that permits U.S. citizens born abroad to vote in the state if Nevada was their parents' last address, arguing the law unconstitutionally dilutes the votes of lawful Nevada voters.

NY.title: Hochul joins calls for U.S. Postal Service to drop plan tied to Trump's election order
NY.summary: Governor Hochul joined eight other Democratic governors urging the U.S. Postal Service to withdraw its proposed rule implementing Trump's executive order that would restrict mail-in ballot delivery, warning the rule could disenfranchise millions of eligible voters in New York.

OH.title: Federal judge orders DHS to restore immigration verification tool used for voter rolls, professional licenses
OH.summary: A Florida federal judge ordered DHS to immediately restore the SAVE immigration verification system's bulk-upload and Social Security number search features, which Ohio and other plaintiff states use to check voter rolls for noncitizen registrations, after a D.C. court had ordered those features disabled in late June.

OK.title: How Oklahoma Determines General Election Ballot Order for Candidates and Political Parties
OK.summary: Oklahoma held its legally required public drawing on July 8 to determine the order in which political parties and candidates will appear on all November General Election ballots statewide, a process mandated by state law every even-numbered year.

OR.title: Even the backers of measure to ban hunting, livestock in Oregon think it will fail
OR.summary: Proponents of Oregon Initiative Petition 28 (the PEACE Act) submitted 142,784 signatures on July 2 to qualify the measure for the November 2026 ballot; state officials now have until August 2 to verify signatures before it can be certified for the ballot.

PA.title: Pennsylvania elections could look very different if Democrats win full control of state government in 2026
PA.summary: If Pennsylvania Democrats win a legislative majority alongside Gov. Shapiro's reelection, they could pass major election reforms including pre-canvassing of mail ballots, same-day voter registration, in-person early voting, and required drop boxes in every county.

RI.title: RI elections board approves early voting regulations
RI.summary: Rhode Island's Board of Elections voted 4-0 to approve new regulations creating uniform statewide rules for early in-person voting available at designated locations 20 days before primary and general elections, though a dispute over buffer zones near early voting sites was left unresolved.

SC.title: Could SC end open primaries? Republicans sue to decide who gets to vote in their elections
SC.summary: The South Carolina Republican Party filed a federal lawsuit seeking to close its primary elections to registered Republicans only, arguing that allowing unaffiliated voters to participate in GOP primaries violates the party's First Amendment rights of association.

SD.title: Doeden stays on message as Sioux Falls Mayor TenHaken endorses Rhoden
SD.summary: With South Dakota's first-ever gubernatorial runoff approaching on July 28, Sioux Falls Mayor Paul TenHaken endorsed incumbent Gov. Larry Rhoden, while challenger Toby Doeden continued campaigning on tax relief and affordability in what is a historic first runoff election for the state.

TN.title: 'What do we have in common': Traveling the 250 miles through Tennessee's House District 9
TN.summary: A report on Tennessee's newly redistricted 9th Congressional District, redrawn by Republican-led mid-decade redistricting to eliminate the state's last Democratic-held House seat, featuring candidates Justin Pearson and London Lamar ahead of the August 6 Democratic primary.

TX.title: Ken Paxton vowed to crack down on 'illegal voting.' He may have violated Texas election law
TX.summary: An investigation found Texas AG Ken Paxton may have voted using an address where he no longer resides, potentially violating the same election residency laws his office enforces; three election lawyers said his actions raise legal concerns under Texas statutes.

UT.title: Gerrymandering: Utah legislative leaders say they won't propose a new Amendment D this year
UT.summary: Utah legislative leaders announced they will not propose a new Amendment D in 2026 to give the Legislature power to repeal voter-approved ballot initiatives, following the Utah Supreme Court's prior ruling that previous Amendment D ballot language was misleading.

WI.title: Wisconsin Supreme Court nixes attempt to get voting eligibility records
WI.summary: The Wisconsin Supreme Court ruled 5-2 that the Wisconsin Voter Alliance cannot obtain confidential court records documenting when individuals are declared incompetent to vote, protecting voter privacy under legislative intent to keep such records closed.

WI.title: Crowley drops gubernatorial bid
WI.summary: Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley ended his Wisconsin Democratic gubernatorial primary campaign, narrowing the August 11 primary field and calling for party unity against Republican frontrunner Tom Tiffany in the wide-open open-seat governor's race.

WI.title: 7th CD GOP candidates debate Trump agenda, private sector experience
WI.summary: Four Republican candidates for Wisconsin's open 7th Congressional District seat held their only televised debate ahead of the August 11 primary, with candidate Michael Alfonso backing the SAVE America Act's voting restrictions; the seat opened when incumbent Rep. Tom Tiffany entered the governor's race.

AK.title: Alaska's news organizations are collaborating on voter guides — and you can help, too
AK.summary: Alaska news organizations are joining forces to produce voter guides for the 2026 election cycle and are soliciting public participation to help inform the collaborative effort.

AZ.title: What you need to know about Arizona's primary election
AZ.summary: A comprehensive guide covering essential information for Arizona voters ahead of the upcoming primary election, including voting options, ballot drop-off locations, and key race overviews.

CO.title: Colorado lawmakers enact omnibus elections bill, seven other election-related laws in 2026 session
CO.summary: Colorado's 2026 legislative session produced HB 1113, a broad omnibus elections bill, along with seven additional election-related laws covering various aspects of state election administration.

HI.title: ʻĀina, Army and Mauna Kea: Office Of Hawaiian Affairs Trustee Candidate Q&As
HI.summary: Office of Hawaiian Affairs trustee candidates respond to questions on key issues including land, military presence, and Mauna Kea ahead of the November 2026 election.

ID.title: Independent John Stegner launches campaign for Idaho governor
ID.summary: John Stegner announced his independent candidacy for Idaho governor, joining the November 2026 general election race alongside the major-party nominees.

IL.title: Illinois 'reviewing' DOJ's threat to prosecute state election officials over noncitizen voting
