IL.summary: The Illinois State Board of Elections said it is reviewing a U.S. Department of Justice letter warning state election officials of potential criminal prosecution for allowing noncitizens to vote, as federal pressure on voter eligibility intensifies ahead of the 2026 midterms.

IN.title: Recount process almost done for Indiana's close primary races
IN.summary: Indiana election officials are nearly finished with the recount process for several contested races from the June 2026 primary election, with final certified results expected shortly.

KS.title: Kansas voter registration deadline nears ahead of Aug. 4 primary
KS.summary: Kansas election officials are reminding eligible voters that the registration deadline is approaching for the August 4 primary, which features competitive races for U.S. Senate and governor.

KS.title: What Kansans will vote on in Aug. 4 primary: U.S. Senate, governor's race, state supreme court
KS.summary: An overview of the contested races and ballot measures Kansas voters will decide in the August 4 primary, including the U.S. Senate race, the governor's contest, and a judicial selection vote.

LA.title: Deadlines for November election are approaching
LA.summary: Louisiana candidates are reminded that deadlines for nominating petitions for the November 2026 election are imminent, with most candidates needing to file by July 8 and U.S. Congressional candidates having until July 9.

MA.title: 'With all due respect': Markey, Moulton trade barbs in heated first debate of Mass. Senate primary
MA.summary: Sen. Ed Markey and Rep. Seth Moulton clashed sharply in their first debate of the Massachusetts Democratic Senate primary, trading barbs over generational change and progressive credentials ahead of the September 15 primary.

ME.title: Who replaces Graham Platner in Maine Senate race? These Democrats could
ME.summary: A look at the Democrats who could step in to replace Graham Platner as the party's candidate in Maine's competitive U.S. Senate race following his withdrawal from the contest.

MI.title: Michigan's Republican gubernatorial hopefuls battle hard in first debate
MI.summary: Republican candidates vying for the Michigan governorship held their first debate, clashing over economic policy, education, and the direction of the state party ahead of the August primary.

MN.title: Minnesota begins routine election machine tests as feds retreat from election security
MN.summary: Minnesota election officials began pre-election testing of voting equipment ahead of the 2026 primary as federal support for election security has diminished under the current administration.

MO.title: Missouri governor's tax plan draws skepticism in crowded state Senate GOP primary
MO.summary: Several Republican candidates competing in Missouri Senate primary races expressed doubts about the governor's proposed tax policies, highlighting intraparty divisions ahead of the August primary.

MT.title: District court judge blocks new state GOP bylaws
MT.summary: A Lewis and Clark County district court judge issued a preliminary injunction blocking new bylaws adopted by the Montana Republican Party, following a legal challenge from county central committees over consolidation of party power.

NC.title: Delayed by budget talks, NC legislature still has plenty to do
NC.summary: The North Carolina General Assembly returns July 27 with a backlog that includes elections omnibus bill HB 958, which passed the House in June and awaits Senate action, along with constitutional amendments and veto overrides.

NV.title: Gavin Newsom launches tour, fundraising campaign for Democrats in Nevada, the South
NV.summary: California Gov. Gavin Newsom kicked off a multi-state campaign tour starting in Nevada, raising money and rallying support for Democratic candidates ahead of the November midterm elections.

OR.title: Proposal to ban hunting in Oregon clears major hurdle for November ballot
OR.summary: Supporters of Initiative Petition 28 submitted over 142,000 signatures to the Oregon Secretary of State, exceeding the threshold needed to potentially place the measure banning hunting, fishing, and trapping on the November 2026 ballot.

TX.title: Talarico's $30 Million Haul Crushes Paxton in Texas Senate Race
TX.summary: Democrat James Talarico raised $30 million in Q2, more than tripling Republican Ken Paxton's $9 million haul in what could be the most expensive Senate race of the 2026 midterms, with 97% of contributions coming from small donors.

VT.title: Candidates For Vermont Governor And Lieutenant Governor Report Large Fundraising Hauls Ahead Of An August Primary Election
VT.summary: Democratic gubernatorial candidate Aly Richards raised $365,867 ahead of Vermont's August 11 primary, while incumbent GOP Gov. Phil Scott raised only $48,000, signaling an unexpectedly competitive race for governor.

WA.title: DOJ threatens WA election officials with prosecution if noncitizens vote
WA.summary: Federal authorities threatened Washington state election officials with criminal prosecution if they fail to prevent noncitizens from voting, with Secretary of State Steve Hobbs criticizing the move as a dangerous escalation of threats against election administrators.

AK.title: Alaska's news organizations are collaborating on voter guides — and you can help, too
AK.summary: Alaska Public Media, Alaska Beacon, KTOO, and the Anchorage Daily News are collaborating on a single voter guide questionnaire sent to 2026 primary candidates, with responses due July 13 ahead of the August 18 primary election.

AL.title: Judge dismisses lawsuit challenging Tuberville's eligibility to run for Alabama governor
AL.summary: A Montgomery County Circuit Judge dismissed a lawsuit questioning whether U.S. Senator Tommy Tuberville meets Alabama's seven-year residency requirement to serve as governor, ruling she lacked jurisdiction to decide candidate eligibility before the general election; the attorney plans to appeal, arguing Tuberville's primary residence is a Florida beach home rather than his claimed Auburn address.

AR.title: Six citizenship voting measures on the ballot in 2026 continue historical trend
AR.summary: Ballotpedia examines the six states with citizenship voting requirements on their 2026 ballots, including Arkansas, noting these measures continue a historical trend and have historically passed by large margins as states codify citizen-only voting requirements in their constitutions.

AZ.title: 8 key races to watch in Arizona's 2026 primary election
AZ.summary: AZFamily identifies eight contested races in Arizona's July 21 primary, including crowded Republican nominations for governor, secretary of state, and attorney general, plus open congressional and legislative district contests.

CA.title: Shasta County completes certification of June election results
CA.summary: Shasta County completed certification of its June 2, 2026 primary election results by the state-mandated July 2 deadline; final tallies are forwarded to the California Secretary of State for statewide certification by July 10, with the Board of Supervisors set to formally declare local results at its July 14 meeting.

CO.title: Victor Marx wins GOP nod for governor, will face Democrat Phil Weiser in November
CO.summary: Ministry founder and former Marine Victor Marx won the Colorado Republican gubernatorial primary over state Sen. Barbara Kirkmeyer by 2,516 votes, with the AP calling the race July 9; he will face Democratic Attorney General Phil Weiser in November.

CT.title: SEEC approves $3.75M campaign grant for Josh Elliott
CT.summary: Connecticut's State Elections Enforcement Commission approved a $3.75 million public financing grant for Democratic gubernatorial challenger Josh Elliott, giving him resources for TV advertising ahead of the August 11 primary against incumbent Gov. Ned Lamont.

DC.title: DOJ warns state officials of prosecution risk over noncitizen voting
DC.summary: The Department of Justice sent letters to all 50 states and Washington, D.C. warning that election officials who knowingly allow noncitizens to remain on voter registration lists could face criminal prosecution under federal law, giving recipients five days to submit compliance plans; critics noted documented cases of noncitizen voting remain extremely rare.

FL.title: July 20 is the deadline to register for the primary election
FL.summary: Florida voters must register by July 20 for the August 18 primary election, with vote-by-mail requests due by August 6 and early voting running August 8–15; the article also highlights NAACP voter registration efforts and addresses misinformation about citizenship requirements at polling locations.

HI.title: Hawaii lawmakers want a 'Plan B' if USPS won't deliver ballots
HI.summary: Hawaii lawmakers pressed the state Office of Elections for a contingency plan in case the U.S. Postal Service follows through on its threat to halt ballot delivery in states that refuse to hand over voter registration lists, but Chief Elections Officer Scott Nago said no backup plan exists.

IA.title: West Des Moines ends use of runoff elections, citing cost, low turnout
IA.summary: The West Des Moines City Council unanimously voted to eliminate runoff elections in favor of a winner-take-all system, citing approximately $35,000-per-election costs and significantly lower turnout in runoff contests compared to initial elections.

KS.title: Kansas City election guide 2026: What Kansas and Missouri voters need to know about their ballots
KS.summary: A comprehensive guide to the August 4 primary covers Kansas races including an open U.S. Senate seat, an open governor race with Gov. Laura Kelly term-limited, and a constitutional amendment asking voters whether to elect state Supreme Court judges.

KY.title: What happens if Mitch McConnell leaves office? Kentucky's Senate vacancy law explained
KY.summary: Kentucky's HB622 eliminated the governor's power to appoint interim U.S. senators, replacing it with a mandatory special election process; the article explains filing windows, sheriff notice requirements, and timing complications as the law faces its first real-world test.

MD.title: Maryland may finally see redistricting action — just not the way Wes Moore wanted
MD.summary: Senate President Bill Ferguson reversed his earlier opposition and will support an August 3–5 special session to consider a constitutional amendment enabling future congressional redistricting, citing the Supreme Court weakening of the federal Voting Rights Act; if voters approve the amendment in November, lawmakers could redraw district boundaries ahead of 2028.

MN.title: Feds leave Minnesota to fend for itself on election security
MN.summary: Minnesota Secretary of State Steve Simon says the Trump administration has cut off intelligence briefings and other federal election security support, leaving the state to defend against threats on its own even as the DOJ sues Minnesota over access to unredacted voter rolls.

MT.title: Judge blocks new Montana GOP bylaws
MT.summary: A Lewis and Clark County district court judge issued a temporary restraining order blocking new Montana Republican Party bylaws that require members to pay dues and sign a loyalty oath — and subject members to removal for 'collaborating with Democrats' — finding plaintiffs showed a likely violation of state election law and constitutional protections.

NE.title: Signatures submitted for four 2026 ballot measures that would limit legislative changes to the initiative process in Arkansas, Missouri, Montana, and Nebraska
NE.summary: Nebraska's 'Respect Nebraska Voters' campaign submitted over 186,000 signatures for a constitutional amendment requiring a four-fifths legislative vote to change or repeal voter-approved ballot initiatives, responding to recent legislative rollbacks of citizen-passed measures on medical marijuana, minimum wage, and paid sick leave.

NJ.title: How New Jersey fills ballot vacancies
NJ.summary: With the November general election approaching, this article explains New Jersey's election procedures for filling ballot vacancies across different races — U.S. Senate, congressional, state legislative, and municipal — detailing how party committees, petition processes, and judicial discretion each play a role.

OH.title: Lawmaker files complaint alleging Ramaswamy improperly reported funds
OH.summary: Ohio Senate Democrats filed a campaign finance complaint with the Secretary of State alleging Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy violated election disclosure law by reporting over $509,000 in credit card spending as monthly lump sums rather than itemizing individual expenditures as required by state campaign finance law.

OR.title: Poll: Oregon governor's race a dead heat between Drazan, Kotek
OR.summary: A new DHM Research poll of 600 likely Oregon voters shows the November 2026 governor race statistically tied, with Republican Christine Drazan at 32% and Democratic incumbent Gov. Tina Kotek at 31%, indicating a highly competitive race heading into the general election.

VA.title: Map Shows States Where Trump Admin is Deploying Election Monitors
VA.summary: The DOJ announced deployment of federal election monitors to 15 jurisdictions in six states for the 2026 primary season, specifically naming Fairfax County and Prince William County in Virginia ahead of the state August 4 primary election.

WI.title: Green Bay city clerk on leave after state calls for investigation into duplicate ballots
WI.summary: The Wisconsin Elections Commission unanimously voted to investigate the Green Bay city clerk office after it twice erroneously mailed duplicate absentee ballots to hundreds of voters in back-to-back elections; City Clerk Celestine Jeffreys was placed on administrative leave and must submit corrective plans by July 31 and August 14.

AK.title: Who votes in Alaska's midterm primaries, and who are the candidates trying to win?
AK.summary: Alaska is in one of its most competitive election cycles in years with 17 gubernatorial candidates and a tight Senate race between incumbent Dan Sullivan and Democrat Mary Peltola. The August 18 top-four open primary advances candidates to a ranked-choice general election; voter registration deadline is July 19 and early voting begins August 3.

CO.title: Victor Marx faces big challenge uniting GOP after winning Colorado's Republican primary for governor
CO.summary: Victor Marx won the Republican gubernatorial primary over state Sen. Barb Kirkmeyer by about 2,500 votes but faces significant party divisions — his primary opponents called him 'unfit' and a 'con man' — and scrutiny over unverified life story claims, as he prepares to face Democrat Phil Weiser in a state that hasn't elected a Republican governor in over two decades.

CT.title: Fazio promises CT voters property tax relief
CT.summary: Republican gubernatorial candidate Ryan Fazio outlined his platform at a Regional Plan Association forum, pledging property tax caps with mandate relief for municipalities, stricter utility regulation, and raising EV registration fees to replenish the Special Transportation Fund, ahead of Connecticut's August 11 primary election.

DC.title: Donald Trump ousts election commission members in latest push to reshape US voting process
DC.summary: President Trump fired the two Democratic members of the bipartisan Election Assistance Commission and accepted the Republican member's resignation, leaving the federal agency that certifies voting systems and distributes election grants unable to function months before the 2026 midterm elections. The EAC had previously declined Trump's request to modify voter registration forms to require proof of citizenship.

GA.title: Advance voting under way in Gwinnett County for US Congressional District 13
GA.summary: Advance in-person voting for Georgia's 13th Congressional District July 28 special election is underway in Gwinnett County, with polling hours Monday–Friday 7 a.m.–7 p.m. and Saturdays 9 a.m.–5 p.m. through July 24. The race fills the seat of the late Rep. David Scott and features five qualified candidates.

IA.title: Sand takes town hall tour to GOP stronghold
IA.summary: Iowa Democratic gubernatorial nominee Rob Sand held a town hall in Sioux Center—a county where Republicans comprise 72% of voters—on July 9, campaigning across four northwest Iowa communities on a tour aimed at rebalancing state politics after a decade of Republican control.

KS.title: ACLU alleges new Kansas election statute violates federal voting rights laws
KS.summary: The ACLU of Kansas and League of Women Voters filed a pre-lawsuit notice against Secretary of State Scott Schwab, alleging that House Bill 2437—the SAVE Kansas Act that took effect July 1—conflicts with the National Voter Registration Act by restricting online voter registration and risking improper deletion of naturalized citizens from voter rolls.

MA.title: Markey, Moulton face off in Chicopee for Mass. Senate primary debate
MA.summary: Incumbent Senator Ed Markey and challenger Rep. Seth Moulton held their first Democratic primary debate in Chicopee, Massachusetts, sparring over age, private equity investments, and approaches to opposing Trump ahead of the September 1 primary.

ME.title: Here's who's vying to replace Graham Platner as Maine Democratic Senate nominee
ME.summary: Following Democratic Senate candidate Graham Platner's suspension of his campaign after a sexual assault allegation, nine Democratic candidates are competing to replace him on the ballot; the Maine Democratic Party must select a replacement by July 27 through a convention process.

MI.title: Cox, Johnson go after gubernatorial frontrunner James in second Republican debate
MI.summary: In Michigan's second Republican gubernatorial debate, candidates Mike Cox and Perry Johnson focused their attacks on Trump-endorsed frontrunner John James, questioning his business practices ahead of the August 4 primary election.

MI.title: US Justice Department threatens Michigan election officials with prosecution if noncitizens vote
MI.summary: The DOJ sent letters to all 50 states threatening criminal prosecution of election officials if noncitizens vote; Michigan's Deputy Secretary of State rejected the warnings as overreach, stating the state already has robust procedures ensuring only eligible citizens can vote.

NH.title: Kelly Ayotte's lead over Warmington shrinks to 5 points as her numbers slide
NH.summary: A University of New Hampshire poll shows Republican Gov. Kelly Ayotte's lead over Democratic challenger Cinde Warmington has narrowed to just 5 percentage points (44% vs. 39%), down from an 8-point advantage in April. Ayotte's support declined 3 points since the spring while Warmington's held steady, and Ayotte's favorability rating has turned negative at minus 4.

NM.title: Democrats' four-day vote to pick Lt. Governor nominee opens July 25
NM.summary: New Mexico Democrats will conduct a four-day voting period from July 25–29 in which approximately 300 State Central Committee members will select a Lieutenant Governor nominee, with results sent to the Secretary of State by July 30 to finalize the November ballot. The process was triggered after Lt. Governor nominee Maggie Toulouse Oliver withdrew June 18 citing health concerns.

NY.title: National Dems embrace Conley's challenge to GOP Rep. Lawler
NY.summary: The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee added Cait Conley, the Democratic nominee in New York's 17th congressional district, to its 'Red to Blue' program, making her the first New York Democratic challenger this cycle to receive the extra organizational and fundraising support from the national party.

OK.title: Drummond, Mazzei Look to Court Primary Voters Ahead of Runoff Election
OK.summary: Oklahoma Attorney General Gentner Drummond and former state Senator Mike Mazzei are both actively campaigning to win over the roughly 44-50% of Republican primary voters who supported other candidates as they head toward the August 25 Republican gubernatorial runoff election.

PA.title: Buchtan sues Washington County officials after losing state Senate challenge to Bartolotta
PA.summary: Greene County businessman Al Buchtan filed a federal lawsuit alleging Washington County Board of Elections officials collaborated with the Senate Republican Campaign Committee to spread false voter fraud claims against him during the 2026 Pennsylvania state Senate primary race.

RI.title: Independents running for R.I. governor in 'do-or-die' race to collect signatures
RI.summary: Nine independent candidates are racing to collect 1,000 signatures by July 10 to qualify for Rhode Island's 2026 gubernatorial ballot, facing significant challenges without the organizational support that major party nominees receive.

SD.title: Erickson picks up two more votes in first day of Sioux Falls mayor's race recount
SD.summary: The Sioux Falls mayoral runoff recount ended its first day with Christine Erickson extending her two-vote lead over Jamie Smith to four votes, though about 31,000 ballots remained uncounted. The recount board spent eight hours debating procedural disputes over signature verification and mail-in ballot eligibility, with litigation expected after the count concludes.

VT.title: Vermont primary election 2026: Look up who's on your ballot
VT.summary: Vermont Public launched an interactive ballot lookup tool for the August 11, 2026 statewide primary, helping voters find candidates for statewide, legislative, and county-wide races. Voters must proactively request absentee ballots through the Vermont Voter Portal, as primary ballots are not mailed automatically.

WV.title: West Virginia gets DOJ letter saying state officials could face criminal charges if noncitizens vote
WV.summary: The DOJ Civil Rights Division sent West Virginia a letter warning that officials who knowingly retain noncitizens on voter rolls or allow ineligible voters to cast ballots could face criminal prosecution, demanding an explanation within five days of how the state would comply with federal voter eligibility requirements.

WV.title: West Virginia response to DOJ letter describing prosecuting officials if noncitizens vote: no need
WV.summary: West Virginia's Secretary of State pushed back on the DOJ warning letter, stating the state is unaware of any noncitizens on its voter rolls and has adequate safeguards in place including citizenship oaths and cooperation programs with federal agencies. The state asked the DOJ to provide any specific evidence of problematic registrations.

WY.title: Casper forum separates US Senate candidates on healthcare, executive power
WY.summary: Republican and Democratic U.S. Senate candidates clashed at a Casper College forum co-sponsored by the League of Women Voters, with Republicans disagreeing on whether a federal rural health program will address Wyoming's cost and access problems, and candidates also differing on executive authority and public lands policy.

WY.title: Who is Curt Blake? The fourth Republican running to be Wyoming governor.
WY.summary: WyoFile profiles Curt Blake, a fifth-generation Wyomingite and rodeo-production professional who filed for the August 18 Republican gubernatorial primary, running a deliberately low-profile campaign without accepting donations, endorsements, or debate invitations, and relying instead on word-of-mouth outreach.

AK.title: To the GOP, he's a sham candidate. At home, he's Mr. Sullivan, ex-teacher and U.S. Senate hopeful
AK.summary: Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., a retired elementary school teacher from Petersburg, is running as an unaffiliated U.S. Senate candidate in Alaska sharing the incumbent Republican senator's name. The Alaska Supreme Court ruled he could remain on the ballot after GOP officials unsuccessfully sought to block his candidacy, alleging the candidacy was designed to confuse voters.

AR.title: Issue Spotlight: What candidates running for Arkansas secretary of state say about paper ballots
AR.summary: The three candidates running for Arkansas secretary of state — Democrat Kelly Grappe, Republican Kim Hammer, and Libertarian Michael Pakko — shared their positions on paper ballots versus electronic voting at the Arkansas Press Association convention, with Grappe noting counties have discretion under current state law.

AZ.title: Battle over county elections in Arizona echoes 2020 showdown
AZ.summary: A dispute between Maricopa County's Republican-led Board of Supervisors and a Trump-aligned county recorder over control of elections is playing out as early voting begins for the July 21 primary, with supervisors accusing the recorder of sowing chaos and undermining voter confidence ahead of the midterms.

AZ.title: Fearing troops or ICE at the polls, Arizona organizers train hundreds as election observers
AZ.summary: Community organizations LUCHA and the Arizona Center for Empowerment trained over 250 people in Phoenix and Tucson as election observers ahead of the July 21 primary, focusing on responses if federal agents or National Guard troops appear at polling locations.

AZ.title: Pima County officials reassure voters ahead of primary, address election security concerns
AZ.summary: Pima County officials held a press conference pledging 'free, fair and safe' elections for the July 21 primary, addressing voter intimidation concerns and a DOJ letter about noncitizen voters, while noting new proof-of-citizenship requirements for voter registration.

CA.title: California earmarks $40 million to speed up vote counting in November — but county elections officials want to temper expectations
CA.summary: California has allocated $40 million to accelerate election result reporting ahead of the November general election, though county officials caution that the faster-counting goal faces real logistical challenges.

CA.title: California Secretary of State Certifies Results of the June 2, 2026, Primary Election
CA.summary: Secretary of State Shirley N. Weber certified the June 2 primary election results, reporting 9,446,461 votes cast at a 40.80% turnout rate among registered voters, with nearly 8.4 million ballots cast by mail.

CT.title: Jillian Gilchrest tries to break through in primary, one door at a time
CT.summary: State Rep. Jillian Gilchrest is running a grassroots door-knocking campaign in Connecticut's competitive four-way Democratic primary for the CT-1 congressional seat ahead of the August 11 primary — the first seriously contested race for that seat in nearly three decades, featuring incumbent Rep. John Larson and two other challengers.

DC.title: The 'SAVE America Act' has brought Congress to a halt. Local election officials say it's an unworkable bill
DC.summary: President Trump has stalled other major legislation to pressure GOP senators into passing the federal SAVE America Act, which would require proof of citizenship to register and photo ID to vote; local election administrators across multiple states, mostly Republicans, say the bill is unnecessary, unworkable, and would impose enormous unfunded mandates on counties ahead of November elections.

DC.title: Judge throws out Justice Department New York voter registration data demand
DC.summary: A federal judge dismissed the DOJ's lawsuit seeking New York's unredacted statewide voter registration list, ruling that neither the Civil Rights Act, NVRA, nor HAVA authorized the demand — marking the administration's 12th consecutive lower-court loss in its effort to force states to hand over voter rolls to the federal government.

FL.title: Vote-by-mail ballots for 2026 Primary Election have been mailed
FL.summary: Alachua County has mailed over 19,000 vote-by-mail ballots ahead of Florida's August 18 primary; voters who requested a ballot should receive it within the week in a pink envelope, and must return it to the Supervisor of Elections by 7 p.m. on Election Day.

GA.title: Georgia audit finds hand-marked ballot errors; machine-marked ballots show 100% accuracy
GA.summary: Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger released an audit of 1.1 million ballots from Georgia's June runoff finding all 23 discrepancies came from hand-marked paper ballots, while 1,079,408 touchscreen-device ballots showed zero errors — a data point Raffensperger is using to argue against replacing Georgia's voting machines as Trump allies push for hand-marked paper ballots.

GA.title: New Georgia Audit Reveals Every Ballot Error Came from Hand-Marked Ballots
GA.summary: Georgia's post-election ballot image audit of the June runoff confirmed a 99.9979% overall accuracy rate, with all errors traceable exclusively to hand-marked ballots, intensifying the debate over the state's planned transition away from touchscreen ballot-marking devices ahead of the November election.

HI.title: New campaign spending reports show fundraising gaps across key Hawaii races
HI.summary: Hawaii's latest campaign finance disclosures show Governor Josh Green holding a commanding fundraising lead over his Republican challenger, Kauai Mayor Derek Kawakami significantly outpacing Rep. Della Au Belatti in the lieutenant governor race, and challenger Yuki Lei Sugimura edging ahead of incumbent Maui Mayor Richard Bissen — all ahead of the August 8 primary.

HI.title: Spending reports in Maui County mayor's race show Sugimura leading Bissen in fundraising
HI.summary: Campaign finance reports through June 30 show Maui Council Vice Chair Yuki Lei Sugimura has raised $335,423 with a 1.6-to-1 cash advantage over incumbent Mayor Richard Bissen ($69,654 on hand), with analysts noting her momentum mirrors Bissen's own 2022 upset as the August 8 primary approaches.

IA.title: Buttigieg calls to abolish Electoral College; Iowa Democrats optimistic for midterms
IA.summary: Former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg headlined the Iowa Democratic Party's 'Liberty and Justice' fundraiser in Altoona, with Iowa Democratic leaders expressing strong optimism about 2026 general election prospects and describing their Senate and gubernatorial nominees as the 'strongest in a generation.'

IA.title: Judge Sets July 21 Evidentiary Hearing in Gluba-Cutler Ballot Access Challenge
IA.summary: A Polk County District Court judge scheduled a full-day evidentiary hearing for July 21 in the lawsuit brought by Libertarian gubernatorial candidates Nicholas Gluba and Jules Cutler, who were removed from Iowa's November general election ballot by the State Objection Panel, with a final ruling expected by July 29.

ID.title: In deep red Idaho, support for ballot question on abortion access is spread across party lines
ID.summary: A Boise State University poll shows nearly 61% of Idaho residents support the Reproductive Freedom and Privacy Act ballot initiative, with 28% of petition signers being registered Republicans, as the measure undergoes final certification by the Idaho Secretary of State's office for the November ballot.

ID.title: Medical marijuana ballot initiative hits setback after signatures turned in late
ID.summary: An Idaho judge ruled that nearly 900 signatures from Minidoka County for the medical marijuana ballot initiative cannot be counted because they were submitted after the 5 p.m. filing deadline, potentially jeopardizing the Natural Medicine Alliance of Idaho's efforts to qualify the measure for November 2026.

IL.title: Illinois 'reviewing' DOJ's threat to prosecute state election officials over noncitizen voting
IL.summary: The Illinois State Board of Elections said it is reviewing a DOJ letter threatening criminal prosecution of officials who retain noncitizens on voter rolls, while the state also faces a separate ongoing DOJ federal lawsuit demanding access to Illinois's complete unredacted voter registration database that courts have so far blocked.

KS.title: Kansas U.S. Senate candidate Sandy Spidel Neumann
KS.summary: Democratic Senate primary candidate Sandy Spidel Neumann, a retired financial services executive, discussed her campaign on KCUR's Kansas City Today ahead of the August 4 primary, in which she faces 10 other Democrats competing for the nomination to challenge Republican incumbent Sen. Roger Marshall.

LA.title: Monroe Senator Stewart Cathey announces bid for Louisiana's 5th Congressional District seat
LA.summary: State Senator Stewart Cathey entered the race for Louisiana's open 5th Congressional District seat being vacated by Rep. Julia Letlow, who is running for Senate. The race features a crowded field including state Reps. Michael Echols and Gabe Firment and Board of Regents Chair Misti Cordell, with qualifying set for August 5-7 and an open primary on November 3.

LA.title: Potential candidates discuss 5th Congressional District run
LA.summary: Six candidates — including Republicans Michael Echols, Misti Cordell, Austin McGee, Gabe Firment, and Stewart Cathey, plus Democrat Dan McKay — discussed their bids for Louisiana's open 5th Congressional District seat. The race will be decided through a jungle primary on November 3 following the late redrawing of the congressional map.

MA.title: Vote by Mail Applications to Begin Arriving in Mailboxes This Week
MA.summary: The Massachusetts Secretary of State announced that all registered voters who have not already applied to vote by mail will receive a pre-addressed, postage pre-paid 2026 Vote by Mail application. Applications for the September 1 State Primary ballot must reach local election offices by 5 p.m. on August 25.

ME.title: Democrats Prepare for Senate Nominee Convention
ME.summary: Maine's Democratic Party announced a July 25 nominating convention at the Cross Insurance Center in Bangor to select a replacement for Graham Platner, who withdrew from the Senate race after sexual assault allegations. Six candidates are vying — including Nirav Shah, Troy Jackson, and Shenna Bellows — with 601 delegates voting until a majority is reached; the winner will face Sen. Susan Collins in November.

ME.title: The rat race to replace Platner: How have candidates campaigned?
ME.summary: An examination of how the field of Democratic candidates seeking to replace Graham Platner as Maine's Senate nominee has campaigned since his withdrawal, covering the approaches taken by frontrunners Nirav Shah, Troy Jackson, and Shenna Bellows ahead of the July 25 convention.

ME.title: Maine Dems announce details for U.S. Senate nominating convention. Here's who's running
ME.summary: The Maine Democratic Party confirmed July 25 as the date for its 601-delegate nominating convention in Bangor to choose a Senate nominee. Eight Democrats are competing for the slot — including former CDC director Nirav Shah, ex-Senate president Troy Jackson, Secretary of State Shenna Bellows, and others — with the deadline to declare candidacy set for July 15.

MI.title: Michigan could approve a constitutional convention this year. What would that mean?
MI.summary: Michigan voters will decide on Proposal 1 in November, which would convene a constitutional convention and potentially rewrite the state's 1963 constitution. A 'yes' vote would trigger elections for delegates within six months, with the convention beginning October 2027, putting all existing constitutional protections — including reproductive rights and redistricting reforms — up for revision; the measure has failed every time it has appeared, most recently 67%-33% in 2010.

MN.title: With less than a month before Minnesota primary, DFL race for U.S. Senate nomination remains close
MN.summary: With the August 11 primary approaching, the DFL Senate primary between Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan and Rep. Angie Craig remains highly competitive, with polls split on who leads. Craig faces scrutiny over her votes for the Laken Riley Act and the GENIUS Act on cryptocurrency, while Flanagan holds the party endorsement; turnout is expected to be the decisive factor in this historically lightly attended August primary.

MO.title: Early Voting Underway As Missouri Voters Prepare To Decide Four Constitutional Amendments
MO.summary: Early voting has begun in Missouri ahead of the August 4 primary. Secretary of State Denny Hoskins explained that voters may choose a party ballot or a nonpartisan ballot focused solely on constitutional amendments covering state parks tax renewal, Jackson County assessor elections, initiative petition process changes, and income tax phase-out.

MS.title: Mississippi residents in DeSoto County file lawsuit over majority-Black judicial subdistrict
MS.summary: Former Republican gubernatorial candidate Robert Foster and other DeSoto County residents filed a federal lawsuit challenging the Legislature's creation of majority-Black judicial subdistricts as unconstitutional under the Voting Rights Act, with a hearing scheduled for July 22.

MS.title: Federal judge rejects challenge to DeSoto County election maps, citing new voting rights standard
MS.summary: U.S. District Judge Glen Davidson upheld DeSoto County's existing election maps, applying the Supreme Court's Louisiana v. Callais standard requiring proof of intentional discrimination. Legal experts warn the ruling may serve as a template for other Southern jurisdictions and will make future Voting Rights Act challenges substantially more difficult.

MT.title: District court judge blocks new state GOP bylaws
MT.summary: A Lewis and Clark County district judge issued a temporary restraining order blocking Montana's Republican Party from implementing new bylaws requiring membership dues and a loyalty oath, finding plaintiffs likely to succeed in showing the bylaws conflict with Montana election law and constitutional protections governing candidacy and elected precinct committee representatives.

NC.title: NC elections board chairman accuses Stein of misrepresenting board's role in early voting plans
NC.summary: State Elections Board chair Francis X. DeLuca disputed Governor Josh Stein's claims that the board was directing counties to eliminate Sunday voting and remove early voting from college campuses, saying county boards independently develop their own early voting plans. The dispute reflects broader tensions over early voting access following Republican gains in election oversight under Auditor David Boliek.

ND.title: Fargo Democrats back independent House candidate after incumbent's death
ND.summary: Fargo Democrats endorsed Cara Cody-Braun as an independent candidate for the North Dakota House seat left vacant by Rep. Liz Conmy's death in an April plane crash. Cody-Braun will campaign alongside Democratic-NPL candidates in District 11, while Republican write-in Doug Sharbono also qualified for the general election ballot.

NE.title: Nebraska Democratic US Senate candidate Cindy Burbank hasn't dropped out of the race yet. Will she?
NE.summary: Two months after winning the Democratic Senate primary, Cindy Burbank has not filed withdrawal paperwork despite earlier signals she would step aside for independent Dan Osborn's challenge to Republican Sen. Pete Ricketts. The August 3 deadline to remove her name from the November ballot is approaching with no action from her campaign.

NH.title: Trump's DOJ sending election monitors to Manchester, Nashua for primaries
NH.summary: The Trump administration announced it would deploy federal election monitors to Manchester and Nashua for New Hampshire's September 8 primary; NH Secretary of State David Scanlan said all are welcome to observe elections, while the announcement follows a dismissed DOJ lawsuit demanding the state's unredacted voter registration data.

NH.title: Election monitors are returning to New England amid DOJ voter roll battle
NH.summary: The DOJ announced election monitors will deploy to Manchester, NH for the September 8 primary as part of a six-state deployment, weeks after a federal judge dismissed the DOJ's lawsuit seeking New Hampshire's unredacted voter data, which the department has since appealed.

NH.title: Trump's Justice Department to send election monitors to Mass., New Hampshire
NH.summary: The DOJ's Civil Rights Division will deploy monitors to Manchester and Nashua for New Hampshire's September 8 primary; critics including the ACLU say the move is politically motivated and unsupported by evidence of widespread voter fraud.

NJ.title: GOP suit claims NJ overseas voting law is unconstitutional
NJ.summary: The RNC and NJGOP filed suit in Mercer County challenging New Jersey's 2022 law allowing US citizen children born abroad to NJ residents to vote in state federal elections, arguing the statute violates the state constitution's residency requirement.

NJ.title: Trump voting losses in court shield New Jersey elections — for now
NJ.summary: Multiple federal court defeats for the Trump administration have protected New Jersey's election procedures, including extended mail-ballot deadlines and voter data privacy rules, though election officials warn the legal landscape could still shift.

NV.title: 'It's threats, it's intimidation': Nevada secretary of state slams Trump DOJ letters targeting election officials over noncitizen voting
NV.summary: Nevada Secretary of State Francisco Aguilar publicly condemned the DOJ's letters threatening criminal prosecution of election officials over noncitizen voting, calling them intimidation targeting Latino voters and noting Nevada already has robust citizenship verification safeguards in place.

OH.title: Ohio election officials meet in Wapakoneta to prep for November 2026
OH.summary: The Ohio Association of Election Officials held its northwest regional meeting in Wapakoneta, where officials from approximately 20 counties received crisis communications training and reviewed ballot procedures in preparation for the November 2026 general election.

OK.title: What to Know About State Question 846, the Voter Identification Measure
OK.summary: State Question 846, appearing on Oklahoma's August 25 runoff ballot alongside the governor race, would enshrine the state's existing voter ID requirement in the constitution, meaning future changes would require voter approval rather than a simple legislative vote. Supporters argue it protects election security, while critics contend it gives the Legislature broad authority to define acceptable identification and could enable more restrictive requirements.

OR.title: Early signs suggest Oregon governor's race is competitive
OR.summary: Political analysts have softened their optimism about incumbent Democratic Gov. Tina Kotek's reelection prospects as early polling shows the November general election race becoming more competitive than expected. A new survey from Public Opinion Strategies shows Republican Christine Drazan leading Kotek 48% to 44%, though analysts still give Kotek the edge heading into the fall.

OR.title: Decision 2026: Survey gives Drazan a slight lead over Kotek in Oregon governor's race
OR.summary: A telephone survey of 600 Oregon voters by Public Opinion Strategies gave Republican Christine Drazan a 4-point advantage over Democratic Gov. Tina Kotek (48% to 44%), with 57% of respondents disapproving of Kotek's job performance. Drazan leads outside the Portland metro area while Kotek's campaign argues she remains well-positioned given the state's track record.

RI.title: Feds threaten Rhode Island's top election official with criminal charges if noncitizens vote
RI.summary: Rhode Island Secretary of State Gregg Amore says the Trump administration has threatened him with criminal charges if election officials fail to prevent noncitizens from voting in the 2026 midterms, after his office received a July 7 letter from Assistant U.S. Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon demanding details on voter roll maintenance. The standoff puts Rhode Island at the center of a national conflict over voter list management heading into the fall election cycle.

RI.title: Signature collection deadline trims governor's race down to five candidates, initial data shows
RI.summary: Rhode Island's July 10 nomination-paper deadline has narrowed the gubernatorial field to five candidates after only those collecting the required 1,000 valid signatures by 4 p.m. qualified for the September 9 primary ballot. The development clears the field ahead of what is shaping up to be a competitive Democratic primary between former CVS executive Helena Foulkes, who leads polls by 34 points, and incumbent Gov. Dan McKee.

SC.title: Republicans scramble to find a replacement for Sen. Lindsey Graham ahead of the midterm elections
SC.summary: Following the sudden death of Republican Sen. Lindsey Graham on July 11, 2026, South Carolina Republicans are racing to identify candidates for both a temporary appointment by Gov. Henry McMaster and a permanent ballot slot through a special primary scheduled for August 11. Potential contenders include Reps. Nancy Mace and Joe Wilson, Lt. Gov. Pamela Evette, and others, while President Trump said he has a preferred successor but declined to name the person.

SC.title: 2026 Senate Special: Election Dates and Ground Rules
SC.summary: South Carolina will hold a Republican special primary on August 11, 2026, to replace Lindsey Graham on the November ballot, with candidate filing opening July 21 and closing July 28; a potential runoff would follow on August 25. A dispute has emerged between election officials and the state GOP over whether voters who participated in the Democratic primary may vote in this special Republican primary.

SC.title: Lindsey Graham leaves behind open Senate seat. What SC leaders are looking to enter the race
SC.summary: Multiple South Carolina political figures are weighing bids for Lindsey Graham's vacant U.S. Senate seat following his July 11 death, with Congressman Ralph Norman reported to be on the verge of announcing a run. Former Gov. Nikki Haley has signaled through a spokesperson that she is not interested in the race.

SD.title: South Dakota Voters Switch Parties Ahead of July 28 Republican Governor Runoff
SD.summary: Some South Dakota voters are temporarily changing their party registration to Republican to participate in the historic July 28 gubernatorial runoff between incumbent Gov. Larry Rhoden and businessman Toby Doeden, with Republican rolls growing by 5,717 in the 37 days after the June 2 primary. The practice has sparked debate, with the state GOP chair opposing it while open-primary advocates argue it reflects the closed primary system's failures.

TN.title: Early voting for Aug. 6 election begins July 17
TN.summary: Tennessee Secretary of State Tre Hargett announced early voting for the State Primary and County General Election runs July 17 through August 1, with photo ID required at the polls.

TN.title: Early voting begins Monday for Tennessee primary
TN.summary: Tennessee's August 6 primary features competitive races across multiple congressional districts reshaped by redistricting, notably the three-way split of Shelby County's former 9th Congressional District.

TX.title: Paxton, Talarico or neither? Cornyn voters weigh in on November
TX.summary: The Tribune interviewed nine GOP primary voters who backed Cornyn to understand how they are approaching the general election matchup between Republican nominee Ken Paxton and Democratic nominee James Talarico.

WA.title: Primary ballots arriving this weekend
WA.summary: Pacific County's Auditor's Office is distributing approximately 18,000 ballots for the August 4 primary, with five drop-box locations across the peninsula and an 18-day voting window opening July 17.

WI.title: Milwaukee polling location changes ahead of the August partisan primary
WI.summary: Several Milwaukee polling places have changed locations ahead of the August 11 partisan primary, affecting approximately 2,700 voters in four wards across two aldermanic districts; voters will be notified by mail and through signage.

WY.title: Who is Curt Blake? The fourth Republican running to be Wyoming governor.
WY.summary: Profile of Curt Blake, a fifth-generation Wyomingite and rodeo-production professional who is the fourth Republican in Wyoming's gubernatorial primary, with moderate stances including support for abortion access and opposition to selling public lands.

AK.title: To the GOP, he's a sham candidate. At home, he's Mr. Sullivan, ex-teacher and Alaska Senate hopeful
AK.summary: AP profile of Daniel J. Sullivan, the same-name Senate candidate whom Republicans call a 'sham' meant to confuse voters and help Democrat Mary Peltola; he remains on the primary ballot after prevailing in court, ahead of the August primary.

AZ.title: Where to vote early in person or drop off your mail-in ballot in Maricopa County
AZ.summary: Straight-news guide detailing early voting locations and mail-ballot drop-off options in Maricopa County ahead of Arizona's July 21 primary election.

CT.title: Elliott gets public grant; Lamont gets $3.5M from a guy named Ned
CT.summary: Reports that Gov. Ned Lamont has spent over $3 million (much of it self-funded) in his primary campaign, while challenger Josh Elliott qualified for $3.75 million in public financing ahead of the August 11 Democratic primary.

FL.title: Duval voters must register by July 20 for Aug. 18 primary and special election
FL.summary: Straight-news report that Duval County voters must register or change party affiliation by July 20 to be eligible for Florida's closed August 18 primary and a special consolidated government election.

ID.title: Initiative to end Idaho's strict abortion ban qualifies for November's general election ballot
ID.summary: Idaho's Secretary of State confirmed the Reproductive Freedom & Privacy Act initiative, backed by over 110,000 signatures (well above the 70,725 required), has officially qualified for the November 3, 2026 general election ballot.

KY.title: Kentucky sees jump in voter registration with over 11K new registrations in June
KY.summary: Kentucky Secretary of State Michael Adams reported the state's largest monthly voter-registration increase since 2024, with 11,440 new registrations in June and net growth of 6,770 voters after removals.

MA.title: Mass. judge allows a Republican accused of signature fraud to return to the ballot, blocks another
MA.summary: The Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court reinstated Republican attorney general candidate Michael Walsh to the September primary ballot despite fraud accusations over his nomination signatures, while a parallel case involving a lieutenant governor candidate remains unresolved.

MI.title: Haley Stevens gets nod from the retiring Gary Peters, the senator whom she seeks to replace
MI.summary: Retiring Sen. Gary Peters endorsed Rep. Haley Stevens in Michigan's contested Democratic U.S. Senate primary, a reversal of his earlier neutrality stance and a boost from the party establishment ahead of the August 4 primary.

MI.title: Full interviews: Hear from 5 candidates running for Michigan governor
MI.summary: Local news interviewed all five candidates running for Michigan governor ahead of the August 4 primary, covering their positions on education, affordability, and public safety.

MO.title: Amendment 4 puts rural Missouri at center of fight over ballot power
MO.summary: Reports on the debate over Missouri's Amendment 4 ballot measure, which would require citizen-initiated constitutional amendments to win a majority in each of the state's eight congressional districts, not just statewide.

NC.title: State Board Meeting (July 16, 2026)
NC.summary: The NC State Board of Elections announced its July 16 meeting agenda, which includes adopting permanent rules on recounts, voter photo ID requirements, and voting site operations, plus campaign finance penalty waiver requests and county board vacancy matters.

TN.title: Here's when early voting starts in Tennessee in 2026
TN.summary: Early voting for Tennessee's August 6 state/federal primary and county general elections runs July 17 through August 1, with the voter registration deadline having passed July 7 and the absentee-ballot request deadline set for July 27.

WI.title: Rodriguez fires campaign manager over finance reports in Wisconsin governor race
WI.summary: Wisconsin Lt. Gov. and Democratic gubernatorial candidate Sara Rodriguez fired her campaign manager after discovering double-counted contributions and undercounted expenses left her campaign with far less cash than believed, complicating her bid ahead of the August 11 primary.

WV.title: Federal judge dismisses U.S. DOJ lawsuit over unredacted West Virginia voter registration data
WV.summary: A federal judge dismissed the Justice Department's lawsuit seeking West Virginia's unredacted voter registration data, ruling the DOJ's demand lacked the factual basis and statement of purpose required under the Civil Rights Act of 1960.

AZ.title: It's the last day to mail in your Arizona primary ballot
AZ.summary: Arizona Republic reports July 14 is the final day for primary voters to mail back their early ballots in time to be counted for the July 21 primary.

CT.title: Veterans group gives Bronin a boost on airwaves ahead of primary
CT.summary: A PAC backing Democratic veterans is launching a nearly $1 million ad campaign for Luke Bronin ahead of the August 11 primary against incumbent Rep. John Larson in Connecticut's 1st Congressional District.

MT.title: Montana court upholds voter photo ID law
MT.summary: A Montana court upheld the state's voter photo ID law, with Secretary of State Christi Jacobsen calling the ruling a win for election integrity while critics warn it could burden some eligible voters.

SD.title: Deadline to get registered to vote or change party affiliation to be eligible to vote in South Dakota's Republican gubernatorial runoff election is Monday; Absentee voting is underway
SD.summary: South Dakota's registration and party-affiliation deadline for the July 28 Republican gubernatorial runoff was July 13, and absentee voting for the runoff is now underway.

DE.title: Candidate Filing Deadline for Delaware General Election is Tuesday, July 14
DE.summary: Delaware's candidate filing deadline for the September 15 primary election closes at noon on Tuesday, July 14, setting the ballot for races including U.S. Senate (Democratic incumbent Chris Coons), U.S. House (incumbent Sarah McBride), and numerous state legislative seats.

SC.title: Election officials prepare for special SC primary to fill Lindsey Graham's Senate seat
SC.summary: South Carolina election officials began preparations for a compressed special Republican primary election on August 11, with candidate filing opening July 21 and the winner to face Democratic nominee Annie Andrews in the November general election.

SD.title: The Republican gubernatorial primary runoff is two weeks away: What you need to know
SD.summary: With two weeks until South Dakota's historic July 28 GOP gubernatorial runoff, KOTATV outlined the race between incumbent Gov. Larry Rhoden and businessman Toby Doeden — the first runoff for governor in state history — explaining why the runoff was triggered and what voters need to know.

AK.title: To vote in Alaska's primary elections, residents must register by July 19 — here's how
AK.summary: Alaska voters must register by July 19 to take part in the August 18 primary election, where they will choose candidates for governor, the state legislature, and Congress under the state's top-four primary system.

KS.title: ACLU alleges new Kansas election statute violates federal voting rights laws
KS.summary: The ACLU of Kansas and League of Women Voters of Kansas warned of a potential lawsuit alleging that House Bill 2437, the SAVE Kansas Act's voter-roll and registration restrictions, conflicts with the federal National Voter Registration Act.

MO.title: Missouri governor signs elections law restoring some voting rights and limiting automatic donations
MO.summary: Gov. Mike Kehoe signed a bill restoring voting rights to many Missourians on probation or parole, while also barring candidates from collecting automatic recurring campaign donations without explicit donor consent.

NJ.title: New Jersey becomes the 11th state to enact a state-level voting rights act
NJ.summary: Gov. Mikie Sherrill signed the John R. Lewis Voter Empowerment Act, making New Jersey the 11th state with a state-level voting rights act and creating a new Division of Voting Rights to enforce state election laws.

VA.title: Early voting underway for Lynchburg's dual primary election
VA.summary: The City of Lynchburg reminded voters that early, no-excuse in-person voting is available through August 1 ahead of the August 4 dual primary election.

ID.title: Idaho AG's office sends icy reply to DOJ's voter roll letter
ID.summary: Idaho Attorney General Raul Labrador's office fired back at the Justice Department for contacting Secretary of State Phil McGrane directly over noncitizen voter rolls, urging DOJ to drop its lawsuit and accusing it of bypassing the state's counsel.

LA.title: Louisiana enacts 20 election bills during 2026 session, including new congressional maps and voter ID changes
LA.summary: Gov. Jeff Landry signed 20 election-related bills from the 2026 session, including a redrawn congressional map following Louisiana v. Callais and stricter voter ID document requirements taking effect in 2027.

NE.title: DNC won't intervene in RNC lawsuit against Nebraska voting law after state pledges defense
NE.summary: The Democratic National Committee withdrew its bid to intervene in the RNC's lawsuit challenging a Nebraska law allowing some U.S. citizens who have never lived in the state to vote, after state officials pledged to defend the statute themselves.

WI.title: The Wisconsin primaries are less than a month away. Here's what to know before you vote.
WI.summary: Wisconsin Elections Commission Administrator Meagan Wolfe outlined voting procedures ahead of the state's August 11 partisan primary, including absentee deadlines and a new rule barring early voters from changing their ballot after casting it.

AZ.title: Arizona's primary election is around the corner. Here are the most consequential races to watch
AZ.summary: With Arizona's primary election a week away, KJZZ previewed the most competitive statewide races, including a contested Republican gubernatorial primary and heated contests for attorney general and secretary of state.

HI.title: Voters to receive ballot by July 21 for upcoming Hawai'i Primary Elections
HI.summary: Hawaii's Office of Elections said primary election ballots will reach voters by July 21, reminding them to sign return envelopes and noting the Aug. 8 receipt deadline.

MO.title: Missouri and other GOP states ask voters to make it harder to pass constitutional amendments
MO.summary: Missouri's Amendment 4 on the August 2026 ballot would require constitutional amendments to pass in each congressional district rather than just statewide, making future ballot initiatives significantly harder to approve.

NC.title: NHC early voting schedule put forth for midterm elections, state approval still needed
NC.summary: New Hanover County's Board of Elections unanimously adopted an early voting plan for the November 2026 general election, spanning Oct. 15-31 across five sites, pending North Carolina State Board approval.

SC.title: Who can vote in the Republican primary to replace Lindsey Graham? SC officials weigh in
SC.summary: The South Carolina Election Commission clarified that voters who cast ballots in the June Republican primary or didn't vote in June are eligible for the Aug. 11 special GOP primary to fill the late Sen. Lindsey Graham's seat, while June Democratic primary voters are excluded.

TN.title: Tennessee early voting begins July 17
TN.summary: Early voting for Tennessee's Aug. 6 primaries, including the governor's race, runs July 17 through Aug. 1, with registered voters required to present valid photo ID.

MI.title: Poll: Where Michigan Democratic voters stand with U.S. Senate candidates Stevens, El-Sayed
MI.summary: A WDIV/Detroit News poll of likely Democratic primary voters, conducted July 8-11, shows how the field stands in Michigan's open U.S. Senate primary ahead of the August election.

NC.title: Should it be easier to throw out NC voters' ballots? Elections board to consider new rules
NC.summary: North Carolina's State Board of Elections is set to consider Republican-backed rule changes that would make it easier for county officials to reject mail ballots over technicalities and to reject voter ID exemption requests by simple majority vote.

AK.title: Have a felony record in Alaska? You may still be eligible to vote
AK.summary: Alaskans with felony convictions may still regain voting eligibility once unconditionally discharged from Department of Corrections supervision, a distinction that can trip up voters ahead of the state's Aug. 18 primary.

KS.title: Kansas judge temporarily blocks election law repealing 3-day grace period for mail-in ballots
KS.summary: A Douglas County judge issued a temporary injunction blocking a Kansas law that repealed the state's 3-day grace period for mail-in ballots, finding challengers substantially likely to prevail.

ME.title: The frenzied sprint among Maine Democrats hoping to replace Graham Platner
ME.summary: Maine Democrats are racing to pick a new U.S. Senate nominee at a July 25 emergency convention after Graham Platner dropped out, with state law setting a July 27 deadline to submit the replacement's name for the ballot.

MO.title: New Missouri law gives voting rights back to select former prisoners
MO.summary: A new Missouri law taking effect Aug. 28 restores voting rights to thousands of formerly incarcerated residents who are on parole or probation for certain nonviolent offenses.

TN.title: Secretary of State reminds Tennesseans of early voting for August Primary and County General Elections
TN.summary: Tennessee's Secretary of State reminded voters that early voting for the Aug. 6 primary and county general elections begins July 17 and runs through Aug. 1.

HI.title: Hawaii to DOJ on election law compliance help: No thanks
HI.summary: Hawaii's chief election officer declined a Department of Justice offer of assistance with federal voter-eligibility compliance, saying the state already has safeguards in place and has found no widespread noncitizen voting.

HI.title: Hawaii officials defend local election security
HI.summary: State and county election officials outlined the safeguards protecting Hawaii's mail-in voting system against tampering and illegal voting, including felony penalties for false ballot affirmations.

NE.title: Dan Osborn officially in Nebraska's U.S. Senate race
NE.summary: The Nebraska Secretary of State certified independent U.S. Senate candidate Dan Osborn's petition signatures, confirming his place on the November ballot against incumbent Republican Pete Ricketts.

FL.title: Here are the key dates you need to know ahead of the 2026 Florida elections
FL.summary: A rundown of key 2026 Florida election deadlines, including the July 20 party-registration deadline for the August primary and voter photo ID requirements.

KS.title: Race against the mail: Kansas judge restores ballot grace period ahead of August primary
KS.summary: A Kansas judge issued a temporary injunction blocking Senate Bill 4's repeal of the three-day mail ballot grace period, restoring the prior rule ahead of the Aug. 4 primary.

MA.title: Ballot stuffer: Mass. officials say record-tying nine questions slated to go before voters in November
MA.summary: Massachusetts certified a record-tying nine ballot questions for the November election, including proposals on election-day registration and a top-two primary system.

NC.title: New elections rules could make ballot rejections easier in North Carolina
NC.summary: North Carolina's State Board of Elections approved new rules making it easier to reject ballots over voter ID issues, requiring only a majority vote instead of bipartisan agreement.

OK.title: Oklahoma election officials highlight security measures amid White House security concerns
OK.summary: Oklahoma's State Election Board detailed its election security protocols, including hand-marked paper ballots and offline voting devices, following White House claims about election interference.

UT.title: Utah Lt. Gov. tells DOJ not to interfere in state's elections
UT.summary: Utah's election director pushed back on a DOJ letter demanding access to the state's voter database, saying Utah already complies with state and federal election law.

AZ.title: AP Decision Notes: What to expect in Arizona's state primary
AZ.summary: Arizona Republicans are set to select a gubernatorial nominee in the July 21 primary, with four candidates competing to challenge Democratic Gov. Katie Hobbs in November.

DC.title: Civil rights leaders announce 'March on Washington' to defend voting rights
DC.summary: Civil rights leaders announced an August 28 march on Washington to oppose a Supreme Court ruling that weakened Voting Rights Act protections against discriminatory voting laws.

FL.title: A key voting deadline is coming up in Florida. Here's what to know
FL.summary: A Tampa Bay Times guide reminds Florida voters that the deadline to register or change party affiliation ahead of the August 18 primary is July 20.

HI.title: Hawaii to DOJ on election help: No thanks
HI.summary: Hawaii's chief election officer declined a U.S. Department of Justice offer of assistance on voter-eligibility compliance, saying the state already follows federal and state election law.

MO.title: Missouri election officials assure voting systems are safe, reliable
MO.summary: Missouri election officials pushed back on claims of voting system vulnerabilities, citing the state's decentralized process and recent legislative improvements to provisional ballot and military voter protocols.

SC.title: Rep. Ralph Norman launches bid for Lindsey Graham's Senate seat
SC.summary: U.S. Rep. Ralph Norman launched his campaign for South Carolina's vacant U.S. Senate seat following Sen. Lindsey Graham's death, becoming the third major candidate in the race.

TX.title: Election Security Update from Texas Secretary of State Nelson
TX.summary: Texas Secretary of State Jane Nelson announced election security initiatives including a review of all 254 counties, removal of over 8,500 voter registrations tied to commercial mailboxes, and a new secure military ballot option.

WA.title: Washington voters begin casting primary election ballots
WA.summary: Washington's 18-day primary voting period began, with all state legislative seats, 10 U.S. House seats, and five state Supreme Court seats on the ballot for the August 4 primary.

FL.title: Orange County voters kept the Supervisor of Elections Office busy Monday
FL.summary: Florida's July 20 book-closing deadline to register or change party affiliation for the August 18 primary drew heavy in-person turnout at county election offices.

GA.title: Congressional District 13 special election voting underway
GA.summary: Early voting is underway for Georgia's 13th Congressional District special election to fill the seat of the late Rep. David Scott, with Election Day set for July 28.

HI.title: History shows every vote counts in Hawaii legislative races
HI.summary: A look at past razor-thin Hawaii legislative races underscores the stakes of the 2026 cycle, where all 51 House seats and 14 of 25 Senate seats are contested.

KS.title: Kansas judge temporarily blocks election law repealing 3-day grace period for mail-in ballots
KS.summary: A Douglas County judge issued a temporary injunction blocking a new Kansas law that would have eliminated the three-day grace period for mail ballots postmarked by Election Day.

KY.title: Beshear questions Kentucky law on filling a U.S. Senate vacancy
KY.summary: Gov. Andy Beshear questioned Kentucky's 2024 law requiring a special election to fill a U.S. Senate vacancy, suggesting the state constitution may give him appointment power instead.

ME.title: Maine Democrats close in on pick to replace Senate candidate Graham Platner
ME.summary: State Senate President Troy Jackson emerged as the frontrunner to replace Graham Platner as Maine's Democratic U.S. Senate nominee after rivals Shenna Bellows and Nirav Shah withdrew.

MN.title: Voting is open for the 2026 primary election. Here's what to know.
MN.summary: Minnesota's August 11 primary voting is underway via mail, early in-person, and Election Day options, with online and Election Day registration still available.

MO.title: Missouri ballot measure campaigns dominate fundraising and spending for August primary
MO.summary: Campaigns around four constitutional amendments on Missouri's August 4 primary ballot have raised more than $27 million, dominating the state's midterm fundraising.

NC.title: State elections board tightens rules for mail ballots
NC.summary: North Carolina's elections board voted along party lines to adopt rules making it easier for county officials to reject mail ballots over envelope or sealing irregularities.

VA.title: Early voting deadline approaches for Virginia primary election
VA.summary: Early voting continues for Virginia's August 4 primary, though turnout has lagged past cycles amid the date's shift from the traditional June primary.

WI.title: Here's what you need to know to vote in the August primary election in Milwaukee
WI.summary: A voter guide for Milwaukee's August 11 partisan primary covers registration deadlines, early voting locations, and drop-box options.

AZ.title: Here are Arizona's 2026 primary election results
AZ.summary: NPR's live results tracker for Arizona's July 21 primary covers the Republican gubernatorial contest and other statewide and U.S. House races.

HI.title: Hawaii enacts seven election bills in 2026 session, including prohibition on corporate political activity
HI.summary: Hawaii's legislature passed seven election bills in its 2026 session, most notably SB 2471, which restricts corporations from engaging in political activity in state elections.

NY.title: NY Elections, Census and Redistricting Update 07/20/26
NY.summary: An update on litigation over NYC's disbanded Charter Revision Commission and its open-primaries ballot proposal, plus a new state law letting the legislature set constitutional amendment ballot language.

VA.title: What to know about Virginia's Aug. 4 Primary Election: Early voting, deadlines and candidates
VA.summary: A voter guide to Virginia's August 4 primary covering early in-person voting through Aug. 1, the July 24 registration and mail-ballot deadlines, and candidates on the ballot.

WA.title: Washington voters begin casting primary election ballots
WA.summary: Voting is underway in Washington's August 4 primary, which will winnow candidates for all state legislative seats, all 10 U.S. House seats, and five state Supreme Court seats.

WI.title: Can Wisconsin voters void a returned absentee ballot? Issue could head back to court
WI.summary: The Wisconsin Elections Commission reversed course and will no longer let voters void an absentee ballot they've already returned, a change that could reignite litigation over ballot spoiling.
