FL.summary: As mail ballots arrive and early voting begins ahead of Florida's Aug. 18 primary, election officials and advocacy groups are urging voters to research their ballots, including down-ballot nonpartisan races and amendments.

MD.title: Maryland lawmakers ask voters to clear the way for a congressional map designed to boost Democrats
MD.summary: Maryland's legislature passed a constitutional amendment for the November ballot that would let lawmakers redraw the state's congressional map to favor Democrats in all eight U.S. House seats.

MN.title: VoteFMWF.org relaunches with Minnesota primary election information ahead of Aug. 11 vote
MN.summary: The Fargo-Moorhead-West Fargo Chamber relaunched its nonpartisan VoteFMWF.org site with candidate and registration information ahead of Minnesota's Aug. 11 primary.

MO.title: Here are the key 2026 primary election results from Missouri
MO.summary: Missouri voters cast primary ballots Aug. 4 to narrow congressional fields and decide four constitutional amendments, including proposals on income tax and citizen initiative petitions.

SC.title: Early voting to open in S.C. primary to replace Lindsey Graham
SC.summary: Early voting was set to open Aug. 5 for South Carolina's special Republican primary to fill the late Sen. Lindsey Graham's seat, with nine candidates on the Aug. 11 ballot.

TN.title: 2026 Voter Guide | The Tennessee Primary Election is almost here. Here's everything voters need to know
TN.summary: A voter guide ahead of Tennessee's Aug. 6 primary, covering candidates for governor, U.S. Senate and Congress, plus registration and photo ID requirements under the state's newly redrawn congressional map.

IL.title: A federal judge rejects President Trump's attempt to access Illinois voter rolls
IL.summary: A federal judge blocked the Trump administration's attempt to obtain Illinois' full voter registration database, ruling that DOJ's stated justification did not relate to any suspected violation of voting law.

MI.title: Here's how to check if you're registered to vote in Michigan
MI.summary: Ahead of Michigan's August 4 primary, this guide explains how voters can verify their registration status, key deadlines, and accepted forms of ID at the polls.

NC.title: N.C. House passes new election law changes
NC.summary: The North Carolina House passed bills shortening early voting from 17 to 10 days and adding new post-election audit and voter-roll verification requirements, sending them to Gov. Josh Stein.

VA.title: Bert Mizusawa projected to win Republican primary for U.S. Senate in Virginia
VA.summary: Retired Army Maj. Gen. Bert Mizusawa won Virginia's Republican Senate primary and will face incumbent Democratic Sen. Mark Warner in November.

WA.title: AP Decision Notes: What to expect in Washington state's primary
WA.summary: Washington voters cast primary ballots for U.S. House and other offices as Spokane-area wildfire evacuations complicated ballot return options, with the AP outlining how winners will be called under the state's top-two primary system.

MD.title: Maryland Republicans predict legal challenge to constitutional amendment on redistricting
MD.summary: The Maryland Senate gave final approval to a constitutional amendment allowing mid-decade congressional redistricting; Republicans say they plan a lawsuit to keep the measure off the November ballot.

NC.title: Gov. Stein says he'll veto early voting reduction, election changes
NC.summary: Gov. Josh Stein said he will veto House Bill 958, which would shorten early voting in primaries from 17 to 10 days and allow ballot challenges up to three days after an election.

OH.title: Ohio voter ID amendment is officially headed to the November ballot
OH.summary: The Ohio Ballot Board approved language for Issue 3, a constitutional amendment that would enshrine the state's existing photo ID voting requirement, sending it to the November ballot.

PA.title: A routine voter roll update in Pa. prompted misinformation from conservative activists
PA.summary: Pennsylvania's routine move of tens of thousands of voters to inactive status was mischaracterized by conservative activists as a mass purge of fraudulent voters; officials say inactive voters remain registered and eligible.

AK.title: Alaskans get to decide if state races should have contribution limits
AK.summary: Alaska voters are deciding a ballot measure that would reinstate campaign contribution limits for state and local races after courts struck down the prior limits as unconstitutional.

CO.title: US District judge dismisses Trump administration lawsuit against Colorado over voter rolls
CO.summary: A federal judge dismissed with prejudice the Trump administration's lawsuit seeking Colorado voters' sensitive personal data, ruling the DOJ was not entitled to it under federal law.

MN.title: Minnesota high court grills Minneapolis on lack of bipartisan election judges for early voting
MN.summary: The Minnesota Supreme Court heard arguments from a voter advocacy group seeking to force Minneapolis to staff early voting locations with bipartisan election judges as state law requires.

RI.title: Rhode Island legislators restrict immigration enforcement near polling places, enact 18 other election bills in 2026 session
RI.summary: Rhode Island's legislature passed 20 election-related bills in its 2026 session, including one barring ICE agents from operating near polling places and election sites.

WA.title: Washington primary election voting ends today. The race for its 3rd Congressional District is just getting started
WA.summary: Washington's top-two primary wrapped up with the 3rd Congressional District seen as one of the few competitive races likely to be a toss-up in the November general election.

CT.title: Early Voting Enters Final Weekend As Officials Encourage Participation And Warn Of Election Related Scams
CT.summary: Connecticut election officials urged voters to use the final weekend of early voting ahead of the Aug. 11 primary while warning residents to watch for election-related scams.

KS.title: Still the same: Kansas voters reject Supreme Court amendment, opt for status quo
KS.summary: Kansas voters rejected by a wide margin a constitutional amendment that would have replaced the state's merit-based judicial nominating process with direct elections for Supreme Court justices.

MI.title: 4 takeaways from Tuesday's primary election results
MI.summary: Progressive Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan's U.S. Senate primary over Rep. Haley Stevens, while Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson and Rep. John James secured their parties' gubernatorial nominations.

MO.title: Missouri August 2026 election results: Key races and issues
MO.summary: Missouri voters approved Amendments 1 and 2 while decisively rejecting Amendments 4 and 5, including a measure that would have phased out the state income tax.

NC.title: North Carolina Governor Signals Veto of Anti-Voter Bill Shortening Early Voting, and Lengthening the Window for Ballot Challenges
NC.summary: Gov. Josh Stein said he intends to veto House Bill 958, which would cut primary early voting from 17 to 10 days, extend the window for challenging ballots, and direct election officials to use the federal SAVE database to remove voters.

NJ.title: NJ voter ID debate grows after Gov. Sherrill signals openness to legislation
NJ.summary: Gov. Mikie Sherrill's openness to a state voter ID law drew pushback from civil rights groups and support from Republican lawmakers, following revelations that a Motor Vehicle Commission software error had registered about 6,600 noncitizens to vote.

WA.title: Washington's primary election results
WA.summary: Washington's 3rd Congressional District primary set up a November rematch between Republican state Sen. John Braun and Democratic Rep. Marie Gluesenkamp Perez in one of the country's most closely watched House races.

AK.title: Saturday is the deadline to request an absentee by-mail ballot in Alaska's primary election
AK.summary: Alaska voters have until Aug. 8 to request an absentee by-mail ballot for the state's Aug. 18 primary election, which decides races for governor, U.S. Senate, U.S. House, and the Legislature.

AR.title: Bill Teeter wins unopposed contest for House District 44
AR.summary: Bill Teeter won the special election for Arkansas House District 44, running unopposed to serve out the remainder of the late Rep. Stan Berry's term.

HI.title: Hawaii election officials urge last-minute votes as primary turnout lags
HI.summary: With turnout trailing the prior primary's pace ahead of Hawaii's all-mail Aug. 8 primary, election officials urged voters to use drop boxes or voter service centers since it is too late to mail ballots.

TN.title: Tennessee primary election results live blog
TN.summary: Tennessee's Aug. 6 midterm primary decided nominees for governor, Congress, and statehouse seats, including Marsha Blackburn's Republican gubernatorial nomination against Democrat Jerri Green in November.

DC.title: DOJ Denied Access to D.C. Voter Rolls by Obama Judge
DC.summary: A federal judge ruled the Justice Department lacks legal authority to compel D.C. to hand over its full voter list, the latest in a long string of DOJ losses in similar suits against states nationwide.

DE.title: Gov. Meyer signs John Lewis Voting Rights Act, enacting state-level voting protections
DE.summary: Governor Matt Meyer signed HB 444, Delaware's own John Lewis Voting Rights Act, creating state-level protections against discriminatory voting practices and empowering the state attorney general to challenge suppressive election practices.

FL.title: All Florida counties will offer early voting for August primary this weekend. Where to find a polling place
FL.summary: Early voting for Florida's Aug. 18 statewide primary begins this weekend in every county, with the article listing voting windows and polling locations for Central Florida counties.

GA.title: Overhaul or gridlock: Georgia's push for new voting system faces tight timeline, legal risks
GA.summary: Georgia's newly formed Election Equipment Specifications and Standards Committee held its first meeting to plan a replacement for the state's touchscreen voting system, with procurement experts warning the transition to hand-marked ballots by 2028 faces a tight timeline and possible vendor litigation.

MN.title: Early Voting In Minnesota Primaries Continue Through Monday
MN.summary: Early voting continues through Monday ahead of Minnesota's Aug. 11 primary, which includes DFL and GOP contests for governor and U.S. Senate.

NV.title: Lawmakers eye proposals to shield elections from federal interference, speed up ballot processing
NV.summary: A Nevada legislative committee voted to sponsor a 2027 bill, modeled on New Mexico legislation, restricting armed federal agents near polling places to shield state-run elections from federal interference.

VA.title: Gov. Spanberger celebrates anniversary of Voting Rights Act Thursday, signs bills aimed at strengthening voting rights
VA.summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger marked the 61st anniversary of the Voting Rights Act in Norfolk by signing a series of bills to strengthen voter protections and election security in Virginia.

AZ.title: Court rejects fears about 2022 voter registration law, allows it to be enforced
AZ.summary: The Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals, sitting en banc, rejected a challenge to an Arizona law restricting who may return another voter's ballot, ruling it is not unconstitutionally vague and can be enforced.

SC.title: ACLU seeks role in lawsuit challenging South Carolina's open primary system
SC.summary: The ACLU of South Carolina moved to intervene in the state Republican Party's federal lawsuit seeking to close primaries, arguing the change would improperly exclude independent voters from taxpayer-funded elections.

TX.title: County officials say Texas law allowing more weekend voting will delay election results, spike costs
TX.summary: Texas election administrators told a House committee that Senate Bill 2753's expanded weekend early-voting schedule, taking effect in late 2027, will raise costs and slow reporting of results.

WV.title: Pritt Voluntarily Removes Himself From General Election Ballot
WV.summary: Former Delegate David Elliott Pritt withdrew from the November ballot after facing child enticement charges; state law bars the Republican Party from naming a replacement, leaving the Democratic candidate unopposed.

WY.title: U.S. Attorney's Office Warns Non-Citizens Against Voting In Upcoming Elections
WY.source: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Wyoming
WY.summary: Ahead of Wyoming's Aug. 18 primary, the U.S. Attorney's Office announced coordination with federal law enforcement to monitor for noncitizen voting and pledged to prosecute violations.

AL.title: Alabama's special primary is Aug. 11: Here's who is running in District 7
AL.summary: Alabama voters in four congressional districts head to the polls Aug. 11 for a special primary, with a competitive Republican race in District 7 and Democrat Terri Sewell advancing unopposed.

HI.title: Incumbents Gov. Green, Maui's Bissen, Reps. Case and Tokuda head to November contest
HI.summary: Hawaii's Aug. 8 primary wrapped up with Gov. Josh Green, Maui Mayor Richard Bissen, and U.S. Reps. Ed Case and Jill Tokuda all winning their primaries and advancing to the November general election.

IN.title: Recount upends election result for Indiana Senate District 23 — Paula Copenhaver beats incumbent Deery
IN.summary: The Indiana Recount Commission reversed the outcome of a three-vote Senate District 23 primary after discarding ballots for missing signatures and seals, handing the race to Trump-backed challenger Paula Copenhaver.

IA.title: Judge rules Gluba-Cutler ticket can't be on Iowa's 2026 ballot
IA.summary: A Polk County judge upheld a State Objections Panel ruling keeping Libertarian candidates Nicholas Gluba and Jules Cutler off Iowa's November ballot after Cutler missed the candidacy affidavit deadline.

MD.title: Maryland's redistricting amendment could reshape 2028 congressional races
MD.summary: Following the Legislature's vote to place a redistricting constitutional amendment on the November ballot, analysts examine how new congressional maps could reshape central Maryland and Eastern Shore districts by 2028.

MA.title: Mass. is set to see 9 ballot questions this fall. One in particular that could upend how Beacon Hill works
MA.summary: Massachusetts voters will decide nine ballot questions in November, including a measure backed by the state auditor that would subject the governor's office and Legislature to the public records law.

MN.title: Choices on the direction of both parties await Minnesota primary voters
MN.summary: Minnesota voters cast primary ballots Aug. 11 in competitive Democratic contests for governor and U.S. Senate that will help define the party's direction heading into the midterms.

NC.title: NC voting bill heads to governor's desk — and he's already planning to reject it
NC.summary: Gov. Josh Stein said he will veto House Bill 958, which would shorten primary early voting from 17 to 10 days, extend post-election ballot challenge windows, and require use of the federal SAVE database to purge voters.

AK.title: Alaska state elections attorney says it's OK for candidates to temporarily conceal finances
AK.summary: An attorney defending the Alaska Division of Elections argued in state court that candidates for state office are not required to disclose their finances when filing, raising concerns about voters' ability to review candidates' finances during the primary.

DE.title: Delaware becomes the 12th state to enact a state-level voting rights act
DE.summary: Gov. Matt Meyer signed the Delaware John Lewis Voting Rights Act, prohibiting voter suppression and vote dilution and allowing private citizens to challenge discriminatory election policies; the law takes effect July 1, 2027.

GA.title: Georgia committee confronts tight timeline for election system overhaul
GA.summary: A newly formed committee of lawmakers and election experts met to begin planning Georgia's transition to a hand-marked paper ballot voting system by 2028.

MA.title: Voter guide: What you need to know about the Massachusetts 2026 primary election
MA.summary: A guide to the September 1 Massachusetts state primary covers registration and voting deadlines, the state's three voting methods, and the competitive federal, state, and local races on the ballot.

OK.title: Oklahoma election officials remind voters of Election Day laws ahead of Aug. 25 runoff
OK.summary: Oklahoma election officials outlined polling-place conduct rules ahead of the Aug. 25 runoff primary, including restrictions on campaigning within 300 feet of polling sites and provisions for voters with emergencies.

OK.title: Oklahomans to decide on adding voter ID requirements to state constitution
OK.summary: State Question 846, on the Aug. 25 ballot, would enshrine photo ID requirements for voting in the Oklahoma Constitution and give the Legislature broader authority to set ID specifications for all voting methods.

WI.title: Wisconsin primary election 2026 voter guide: What to know before you vote Tuesday
WI.summary: A guide ahead of Wisconsin's Aug. 11 partisan primary covers polling locations, required photo ID, and absentee ballot procedures, noting voters may participate in only one party's primary.

DC.title: Judge dismissed DOJ suit seeking a full, unredacted copy of DC's voter registration data
DC.summary: A federal judge dismissed the Justice Department's lawsuit seeking a full, unredacted copy of D.C.'s voter registration data, ruling the administration lacked legal authority to obtain the complete list.

KY.title: Beshear: Aug. 3 no legal deadline for Senate vacancy amid McConnell's absence
KY.summary: Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear said the oft-cited Aug. 3 deadline has no legal bearing on his options for calling a special election, amid ongoing questions about Sen. Mitch McConnell's extended absence.

MD.title: Maryland Democrats put measure on 2026 ballot, making it the fourth state to take action towards redistricting ahead of 2028
MD.summary: Maryland's General Assembly voted to place a constitutional amendment on the 2026 ballot removing redistricting-criteria requirements for congressional maps, part of a wave of states positioning ahead of 2028 redistricting.

AL.title: 2026 Alabama special congressional primary results
AL.summary: Alabama voters selected U.S. House nominees in four congressional districts under a newly redrawn map that eliminates one of the state's two majority-Black districts, after the primaries were postponed from May following a Supreme Court decision on Southern congressional maps.

GA.title: The 2026 midterms are heating up, but this election panel is focused on 2028
GA.summary: A newly formed legislative committee began mapping out Georgia's transition to a hand-marked paper ballot voting system by 2028, working under a tight timeline to recommend a replacement for the state's current ballot-marking-device system.

MN.title: Governor, Senate nominees give Minnesota voters a choice between accomplished women
MN.summary: Minnesota's Aug. 11 primary set the fall ticket, with Amy Klobuchar and Lisa Demuth advancing in the governor's race and Peggy Flanagan and Michele Tafoya advancing for U.S. Senate.

NH.title: Get ready to vote in NH: How to register, what documents to bring and more
NH.summary: A guide to New Hampshire's 2026 midterm elections outlines voter registration requirements, the documentation needed to prove identity, age, citizenship, and domicile, and key registration deadlines.

SC.title: In South Carolina, Sen. Darline Graham advances to a GOP special primary runoff
SC.summary: Sen. Darline Graham, appointed to complete her late brother Lindsey Graham's term, advanced to an Aug. 25 GOP primary runoff against Rep. Ralph Norman for the U.S. Senate nomination.

WI.title: David Crowley pulls off upset over Francesca Hong in Wisconsin's Democratic primary for governor
WI.summary: Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley narrowly defeated democratic socialist state lawmaker Francesca Hong in Wisconsin's Aug. 11 Democratic gubernatorial primary; Crowley will face Republican Rep. Tom Tiffany in November.

CT.title: CT Gov. Ned Lamont defeats Josh Elliott in Democratic primary
CT.summary: Incumbent Gov. Ned Lamont won Connecticut's Aug. 11 Democratic gubernatorial primary with 68% of the vote, while longtime U.S. Rep. John Larson lost his 1st District primary to former Hartford mayor Luke Bronin.

DC.title: Federal court blocks another part of Trump mail-in voting executive order
DC.summary: A federal judge blocked the U.S. Postal Service from implementing part of a presidential executive order restricting mail-in voting ahead of the November midterms, ruling the executive branch lacks authority to regulate elections.

SC.title: GOP Special Primary Runoff set for August 25 between Graham and Norman
SC.summary: After no candidate cleared 50% in South Carolina's special U.S. Senate primary, Sen. Darline Graham and Rep. Ralph Norman advanced to an Aug. 25 Republican runoff, with early voting set for Aug. 19-21.

VT.title: The results from Vermont's 2026 primary election
VT.summary: Vermont voters cast ballots in contested Aug. 11 primaries, with Amanda Janoo narrowly winning the Democratic gubernatorial nomination and Molly Gray winning the Democratic lieutenant governor primary.

NH.title: Lawsuit challenges repeal of student IDs for voting in NH
NH.summary: A voting rights group sued to reinstate school-issued IDs as acceptable identification for voter registration and ballot access in New Hampshire, arguing the 2026 repeal disproportionately burdens young voters.

OK.title: Oklahomans to decide on adding voter ID requirements to state constitution
OK.summary: Oklahoma voters will decide State Question 846 on Aug. 25, a constitutional amendment that would enshrine voter ID requirements and give the legislature expanded authority to set election law.

TX.title: Appeals court revives key parts of Texas voter suppression law found to harm voters with disabilities
TX.summary: The Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals reversed a lower court decision and revived nine provisions of Texas's Senate Bill 1 restricting mail-in voting and voter assistance, rejecting disability-rights challenges largely on standing grounds.

NE.title: Judge dismisses lawsuit from RNC challenging Nebraska voter law
NE.summary: A Lancaster County district judge dismissed with prejudice the RNC's lawsuit challenging a Nebraska law that lets certain overseas voters with a Nebraska-registered parent vote in the state, ruling the law had at least one constitutional application.

AL.title: Alabama special primary round-up: Low turnout, few surprises in congressional races
AL.summary: A round-up of Alabama's Aug. 11 special congressional primaries found low turnout and few upsets, with Jerry Carl winning the District 1 GOP nomination and Rhett Marques winning District 2's crowded Republican primary.

AK.title: What to know about Tuesday's primary election
AK.summary: A guide to Alaska's Aug. 18 top-four primary covering which races are on the ballot, voting procedures, and Ballot Measure 1 on campaign contribution limits.

FL.title: Florida primary ballots top 900,000 amid mail-in, early voting
FL.summary: More than 900,000 ballots had been cast ahead of Florida's Aug. 18 primary through mail and early voting, with Republicans favoring in-person early voting and Democrats favoring mail ballots.

FL.title: Early voting ballots trickle in ahead of Tuesday's primary elections
FL.summary: An update on early voting turnout in Florida as the state heads into its Aug. 18 primary election.

GA.title: Republicans outraise Democrats in most — but not all — statewide races
GA.summary: New campaign finance filings show Republican candidates outraising Democrats in most of Georgia's statewide 2026 races, ahead of the state's November general election.

HI.title: 5 takeaways from the 2026 primary election
HI.summary: A recap of Hawaii's Aug. 8 primary election, which saw historically low turnout of about 33% and incumbents largely holding their seats.

IN.title: Paperwork snafu leaves Democrats without candidate for Indiana Senate seat
IN.summary: A Democratic Party filing error left the four-term mayor of Vincennes off the November ballot for an Indiana state Senate seat.

MS.title: 'One person, one vote:' redistricting panel gets primer
MS.summary: A Mississippi House select committee on redistricting received a briefing on redistricting basics, amid concerns raised by a recent U.S. Supreme Court decision affecting majority-Black districts.

MT.title: Alani Bankhead stays in Montana U.S. Senate race
MT.summary: Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Alani Bankhead confirmed she will remain in Montana's 2026 Senate race past the withdrawal deadline, despite pressure from within her party to drop out.

SC.title: Endorsements pile up for Graham, Norman in SC Senate primary runoff
SC.summary: Endorsements are piling up for Sen. Darline Graham and Rep. Ralph Norman ahead of their Aug. 25 Republican runoff for South Carolina's U.S. Senate seat.

FL.title: Nearly 1.5 million Floridians have voted in advance of Tuesday's primary elections
FL.summary: Of the 1.47 million ballots cast so far in Florida's Aug. 18 primary, 665,003 came from Republicans, 611,882 from Democrats, and 172,268 from no-party-affiliation voters.

AK.title: Alaska primary early vote total nears all-time record
AK.summary: Early voting for Alaska's Aug. 18 primary approached the all-time record, with ballots received climbing toward the 2022 primary high as Election Day neared.

AZ.title: Court revives Arizona voting restrictions ahead of midterms
AZ.summary: The Ninth Circuit reinstated two provisions of Arizona's 2022 voter registration law - automatic cancellation when voters move counties and criminalized 'mechanisms for voting' - allowing them to take effect before the midterms.

CT.title: Connecticut live primary results: Democratic Rep. Larson loses to challenger
CT.summary: U.S. Rep. John Larson lost the Democratic primary in Connecticut's 1st Congressional District to former Hartford Mayor Luke Bronin, ending Larson's 14-term tenure in the House.

FL.title: Early voting wrapping up in Florida, winner predictions stay unchanged
FL.summary: Florida's mandatory early-voting period for the Aug. 18 primary wrapped up across most counties, with some running an extra day under local extensions.

TX.title: Texas' mail ballot ID requirements restored by federal appeals court
TX.summary: The 5th Circuit restored nine provisions of Texas's 2021 election law (SB 1), including mail-ballot ID and voter-assistance requirements, after finding the challengers lacked standing.

GA.title: Georgia 2026 election: Registration opens for absentee ballots
GA.summary: Georgia voters can begin requesting absentee ballots on Aug. 17 for the Nov. 3 general election, with the application deadline set for Oct. 23.

MD.title: Maryland election board 'extended' ballot comment period. DeMarinis says it didn't.
MD.summary: The Maryland State Board of Elections said it extended the public-comment deadline for Prince George's County ballot questions to Aug. 11, but the county's elections administrator says she was never notified and closed the comment period under the original July 30 deadline.

MN.title: Minnesota authorities reviewing voting vouching stunt by conservative influencer
MN.summary: A conservative influencer dressed in a niqab visited Minneapolis polling sites during the primary to impersonate registered voters; state officials condemned the stunt and law enforcement is investigating possible violations of state ballot-application laws.

NC.title: NC Gov. Stein vetoes elections, judicial discipline bills
NC.summary: Gov. Josh Stein vetoed House Bill 958, a Republican-backed measure that would have shortened the early voting period in primaries from 17 to 10 days and allowed ballot challenges to extend three days after Election Day.

WY.title: Wyoming Voters Decide Crowded Statewide Primaries Tuesday
WY.summary: Wyoming holds its 2026 primary election Aug. 18, with crowded Republican fields for governor, the state's lone U.S. House seat, and U.S. Senate all decided by plurality vote with no runoff.

AK.title: Alaska's primary election day is Tuesday. Here's what to know.
AK.summary: Alaska voters have until 8 p.m. Tuesday to cast ballots in the nonpartisan blanket primary, which advances the top four finishers to a ranked-choice general election; over 31,000 ballots had already been cast early.

FL.title: Florida primary election 2026: Polls open as voters cast ballots in key races
FL.summary: Polls opened across Florida Tuesday for the 2026 primary, deciding nominees for governor, several congressional districts, and a U.S. Senate special election.

MA.title: Massachusetts elections 2026: Everything you need to know to vote
MA.summary: A voter guide lays out key dates for Massachusetts' September 1 primary, including the August 22 voter registration deadline and mail-ballot request deadline.

NH.title: Lawsuit Challenges NH Student ID Voter Restriction
NH.summary: A new lawsuit challenges a New Hampshire restriction on using student IDs for voter registration, the latest in a series of legal fights over the state's voter identification requirements ahead of the 2026 midterms.
